member of the commission. − mr president, i will try to be extremely brief. first, regarding the question asked by the earl of dartmouth, in a case involving the infringement of intellectual property rights, including patents in third countries, it is appropriate that the operators concerned have recourse to the available enforcement means, including legal proceedings if necessary, as this is a case between two private firms. in the specific case of avon protection, it would be appropriate for your constituent first to seek redress for the alleged infringement of the patent via the existing legal framework in korea. should the available enforcement in korea not be fair or expeditious enough, then the commission could look into the matter. regarding the remarks made by mr jadot, the initial draft of the korean legislation would have forced eu car makers to reduce the co2 emissions of their cars twice as much as korean car makers. this was mainly because the proposed emission cuts were not proportional, but highly progressive, depending on the level of emissions of the respective cars. consequently, despite being responsible for only a small share of car sales in korea – 3% in 2009 – and therefore of total co2 car emissions in korea, eu car makers would have been asked to contribute disproportionately. their average emissions reduction between 2009 and 2015 would have been 23%, compared with just 10% for their korean counterparts, which account for 95% of total car sales in korea. such burden sharing would not have been fair, and that is why we discussed it with the korean counterpart. finally, i would like to thank everybody involved in this legislative process – the committee on international trade (inta), the commission rapporteurs, the chair of the inta committee, the council and my own staff at the commission – for what, i would say, is a very good example of what the ratification procedure should be under the lisbon treaty.
in writing. i believe that the entry into force of the eu-korea free trade agreement would have positive effects on the union's economy. first, it would allow savings of an estimated eur 1,6 billion per year in customs duties. we would also see increased trade, particularly in services, where future trade growth is estimated at 70%, and in agriculture, where, at present, the european union's annual exports to korea are worth €1 billion. this agreement is also ambitious and innovative, the first of a new generation of bilateral free trade agreements which includes both a chapter on sustainable development and labour standards and a monitoring mechanism in which civil society will be involved. concerns about the difficulties that korean competition might cause to more sensitive union industries, such as the automotive industry, are allayed by the inclusion of the safeguard clause in the agreement. it will impose measures to monitor imports and exports and to assess the impact of the agreement on the various sectors.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i wish to thank the rapporteur, mr kalfin, and other members of this parliament for their constructive approach to the proposal, which highlights the significant interest parliament shows in the european investment bank’s activities. i believe that parliament has now achieved a balanced report which will provide a solid basis for the upcoming negotiations with the commission and the council. last april, the commission issued a legislative proposal to amend decision 633/2009/ec following a mid-term review of the application of the eib external mandate. it is now essential to make a timely decision allowing the eib to pursue its external work until 2013, while at the same time enhancing the mandate to ensure that eib investments outside the eu are increasingly aligned with eu policy objectives, in particular in the areas of climate change and development. as regards today’s vote, several amendments put forward are acceptable to the commission. those amendments relate to, firstly, the request to enhance the development aspects of eib activity and, secondly, the call for an increase in the regional ceilings of the general mandate. this could, inter alia, allow the eib to maintain a reasonable level of activity in certain regions, notably pre-accession. it should also be instrumental in helping the eib to take part in our joint efforts to provide support to tunisia and egypt in the democratic transition process. thirdly, the general request for more transparency, better reporting and better efficiency. on the other hand, additional negotiation will be needed in the context of the trialogue for other amendments. those points relate to, firstly, the restriction from eligibility under the climate change mandate of countries deemed by the council not to have committed to meeting appropriate climate-change-related targets. secondly, there are some amendments aimed at establishing the regional operational guidelines as delegated acts, which would not allow them to be operational and flexible general orientations as we initially foresaw them in the commission proposal. thirdly and finally, there are some amendments which relate to longer-term issues such as the creation of an eu platform for cooperation and development, or the reflections on longer-term perspectives for cooperation and development financing, that are not strictly related to the implementation of the current mandate. we should be careful, because the negotiation on these amendments might delay the adoption of the decision, and we might consider not engaging in lengthy and complicated negotiations in the framework of this decision. trialogue between the institutions will start on the basis of the report adopted today. the common aim is to have the decision adopted before the summer in order to pre-empt any risk of non-decision by october 2011, which would cause the suspension of eib external activities after vice-president of the commission. − mr president, of course, i do not know how much you know of the history of this issue, but i am particularly pleased to replace my colleague, maroš šefčovič, in replying to this question, because for the last five years it has been my domain. i was responsible for this area and am very pleased to tell you what has really been changed. it was an expert groups issue and, of course, unfortunately i have only three minutes to reply to your question. i will try to do my best. as we mentioned, the new framework for commission expert group was adopted in november 2010. it provides that, when defining the composition of these groups, the commission departments concerned shall aim to ensure the balanced representation of relevant areas of expertise and areas of interest, while taking into account the work to be carried out and the specific expertise required. the new framework for commission expert groups provides for clearer and stronger horizontal rules on how to manage conflicts of interest. according to these rules, the relevant commission services shall inform experts who are appointed in a personal capacity that, by accepting to be members of the group, they commit themselves to acting independently and in the public interest. these rules, which apply to all expert groups, constitute the commission’s sole policy on this matter and are requirements that all services must fulfil. in october 2005, in an example of good cooperation with parliament and jens bonde, mep, the commission launched an online public register of expert groups which provided valuable information on different aspects, such as the group’s mission, tasks and composition. since 2007, the commission has been gradually publishing the names of expert group members, whether formally or informally established. this goes beyond the commitment made by the commission in the 2005 framework for expert groups, which applied only to members of formal groups. in 2009, the composition of expert groups was fully disclosed in the register. thus, in principle, the names of all members of expert groups are available. this was a very strong requirement that parliament imposed in 2005 and it has been complied with. following the adoption of the new framework for commission expert groups, the commission drew up a new version of the register in december 2010. this new version enhances transparency by providing new and more accurate information, notably on the type of entities listed and the procedures used to select members. furthermore, the new register increases transparency on the activities carried out by each group by allowing commission departments to either publish relevant information in the register, or to provide a link from the register to a dedicated website where information can be found. finally, the presentation and readability of data encoded in the register has also been improved. given the huge amount of information to be treated, the transition from the old to the new version of the register is still ongoing. thus, some of the data still needs to be validated. the transition needs to be completed over the next few months. moreover, because for five and a half years i discussed these issues with various civil society organisations and members of parliament, i would ask you not to mystify the experts. there is no arithmetical link between the composition of expert groups and a decision. the decision is the commission’s political responsibility. parliament’s committees have the same political responsibility when they meet in the presence of the same lobbyists. do not forget that in 2005 we also launched a transparency register, then called the ‘lobbyist register’ and now the ‘register of interest representatives’, which has now developed into a joint register with parliament. that is a great step ahead. so something has been done. things do not look so bad.

in writing. − rising food prices in the european union and worldwide are a major concern in 2011. the causes are diverse and difficult to anticipate and control. but there are also causes that we can and must control. a heavy supply chain with too many intermediaries, natural disasters caused by climate change, low incomes from agriculture or volatility in the agricultural market are just some of the reasons why the price of agricultural products has risen unjustifiably at european level. i believe that decision-makers at european level must make lower food prices a major objective on the european and global political agenda. we are not talking here of interfering with the free market, of course, but of eliminating those speculative activities which unjustifiably parasitize the supply-demand path, illegitimately influencing and distorting price formation. i voted in favour of this resolution because europe needs measures to ensure that food prices are not artificially raised by speculative intermediaries. the european union needs a simplification of the food supply chain so that tick-peddlers are eliminated from the trade flow. in this way, citizens and producers alike will benefit and the economic crisis will be more easily overcome.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document. although the forecasts show that world stocks of grain, wheat and sugar will be higher than in 2007, although the situation that led to the food crisis in 2008 does not seem to be repeated, there is an overreaction of the markets, excessive volatility, explained by the actions of investment funds speculators. moreover, entire sectors of agriculture are threatened. i see this in my country, in romania. and the 5 percent increase in the vat, which went up to 24 percent, was immediately reflected in the price increases. it is hard to accept that a farmer who works hard every day is the victim of a market game, a game played tens of thousands of miles away on the computers of companies that have nothing to do with agriculture but have enough money to unbalance world markets.
in writing. − global food prices have reached dramatic levels in recent times. thus, in december last year, they exceeded those recorded at the height of the economic crisis. the un recently declared that the scenario of over-supply underlying these price fluctuations is implausible. in the mid-1990s, a speculative market was created, centered on food, and it was amplified by the financial crisis. today, speculators profit from the unregulated markets and make millions from this activity. this speculative behaviour directly affects people's living standards and can contribute to political instability. i therefore consider that the union should aim to combat food price speculation through regulation and transparency. for this reason, i voted in favour of the resolution on food price increases.
in writing. − the global economic crisis and rising food and fuel prices have brought poverty and hunger to millions of citizens, but especially to poor people in developing countries, who are most exposed to the negative impact of price volatility and the food crisis. the european union as a whole is and remains the main producer of food. therefore, joint research and training capacities in the field of sustainable agricultural methods and new technologies should be developed at community level in order to mitigate the collapse of agricultural systems and temporarily prevent this crisis. i believe it is the duty of the european union and the member states to adopt a common trade strategy that adequately protects food markets and to decide together on their own agricultural and food production policies.

rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on industry, research and energy. − achieving european objectives on sustainable development, energy security and climate change requires a substantial financial commitment, particularly in terms of innovation and research, as well as new ways to complement existing funding. the commission should therefore examine the feasibility of introducing a carbon tax, similar to vat, to be applied to every product on the internal market. it is very important, however, to eliminate the possibility of passing this tax on to consumers, and to analyse the risk to the competitiveness of european industries in the single market. the efficiency of the use of structural funds and european investment bank funds, as well as the coordination between union, national and other forms of support that can act as a lever to stimulate investment in energy efficiency, needs to be improved. appropriate investment in energy supply and energy efficiency leads to reduced dependence on market fluctuations and positive consequences for the union economy. the commission should carry out as soon as possible an impact study on the taxation of financial transactions at union and global level, analysing its effect and the economic benefit created by reducing the volume of speculative financial transactions that are currently causing serious market disruption. the study should analyse whether taxation of the financial sector at union level can indeed be a source of own resources for the union and contain concrete proposals on the procedure for introducing that tax.
the european union already has a higher tax burden than the united states, japan and other global economic powers, by almost 10 percentage points, and this means that european firms are at a competitive disadvantage to american firms and other firms that operate globally. sure, there's a lot of excitement about introducing a new financial transaction tax. but we all know that this financial sector has an incredible ability to shift any cost onto citizens and businesses. that is why i believe that we can only talk about a financial transaction tax in the european union if we also have a global agreement on this issue. secondly, i want to support fully the introduction of the european bond for the financing of european infrastructure projects as a means of attracting resources and of attracting resources from the private sector to finance these projects.
i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mrs podimata. the economic and financial crisis has exposed a number of disproportionate incentives in the financial sector, as well as weaknesses in the regulatory and supervisory framework of the financial system. it should contribute more equitably and sustainably to the cost of this crisis. but we must ensure that the financial transaction tax, introduced as a result of an impact assessment, is not ultimately passed on to consumers, and therefore to citizens. we therefore believe that clear rules should be established to prevent this. public procurement represents 17% of the eu's gdp and is an important market, particularly in areas such as health, transport and energy. the implementation of electronic public procurement systems in the member states has led to increased transparency and significant savings to national budgets. i call on the commission and the member states to ensure that by 2015 at least 50% of public procurement is carried out through electronic public procurement systems, thus fulfilling the commitments made by the member states in manchester in 2005. i also ask the commission to implement the e-invoice initiative, which is an important tool for reducing tax evasion. member states should substantially improve their use of existing structural funds for research and innovation, transport and energy efficiency projects, by supporting citizens to acquire the necessary skills, improving the performance of national systems and implementing smart specialisation strategies and transnational projects. in this context, we support the issuance of european bonds to finance infrastructure projects. i also draw attention to the under-exploited potential of innovative revolving financial instruments aimed at increasing the energy efficiency of buildings. member states should also initiate the preparation of post-2013 structural funds programmes with a particular focus on innovation, transport, energy efficiency and smart specialisation.
achieving the europe 2020 goals requires massive investment at european level in research, education and infrastructure. however, in the context of austerity policies pursued by european governments and growing deficits, these objectives can only be achieved through alternative financing methods. i am referring both to the joint issue of bonds to enable member states to cover their deficits by converting part of their own debts into european debts and facilitating access to low-interest loans, and to the financial transaction tax. the latter would envisage a minimum tax on the financial sector, whose activities account for some 73% of global gdp, and would be used to discourage financial speculation, regulate markets and invest in european projects. the union needs to send a strong signal for solutions to the financial crisis, by implementing these taxes in the first place.
a financial transaction tax would hurt competitiveness, but a fairly globally applied tax could be a way of raising additional funds for global policies. in order to have a coherent position, the eu needs to make an impact assessment of the introduction of such a tax. the study should include the possibility of the risk of relocation of foreign investments to less transparent areas. it is therefore necessary to examine to what extent the options under consideration can be used as innovative financial mechanisms. such a fee should not have a negative impact on the banking system. avoiding possible consequences for smes and individual investments are also two very important issues. finally, i would stress that only a financial activities tax could be feasible at european level. that way, you would tax corporations, not every participant in a financial transaction.
in writing. having lived through the experience of the financial crisis, which demonstrated the volatility of financial institutions' shares, i considered it necessary to introduce a financial transaction tax at european level, a subject which was also discussed intensively at european council level. the s&d group, from which the rapporteur was also appointed, has the main credit for the success of the report. we have succeeded in sending a strong signal, in particular by adopting the most problematic amendment, which aims to introduce this tax at european level, rather than at global level. in this way, we show our good intentions and our belief that within the union measures can be more effective with quantifiable and immediate benefits. in this respect, i must repeat that the austerity policy, which is being vigorously promoted by conservative governments, is deeply unfair and even demagogic, all the more so since the economic crisis was not triggered by ordinary people but by financial and banking institutions, which had a much too liberal view of the financial system. the recovery must be thought of in terms of fairness and that is why this tax is the best measure we have at our disposal.

the current economic and financial crisis has hit the healthcare sector hard, with many member states cutting public health budgets. some have even decided to close hospitals in smaller towns or that perform a small number of surgeries. especially are patients in rural areas or isolated communities forced to travel tens of miles to receive specialized medical care. health inequalities therefore exist not only between member states but also between their regions. budget cuts to national health programs are jeopardizing access to the latest and most effective treatments. also, reducing subsidies for some treatments means that patients cannot continue treatment, with much higher consequences and costs for their health. inequalities in the european health system also cause medical staff to migrate to another member state to practice their profession. that is why the commission (president interrupts)
inequalities in health are a challenge to the union's commitment to solidarity, social and economic cohesion, human rights and equal opportunities. the health dimension must therefore be present in all union policies. member states should be encouraged to include the principle of health in all policies, in the development of new action plans in any field, in order to contribute to reducing inequalities and to creating a high level of health protection. i support the need to develop a set of specific indicators to monitor health inequalities and comparable indicators that could enable national authorities to assess progress in this area with a view to improving health systems. as part of the effort to tackle health inequalities, we also need to see the establishment of a strategic workforce planning mechanism to ensure that the recruitment and retention of health professionals is carried out.
the world health organization estimates that smoking, alcohol, lack of exercise and poor diet will cause 70 percent of all disease and premature death by 2020. the fact that there is a systematic correlation between health status and social class indicates that these differences result from inadequate access to basic social services. this shows that health inequalities are not the result of individual choice but are avoidable and unjust. for the first time in the 2007-13 budgetary programming, health was proposed as one of the top 10 priorities of the structural funds. the european commission must, however, include in its monitoring procedures of the europe 2020 strategy stratified comparative indicators according to socioeconomic status and take into account discrimination based on age criteria.
in writing. there are major differences between health systems both within and between member states. i want to emphasize that in times of economic crisis, no government should have the right to drastically cut health budgets. i would like to draw your attention to the situation of the health system in romania. due to budget cuts by the current government, an impressive number of romanian medical specialists are emigrating, the chronically ill no longer have access to medical services and compensated medication, and hospital equipment is outdated. in addition, the right-wing government proposes that hospitals be pooled, although in some medical units there are not enough beds for all patients and they must always be supplemented. i therefore want to call on the european commission to do more to align health service standards and to put pressure on member states to allocate adequate budgets to guarantee citizens affordable and quality health services.
in the current economic crisis, the promotion of good governance in tax matters is imperative both within and outside the eu. i would point out that each state is responsible for deciding its own tax policy. in this context, obstacles must be avoided and cooperation between states must be promoted. the fight against tax havens is a key priority. they contribute to the decline of the quality of the political system in developing countries. it also encourages economic crime, making it more profitable. in this way, the inequitable distribution of tax revenues is in turn increased. another measure concerns the enhancement of the exchange of information between all member states. it is also necessary to increase the participation of developing countries in relevant international fora.
in writing. the report demonstrates that the eu is highly dependent on protein imports from third countries and the need for measures to ensure a greater degree of autonomy in this respect. unblocking the process of authorising the cultivation of genetically modified soybeans in european countries would be a response to this problem and also an important source of revenue for european agriculture, which has been severely affected by the financial crisis. in the context of the new legislative framework proposed by the european commission regarding the right of member states to prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory, in application of the principle of subsidiarity, european states could decide individually whether or not they want to cultivate this product.
rapporteur. − madam president, firstly let me wish all women a happy anniversary on this important date, 8 march, the day which marks the 100th anniversary of international women’s day, 100 years of struggle for women’s rights. i would like to thank all my colleagues, the shadow rapporteurs and the members of the secretariat for their contributions to this report. my report deals with an issue which is both general and eminently concrete in terms of its consequences: female poverty. 85 million europeans live below the poverty line and 17% of all women in the eu are classed as living in poverty. these are the facts. the economic, financial and social crisis affects all of us, but it particularly harms women in the labour market and in their personal lives, since they are more likely to be in insecure jobs, more likely to be made redundant and less likely to have social security. this is how things stand at present. what can we do? women are expecting us to provide concrete proposals, concrete measures. it is 8 march, and i shall try to summarise my report in eight points. first and foremost, we call on the member states to take into account the gender dimension in their plans for recovery from the recession by promoting and boosting the employment of women, and adopting specific measures as well as adjusting budgets to ensure equality of access to public sector expenditure, with a view to both enhancing productive capacity and meeting women’s social and environmental needs. second, we call on the commission and the member states to take the appropriate measures to eliminate gender inequalities in employment as part of europe 2020. i strongly encourage establishing as an objective the reduction of the gender pay gap by 1% each year, in order to achieve the target of 10% reduction by 2020. i stress also the need for positive action to increase women’s representation in political, economic and corporate decision-making bodies. the third issue is related to reconciliation between private and professional life. i call on the council and the member states to renew and fulfil their commitments related to the barcelona targets for the provision of accessible, affordable and high-quality childcare, and to develop new targets for the care of dependent persons. fourth, we call on the commission and member states to frame health policies which aim to combat and prevent practices that harm women’s health and cause social exclusion and poverty. fifth, we call on the member states to adopt the necessary measures in order to offer better opportunities for women in education while fighting stereotypes and eliminating traditional role models in school curricula. our sixth point is that there is a direct link between families’ social circumstances and children’s growth. therefore we call on the commission and the council to develop and implement a strategy to halve child poverty by 2012. seventh, we should not ignore violence against women. it has an increasing impact on the risk of marginalisation, poverty and social exclusion. i call on the commission to establish a european year for combating violence against women. eighth, let us underline the importance of the structural funds, and in particular the european social fund, as key tools to assist member states to combat poverty and social exclusion. i think that we can do it. we have the power. we have the strength and the intelligence to tackle this important issue at european level and in all member states.
rapporteur. − madam president, i would like to thank commissioners reding and andor for their strong commitments on these important issues. i would also like to thank all my colleagues for their strong messages on this important debate today. first of all, i would like to say that gender equality is not only a matter of social justice, it is also a matter for progress and we need to build together a fair society for all of us. next, i would like to say that i strongly support quotas. yes, we need women in top positions, but let us not forget poverty. we have to tackle and we have to prevent and reduce poverty and we need concrete measures. preventing and reducing poverty is an important component of social solidarity and i strongly believe in women’s solidarity. we need support for all citizens; we need support from the whole society and i would like to thank the ngos, the social partners and all women and men in society who are fighting year by year, day by day, to achieve gender equality. we have to make this gender equality become a reality. we can accelerate on the track today; together let us make things happen. and once again i wish all women happy days.
in writing. on this international women's day, i support the principles set out in the report on 'equality between women and men in 2010'. however, i believe that in the coming period we must move from sound principles to concrete measures to reduce the current gender inequalities. i come from a country, romania, which in 2010 was in the middle of the global gender gap index, more precisely 64th in terms of discrimination between women and men. women in romania are generally more educated than men, and the share of women in the total higher education graduates has been steadily increasing. it has reached 60% of graduates are women and only 40% are men. however, women's income continues to be lower than that of men. from the increased risk of poverty to the blocking of access to key positions, the gender risks affecting women's chances in the labour market are still extremely strong. in the hope that the labour market will treat women more fairly, i want us to be part of that change, and this report is an important step.
in writing. i would like to acknowledge the many issues raised by this report, which has made it possible for us, irrespective of the committee in which we work, to find a number of correlations that need to be made in order to ensure a greater contribution to the achievement of the eu 2020 objectives. as you have noted, action is required at national and european level to promote entrepreneurship among women by creating training and vocational and legal counselling structures, and by facilitating access to public and private funding. i particularly appreciate the need to develop entrepreneurship at local and regional level as the main source of job creation and economic development. the potential of women in business development is under-utilized and i therefore believe that both the european social fund and the european regional development fund should support actions to develop female entrepreneurship. of course, there may be cultural, material or economic differences that prevent this, but these are the aspects that we must take into account and create the necessary framework to overcome them.
in writing. − the products available on the internal market have been constantly evolving and multiplying over the last 10 years, around the time the general product safety directive was issued, which regulates the general requirements for products so that they do not endanger anyone. the proposal to revise this directive is therefore more than appropriate. at the moment we have a directive which only partially overlaps the new legislative framework adopted in mid-2008. by aligning regulations we would be more likely to achieve the objective of a coherent internal market for both harmonised and non-harmonised products, and to ensure comprehensive protection of consumer interests. at the same time, these regulations must be fully transparent, so that they are accessible to producers. it is therefore important to ensure that the two overlapping levels of divergent market surveillance rules applying to harmonised goods depending on whether they are consumer products or not are eliminated. market surveillance is closely linked to product safety as it is an essential element in ensuring that products comply with the requirements laid down in the relevant community harmonisation legislation and that they are not dangerous.
in writing. − i welcome this initiative which aims to ensure better vigilance and full transparency on the evaluation of medicines recommended in health emergencies and improved vaccination and communication strategies to prevent and contain pandemics. i believe that the european union should devote more resources to research and development on preventive public health measures, to increased investment in better evaluation and anticipation of the impact of an influenza virus, both between pandemics and at the beginning of a pandemic, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that there is a need for better coordination at european level in the response to epidemiological risks. the h1n1 case demonstrated poor risk management globally, mainly due to an inadequate correlation between alert levels and actual dangers, leading, among other things, to a large waste of funds. in this context, i believe that the european union needs to implement an independent system for the assessment of pandemic risks and also better coordination in managing these risks. in this context, the european centre for disease prevention and control should be equipped with the necessary capacities to play a more active role in this area.
in writing. − given the severity of the h1n1 influenza and the importance of the health of our citizens, i consider this report to be of particular importance, as it also underlines the proper management of these situations. the moderate severity of this disease, confirmed as early as 2009 by the world health organisation, and the different approach of the member states, which has caused very high costs, the sale of vaccines produced under emergency conditions and the revision of the definition of a pandemic, taking into account not only the criterion of geographical spread but also its severity, indicate that a different approach is absolutely necessary. the european union needs more cooperation, transparency and independence in dealing with these situations.
in writing. − the report considers that better cooperation is needed in response to pandemics and calls for a review of the prevention plans established in the eu and its member states (mss). it also calls for reinforced cooperation between mss and coordination of mss with the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc). it also urges the who to revise the definition of a pandemic, based on its geographical spread and severity. the ecdc is invited to apply its competences as an independent agency to assess and communicate the severity of infection risks within the eu, making recommendations on best practices in areas such as crisis management techniques, vaccination and communication strategies. moreover, the report calls for an assessment of the influenza vaccination strategies recommended in the eu and applied in mss, covering the efficacy of the vaccines, their risk-benefit balance and the different target groups recommended, with regard to a safe and effective use and mss’ reports on relevant information to the commission (i.e. the number of doses of vaccines purchased and actually used, the number of h1n1 infections and people that died due to the infection, etc.). the eu needs to improve cooperation, independence and transparency in the management of future pandemic crises.
in writing. - the adoption of this report by the plenary shows a path the european union seems to want to take. although the idea of introducing a financial transaction tax, even if the g20 leaders do not agree on such a contribution to be set at global level, seems to be in support of citizens, i cannot help but note that this could lead to adverse effects in the medium and long term. these effects consist in the fact that such a tax, imposed only on capital established in the eu, will certainly cause that capital to migrate to developed or emerging countries outside the eu. or it will, at least initially, have this charge passed on, in the form of costs, to the consumer of the credit or other financial services. whatever the case, the perverse effect is that the eu will move closer to the dangerous situation where it will lose its competitiveness to other countries such as the usa, japan or the bric countries, which will slow down economic growth and create problems for the real economy, which is dependent on cheap financing.
in writing. − in recent years, the global economic and financial crisis has exposed major weaknesses in the regulatory and supervisory framework of the global financial system. financial transactions are characterised by a substantial increase in volume and a marked discrepancy between the volume of financial transactions and the needs of the real economy. short-term investments, which are predominant, have led to volatility and excessive risk-taking. short-term speculative transactions were at the heart of that crisis and underlined the clear link between inefficient financial regulation and supervision and the sustainability of public finances. i voted in favour of this report because the problems caused by this market behaviour have had a major impact on public finances and on european citizens and beyond. the report proposes the creation of instruments to reduce speculation, ensure a fair burden-sharing between the main financial players and create additional new resources to respond to major challenges. tax evasion and fraud are currently estimated in the eu member states at around eur 250 billion per year. the novelty is the financial transaction tax, which would translate into revenues of around €200 billion a year for the eu and discourage speculative transactions.
in writing. − the crisis has severely affected the healthcare sector in several eu member states in terms of both supply and demand. on the supply side, the economic and financial crisis has led to a decline in the level of funding for public health and health services and, in the long term, to budget cuts and lower tax revenues, while the demand for health services and in the long term has increased due to a combination of factors contributing to the deterioration of the health of the general population. several member states have included in their recovery packages measures to mitigate the effects of the economic crisis on the health services sector, investing in health infrastructure, optimising the funds allocated to the health services sector and restructuring and reorganising the health services system. however, there are wide differences in the measures taken to combat inequalities across member states. access is a key aspect of all public services. the collection and exchange of evidence on effective strategies, policies and measures will help to build support at the level of the administration and the different sectors.
in writing. − differences in life expectancy within the eu vary from one country to another, ranging from 14.2 years for men to 8.3 years for women (in romania, 11.86 for men and 7.38 for women). even at the domestic level, groups with different educational or social backgrounds have different views of health. a rise in unemployment and austerity measures could exacerbate existing health inequalities in the eu. we voted this resolution to call for improved disease monitoring and prevention measures, as well as a focus on vulnerable groups.
in writing. − i support the vital role of the agricultural sector in employment and the maintenance of the european agri-food model, which is a strategic component of the european economy. given that the european union is the world's largest importer of agricultural goods, the production methods for exports to the union from third countries should offer european consumers the same guarantees in terms of health, food safety, sustainable development and minimum social standards as those imposed on european producers. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that agricultural and food policies must serve fundamental objectives such as food security and safety.
in writing. − in the context of the future eu common agricultural policy, we need to consider the balance between domestic production and imports. our efforts will have to be directed towards a better match between market liberalisation and the protection of the domestic economic sector. ensuring food security at member state level is achieved by maintaining a stable agricultural sector, without being jeopardised by foreign trade policy, against the background of increased market volatility. small farmers make a significant contribution to the food security of the regions in which they operate. i think it is necessary that trade agreements on the import of agricultural products with third countries be achieved by compensating farmers for any losses. i also support a more targeted agricultural policy to ensure that eu agricultural products have access to third country markets. the promotion of products with the eu regional label is intended to make them known externally and would, by implication, stimulate their consumption. according to recent studies, the global population is growing at a rate far faster than the world's grain production. there are many eu regions that have the capacity to exploit the potential of cereal production more effectively and can make an effective contribution to reducing these differences.

in writing. − the common agricultural policy (cap) is a symbol of european integration, representing one of the most developed forms of the eu's supranational decision-making process. internal eu pressures towards market orientation of the cap and a greater focus on other european policies are equally reflected in the eu's external trade policy, with a view to ensuring the opening of the agricultural market in exchange for improved access for european services and industrial products to third country markets, and maintaining the european agricultural model and a fair competitive environment for european producers on the world market. the multifunctional role of the european agricultural sector can serve as a catalyst for new paradigms: food security, safety and quality at a reasonable price for european citizens. globally, demand for food is increasing, driven by rising production costs, increased volatility in agricultural markets, decreasing land and water cover, and reduced energy inputs. a strong common agricultural policy is fundamental to the maintenance, environmental sustainability and economic development of rural areas in the eu in the face of the threat of land abandonment and rural depopulation.

in writing. − i voted for the report on eu agriculture and international trade because it is necessary to ensure coherence between eu policies in the fields of agriculture, trade and development. eu agriculture plays a vital role in employment and maintaining the vitality of rural areas, and the european agri-food model is a strategic component of the european economy. globally, demand for food has increased due to the effects of climate change, rising production costs, reduced agricultural land and reduced drinking water resources. i stress the importance of trade in agricultural products for economic development and poverty eradication and call for eu support measures for the countries most affected by the food crisis. the eu's share of world agricultural exports is declining. in this context, i consider the eu-mercosur association agreement to be a very important agreement and therefore the european parliament should be closely involved in all negotiations. we demand that agricultural imports into the eu offer european consumers the same guarantees in terms of consumer protection, quality of animal life, environmental protection and minimum social standards as those offered by european production methods.
in writing. − imports of protein crops represent the equivalent of 20 million hectares cultivated outside europe, i.e. more than 10% of the eu's arable land, and these crops are not subject to the same health and environmental requirements as european ones. the import gaps represent an additional financial burden for the livestock and feed sectors, endangering the economic viability of domestic meat production. rebalancing the supply and consumption of cereals, protein crops and oilseeds in the european union would have major economic benefits for farmers and the food and feed industry, as well as improving the variety of healthy and high-quality food for consumers. in addition, in the context of climate change, protein crops can contribute to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions by absorbing and storing nitrogen in the soil and therefore have the effect of reducing the use of synthetic nitrogen fertilisers. these crops also contribute to reducing soil acidification, improving soil structure, reducing the use of herbicides and increasing biodiversity favourable to pollination. i voted in favour of this report because i support improving the balance between the production of plant and animal proteins and also the use of indigenous protein crops.
in writing. − over the last decade, plant protein production has declined in the eu - protein crops now account for only 3% of the eu's arable land and provide only 30% of the protein used in animal feed. i support the rapporteur's view that this must be changed, as this will benefit human health, the environment and biodiversity. the european commission should report on the possibilities and options for increasing domestic production of proteaginous substances in the eu through new policy instruments. the establishment of a mechanism to monitor the origin of protein crops imported into the eu is also useful.

on behalf of the epp group. today we are discussing a european roma strategy, an important step towards integrating the largest minority in the union. the european union must face up to the reality of the roma problem, a problem caused by the economic situation of the roma in general, but above all by aspects of their own tradition: nomadism and low levels of education and, consequently, lack of vocational qualifications. education means the opportunity to have a qualification, a profession, a job, the absolutely necessary step towards the social integration of roma. the responsibility for integration is not entirely with the authorities. the roma community must understand that they must make the necessary effort, they must really want to integrate into society, regardless of their country of origin or residence. the strategy should include as priority areas the increase of civic education, the adaptation of the cultural and traditional aspects of the roma population to contemporary civilization and the promotion of vocational qualification and retraining. i believe that these areas, along with education, should be fundamental objectives. the home member states must contribute the most to integration, but the european approach also has a very important role to play. the future strategy developed by the commission should propose framework programmes adapted to the nomadic nature of part of the roma community, to be developed and implemented in a similar way in all member states.
on behalf of the alde group. – madam president, we have finally come to the moment when we will have to vote on this report. in my view, this is not necessarily a moment of celebration: i prefer to see it as a moment when we have to be wise and to look at what we have achieved so far and what we want to achieve in the future. however, because i am aware of the huge amount of work that has been put into this report, please allow me to congratulate and thank not only the rapporteur and the other members involved, but also the staff of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs and our policy advisers. when we first began discussing this issue we were all hoping that the union was actually moving towards an eu strategy on roma inclusion. instead we will have a framework, and then the member states will decide whether or not to draw up their own strategies. i am afraid, given past experience – and please allow me to be pessimistic here – that this may be a process that is very much money driven, funding driven. in my view, people in the developed countries ‘discovered’ the roma not necessarily because they recognised the bad conditions in which roma were living in their countries of origin, but because they were bothered by the presence of roma in the streets and on the margins of cities. this is about more than funding. it is very much about the basic human rights of this population group. the commissioner spoke of work in progress. i hope that we shall see not only work but also some real progress.
i appreciate the excellent work done by my colleague járóka in producing this report and i congratulate her sincerely. i would like to point out, however, that the failure of roma integration policies to date has not been due to a lack of strategies, plans on paper or funds. real integration can only be achieved through the involvement of roma communities, roma, that is, people who, together with local authorities, have the capacity and, above all, the desire to implement the programmes. who knows the deep issues of this community better than the community itself? also, the local government, the one that handles their day-to-day affairs. the implementation of the future strategy must be based on structured dialogue and collaboration between roma communities, local authorities and the non-governmental environment. the roma must move from being spectators to being actors involved in the implementation of the measures that are intended for them. it's time to move from talk to action.
i join those who appreciate the efforts and work of those who have drawn up the report we are debating today, but at the same time we must be realistic, realize how many documents we have on the situation of the roma, which are not always reflected in the concrete results on the ground. formally, none of the member states has any legislative or policy obstacles that are discriminatory, implicit or explicit, towards roma. however, forms of discrimination exist and have been referred to here, if we refer to the values declared and assumed by the european union. there are, we must also recognize, cultural differences which sometimes seem irreconcilable, and i believe that, beyond any other policy aimed at social integration, the most powerful instrument for improving the situation of this community is education. at the same time, we must take into account the peculiarities of this ethnic group, which are often at the root of their problems. romania, for example, has implemented affirmative action mechanisms, including the reservation of special places in high schools and colleges, but, discouragingly, many such places, funded with public money, have remained unoccupied. the measures proposed in the report are important and necessary and i hope that they will be put into practice by all the governments of the member states. at the same time, the roma community needs to take responsibility for changing their situation for the better.
the problem of the social and economic exclusion of roma has been a matter of debate in europe since the accession of the central and eastern european states. but that doesn't mean that the phenomenon wasn't well known before. i myself live in a member state, romania, where the otherwise diverse roma community has lived for decades alongside romanians and hungarians. although the relationship has never been without friction, tensions have increased in the two decades since the fall of communism. in the former socialist countries, the roma suffered the most from the transition to a market economy, as the activities that sustained these communities disappeared or were reduced. the responsibility is shared, we are all responsible, but the roma communities are responsible for their fate, and so is europe, which has not yet taken note of the problem. the most important message of the járóka lívia report is that the prohibition of discrimination, the total elimination of discrimination, is far from solving, i repeat, this european problem.
the socioeconomic integration of the roma population is a challenge in most eu countries. we're talking about a diverse population, significant in number, but one that needs to be treated as a whole. the fate of this community has often been the subject of election campaigns. to truly contribute to the well-being of roma citizens, the proper use and interaction of structural funds resources is a priority. building new homes and renovating existing ones, improving access to utilities, but also to education, health care and jobs, are viable solutions to achieve our goal. at the same time, we must take advantage of the peculiarities of this population, the customs, culture and traditional crafts of the roma. by designating a european year of roma integration, we will help to familiarise people with the problems of this community. table and performance sports are also a sure way of integrating the roma population.
madam president, with about 1.5 million members of this minority, romania is home to the largest roma community in europe. the social integration of roma lags behind, being considered utopian by many, both in the administration and in the community. actually the romanian government deals fully with the integration of this minority, therefore we need a european strategy to frame the national efforts aimed at providing socio-economic inclusion for the roma, education, training opportunities and job assistance, especially for women. it is crucial to support efforts to help equip them for continued employment in order to avoid social exclusion and poverty. i strongly support the idea that the commission should present annually a follow-up of eu strategy on roma inclusion. i would like to congratulate mrs járóka and also mrs kinga göncz, and i welcome the commitment of the council and the commission.
the fact that we are talking today about the development of a european strategy for roma citizens is finally a recognition that this issue is a matter of european competence and not just national. for a better implementation of this, i support the idea of setting up a european agency for the roma. we will thus be able to put an end to discrimination on the basis of ethnicity, with all the consequences that follow from this. if there is to be a system for monitoring the implementation of the strategy, it must be applied to all member states and not just to countries with a large number of this population. there is a risk that eu funds managed by ngos will not lead to concrete results. public authorities should act as beneficiary organisations of projects. i also support the idea in the report to create a european crisis map, containing the eu's micro-regions most affected by poverty, social exclusion and discrimination.

madam president, first of all i would like to congratulate mr lange on the completion of this important report. it is very important during these times of economic austerity that the european institutions are pushing for a strong cohesive industrial policy to maintain jobs in europe and to encourage renewed competitiveness. vice-president tajani has stated that industry is at the heart of europe and is indispensable for finding solutions to the challenges of our society today and in the future. the s&d group position is that industry plays a key role for jobs in europe. this is why we must enhance efforts to maintain a strong industrial base in europe. i am specifically concerned about developing the necessary infrastructure where it does not exist. finally, i am glad to see that the final report strongly advocates the significance of raw materials in the industrial sector of the future.
the union's industrial policy must create the appropriate framework to increase the contribution of the industrial sector to the union's gdp, improve the competitiveness of the european union and create jobs throughout its territory. the industrial strategy must identify the strategic areas in which to invest, as well as the sources of the raw materials needed. i ask the commission and the member states to support these priorities through the future financial perspective, the annual budgets and the community's sectoral policies. energy consumption is an indicator of industrial production. we need an eco-efficient industrial policy that ensures both the production capacity of the eu in a sustainable way and the reduction of the union's energy dependence. the competitiveness of the union depends to a large extent on the capacity to innovate, on research and development and on the link between innovation and the production process. increasing public funding for r & d is needed to mobilise private investment, and simplifying procedures and reducing red tape is a key condition for increased industry involvement.
rare earth elements are essential for the production of watches, mobile phones, for the manufacture of high-performance permanent magnets, in wind turbines or electric vehicles, catalytic converters for automobiles, printed circuit boards, optical fibers. they are therefore also essential for new clean energy sources. although traded on a global scale, the market for certain raw materials and rare earth elements is not very transparent and the volumes traded are small. the union is almost entirely dependent on imports of rare earth elements, 97% of the world production of which is concentrated in china. demand for raw materials will be driven by the growth of emerging economies and the rapid diffusion of new technologies. mining, refining and recycling of rare earth elements have serious environmental consequences if not managed properly. the union should focus its efforts on making the use and recycling of rare earth elements more efficient and on research into the substitution of less critical raw materials for critical raw materials. we request, commissioner, that the list of raw materials be updated periodically.
it is already known that the world's hydrocarbon reserves are approaching exhaustion. this will be reflected in higher extraction costs, so huge prices. gas from alternative sources would play an important role in the european energy market. by using it, europe could diversify its energy sources, thus reducing its dependence on third countries. one alternative is to exploit europe's gas reserves in an unconventional way. in romania, three oil companies have already obtained a licence to do so. the great wealth of the black sea is gas hydrates, also known as "flammable ice". if exploited locally, this wealth will lessen the eu's dependence on russian pipelines. the biogas market is also one of the most developed in europe. in countries like romania there is potential for biogas production, but its exploitation still requires investment in technology.
on 4 february, the european council recommended that member states explore shale gas and oil shale resources in europe. however, the exploitation of unconventional gas sources poses significant environmental and social risks. no exploitation of shale gas shall take place without an impact study presenting the associated risks and the measures necessary to protect the resident population and owners, taking into account the environmental risks. commissioner, the european union's energy security policy is based on diversifying sources and supply routes. reducing dependence on russian gas can also be achieved by implementing projects such as nabucco, a key priority for the european union, alongside other smaller projects such as the trans adriatic pipeline, the turkey-greece-italy interconnection or the azerbaijan-georgia-romania interconnection, which highlight the particular importance of the black sea for the union's energy security.

mr president, the recent events of historical importance in our southern neighbourhood call for a resetting of our policies there, but we have to start with the lessons to be learnt. firstly, we must learn that relying on authoritarian leaders or imposing our model of life is wrong. we must leave those people to build their democracy in their way and under their conditions. secondly, we must understand that the national fragmentation of our aid-for-development policy that sometimes allows the promotion of national geopolitical agendas deprives us and the countries in the area of the benefits of security through development. thirdly, our lack of vision and political will in addressing the regional security challenges, mainly the israeli-palestinian issue, leads us towards ever worse crises. on libya, amongst other countries, we must remember that not all those fighting a dictator are democrats and change per se is not always for the better. we can therefore speak about dialogue, engagement, humanitarian assistance, but recognition might be too early, and recourse to military means should be ruled out or, at any rate, be subject to united nations approval and arab league cooperation. otherwise, we could be led into an adventure, the results of which may be difficult to cope with.
a few days ago, the gaddafi regime addressed a letter to the united nations security council expressing its surprise at the sanctions adopted on february 26, claiming that there was only a "moderate" remedy, gaddafi said, against "subversive acts". it's the clear sign of a dictator who knows he's lost the game and can no longer recognize the gravity of the acts he's committing. the brutality of the last three weeks in libya is thus minimized with incredible cynicism. on the other hand, it is clear that the reaction of the gaddafi regime shows that it is not indifferent to the sanctions adopted so far. so i think we need to have the toughest sanctions possible, under the un mandate, obviously, but i think we need to go beyond the no-fly zones, supporting those who have to defeat gaddafi, also being in solidarity with our southern states that will be receiving a wave of refugees; that's also clear.

in writing. − the 10-12 million roma should benefit from eu-wide minimum standards for access to jobs and education. the european parliament resolution seeking to influence the future roma inclusion strategy proposes better protection of fundamental rights as well as increased eu funding. romania understands best the difficulties and inertia of this minority. the union should be aware that resistance to change and social inclusion is very high in this ethnic group. gypsies have been victims of discrimination for centuries but at the same time of self-exclusion. this statement is very correct, but it must be understood that often the solutions we come up with are not adequate or are not understood by the roma. it is clear that the future eu strategy on the roma minority must focus on meeting and promoting the fundamental rights to work, housing, health and, in particular, education, even in the face of parental resistance. but no one should expect change to come quickly, and it may take several generations for this minority to adopt certain rules of social coexistence.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that a european-wide strategy for the integration of the roma minority is positive and welcome. this community needs special attention at european level, given the persistent problems of social and economic integration and the particular mobility of its members. however, i believe that the most important effort is yet to be made. strategies and action plans for roma integration have existed and exist at all levels, but what is missing is their proper implementation. to be successful, this new strategy must be implemented in the most appropriate way. in this regard, i believe that a structured dialogue between roma communities, the non-governmental environment and local authorities must be the basis for the implementation of the future strategy.
in writing. − the european approach to the roma problem has been and remains a deficient one. the report by lívia járóka in the libe committee, with the contributions of the other associated committees, should be a new impetus towards a real strategy for roma integration, a strategy that we expect from the commission next month. i believe that we are all keen to bring about real change for the roma community, to give them all the necessary conditions for social inclusion. that is why we need to focus on the political and financial instruments at our disposal and act directly in key areas such as education and health. collaboration at all levels, from the european to the local, is also fundamental, because without concerted action, all resources are lost. roma involvement in policy-making is a necessity and therefore solutions must be found to bring those who link the decision-making and implementation levels closer together. finally, we must recognise the importance of the message we are sending with this report, but we must not forget that the messages have been many and that the time has come for concrete action.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i appreciate that it is extremely attentive to the complexity of the roma community in the eu and i dare say that when we have solved most of these problems, it means that most of the problems we are facing now as a european society will have been solved. i would just like to refer to how the use of the structural funds could support the priorities of the eu roma inclusion strategy. i think that a substantial allocation is needed for the economic and social development of these communities. if interventions are not supported financially or over a relevant period of time to produce the expected impact, the effects will not be what we expect today. it takes prioritization, smart spending and political commitment. otherwise, financial resources will be wasted. following this report, i look forward to the next steps the commission will take and hope that this strategy will bring the added value needed to deliver on the european approach to roma inclusion.
in writing. − a european strategy on roma is undoubtedly essential, as they are a european minority and are characterised by a high degree of cross-border mobility, given their way of life. i voted in favour of the resolution, mainly because it underlines the role that quality education and training plays as a factor influencing people's personal and professional lives and that education is therefore the surest way to ensure the integration of roma into society.
in writing. − we know that 10-12 million european roma continue to suffer serious systematic discrimination in education (where they are victims particularly of segregation), housing (particularly with forced evictions and sub-standard living conditions, often in ghettos), employment (their particularly low employment rate) and equal access to healthcare systems and other public services, as well as an astoundingly low level of political participation. the eu strategy on roma inclusion should embrace measures to ensure the monitoring of the situation of the roma in relation to the respect and promotion of their fundamental social rights, equality, non-discrimination and free movement in the eu, and also to provide education, training opportunities and job assistance for adults, which are crucial in order to support the recruitment and continued employment of the roma with the aim of avoiding the perpetuation of social exclusion. the commission and member states should address the particular needs of roma women by applying a gender perspective in all policies for roma inclusion and providing protection for especially vulnerable subgroups. therefore, i ask the commission to present annually to the european parliament a follow up of the eu strategy on roma inclusion in order to monitor the progress made at national level.
in writing. − the global economic crisis has affected european industry, making it even more difficult to adapt to the challenges of the shift to a knowledge-based and profitable industry, which is having a severe impact on industrial development and the labour market. to meet these challenges, i believe that an industrial policy approach is needed that combines competitiveness, sustainability and decent work and can lead to economic and employment boost, reduction of environmental degradation and improvement of the quality of life in the european union. this report supports industrial progress through smart and forward-looking regulation and market stimulation, based on coherent insights into market developments and supporting global trends towards green, sustainable and innovative forms of production, distribution and consumption. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the success of the industrial policy of the european union depends on its being firmly anchored in a new architecture of the financial sector, which promotes investment and prevents speculation, and in a macroeconomic policy in which the fiscal, economic and budgetary policy of the union is geared towards sustainable growth and job creation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it represents the way forward for a robust, cohesive and employment-based industrial policy for the european workforce. r&d is a key driver for innovation and trade and will remain one of the cornerstones for industrial policy in the eu. i believe that industry plays a key role in keeping jobs in europe and this is why we must enhance efforts to maintain a strong industrial base, become the most competitive economy in the world and ensure close-knit networks between companies in different member states in order to achieve shared industrial priorities. some of my amendments included in the report concern shortening the time to market for new products, ensuring that european manufacturing strengthens the foundations of the european economy and simplification of funding programmes for industry.
in writing. − the recent economic crisis has confirmed that smes remain the engine of economic and social development, with a key role in promoting economic competitiveness and job creation. i welcome this report and believe that the eu's instruments supporting competitiveness need to be reviewed and strengthened, with a view to streamlining administrative procedures and facilitating access to finance for smes. it is also imperative to introduce innovative incentive mechanisms based on the achievement of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth objectives and to promote closer cooperation with financial institutions. an important form of innovation funding for smes through the european investment bank is the risk-sharing financing mechanism. but for it to succeed, the european commission needs to make much more resources available, including through the erdf innovation funds, to promote private direct investment and innovative financing mechanisms in favour of high-risk innovative projects and projects involving smes.
in writing. − eu industry is responsible for about 1/3 of the eu's gross value added, almost 3/4 of european exports are industrial goods, and 1/3 of employment, providing the livelihoods of some 57 million citizens (plus its multiplier effect, whereby each industrial job creates about two jobs in related services). there are 15 key elements: building an innovation chain, using resources more efficiently, clear targets for sustainable products, public procurement, improving clean energy production, a raw materials strategy, reorganising trade for fair coexistence and sustainable production, shaping a binding sectoral industrial policy, involving smes, regional areas of action, ensuring anticipation of industrial transformation, restructuring, upskilling, worker participation in decision-making, long-term policies. the eu's industrial policy must be geared both to a sustainable, environmentally efficient and globally competitive renewal of the industrial base and to a sustainable transition from a predominantly manufacturing-based industry to a knowledge-based industry, clearly committed to investing in the eu and to strategic partnerships between firms in the union.
