in writing. the situation in the middle east and the mediterranean is at a particularly sensitive moment, as the high representative also mentioned in his speech. i think this is a good opportunity for the eu to focus on the peace process in the region. israel is one of the union's most important trading partners, while thanks to university international exchange programmes, students from all over europe have access to study centres in israel. i also remind you that the middle east is where the challenges of the future are already taking concrete form. one example is drinking water management. the arab revolutions have created an atmosphere of instability in the mediterranean region, and israel is particularly affected. recently, due to such security risks, a border crossing point was closed, with kerem shalom remaining the only fully secure commercial crossing. here the israeli authorities concentrate their efforts to ensure the normal flow of civil and commercial traffic. in this context, i believe that the swift resumption of negotiations to reach a peaceful solution is vital. and the eu's involvement in this process can provide the necessary support for the smooth running of the dialogue.
as regards the alignment of unit costs with labour and productivity levels, i believe that we should focus on framework conditions and less on indicators. it's not clear that we can achieve this alignment. productivity depends, first of all, on factors like the accumulated capital stock which is extremely different. the categorical difference between romania and germany is noticeable. this is due to the different quality of economic policies over time, and such gaps cannot be recovered overnight. my country has made efforts towards pension and welfare reform. i would therefore like to suggest that such provisions be included in the competitiveness pact. i support the need to correlate retirement age with demographic trends. the impact of a coherent and realistic pension policy on public finances must be taken into account.
i understand very well the principle of subsidiarity, but i think pensions have moved beyond the national sphere and are now the subject of a european debate. we are talking about unsustainable pension systems as a result of common challenges such as the financial crisis, the ageing population and the declining birth rate. the principle of solidarity between generations is at risk of becoming obsolete, as citizens are encouraged to contribute to private pensions. what, though, about those who no longer have enough time to contribute to such pensions? in addition, european citizens are dependent on public pensions. in romania the gross minimum wage per economy is about 160 euros. that's why investing in private pensions or saving, in my view, are utopias. i believe that the european commission needs to be more involved in proposing a minimum level for both wages and pensions at european level, and a first step in this direction could be a comparative analysis of pension systems.
in writing. according to eurostat, in january 2011, the minimum monthly income varies between eur 123 in bulgaria, eur 157 in romania and eur 1758 in luxembourg. in 20 of the 27 member states, the minimum income is set by law or by a national cross-sectoral agreement. in 11 member states the minimum income is between 100 and 400 eur/month, in 5 member states between 550 and 950 eur/month and in 6 member states it exceeds 1100 eur/month. the development and strengthening of the internal market ensures that businesses have access to the more than 500 million european consumers. however, the persisting gap between minimum income levels in the member states is a barrier to both the accessibility of european companies to european consumers and their access to quality products and services. i consider social dialogue to be particularly important for ensuring social equity and a decent living for all european citizens. we call on the commission and the member states to guarantee equal pay for equal work in the internal labour market, to remove barriers to the free movement of workers and to examine the possibility of ensuring a minimum wage, agreed by law or through collective bargaining, which guarantees european citizens a decent living.
after the ecological disaster in hungary last october, i raised the issue of disaster prevention in the extractive industry with the european commission on several occasions. in mining, the impact of accidents can often be transboundary. the european union is even more obliged to ensure that all possible measures are taken to reduce the risk of accidents and to improve the speed and efficiency of responses should they nevertheless occur. in response to my questions, i received confirmation from the commission that the waste dumped into the environment, including the danube, in the case of the accident in hungary, was in fact toxic, although this fact had initially been denied by the authorities. it's a clear example of regulations not being applied, and this situation needs to change as quickly as possible. the european commission has a duty to act urgently following the resolution adopted by parliament last year calling for a ban on the use of cyanide-based technologies in mining, as they pose huge cross-border threats to ecosystems.
the report on a community approach to the prevention of natural and man-made disasters, adopted in september 2010, contains several important references directly concerning agriculture. in particular, the report refers to the fact that agricultural production is vulnerable to climatic phenomena such as drought, frost, hail, forest fires, floods, landslides and others. the report also contains a number of important suggestions for mitigating the consequences of these problems; the author has already mentioned the idea of insurance for agriculture. i would like to draw attention to the importance of effectively managing these challenges, especially in the context of a future common agricultural policy which proposes agriculture as both a food and a significant environmental protection role.
one of the biggest challenges facing the european union today is the increase in the intensity and consequences of natural disasters. according to statistics, in the last 20 years, 953 disasters in europe have caused almost 90 000 deaths and economic losses of 269 billion dollars. to counteract the effects of these phenomena, a risk map and a coherent environmental management plan are needed. the preservation and expansion of forest areas and urban green spaces must be a priority for all of us. it is essential to give due weight to information and education of the population in order to prevent the effects of disasters. the international day for disaster risk reduction is a good example of this. i also think that all the instruments should be made more efficient... author. - the volcanic eruption last april led to the closure of many sectors of european airspace. the ensuing crisis affected over 10 million passengers and had severe economic repercussions; due to the lack of coordination between institutions, the lack of specifications and flexibility, and the under-utilisation of technical resources, the solution of the volcanic ash crisis was left undesirable. i said then and i still say that it is extremely important to take the necessary measures to ensure that a new volcanic eruption does not have the same repercussions. the responsibility for the safety of a flight, including the avoidance of a gray area, shall be the responsibility of the operator and the crew. operators need to be provided with accurate data to enable them to apply optimal solutions. pilots shall be prepared to handle extraordinary flight conditions and have the experience to assess risk and make decisions related to flight re-routing. for this process to work as well as possible, several elements are needed: improved surveillance and forecasting, more investment in ground and airborne equipment. the technical structure must be able to provide accurate real-time data and stable forecasts, and current technology can ensure this. the use of more centres to collect and transmit this information will improve risk assessment and appropriate flight planning. in order to provide operators with this information for decision-making, the role of the institutions involved in crisis management needs to be clarified. the regulatory body should be responsible for oversight, the ash advisory centres are responsible for notifying air navigation service providers of eruptions and high risk areas. service providers must inform aircraft crews of areas at high risk of ash contamination. the parties involved shall be prepared for effective crisis management through simulation exercises. i consider it absolutely necessary that easa develop the necessary specifications clarifying the responsibilities and control at operational level. the achievement of the single european sky and the implementation of sesar would greatly facilitate decision-making and considerably reduce the impact in crisis situations. i think these are the key points that need to be addressed to ensure that we are prepared to manage this kind of situation successfully in the future.
the icelandic volcanic eruption, as well as the massive snowfall last year, have seriously disrupted european air traffic, with significant economic and social consequences. in order to avoid such situations in the future, i would like to ask the commission what are the main new regulations it is considering to strengthen the legislative framework on air passenger rights. in addition to the ash cloud centres of expertise in london and toulouse, which are part of the international system of nine such centres established by icao and the london centre for the issuance of ash cloud risk maps, there is a need to improve the european infrastructure also through a real-time ash cloud concentration measurement system. regulation 1070/2009 on improving the performance of the european aviation system requires member states to take the necessary measures to ensure the implementation of functional airspace blocks by 4 december 2012. i ask the commission whether the implementation of the single european sky will respect the established timetable. the european union also needs convenience and a system of booking and ticketing for european routes involving several modes of transport. the european union needs a high-speed rail system that links all the capitals and major european cities.

mr president, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur mr schwab and his team of rapporteurs for opinions and shadow rapporteurs for their very good work on this report. it took a long time to choose a line that would be balanced enough for both consumers and businesses. i welcome the overall compromise that has been agreed by all political groups and i believe that this is an important step forward for all consumers in the european union. there are significant improvements such as the provision of clear information requirements in contracts, and the harmonisation of the provisions on the right of withdrawal. of course it is a compromise, it is not perfect. an example is article 22a which obliges the trader to deliver in other member states. there are products and services which due to their nature should not be covered here, namely perishable goods. problems might also arise with digital products. the initial intention of promoting cross-border business is very important and is very good, and i really hope that during the forthcoming negotiations with the council we will manage to make these adjustments to achieve an optimal result.
i believe that all consumers should have the right to receive information before entering into a contract. traders should inform consumers and obtain their consent, including to any condition whereby an amount is blocked on their credit or debit card. it is also important to protect consumers from abusive contractual clauses. unfortunately, many times, for banking, insurance, electronic communications, or tourism services, the contract terms are written on the back in very small letters, and often the customer signs the sign-up form or invoice without reading the contract terms on the back. even if they read all the terms of the contract and disagree with one of them, the customers have no bargaining power. in such a case, the first response the consumer receives is that there is a standard contract of the company and that it cannot be changed. national consumer protection authorities should check these standard contracts to protect consumers against unfair terms.
in line with the eu 2020 strategy, a high level of consumer protection guarantees high quality products but also guarantees consumer confidence, thus fostering the effectiveness of the internal markets. in view of consumer rights, the current minimum rules give all member states the freedom to adapt european-level rules to domestic principles, and i believe that this approach should be maintained. the european union can facilitate better harmonisation of the internal market with a higher level of consumer protection by raising the minimum level of harmonisation currently practised to the level of best practices existing at national level. i believe that the european system of non-compliance liability must be fair so that consumer protection and confidence in the markets are improved and the useful life of products is extended.

the reporter. − the treaty of lisbon, which entered into force on 1 december 2009, increases the number of situations in which parliament's consent is required for the conclusion of an international agreement. air transport agreements now fall into this category as they concern an area to which the ordinary legislative procedure applies. before this agreement, aviation was covered by bilateral agreements with 19 of the member states of the european union - so i am referring to the agreements between the european union and canada. many of these agreements contained numerous restrictions and did not provide full access to the respective markets. in november 2002, the court of justice of the european union declared certain provisions of the bilateral agreements in question to be incompatible with community law. the negotiating mandate sets out the objective of creating an open aviation space between the european union and canada. this would create a single air transport market between the european union and canada, in which investment could flow freely and in which european and canadian airlines could provide air services without any restrictions, including on the domestic markets of the two parties. the eu-canada air transport agreement was initialled on 30 november 2008, received support at the eu-canada summit on 6 may 2009 and was signed on 17-18 december 2009. what the agreement contains: the agreement includes a gradual phasing-out of traffic rights, investment opportunities and large-scale cooperation on a range of issues including safety, security, social issues, consumer interests, the environment, air traffic management, state aid and competition. all european union airlines will be able to operate direct flights to canada from anywhere in europe. the agreement removes all restrictions on routes, prices or the number of weekly flights between canada and the european union. air carriers are free to enter into commercial agreements, such as code-sharing agreements, which are important for airlines serving a large number of destinations, and to set their fares in accordance with competition law. the agreement contains provisions on the phased opening of the market. the first stage applies when the foreign capital of the airlines is limited to 25% and when the negotiations on the agreement have been concluded. the second stage shall commence as soon as canada has taken the necessary measures to allow european investors to hold up to 49% of the voting shares of canadian air carriers. the third stage starts as soon as both parties introduce the possibility for investors to set up and operate new airlines in the other party's market. the fourth and final stage provides full operating rights between, within and beyond both markets, including between points in the territory of the other party - i am referring to cabotage. i would like to say a few things about this report: although the agreement is more ambitious than the one with the usa in terms of market access, it is less explicit in terms of recognising the importance of the social dimension. it is important that the commission use the agreement and in particular the possibility to address the joint committee to promote compliance with relevant international legislation on social rights, in particular labour standards included in the core conventions of the international labour organisation. given the important role played by the joint committee, including on politically sensitive issues as well as on environmental and labour standards, it is important that the commission ensures that parliament is fully informed and consulted on the work of the committee and also on future treaty amendments.
i want to congratulate adriana ticău on the ambitious agreement with canada. the agreement is an important step in the process of opening up the market and will at the same time lead to the emergence of new air routes and the development of new opportunities for investors on both sides of the atlantic, both in terms of the development of new investments and the emergence of new services for european and canadian citizens. i welcome the decision to allow airlines to operate without restrictions anywhere in europe and anywhere in canada, which will benefit consumers, airlines and, in general, the economies of both sides. the implementation of this agreement will lead to more services operated by one airline and new possibilities for the transport of goods, but this must also lead to greater concern with respect to the impact on climate change. in addition, the agreement will make the european and canadian markets safer by strengthening cooperation on compliance with certification and inspection procedures to ensure the highest level of safety for persons and goods.
the reporter. − the eu-canada air transport agreement can be described as the most ambitious air transport agreement between the eu and a major global partner. it will significantly improve the links between the two parties' markets and between people, while creating new opportunities for the aviation sector through the progressive liberalisation of foreign capital rules. in particular, the agreement is more ambitious and more specific than the agreement between the european union and the united states of america on traffic, ownership and control rights, even after the provisional application of the amending protocol - the second stage. according to a study initiated by the commission, an open agreement with canada would generate half a million additional passengers in the first year and within a few years, 3.5 million new passengers are expected to take advantage of the opportunities offered by such an agreement. the agreement could generate consumer benefits of at least eur 72 million through lower tariffs and lead to the creation of new jobs. madam president, we welcome the ambitious nature of this agreement. it should serve as an objective and model for other ongoing negotiations. in conclusion, i recommend that parliament approve the air transport agreement between the european union and canada.
in writing. − russia is an important market for moldovan winemakers, but lately the russian market is no longer safe for the export of wine products. in search of an alternative to the russian market, the european commission has proposed to increase the duty-free quotas from 100 000 hectolitres (hl) to 150 000 hl this year, from 120 000 hl to 180 000 hl in 2012 and to 240 000 hl from 2013. i voted in favour of this change in trade relations with the republic of moldova, to increase the volume of duty-free wine imports. this amendment to regulation (ec) no 55/2008 may be a solution for wine producers in the republic of moldova, so that they benefit from a safer market, given that russia imposed an embargo on moldovan wines in 2006 and 2010, sending several winemakers into bankruptcy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the introduction of autonomous trade preferences for the republic of moldova, considering that it is a positive signal from the eu to this eastern partnership country, which recently stated that it hopes to be able to apply for eu membership in 2011. moldova has undertaken an ambitious set of political, economic and social reforms, the continuity of which should be encouraged. at the same time, the republic of moldova has been hit hard by the economic and financial crisis. in the last 4 years, 40% of its winegrowing enterprises have either ceased their activity or have gone into insolvency proceedings, and the companies still active in this key sector of its economy have accumulated losses. the increase of the duty-free tariff quota for wine and the extension of council regulation (ec) no 55/2008 until the end of 2015 would help this country, whose wine industry employs 300 000 people and whose agricultural sector accounts for 40% of its gross domestic product, without affecting the union economy. these measures would also leave sufficient time for the preparation of negotiations on the creation of a deep and comprehensive free trade area, a common objective of the eu and the republic of moldova.
in writing. − i will always declare that the republic of moldova has to be encouraged in its pro-european path. moldova is experiencing difficulties with its wine exports to some of its traditional markets, which threaten its economic recovery and the reform process that it is vigorously pursuing. the arguments given in vital moreira’s report are convincing, moldova needs council regulation (ec) no 55/2008 to be extended for a further three years, until 31 of december 2015. the request made by the republic of moldova in july 2010 is justified. moldova needs the european union to be a trustworthy partner. for these reasons, i endorse the report drafted by vital moreira on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament
in writing. - i welcome the vote in favour of this report. the republic of moldova needs the support of the european union at this time, when it is facing economic difficulties, as are most countries in the world, but also the difficulties inherent in a political transition. in view of the fact that moldova is facing a virtual boycott of the russian federation market for wine exports, the increase in the tariff quota exempted from customs duties for wine is a timely measure and, i hope, useful for the economy of this country.
in writing. − i decided to vote in favour of the report on generalised tariff preferences because it proposed both the immediate adaptation of the 'gsp' to the provisions of the lisbon treaty and a general revision of it in the future. this general review would aim at better involving beneficiary countries in their reform processes, providing technical assistance for the development of their institutional capacity and revising and harmonising the rules of origin.
in writing. − while far from perfect, the eu-us air transport agreement is a step forward, opening the way to future opportunities in terms of additional investment and market access, as well as enhanced safety and security measures. the air transport market is not fully open by both sides, as a result of the negotiated version of the agreement, but it has sufficient incentives to encourage reform. the us needs to change its domestic law to allow eu investors to become majority shareholders in us companies, generating reciprocal eu action. the eu-us joint committee has been given increased powers, which means it will be able to improve cooperation by promoting new initiatives. the new rules will reduce red tape, including through mutual recognition of regulatory decisions, and avoid unnecessary overlapping of resources. the recognition of the importance of the social dimension and the responsibility given to the joint committee to monitor the social effects of the agreement and to develop appropriate measures to address those effects as appropriate is an innovation introduced into the agreement in the second stage.
in writing. − the european union and canada have agreed to cooperate in the field of air transport with the aim of mitigating the impact of aviation on climate change. as regards passenger safety and security, the agreement envisages the mutual recognition of standards and the single security check. all european union airlines will be able to operate weekly flights between canada and the european union. this agreement will significantly improve the links between the two parties' markets and people, creating new opportunities for the aviation sector through the progressive liberalisation of foreign capital rules. i voted in favour of this report because it contains specific provisions on improving consumer interests.
in writing. − the european union and the gulf cooperation council have been negotiating a free trade agreement for almost twenty years. a strengthening of relations would be beneficial to both sides, especially as there are many possibilities for cooperation in the fields of education, scientific research, renewable energy. internally, the gcc countries have been undergoing a new process of political and social modernisation for several years, which should be supported and encouraged. i believe that we need a continuous dialogue between the european union and the gulf cooperation council to advance the promotion of human and minority rights and freedoms and the fight against all forms of discrimination, including discrimination on grounds of gender or religion. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − it is more important than ever for the european union to have a free trade agreement with the gulf countries. the negotiations for such an agreement have a negative record in terms of their duration and it is clear that in the 20 years since they began, the context has changed several times. the geopolitical climate in the gulf is different now, with global and regional implications. we are dealing with a process of liberalization and diversification of the economies of these countries. the gulf states are much more than just trading partners at this point, they are increasingly influential in the financial, diplomatic and other fields. and their influence will continue to grow. this brings a new perspective to the european union, which understands that cooperation between the two regions goes beyond the commercial framework. we have common interests in international security, the fight against terrorism, diplomatic mediation in the tense middle east, regional crisis management, intercultural dialogue and global economic governance. the eu has comparative advantages to be exploited with the new actors in the gulf region, provided there is political will at the highest level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of mrs francesca balzani's report because, in accordance with that document, i believe that the 2012 budget of the european union should be drawn up in order to pursue the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. despite the current economic and financial crisis, it is important now to lay the foundations for solid future economic growth through investment in education, research and development, innovation and smes. these areas are at the heart of the eu's progress and competitiveness and need to be developed in the context of job creation and territorial and social cohesion. i stress that we must not reduce funding in these areas and it is essential to ensure that the available resources are managed as efficiently as possible. i also believe that the synergy between national budgetary priorities and the eu budget is fundamental. on this occasion, i welcome the efforts of president herman van rompuy, in the context of the european semester, to strengthen the discipline of the eu member states by promoting clear, measurable and realistic targets for each country. parliament is the most democratic european institution and the one that directly represents the interests of the citizens of the union. i therefore say that parliament should be involved in a much more active way in the exercise of the european semester.
in writing. − i would like to stress the importance of this report because the 2012 eu budget will help to revitalise the european economy. at the same time, the eu budget for next year must be the main instrument in revitalising the european economy, with a strong focus on employment, governance and growth. i believe that the 2012 budget must contribute to the implementation of the five objectives of the eu 2020 strategy: employment, innovation, research and development, climate change and energy, education and social inclusion. the eu budget is an investment budget and 2012 is the sixth year in the current 'financial perspective' (2007-2013), with projects progressing at a normal pace, leading to higher payment amounts as work is carried out. in my view, the increase in the level of payments in 2012 is foreseeable.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because i believe that the european union needs uniform administrative procedures with regard to migrant workers from third countries. the adoption of this act will have significant benefits: it will reduce public sector spending, discourage illegal immigration and ensure fair rights for third country nationals wishing to work in the european union. economic immigration is a necessity and must be encouraged in a controlled manner, given the demographic and economic challenges the union will face. let's not forget that the progress of countries like the united states, canada and australia is due to immigrants. they are a very dynamic social category, bringing new enthusiasm and fresh perspectives to the adoptive societies, increasing their competitiveness. it is essential that we ensure that they can work legally and pursue their dreams without unnecessary bureaucratic obstacles. i would like to express my hope that in the very near future, the problem of access to the labour market throughout the european union will be solved once and for all, also for the citizens of the member states romania and bulgaria.
in writing. − the adoption of the directive on the establishment of a single procedure for obtaining a work permit in the eu territory for third-country nationals will significantly simplify the system now decided by each member state. two separate procedures imply a longer time for processing applications and a higher administrative cost. through this one-stop-shop system, the administrative procedure will be simpler, cheaper and faster. moreover, the issuing of a single document will also facilitate the control of persons admitted to the territory of a member state and authorised to take up employment. this document will follow the format of the residence permit common to all member states. member states will also be able to decide to introduce a complementary document which will be of purely informative value. it will supplement the information provided by the single permit and thus facilitate checks. so we have to deal with advantages from all sides - immigrants, employers, national administrations. by establishing a single application procedure, this directive will simplify the often complex administrative procedures for the admission of economic migrants. this would contribute to an adequate response to the labour force challenges that the eu is facing and will continue to face.
in writing. − this report is a very important step for european union legislation on legal migration, as it creates a single application procedure for third country nationals. i welcome the fact that the text adopted today excludes any reference to the possibility for a member state to introduce additional documents for obtaining a third-country person's work permit. the commission will also continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on migration and asylum, in particular by ensuring that the union's external borders are not crossed. what is important about this report is that it sets out a set of common measures on the rights of workers from third countries, facilitating the legal migration that the european union needs. the requirement for member states to draw up correlation tables is welcome as it will allow us to check the correct transposition of the directive.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that non-eu workers should enjoy the same rights as eu citizens in terms of working conditions, in accordance with the single permit directive. i would like to mention here in particular working time, leave and social security. this draft law aims to reduce red tape and simplify the application procedures for residence and work in an eu member state for both migrants and their employers through a combined residence and work permit. the proposal does not lay down the conditions for the admission of third-country nationals. member states retain the power to determine those conditions of admission and the number of migrants they wish to admit to their territory for the purpose of employment. the new rules will apply to non-eu citizens who already live legally in a member country or who wish to do so.
in writing. − economic immigration is a reality that we must organise, but also a necessity, if we are to respond to the demographic and economic challenges that the eu will face in the near future. immigration policy must be conceived as a tool to regulate our labour needs, which will contribute to the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy. the existence of a single procedure allowing for the issue of a single document authorising residence and access to the labour market constitutes a remarkable simplification of the admission regime. the directive will apply to any third-country national admitted to the territory of a member state for the purpose of employment, as well as to those who were initially admitted on other grounds but who have acquired the right to work in that member state under national or community law. each member state must lay down the conditions under which social security benefits are granted, as well as the amount of such benefits and the period for which they are granted. i regret that seasonal workers and workers posted within their undertakings are excluded from this directive, but i ask that the commission submit a proposal to this effect soon.
in writing. − according to the eu 2020 strategy, high-quality and environmentally sustainable production is one of the eu's competitive advantages. a high level of consumer protection guarantees high quality products and increases consumer confidence, thus fostering the effectiveness of the internal market. the commission's proposals for a new consumer rights directive are welcome as they aim to provide transparency for businesses, with a view to unlocking the potential of cross-border trade in the eu. the new consumer rights rules cover almost all types of sales, in-store, by telephone or online, and strengthen in particular the provisions on international sales, as proposed in the report drawn up by my colleague andreas schwab. unlike the four current consumer protection directives, i believe that the new legislation brings added value by providing what information the buyer must receive from the seller, the delivery conditions and the rules that apply when the risk is borne by the buyer, and the buyer's right to cancel or refuse purchases or the right to have a good repaired or replaced.
in writing. − the european agency for network and information security has a special role in supporting member states' cooperation efforts in this field at community level. information and communication technologies have become essential elements for the economy and society as a whole. they are vulnerable to threats that no longer respect national borders, are interconnected and interdependent with other infrastructures, and their security and resilience cannot be ensured by strictly national approaches. the report puts the emphasis on protecting europe against cyber attacks and disruption of information systems by increasing preparedness, security and resilience. i voted in favour of the report because it aims to develop a culture of cyber and data security for the benefit of citizens, businesses and public sector organisations in the european union. i believe that the mandate of the european cybersecurity agency is necessary to enable the european union, the member states and stakeholders to develop a preparedness and capacity to prevent, detect and respond more effectively to network and information security issues.
in writing. − i have chosen to vote on this report because i believe it is necessary to extend the mandate of the european agency for the security of information networks until 2013. this agency was established for a period of five years in march 2004 and then extended until march 2012. the main objective was to ensure effective security of the union's it networks. as we live in a world that has become increasingly dependent on the internet, we need to become more aware of the problem of internet security, cybercrime is not just virtual, it has a real impact on our lives. this issue is also on the nato agenda, and as a result an eu-us working group on cybercrime and security is being set up, which is a very important step in protecting the cyber infrastructure. i really think we still need the european cyber security agency.
in writing. − i was delighted to vote in favour of the extension of the mandate of the european network and information security agency (enisa) until september 2013. this agency was established in 2002 for an initial period of five years. enisa’s mandate is important as it was set by the eu to carry out very specific technical and scientific tasks in the field of information security. it is important to have such an agency in place in order to ensure the smooth functioning of the internal market that concretely affects the daily lives of the citizens and business alike, using broadband, online banking, e-commerce and mobile phones. given the fact that attacks on information systems are constantly increasing, it is a critical time to have effective security measures in place in order to protect the integrity of europe’s information systems. a top-down eu approach is required to protect the information society sector. member states cannot do this sufficiently by themselves. it is estimated that the necessary funding for the extension of enisa’s current mandate would be eur 12.698 million in commitments.

member of the commission. − mr president, every day, european businesses have to compete in an ever-changing and more competitive environment. the questions of dependability and timely delivery are as important as those of quality and price. exports of dual-use items create particular challenges in this regard, as such exports are subject to authorisation requirements. dual-use items are not niche goods. they are very much items legitimately used in a broad variety of industrial sectors – the space industry, the telecommunications industry, aviation, the chemical industry and many others. the goods are controlled because they could also potentially be used for military purposes. many member states make special export facilitations available to their exporters. these facilitations take the form of general licences and allow businesses in certain member states to export dual-use items with the minimum burden. following an analysis of these national facilitation measures, in 2008 the commission put forward its proposal aimed at extending these national facilitations to exporters throughout the union. the proposal for a new eu general export authorisation is designed to allow exporters in all member states to reap the benefits of simplified export procedures for certain dual-use items to certain destinations. in this way, participation in international exhibitions and fairs will become easier. exporting items after they have been repaired will also become simpler, and exports of telecommunications equipment and certain industrial chemicals will be simplified. on the other hand, member states will be able to concentrate their limited resources on transactions that actually do pose a risk. the commission regularly receives complaints from industry that certain exports are being prevented from entering one member state while identical transactions are given a green light in other member states. the proposal in front of you is a first step towards eliminating these inequalities within our single market. many other countries are taking similar steps to prioritise their work on export control, and we should not be left behind. i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr leichtfried, and other members for their very constructive work on the proposal. the report presented by you and your committee is definitely a step in the right direction and is broadly consistent with the commission’s view.
on behalf of the s&d group, i would first like to congratulate my colleague on the work he has done on this report, which is so technical but has real implications for the safety of european citizens. the european union has been applying export control measures to dual-use items for almost 15 years. thus, through preventive measures such as export authorisation and customs registration requirements, the european union is ensuring that the proliferation of weapons, in particular weapons of mass destruction, is prevented. however, the eu's dual-use regime needs to be more transparent and democratized. it is necessary to create a secure system through which notifications of exports of products for both civilian and military use are collected, transmitted and stored in order to prevent the danger of proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. i also welcome the rapporteur's proposal that the coordination group on dual-use products should submit an annual report to the european parliament to facilitate the exercise of the latter's monitoring function. the european commission, for its part, is required to inform parliament on the implementation of the provision of the regulation establishing a community regime for the control of exports of dual-use items and technologies and to present an impact study of the proposed measures. last but not least, the representation of the european union in international export control regimes needs to be improved. unfortunately, the lists of controlled products are updated by international regimes and transposed into european union legislation without the european parliament being able to participate in this process. i therefore call for better control by parliament and for the legislative role of parliament to be facilitated, as provided for in the treaty of lisbon.
mr president, the topic of the report is doubly sensitive, both politically and economically. on the one hand, the eu wants to prevent dual-used goods to be used for military purposes and/or against people. on the other hand, it has to consider the economic interests of producers and users. the regulation is therefore inevitably bushy, having to cover for both existing intentional loopholes and anticipate for others in the future. moreover, while for some the regulation would appear too strong for others it would appear too weak, requiring constant revision. as a member of the committee on foreign affairs, i fully support the need for a more transparent and stricter regulation. i am therefore totally in favour of authorisation before export and not vice versa. particularly after lisbon, parliament can only help, and this is exactly what it is doing here and now. consequently, its role should be strengthened, not overlooked.
on behalf of the s&d group, i would like to congratulate my colleague brian simpson on this report on the european regulation establishing a common framework for the development, production and dissemination of european statistics on tourism. it is the member states which collect, compile, process and transmit harmonised statistics on tourism demand and supply. the majority of tourism enterprises are small and medium-sized enterprises, and their strategic importance is not limited to their economic value, but must above all be recognised for the substantial job-creation potential they have. according to eurostat data for 2007, one in three european families could not afford to pay for one week of tourism a year. the economic crisis has increased the number of europeans at risk of poverty and, by implication, further reduced the number of those who can afford to take a week of tourism a year. i therefore believe that statistics on tourism are necessary and relevant for assessing the social dimension of this sector. social tourism increases the number of european tourists, helps to combat seasonality, reinforces the notion of european citizenship and promotes regional development. statistical data on social tourism would enable the commission and the member states to identify the specific needs of different social groups and to develop appropriate programmes. when compiling european statistics under this regulation, national statistical authorities should also provide data on the funds used for tourism by each member state, in particular for european funds. last but not least, i believe that european statistics on tourism should not be lacking in data on staff employed, their seasonality, vocational training and qualifications, and data on existing working conditions. without well-trained human resources, we cannot have good quality tourism.
i regret that there are no official statistics on rural tourism and agro-tourism, the only data available being estimates. in this context, i welcome the actions envisaged by the european commission to strengthen the socioeconomic knowledge base on tourism. i also stress the importance of the 'ict and tourism' platform proposed by the commission, but i believe that more intensive efforts are needed to equip rural areas with state-of-the-art it infrastructure, for example the provision of broadband internet. rural and agro-tourism accounts for over 500 000 accommodation units with over six million beds. these two sectors have had an average annual growth of 10-15% in recent years, thus making a key contribution to improving the quality of life in rural areas and diversifying the rural economy.
mr simpson's report is an important achievement for the statistical framework for tourism at european level. with its high potential, tourism thus contributes to employment and economic growth. improvements in the efficiency of data processing and the comparability of the statistics transmitted are necessary. to cope with the global tourism competition, romania has professionally built a strategy to stand out from other tourist destinations in the world. the strategy is based on the country brand of romania, a concept through which we present to potential tourists the authenticity of our traditions and fairy landscapes. i would stress that the development of tourism could also help to reduce inequalities in the regions of south-eastern europe. the emphasis must therefore be on diversity.
in writing. there is now a growing talk about increasing the eu's global competitiveness; tourism is one of the most important socio-economic activities, generating around 5% of the eu's gdp. the updating and optimisation of the legal framework for european statistics in this field is a pressing need for the development of sustainable, responsible and quality tourism. by achieving better quality statistical reporting, based on comparative and reliable data, we will benefit from a solid basis in the decision-making process for the development of community policies and financial instruments. i believe that we must do everything we can to remain the world's number one tourist destination, and to do that we must make the most of all possible funding opportunities. in this regard, i call on the european executive to develop and mobilise specific community support instruments and programmes for the development of european tourism, in line with the europe 2020 strategy.

in writing. almost a quarter of women in europe have suffered at least one act of physical violence and over a tenth have been victims of sexual violence. the economic crisis has contributed, through its social consequences, to worsen the situation, with poverty and lack of education being factors that favour gender-based violence. i therefore consider that coordinated measures against the cases, as well as legislative harmonisation and closer judicial cooperation between member states, are necessary in order to make investigations more efficient. information and awareness campaigns, the creation of victim reception centres, the establishment of a single european telephone number for immediate assistance and support for highly vulnerable groups such as migrant and asylum-seeking women are some of the actions that states and eu institutions have a duty to take as a matter of urgency to stop violence against women.
member of the commission. − madam president, some honourable members may be getting tired of me but i think this joint debate on migration flows is very timely. this will be both a general discussion of the role and scope of eu foreign policy, as outlined in mr provera’s report, and an opportunity for me to inform you about how the eu is responding to the crisis in the southern mediterranean. let me start by thanking mr provera for his excellent report which i read with great interest. it is a very timely subject for discussion, as is the role that eu foreign policy should play with regard to the very complex and multifaceted nature of migration. let me start by outlining some elements of the eu response to the crisis in the southern mediterranean and then move to the more general role of eu foreign policy. as you all know, we are faced with a situation in the southern mediterranean that has become very critical in recent weeks with regard to the migration flows involved. more than 400 000 people have been displaced since the outbreak of the changes in northern africa and in libya. most of these people are third-country nationals who have come to tunisia or to egypt. a majority of them have been repatriated to their countries but a few thousand are still there and i will come back to them in a little while. around 20 000 migrants, mainly from tunisia and, to a lesser extent from other african countries, have managed to enter the european union irregularly, reaching the shores of lampedusa and malta. both of these islands are therefore under strong migratory pressure. the european union has already responded to these serious, but different, challenges in an effective and rapid manner, taking three concrete actions. firstly, the commission has mobilised eur 30 million to manage the humanitarian emergency generated by the sudden inflows of migrants and refugees in the countries neighbouring libya. with the assistance of funds provided on a bilateral basis by the member states and other international donors, it has been possible to offer temporary shelter to migrants and refugees, to meet their basic needs and to return them to their respective countries of origin. secondly, we have reacted to the irregular and mixed flows across the mediterranean sea. frontex, with the assistance of several member states, launched joint operation hermes, aimed at assisting italy in controlling vessels that carry migrants and refugees. what is more, europol has deployed a team of experts to italy, with the aim of helping the law enforcement authorities to identify possible criminal networks involved in trafficking. thirdly, the commission has tried to ensure that, in the very short term, the member states exposed to the growing flows of refugees and irregular migrants could cope with the financial consequences of this displacement. we have rapidly identified eur 25 million which could be mobilised under the external borders fund and european refugee fund if and when specific requests are made by the member states. only one request has been made so far but we are ready to consider further urgent requests. i believe that this first response has been comprehensive; it is clear, however, that we need to do more. we need to set up a more structured, sustainable plan able to cover the various dimensions of this phenomenon, based on solidarity between member states and in full respect of the european union’s international obligations. i have visited egypt with the hungarian minister of foreign affairs, mr martonyi, and tunisia with my colleague commissioner füle, who is responsible for neighbourhood policy. this was partly in response to the conclusions of the european council, which asked the commission to liaise very actively with these two countries. in the run-up to our june jha council, i intend to propose a package of proposals to the commission in may that will address the eu approach in the area of migration, mobility and security with the southern mediterranean countries. several measures need to be taken in the short term. on the continuous and possible increase of flows of refugees coming from the libyan territory, the following actions will be considered: an adequate level of funds needs to remain available to support the provision of humanitarian assistance. in this context, funds will have to be earmarked to meet the basic needs of the refugees, to facilitate their return to their countries of origin, when appropriate, and to support their successful social and professional reintegration back home. moreover, an increasing number of refugees fleeing libya are third-country nationals who were residing in libya as refugees or asylum seekers. these people, a few thousand, cannot be returned to their countries of origin. resettlement needs to be considered. the commission is ready to facilitate this process and calls upon the member states to take responsibility and to engage in such resettlement efforts. there will be financial support for this, from the european refugee fund in particular. in this context, it is imperative that the council and the european parliament make an effort to rapidly achieve an agreement on the european resettlement programme. all three institutions are in agreement on the political aim of this; we must find a way out of this institutional deadlock. it is also urgent to develop a regional protection programme encompassing egypt, libya and tunisia. under the thematic programme for cooperation with third countries, the commission has plans to allocate eur 3.6 million to support such a programme. the deployment of easo teams to the member states affected by these flows will also be considered, with a view to helping the authorities screen the asylum seekers. finally, in the event of a massive influx of displaced persons and if the conditions foreseen in the directive are met, the commission would be ready to consider making use of the mechanisms foreseen under the 2001 temporary protection directive so as to provide immediate protection for these people on the territory of other eu member states. the intention would be to give breathing space to the national asylum systems and to promote voluntary solidarity measures between member states. with regard to the continuous inflows of irregular migrants coming from the southern mediterranean, which could increase, the commission believes that joint operation hermes, coordinated by frontex, should receive additional resources from member states. frontex will stand ready to provide logistical and financial support to assist the member states concerned, to organise return flights and to deploy rapid border intervention teams if they wish. it is essential that the competences of frontex are strengthened rapidly and more effective tools are put at its disposal. the amended regulation establishing the frontex agency should be adopted by the council and the european parliament as soon as possible. specific projects are also being prepared by eu services and will shortly be launched, in partnership with the countries concerned, starting with tunisia and egypt. the aim is to enhance their capacity to control their borders – in cooperation with the relevant authorities – to fight against criminal organisations promoting the smuggling of migrants and people trafficking, to facilitate readmission and social and professional reintegration and to identify and register migrants entering the territory and treat them in accordance with international standards by offering asylum to those in need of international protection. these measures represent the immediate answer to the situation. however, we also need implement long-term, sustainable programmes. with my partners in tunisia and egypt we discussed bringing in working arrangements on a variety of issues covered under the mobility partnership. this could take the form of a new tailor-made eu approach, considering each country on its own merits, and taking into account the eu’s overall foreign policy with a given country. partnerships could cover everything from visa facilitation, under certain conditions and for specific categories, labour migration, preventing irregular migrant flows, setting up asylum systems, readmission, law enforcement, approach will help to set up a long-term system to address migration flows and this brings me to mr provera’s report. protracted, long-standing conflicts and humanitarian crises in regions, such as the one we are talking about, are important factors fuelling south-south migration and migration towards the eu. our main global challenges, such as migration, fully underline the importance of developing a comprehensive approach linking security, stability, crisis management and development. as the report suggests, such an approach must be based on a strong human rights approach, notably with regard to migrants’ rights. special attention must be given to the situation of vulnerable groups. we share the view that it is crucial to put in place more long-term, sustainable cooperation programmes to address migration, mobility and security, in combination with the promotion of democracy, the rule of law and good governance with third countries. this approach should be tailor-made, eradication, early-warning systems and preventive diplomacy, humanitarian aid, crisis response actions, including sanctions, crisis management missions and post-conflict reconstruction and peace building. this report is therefore very timely, as the eu currently has to deal with a crisis. but it also represents a possibility to start something new, the possibility to support the fantastic new migration policy, is to be based on a genuine partnership with third countries. this is mentioned in the stockholm programme and the stockholm action plan and we will provide further initiatives in the reporter. − the accession treaties of three member states, slovakia, bulgaria and lithuania, included the requirement to decommission a number of nuclear reactors that no longer met safety requirements and could not be cost-effectively upgraded. the financial assistance provided by the european union was not intended to cover the full cost of decommissioning. assistance was intended for measures for decommissioning, maintenance and after-shutdown supervision, waste treatment, storage and decontamination of waste and spent fuel and dismantling works, in the energy field (for replacing the production capacity of closed units, increasing the security of energy supply and energy efficiency and other measures contributing to the necessary restructuring and modernisation of the energy infrastructure) and in terms of social consequences (for supporting the staff of the plant in maintaining a high level of safety after shutdown and retraining staff for tasks in the decommissioning process). the fact that the financial assistance was set without a ceiling, a situation which persisted after the development of decommissioning plans and strategies, made further financial supplements possible. the european union has funded this activity with large sums of money, some €2.8 billion since 1999. the report calls for the following to be clarified in future evaluations by the european commission and the european court of auditors: whether the funds allocated by the european union have been used to ensure the security of the decommissioning activity; whether the decommissioning ensures the safe storage of nuclear waste; whether there has been adequate coordination between the three existing programmes, thus making effective use of the experience gained and following the pattern of previously prepared and financed projects to generate cost savings; whether current plans and strategies are complete or whether there is still scope to add new activities and subsequently additional funds; whether additional amounts still need to be allocated to energy projects or whether it is necessary to focus more on decommissioning projects and whether the financing of these activities from community funds is necessary.
there are 143 nuclear power plants in the european union and, according to data published by the energy dg in march 2010, nuclear energy accounts for approximately 28% of the eu's energy mix. the events in japan have raised the alarm about the risks associated with nuclear power plants. early closure and decommissioning of nuclear facilities represents a major financial and economic burden and therefore the european union can provide financial assistance to the member states concerned - i am referring to lithuania, slovakia and bulgaria. the lack of funding for decommissioning measures will delay this process, which would pose a threat to the environment and human health. we urge the national competent bodies to finalise the detailed decommissioning plans and the commission to report on this process, to clearly describe the scope of eu funding in these cases and to provide a detailed long-term financial planning of decommissioning projects.

member of the commission. − madam president, i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr ivan, for his constructive report. i will concentrate my remarks on six very important elements of it. firstly, the question of the information provided in the report on the protection of financial interests. the 2009 report already includes new detailed information on levels of fraud and irregularities, and indicates the suspected fraud rate per member state for the 2000-2006 cohesion programmes. further improvements are always possible, and i will take due account of your suggestions. secondly, on the issue of the convention on the protection of financial interests, i am preparing a communication for next may, together with vice-president reding. it will present a strategy for the protection of eu public money against all forms of illegal conduct, including fraud, and will look at procedures, substantive criminal law and the institutional framework. thirdly, turning to own resources, in 2010 the commission started to visit all member states to examine simplified customs import procedures. it will report to the parliament as soon as enough information has been gathered for a meaningful analysis of their implementation and performance. fourthly, on cigarette smuggling, agreements have now been concluded with four tobacco manufacturers. we will continue to push for a protocol on the elimination of the illicit trade in tobacco products under the who convention on tobacco control. on the fifth point, i fully agree that failures in applying public procurement rules are an important source of errors and fraud. the commission vigorously implements financial corrections with rates of up to 100% of the allocated funding, depending on the gravity of the irregularities. we propose simplification and clarification of eu procurements directives by 2012, in line with the green paper published earlier this year. finally, i share the view that the recovery of unduly paid funds is a key element in protecting the eu’s financial interests. for multiannual cohesion programmes, the commission is making extensive use of the interruption and suspension of payments, avoiding payments to member states where management and control systems are found not be effective. in 2010, more than eur 2.4 billion of payments under the regional and social funds were preventively interrupted. the commission will continue to push member states towards more efficient management of recovery from final beneficiaries. the situation is improving. in the agricultural sector, for example, the recovery rate at the end of 2010 went up to 53% for new 2007 cases, compared to 10% for cases dating from before 2006. let me stress, however, that for multiannual programmes the full picture is only seen when the programmes are closed, after any irregularities have been satisfactorily dealt with by the member states. to conclude, the commission will endeavour to actively follow up the actions which parliament has proposed. thank you for your attention.
on behalf of the ppe group. – madam president, i believe we have to talk about what we need to correct, so i will refer to the critical issues. the first of them is the fact that the commission’s report did not provide information on the estimated level of irregularities and fraud in individual member states. therefore, we lack a clear picture of the problem at member state level. in addition, the commission dealt broadly with irregularities but failed to look at fraud in detail. we expect that to change in the report for the following year. the second issue concerns public procurement, which, as we all know, is the area with the highest risk of fraud and corruption. what we call for in this report is for the commission to focus on regulating public procurement: to apply uniform systems of procurement; to define and implement clear conditions for participation in public procurement; to implement criteria for decision-making on public procurement and bring transparency to these decisions; and also to review public procurement decisions and ensure transparency and accountability in public finances. we expect the commission and the council to finalise the adoption of the public procurement reform and to consult with us on this. the third issue concerns the transparency of beneficiaries’ funding. there is a page on the commission’s website where we can see some of the beneficiaries of european funds in the member states. however, we need to improve this greatly. we need one-stop transparency. we need a single website that publishes all the beneficiaries of eu funds on the basis of standard categories of information to be supplied by all the member states in at least one working language of the union. otherwise we will be lost in a lot of diverse information that fails to provide any overall picture and cannot offer transparency. as the commissioner said, there is always room for improvement, and i hope to see improvement in the areas i have mentioned.

an ambitious programme which is at the same time realistic and necessary to restore the strength of the internal market. i am convinced that if these measures are implemented, they will make the internal market more attractive to our citizens and businesses and will bring more efficiency to its overall functioning. concerning my report, i have to say that we did not have an easy task. our task was ambitious because we had to find a consensus on the measures laying the foundations for a strong and modern single market which would contribute to future growth and which would, above all, meet the expectations of our citizens and businesses. we considered whether the emphasis should be on innovation, what should be done in the field of intellectual property rights, and what fiscal measures are appropriate in order to enhance the single market while respecting the sovereignty of the member states. following our discussions, and after many contributions for which i would like to thank all the shadow rapporteurs, the rapporteurs for opinions and all the other colleagues who tabled amendments we managed to identify a set of five priorities to be implemented immediately. the first priority refers to the means to support innovation and creativity in the single market, which is essential if we want stronger and more sustainable growth. the creation of an eu patent and of a unified litigation system, which is already under way, as well as the improvement to management of copyrights, are of paramount importance. if we want innovation, we also need to come up with a solution for financing it, such as long-term investment and a framework that would make it easier for venture capital funds to be invested effectively. eu project bonds can also be a great opportunity for infrastructure investments in the field of energy or telecommunications. our third priority seeks to bring the single market in line with our digital agenda by stimulating e-commerce. this requires measures that would enhance consumer and business confidence in e-commerce, such as fighting counterfeiting and piracy and facilitating cross-border deliveries and cross-border debt recovery. the fourth priority aims to make the single market a better environment for smes, given their importance for economic growth and their job creation potential. they need better access to capital markets. fiscal measures such as the introduction of a common consolidated corporate tax base, a clear vat framework and reducing administrative burdens could encourage smes to do cross-border business. finally, public procurement procedures need to be rationalised. they need simplification to allow smes to take part in procedures, and they should be better used in order to support smart, sustainable and inclusive growth.

in writing. the economic and financial crisis we are going through has shown us that if we move away from the fundamental objective of the economy which is to ensure the well-being of citizens, we risk pushing the whole society towards collapse. this is also true for the single market. we must not forget that its role is to enable every european citizen to enjoy throughout the union equivalent economic and social rights that ensure his well-being. the single market must be deepened and reoriented towards citizens and their interests. i think that in this time of crisis it is important to make the most of what europe has most precious, namely human capital. the mobility of workers within the eu is the key to economic recovery and the development of the single market. we must encourage this mobility, and the first thing worth doing is to remove any barriers to the movement of labour within the eu. restrictions on workers in the new member states are an obstacle to the harmonious development of the single market and must be removed immediately.
in writing. – in my opinion, a single market for europeans should also mean a single market of quality. unfortunately, this report does not make any kind of reference to this issue. in the european union, products are sometimes offered under the same brand names, but with a different product formulation, in different countries. products reportedly have the same brand name but are available in different concentrations or strengths. situations have been reported where products of four different quality categories were sold under the same brand, depending on the destination country. as a result, the – apparently – same product is of different quality depending on the country of purchase. as a brand name is associated with perceived quality, this practice could result in misleading the public. businesses must avoid misleading consumers about the advantages related to the brand of goods. if producers want to reduce the quality of the goods they offer, they should use a different brand name. our citizens believe that the quality of brand goods should be identical on every market, based on the principle that one brand equals one level of quality. as my constituents are preoccupied by this issue, i would like to see it raised in our discussions in this house.
