in writing. - i voted in favour of our rapporteur's proposal and believe that by fulfilling the obligations assumed under this protocol, both sides will benefit. the union a solid, stable and democratic partner on the eastern border, and the citizens of ukraine a somewhat clearer european perspective.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the council decision on a framework agreement between the european union and ukraine on the general principles for the participation of that country in union programmes. this document is part of the european neighbourhood policy, but also meets ukraine's desire to participate in several current and future eu programmes. in addition, ukraine will be able to request union assistance for participation in a specific programme in accordance with the general provisions on the establishment of a european neighbourhood and partnership instrument or under any other similar regulation providing for external assistance. in this way, romania's relations with ukraine can also benefit from a new breath. we need to develop these links in a pragmatic way so that citizens are the direct beneficiaries of our political decisions.
in writing. − despite the efforts to harmonise asylum over the past decade, there are still significant differences between national provisions and their application. such discrepancies are incompatible with a common european asylum system and constitute obstacles to its establishment. they contradict one of the basic principles of the dublin system, which is based on the presumption that the asylum systems of the member states are comparable. regardless of the member state in which persons apply for asylum, they must enjoy a high and equivalent level of protection throughout the union. if legislative harmonisation will not be sufficient to reduce these differences and will need to be complemented by a strengthening of practical cooperation between member states, the adoption of a sound european legal framework is a sine qua non condition for the union to implement a common european asylum system in an adequate and effective manner, as it has repeatedly committed to do. the commission's proposal is to make up for past mistakes, as the previous approach to asylum has encouraged a number of shortcomings in the procedural guarantees for asylum seekers.
in writing. − tourism statistics are a major aspect in the development of more effective tourism policies at european, national, regional, regional and local levels. however, these statistics are not only used to monitor tourism-specific policies, but at the same time play a key role in the context of regional policy and sustainable development. i believe that the european union's tourism sector needs to be strengthened by coordinated measures at community level to complement the initiatives of the member states. i welcome the updating and optimisation of the legal framework for european tourism statistics to better respond to the challenges facing the sector, such as climate change, environmental constraints, global competition, demographic trends and the seasonal distribution of tourist trips. this new common framework for the systematic production of european statistics on tourism should be established by the collection, compilation, processing and transmission by member states of harmonised statistics on demand and supply. i voted in favour of this report because tourism is an important economic activity in the european union, contributing to employment and growth.
in writing. − europe ranks 7th in the top 10 destinations in a statistic covering the 50 most admired countries in the world. it is a very good proof that europe has a great tourist and cultural potential, but that there are still opportunities for exploitation, including for european citizens. i believe that one such possibility is the participation of older people, but also of young people and families with difficulties, as well as of people with reduced mobility, in the programmes developed by the union in the field of social tourism. however, this requires appropriate statistical data - based on common collection methods - for the development of programmes for these categories of tourists in all member states of the union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european statistics on tourism report today. it is a positive step to establish a regulation that will take account of tourism statistics from all member states. the importance of tourism in european law was greatly elevated when it was made a competence under the lisbon treaty in december 2009. going forward, member states will have to ensure the accuracy of statistical data transmitted in order to achieve quality results. while european-level coordination will be very beneficial for the european tourism sector, any pan-european initiatives should seek to complement member states’ initiatives and tourism strategies. by providing statistical data, the eu will be in a better position to help the tourism industry, including smes, and to improve the overall marketing of europe as a highly desirable tourist destination. the distinction between internal and national tourism is drawn in the report. internal tourism covers the capacity of tourist accommodation establishments, and national tourism covers participation in tourism, including excursions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that we must do everything we can to remain the world's number one tourist destination and, to do so, we must make the most of all possible funding opportunities. the development of sustainable, responsible and quality tourism requires updating and optimising the legal framework for european statistics in this field. by achieving better quality statistical reporting, based on comparative and reliable data, we will benefit from a solid basis in the decision-making process for the development of community policies and financial instruments.
in writing. − i supported this report because regulation (ec) no 861/2006 laying down community financial measures for the implementation of the common fisheries policy and the law of the sea is an important instrument for eu funding in the fisheries sector and one of the two main instruments used to implement the cfp, the other being the european fisheries fund. like the rapporteur, i believe it is becoming increasingly clear that fisheries management must be based on the latest scientific information on the state of stocks. this is an indispensable condition for the sustainable development of the fisheries sector. as regards control, its importance for the future and sustainability of the fisheries sector and as a means of promoting a culture of compliance is certainly more widely recognised today. member states and their control authorities play and must continue to play a central role in the process of monitoring and enforcing control measures in their territorial waters. this is a key way to ensure compliance and stock levels.
in writing. − i believe that the aquaculture sector is growing in importance, as this report shows, which highlights 'a new impetus for the sustainable development strategy for european aquaculture' and offers real opportunities for the development of this sector. properly conducted environmental and health monitoring and surveillance thus contributes to the sustainability of this important sector.
in writing. - i voted for mr fernandes' report. this report allows us to analyse the 2012 budget for the european parliament objectively. surely, it will have to be a rigorous budget of austerity. it is important to take inflation into account, and this means that the 2012 budget actually implies a reduction in the amounts available. all expenditure must be justified and substantiated. variable costs must be processed in cost-benefit analyses in order to avoid any additional costs in the future. in 2012, we have to improve the situation of young people. the objectives set must relate primarily to young people. i would like to stress that young people must be helped in vocational training and in the fight against school dropout. in this respect, more money must be made available for projects aimed at young people. they need support to integrate into the labour market.
in writing. − i supported this resolution because i believe that health claims can influence consumer choices and that these claims must be used responsibly on the basis of the highest quality scientific evaluation. it is very true that the presence of adh in breast milk has positive effects on the development of visual function in infants up to 12 months of age, but this does not automatically mean that synthesised adh, included in other forms of infant milk, has the same effects. in breast milk, adh is accompanied by other co-enzymes and co-factors, which together have this effect on the development of visual function. there is currently no scientific consensus on the positive effects of adh-enriched milk products for infants. therefore, i consider it premature to authorize the use of such a term until we have tangible scientific evidence to that effect. a health claim of this kind may mislead consumers and may have undesirable effects on the health of children.
in writing. − future european policy must promote sustainable, environmentally friendly investment, especially in the extractive industries, and encourage good working conditions in the enterprises targeted by international investment. i believe that any investment agreement should be accompanied by a set of social and environmental rules, both in the case of negotiating a chapter in a free trade agreement and in the case of an autonomous investment agreement. european policy must protect biodiversity and promote technology transfer and infrastructure improvements. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the european union needs a coherent investment policy that makes a positive contribution to economic growth and sustainable development and to employment.
in writing. - my vote was for this report. we all know that under the lisbon treaty, foreign investment is the exclusive competence of the eu. on the basis of this new competence, both the commission and the member states can, together with parliament, develop a policy to promote high-quality investment with a positive impact on growth and employment. the crisis naturally reduced the volume of foreign direct investment, which in 2007 had reached eur 1 500 billion. i also welcome the proposal to introduce the term 'eu investor' and believe that the protection of all eu investors should be the top priority of investment agreements.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that we must guarantee external competitiveness and the equal treatment of all eu investors and we must have maximum leverage in international investment negotiations. they must cover all types of investment and the eu must ensure that no eu investor is treated worse than under bilateral investment treaties between member states. investment liberalisation and protection are becoming fundamental instruments of a common international investment policy. however, member states will continue to implement investment promotion policies which are complementary to and compatible with the common international investment policy.

in writing. − taking into account the amount of fraud compared to irregularities in the own resources sector for the member states austria, spain, italy, romania and slovakia, where fraud constitutes more than half of the total amount of irregularities in each member state, and also the shortcomings in national customs supervision, i consider it necessary to strengthen customs supervision systems. in parallel, the european commission must exercise its responsibility to ensure that member states comply with their reporting obligations in order to provide reliable and comparable data on irregularities and fraud.
in writing. − this report summarises the statistics on irregularities reported by the member states in the areas where they implement the budget (agricultural policy, cohesion policy and pre-accession funds, i.e. about 80% of the budget) and on the collection of the eu's traditional own resources. i consider that the protection of the eu's financial interests and the fight against fraud are particularly important areas and that the responsibility lies with both the european union and the member states. the report also provides an estimate of irregularities in the area of expenditure managed directly by the commission and an overview of the operational work of the european anti-fraud office.
in writing. − the european union is a mosaic of diverse nations, cultures, opinions and beliefs which, in the current social and political context, must be uniformly represented and equally supported in legislative forums, whether national or european. the concept of representativeness is at the heart of the european construction and it will have to be maintained and supported because only then can the project of a united europe make sense. i believe that relaxing the funding regime for political parties at european level can lead to strengthening and promoting in the future the principle of representative democracy and, consequently, the interests of all european citizens who contribute to the union budget. in the process of moving from the concept of the european polis to the sense of european political identity, we must strive to simplify direct contact between citizens and european political parties. in her report, mrs giannakou stresses that this is not possible without a rethinking of the statute and funding of european parties. the emphasis should be on the de-bureaucratization of the procedures for granting funding, as the report rightly points out, but with the introduction of drastic sanctions in the event of irregularities or non-compliance with existing rules. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − i supported the proposals of the rapporteur and the approach in the commission communication 'towards a single market act', but also the idea that an annual single market forum is necessary. local and regional authorities should be more involved in creating the single market, and dialogue with social partners and civil society helps to restore confidence in the single market. and i think that using regulations instead of directives would create a clearer regulatory environment and reduce the costs of implementation. i also think it is useful to have an assessment of the single market situation at each spring european council and that we need a legislative proposal from the commission on alternative dispute resolution by the end of this year.
in writing. − member states must adopt a firm common position to improve the functioning of the european single market and avoid the re-emergence of economic protectionism, which would lead to the fragmentation of the internal market and harm competitiveness. the single european market act aims to develop administrative cooperation between member states, including by increasing the role of regional authorities to achieve coordination at their level. unfortunately, registration of such programmes at regional level is relatively difficult to achieve due to economic disparities between eu regions. to revitalise the less developed regions, we need to focus on human capital. the prosperity of a region is determined in part by the productivity of its people, their skills, together with the scale of capital investment and the capacity for innovation. however, there are major differences even between regions within the same member state. i believe that adapting the european single market to the needs of european citizens is achieved primarily by improving the mobility of workers. the free movement of labour can make a considerable contribution to reducing disparities between regions. another key aspect is the education and continuing training of human capital. skilled workers and workers made redundant can more easily meet the specific needs of the market, due to their high degree of mobility.
in writing. − a barrier-free and competitive single market should be completed to bring tangible benefits to workers, students, pensioners and citizens in general, as well as to businesses, in particular smes. good governance and legal certainty are essential to achieve the economic and social objectives of the single market, such as the free movement of workers, the promotion of a high level of employment, the guarantee of adequate social protection, the fight against social exclusion, a high level of education and training and the transferability of pensions. the european executive should further promote the one-stop shop, integrating all existing services into a single point of access and providing citizens and businesses with information and support on their rights in the single market, as well as practical information on national rules and procedures. i call on the member states to make the public better aware of the one-stop shop and its component services. the ec must integrate fundamental rights into all single market legislation. the implementation of the fundamental economic freedoms of the single market should not affect the rights to collective bargaining and the right to strike as defined in national law.

first of all, i would like to express my admiration and respect for the attitude of the japanese people towards the extraordinary situation they are going through. this situation has led to heated discussions about the future of nuclear power continue or stop. i think we need to have a balanced approach, which takes into account all the aspects: the demands of the economy, the security of citizens, climate change. i believe that the future energy policy must be based on a balance between renewable energy, new technologies for conventional resources and nuclear energy, under safe conditions. we need to invest in research for efficient renewable energy production. we need to invest to secure new sources of conventional raw materials and new supply routes for europe the southern corridor. at the same time, research and innovation is needed for new technologies that eliminate the polluting effect of conventional energy production on the environment. the nuclear safety directive needs to be revised to make it more stringent. the commission's proposed stress tests are needed. the criteria must be developed taking into account all aspects: age, technologies, natural hazards. the tests shall be carried out with the participation of the commission. the results of the tests are to be used in the revision of the directive. the consequences of the tests must be very clear. whoever falls in, keeps going, whoever doesn't, doesn't stop. i would draw attention to the need for a european policy for the treatment and storage of nuclear waste and for decommissioning power stations. last but not least, the public must maintain its confidence in atomic energy and must be properly informed.
i welcome the commission's decision to subject nuclear reactors in the european union to stress tests. we call for these checks to be carried out on the basis of common and detailed evaluation criteria, in order to further improve nuclear safety in the european union. today, there are 143 nuclear reactors in the union, with nuclear energy accounting for 30% of the european energy mix. member states are responsible for their own energy mix, but nuclear safety is our responsibility, everyone's. that is why it is important that we have a resolution on nuclear safety in the european union. i would stress that for each nuclear reactor, the investment for nuclear safety must be ensured by the end of its planned operational period. as a result of the stress tests, the standards for future nuclear reactors and, by implication, the cost of nuclear power will rise. the union therefore needs to invest substantially in energy efficiency measures and in the production and use of energy from renewable sources, in particular for the buildings and transport sectors.
in writing. in the wake of the fukushima nuclear disaster, safety rules in the nuclear industry need to be re-examined. we're talking about the more than 400 nuclear reactors around the world. it is therefore advisable to set up a stress test as soon as possible. but this is not enough - a nuclear safety culture is needed. i am reminded of the chernobyl accident in 1986, which introduced the concept of 'nuclear safety'. as regards romania, i would stress that there is no risk that an earthquake will endanger the operation of the cernavoda nuclear power plant. preventive checks have shown that the two reactors are operating safely. they produce about 20% of the country's energy consumption. the unit is resistant to earthquakes with a magnitude of eight on the richter scale, and the earthquakes that can occur in romania have an average intensity between 7 and 7,5 degrees.
in writing. – the nuclear accident in japan has raised fresh concerns about the safety of nuclear power across the globe. in romania, the nuclear power plant at cernavodă has been assessed by various bodies, including the european commission and the international atomic energy association. a study in 2004 identified seismic hazard as being the single biggest risk factor for safety at the plant. this risk must be managed effectively and, as the tragic events in japan remind us, as a matter of urgency. i therefore welcome the recent proposal to introduce stress tests for nuclear installations, as well as the entry into force of the directive on nuclear safety. regardless of what we decide about the future energy mix and how we meet our low-carbon objectives, the safety of nuclear facilities, including long-term depositories, will continue to be of the upmost importance for both current and future generations.
in writing. nuclear energy is a resource that the global economy cannot do without in the long term. the fact that dangerous accidents occur in the operation of nuclear power stations should not lead us to the conclusion that nuclear energy is rejected. the solution is to allocate more resources to research in this area and to improve nuclear technology so that we reduce the risks of accidents.

the president of the council. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen of the house. i very much appreciate the european parliament's active involvement in the enlargement process and its constructive participation in the general enlargement debate and, in particular, of course, in the icelandic accession process. the enlargement of the european union, one of the most successful policies of the union, is one of the most important priorities of our presidency in the history of the eu. on 17 june 2010, the european council unanimously decided to grant iceland the status of candidate country. the first meeting of the ministerial accession conference was held on 27 july 2010 and the screening process was launched in november 2010 and is proceeding as planned. the next ministerial accession conference is scheduled for 27 june, so that we can take stock of the progress made and hopefully open as many chapters as possible. there are a number of areas which are particularly important and i would like to draw particular attention to them. your draft resolution does a good job of identifying these issues. in its 2010 progress report, the commission concluded that iceland fulfilled the political criteria for membership and that, despite being severely affected by the economic and financial crisis, it was sufficiently prepared to take the necessary measures to meet the requirements of eu membership. on 14 december 2010, the council concluded that iceland has a long history of well-functioning democracy, strong institutions and close links with the union. it also concluded that iceland was generally well prepared to transpose and apply the union acquis, in particular as a member of the european economic area and a party to the schengen agreement. iceland is considered to be a functioning market economy and may regain its ability to withstand the competitive constraints and market forces in the single market in the medium term. the council recalled that the negotiations aimed at iceland's full transposition and application of the union acquis. the course of the negotiations will be determined by whether iceland fulfils all its obligations under the eea agreement, taking fully into account, inter alia, the conclusions of the european council of 17 june 2010, and by the outcome of the other deficiencies identified in the commission's opinion. in parallel, the council recalled that the eea agreement remains the fundamental contractual basis for relations between the eu and iceland as long as accession negotiations are ongoing and that iceland has been an active and constructive partner within this framework and with regard to the schengen area over the past two years. it also has a good track record in applying the evolving eu acquis. the council therefore encouraged iceland to continue this practice. the european parliament's draft resolution gives an overview of the achievements and the challenges to be tackled. in the latter case, i would like to draw their attention to our common task, the need for fair and in-depth communication with the public, both with the icelandic and the eu citizens. in the light of the above, i would like to point out again that there is still a lot to be done under the hungarian presidency. as for the presidency, we naturally expect all the member states, the commission and, of course, the european parliament to help iceland in this endeavour. it is essential to keep the momentum going and to make the most of the negotiations this semester. i am convinced that iceland's accession can be a success story. it can give impetus to the whole of enlargement policy and increase its success. the motto and goal of the hungarian presidency is a strong europe. any progress in iceland's accession process will contribute to this.
member of the commission. − mr president, today’s debate on iceland and the next steps in its accession process is very opportune. i would like to thank the house for its support for icelandic membership and to congratulate the rapporteur, mr preda, for his high quality report. the resolution under discussion is a helpful contribution to the process: it delivers the right messages to iceland at the right moment. the assessment of iceland’s compliance with the acquis – the screening exercise – is on track. since november 2010, 24 chapters have been discussed and 23 bilateral screening meetings have been completed, covering fisheries, agriculture, environment, regional policy and financial services. screening is an important technical process and the meetings have already identified sensitive issues and challenges in key chapters, such as agriculture, environment and fisheries. this stage of the negotiation process will be completed by june 2011. i can confirm that we expect actual negotiations to start towards the end of the hungarian presidency, with the opening of some chapters at the accession conference scheduled for 27 june 2011. this is an ambitious but european investment bank a rather unique institution. the first is that, contrary to what has been said by one of you, we do not use taxpayers' money. - to be clear, we do not ask the uk taxpayer for one single cent. we don't use taxpayers' money, we use resources that we take every day from financial markets around the world. and that's why it's essential that we retain the triple a rating. we borrow in asia and the united states, and with the resources thus collected, we can finance projects on good terms. the only budgetary impact is the guarantee given concerning the political risk for the implementation of the external mandate that the council and parliament give us. there is a guarantee which has a provisional cost to the european budget, since 9% of the total loans made on the basis of the external mandate are provisioned - provisioning is made two years after the first disbursement and, of course, this provision is reduced as the repayment proceeds. so, since we do not actually use the guarantee, the cost to the european budget is zero. i'm not going anywhere. so it is clear that we are not an institution that costs the taxpayer. secondly, we are the only financial institution which is truly european. the shareholders of which are all member states and only the member states of the european union. we are the only financial institution that is legally obliged, under the treaty, to financially support the political objectives of the european union. we are the only financial institution that can finance a project only if it has received the european commission's favourable opinion beforehand. and the european commission gives this opinion after an examination by all the departments, by all the directorates-general, of competition and the environment. we are therefore obliged to strictly apply european rules and policies. we are subject to the control of the court of auditors to the extent provided for in the tripartite agreement. we are in constant cooperation with olaf, and i would add that we are on the verge of accepting supervision by the new european banking supervisory authority. in any case, we in the european investment bank would be very happy to be officially subject to some form of banking supervision. we do this indirectly, in particular by involving people with experience in banking supervision in our audit committee. but i would like to confirm once again that we are quite open to proper supervision by this new european authority. and finally, the third feature i would like to stress in conclusion is in writing. − i believe that we must avoid making radical and immediate political decisions on the role of nuclear energy in the medium to long-term energy mix. it's important that we have a clear picture, based on accurate data, of what happened at the fukushima nuclear plant. we must not lose sight of the advantages of nuclear energy, which generates low carbon dioxide emissions, has relatively low costs and ensures energy independence. to date, nuclear energy has been statistically the safest with the lowest casualty rate in accidents compared to other energy sources (e.g. gas, oil). it is also essential to respect member states' decisions to determine the composition of their energy mix. the role of nuclear energy is important for the achievement of the union's objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy and the energy strategy for the current decade.
in writing. - i voted against the resolution on nuclear safety in europe which is being called for in the wake of the nuclear accident in japan. the reason for the vote against is the resolution's request to institute a moratorium on the development of new nuclear power plants. i believe that the production of nuclear energy under safe conditions is extremely important. i'm fine with the stress tests. i do not think it is appropriate to impose a moratorium on a period that cannot be determined in time. this period can be very important for power plants that are currently under development, especially in terms of financing. the structure of the energy mix is the responsibility of the member states and therefore i do not think that such a decision can be imposed at community level.
in writing. - i voted against the joint motion for a resolution on the conclusions on nuclear safety in europe following the nuclear accident in japan for the following reasons: at least seven of the amendments tabled are scientifically unrealistic; many parts of the text are mere slogans without any real basis, and those who are against nuclear energy do not even offer alternative solutions to its use. last but not least, i regret that the european parliament has not adopted a position on this subject, but such a position, if it is to be adopted, must be balanced, pragmatic, based on scientifically documented facts and realistic solutions.
in writing. − i voted for the european parliament resolution on the lessons to be learned on nuclear safety in europe following the nuclear accident in japan, because its objective is to increase nuclear safety in the eu, and not to ban the production and use of nuclear energy. that is why i voted against all the amendments which aimed to remove nuclear energy from the european energy mix. although i did not vote for a moratorium on the construction of new nuclear reactors, i considered that if such a moratorium were to be introduced, it should be limited to the period of 'stress tests' to which eu nuclear reactors will be subjected. the construction of new reactors would thus benefit from the findings of the stress tests and nuclear safety would increase. today, nuclear energy accounts for 30% of the european energy mix. the achievement of the european union's 20-20-20 target depends to a large extent on the energy mix of the member states. we cannot decide to phase out nuclear power without establishing sustainable sources of energy that can meet the eu's energy demand in the coming years at prices that are affordable to citizens. the eu needs to invest in energy efficiency measures, particularly in the buildings and transport sectors, and in the use of renewable energy.
in writing. − the nuclear crisis in japan set into motion a number of ideas that amount to an irrational tsunami. nuclear energy is now demonised and there is growing pressure demanding a complete switch from nuclear to so-called alternative sources of energy. but this school of thought is bordering on outright superstition. the nuclear reactor of fukushima was hit by an unprecedented combination of catastrophes. this proves that nature is unpredictable and that tsunamis cannot be banned, but it does not prove that nuclear energy is at fault. nuclear energy has a much safer record than any other source of energy. while oil arguably generates exploitation, dependence, wars and dictatorships, nuclear energy is historically much safer. our main concern with nuclear energy should indeed be risk assessment and unitary safety procedures at a european level. with these criteria fulfilled and observed, nuclear energy could put an end or severely limit the politics of energy dependence. and while natural disasters cannot be prevented, nuclear energy is not a serious risk per se. the real danger does not come from well serviced nuclear reactors, but from nuclear reactors under the wrong political control. in other words, look iran, not japan.
in writing. − i believe that the european union must now more than ever promote democratic values and stand with the peoples of the southern mediterranean countries in their aspiration to a democratic society. the situation in the arab countries reminds me of the fall of the communist regimes in central and eastern europe. we have been through similar times and we can understand the demands of these peoples, for which we have a moral duty to show solidarity. the protests that have been taking place in these countries for several weeks are clear evidence that undemocratic regimes do not meet the expectations of the population and that they cannot provide political stability and prosperity for these societies. the high representative and the commission should take a firm stand against the use of violence against protesters and pressure the authorities in syria, yemen and bahrain to engage in constructive political dialogue to resolve the situation. i also believe that the conclusion of the eu-syria association agreement should be conditional on the willingness of the syrian authorities to make democratic reforms. the union has this instrument at its disposal and i believe it should use it as much as possible to support the democratization of the arab countries.
in writing. − bahrain risks becoming the scene of a confrontation between iran and saudi arabia. in this context, we cannot overlook the religious component of developments in the area, as the shiite opposition is supported by iran and the sunni dynasty enjoys the support of the monarchies in the region. also, the close relations between iran, syria, hamas and hezbollah, as well as the religious tensions between sunnis and alawites in syria should urge us to be cautious, because there is a huge risk that the escalation of violence will push syria into a civil war, too, with foreign interference. the massacre of hama in 1982, in which 20,000 syrians were killed, is a tragic warning in this regard, as are the failures in somalia, afghanistan and iraq in terms of how the west must act in a space whose very pronounced particularities cannot be overlooked. i think we need more diplomacy and less armed force, more concern for the defense of human rights and the protection of civilians and less concern for the electoral potential of foreign intervention, and more attention to the poverty and corruption that these societies, especially the yemeni one, are facing.
in writing. − the situation in syria, bahrain and yemen is an unpredictable ongoing process and not a bloody but unstoppable march toward democracy. the political background in syria and yemen has been for a long time authoritarian or outright dictatorial. yet this is not making the opposition a fully democratic alternative. especially in yemen, a lawless, fragmented polity, the forces gathering under the opposition umbrella are hosting or could give way to terrorist or radical anti-democratic forces. in the past, ‘stability’ in the foreign policy for the middle east was a substitute for inaction or the status quo. it was certainly an overrated concept. now it could become underrated. the european and largely the democratic interest would be better served by a rational, non-emotional approach. the need for democracy in countries with a long record of political oppression should not become the undoing of future democratic process. this does not mean that the assad or saleh regimes should be propped up, but it means that the solution should be a negotiated exit strategy rather than a violent and uncontrolled regime change. caution and clear headed policies are much more appropriate in countries and regions that could turn from one system of oppression to another.
in writing. − having focused on principles in previous conferences, i express my hope that the fourth un conference will be results-oriented, formulating clear indicators to halve the number of least developed countries by 2020. of the 51 ldcs, where 78 percent of the population lives on less than $1.25 a day, only three have exceeded that threshold in recent years. the situation is worrying, as these countries are the most vulnerable to shocks such as financial and food crises, climate change, and also face extreme poverty, lack of infrastructure and rising unemployment. this shows that the international community has unfortunately not fulfilled the commitments made in the brussels action programme. i hope that at the conference, where i will be representing the socialist group, we will focus on policy coherence for development and ways of implementing innovative financing mechanisms to help these countries more effectively, which must be encouraged to implement appropriate policies.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the commission and council initiative to review the european neighbourhood policy - the eastern dimension. this policy has worked because of its flexibility and now needs to adapt to the new realities in the european region. this is why better adjustment to the specificities of each country included in the programme is needed. i believe that it is not the geographical location but the commitment of the partner countries that should play the most important role. but the people are at the heart of reforms in a state. the east and the south must have the same chances, and a rebalancing of the neighbourhood policy is needed. the former soviet states also need cooperation with the eu, something that joe biden also advocated during his recent visit to chisinau. i would like to point out that the republic of moldova is the leader of reforms in the eastern partnership.
in writing. − the commission's reports on the enp provide a picture of the real benefits of good neighbourliness policy, but also of the challenges. a review of the enp is needed and a different approach to how the union responds to the progress made by neighbouring countries in socio-economic reforms, by providing financial and political support and by adapting to the specific needs of each country. the eastern partnership provides a political framework for strengthening relations between the eu and its eastern neighbours and for pursuing socio-economic reforms in partner countries. an assessment of the progress made by each country is required by means of a benchmarking based on pre-established criteria, but not without taking into account the particularities of each country. a european perspective, including article 49 of the treaty, is a driving force behind reforms in these countries. parliament has an important role to play both in setting the evaluation criteria and in strengthening freedom and democracy in the neighbouring partner countries.
in writing. − i have always encouraged the eastern neighbourhood policy of the european union and this can be seen from my previous activities. i endorse the review of the european neighbourhood policy, mainly because it is needed to make a substantial contribution to ensuring that human rights and political principles are more strongly integrated into the analysis of the political situation in third countries. it underlines the positive developments concerning human rights and democratisation in some partner countries and some negative developments in others, particularly in belarus. i also found important the fact that it pays particular attention to the mobility of students, academics, researchers and businessmen by ensuring that sufficient resources are available and by strengthening existing scholarship programmes. for all these reasons i support the review of the european neighbourhood policy.
in writing. − the revision of the neighbourhood policy must continue to ensure that the specific problems faced by the regions on the european union's border are addressed. i believe that it takes significant administrative capacity to be able to manage such a diverse range of issues. in addition to demographic challenges, climate change, economic competitiveness and quality of life, regions bordering non-member states face a number of consequences of poorly managed problems. this is the case with how natural disasters are managed, for example. emergency response is extremely difficult if neighbours do not have the capacity to respond and the region itself cannot respond to the whole situation. i have therefore proposed that eu border regions which border at least 2 non-eu countries should be considered platform regions and supported accordingly. neighbourhood policy needs to take into account the capacity of regions within the eu but with external borders to deal with problems that are much more complex, and financial support needs to be tailored.

positive development is immediately crushed by outbursts of political repression and violence. this is exactly what happened again just a couple of months ago. the european union therefore had to proceed to renew its restrictive measures, for the eighth time, in february this year. by this clear gesture, we wanted to underline the critical importance of an agreement between the government parties on the necessary steps leading to elections in the country. in this context, the eu emphasised its willingness to revise its decision in response to further concrete developments on the ground. the eu is deeply concerned at the upsurge in political violence seen in recent months in zimbabwe. on 11 march, together with 21 embassies and representations, the eu issued a statement to express its concerns over the increase in what appears to be politically-motivated intimidation and violence. in this context, the eu welcomes the outcome of the recent sadc summit on 31 march 2011. the sadc communiqué calls for an immediate end to violence, intimidation, hate speech and harassment and calls upon the government of zimbabwe to complete all necessary steps to hold an election. it offers assistance so that elections can be organised in accordance with sadc principles and guidelines governing democratic elections. for that reason, the sadc will appoint officials to join the south african facilitation team and work with the joint monitoring and implementation committee. the eu believes that strengthened facilitation and mediation efforts by sadc and south africa are key to preventing further instability in zimbabwe. the eu welcomes the region’s efforts to mediate in the zimbabwean crisis. south africa, in its capacity as facilitator, together with the sadc, as guarantor of the global political agreement, has decided to accredit the zimbabwean ambassador. at this point in time, keeping a formal channel of communication open with zimbabwe and maintaining a dialogue with the inclusive government is vital, and we should not jeopardise the position of the eu ambassador in harare. the eu will act and proceed in close coordination with all eu member states. the eu remains the largest provider of development assistance to zimbabwe. we want to clearly express that we are tough on the regime, but we try to assist the people. with the disbursement of approximately 365 million since the establishment of the global political agreement in 2009, we are – as i said – the largest donor. resources are only channelled through un bodies and specialised ngos. since 2009, the eu has also supported governance reforms, as stipulated in the global political agreement, including the constitutional reform process. the eu also funds human rights programmes, including programmes from human rights defenders. we just have to hope that all the international pressure will finally lead to free and fair elections in zimbabwe and to the gradual normalisation of the very difficult situation in this country.

we have to be aware that oil prices will remain high and that we will never go back to the $30 to $40 a barrel. the era of cheap oil is over. for 2011, at least, the average will still be $80 to $100 a barrel. under these circumstances, the negative impact on the economy is expected to continue. in the fisheries sector, new measures are needed, especially as european fishermen face strong international competition. in many regions, fishing is the only viable economic activity and is important for maintaining employment. as we have seen, high oil prices are still to be expected, and this economic situation primarily affects those involved in small-scale fishing. an important question in this context is: what is the future of the common fisheries policy and what is the future of the european fisheries fund? if this fund is underused, it means that it needs to be analysed and reformed.
the decision discussed today establishes the first european programme for radio spectrum policy. this appropriation is intended to cover the financing of the purchase, hire, maintenance and repair of equipment and installations necessary for the operation of the european space station and the related technical equipment, including the replacement of equipment and installations, and the replacement of equipment and installations for the maintenance of the space station and the replacement of equipment and installations for the maintenance of the space station. in practice, the programme will facilitate ensuring availability and maximising flexibility of spectrum, increasing efficiency of spectrum use through general authorisations, avoiding distortion of competition and harmful interference and disturbance, harmonising technical conditions and ensuring health protection. according to the decision, the commission together with the member states will carry out an inventory of existing spectrum uses and possible future spectrum needs in the union, in particular in the 300 mhz-3 ghz band. in the amendments tabled, we called for the digital divide to be closed so that all union citizens have access to broadband communications infrastructure of at least 30mbps by 2020 and for opportunities to be guaranteed for both the commercial sector and public services through increased broadband capacity. i also called for new equipment and technologies to be accessible to consumers so that the shift to digital technology and the effective use of the digital dividend is supported by consumers. i welcome the importance attached to ensuring the availability of the radio spectrum needed for monitoring the atmosphere and the earth's surface, enabling the development and exploitation of space applications, and the improvement of transport systems, in particular for the galileo system, the gms system and intelligent transport safety and management systems.
vice-president of the commission. − madam president, today we are discussing a legislative proposal for emergency autonomous trade preferences for pakistan. this proposal was tabled by the commission at the express request of the european council in the immediate aftermath of the floods that hit pakistan in the summer of last year and brought widespread devastation to the country and to its people. i would like to thank the rapporteur and the committee on international trade for their hard work and their support for the proposal. the commission proposal aims at the introduction of a unilateral and temporary suspension of import duties on 75 export items from pakistan. these trade preferences would liberalise about a quarter of pakistani imports to the eu and be available for two years, with a possible extension for another year. the european union is aware that such trade concessions, especially in sensitive sectors such as textiles, might have an impact on eu industry, and therefore we have ensured that a balance is kept between the needs of pakistan and the interests of our own industry and other supplier countries. the number of products selected is limited. we have set a ceiling on the liberalisation of very sensitive items, and liberalisation would only be of limited duration. in the meantime we have also requested the world trade organisation to grant us a waiver of the applicable wto rules to enable us to implement the proposed measures. as you know, we are still discussing this issue with other wto members and hope to come to a solution soon. the images of people having lost their livelihoods might not be present any more in everyone’s mind, but we should not forget the immense cost of those devastating floods, both in terms of humanitarian needs and economic devastation. these trade measures are not ‘stand-alone’, and come on top of the significant humanitarian and development assistance – amounting to eur 480 million – that the eu has granted to pakistan. however, ambitious trade measures are essential for the sustained economic recovery of pakistan’s economy and should be part of our medium-term response to those unprecedented natural disasters. i therefore hope that parliament will support the proposal. let me now turn to some of the amendments that have been proposed. i will not go into detail on all of them, but let me highlight the most important ones. i know that there are requests for making the granting of autonomous trade preferences conditional upon pakistan respecting certain fundamental principles. i understand the concerns that may exist in that respect, and you are aware that human rights issues are an integral element of our long-term relationship with pakistan. however, given the temporary nature of the waiver to address an emergency situation, the commission believes those conditionalities would not be appropriate. our human rights dialogue, in the context of our partnership and cooperation agreement with pakistan, is the appropriate forum to address such issues with pakistan and reach sustainable solutions. as regards provisions that would oblige pakistan to abstain from maintaining, introducing or increasing duties or charges having equivalent effect, or any other restriction on the export or import of certain products, i believe that such conditions would seriously undermine the granting of the preferences and are contrary to the spirit, the nature and the purpose of our regulation. moreover, we cannot prohibit pakistan, through this regulation, from implementing measures that are consistent with its international obligations. on the other hand, we could agree to the introduction of a mechanism allowing the imposition of limits to duty-free imports for pakistan tariff rate quotas where volumes of imports of products liberalised increase beyond certain levels. i also agree that preferences should be removed for any product causing or threatening to cause serious difficulties to a union producer of like or directly competing products, as determined by an investigation carried out by the commission. we could also agree with mechanisms to establish customs surveillance on imports covered by the regulation, linked with quarterly reporting. however, a prior surveillance mechanism would create an undue burden in terms of administrations’ licensing requirements. i note, finally, that there are requests to limit the duration of the trade preferences to one year from the date on which the waiver takes effect. i think that would be very problematic. the commission initially proposed applying exceptional measures for a period of three years. in its compromise proposal, which was reflected in the wto waiver request, the council limited the duration to two years, with the possibility of extending it by one more year. however, to limit the duration even further to one year would erode the advantages of the autonomous trade preferences measure, and they would become meaningless. let me also point out that a compromise reached in the council on 10 november was based on subjecting seven textile and clothing products to tariff rate quotas rather than full liberalisation. this compromise became the basis for the subsequent request for a wto waiver. however this is not reflected in the european parliament amendments, and as a result of the consultation with wto members it might be necessary to subject a few more products to tariff rate quotas. the waiver, if granted, would constitute a maximum of preferences the eu could grant to pakistan on those terms and, as a consequence, the regulation will have to reflect the content of the wto waiver once it is agreed in the wto. let me also reassure you that the commission will conduct an annual impact assessment on the autonomous trade preferences granted to pakistan and present it to parliament and the council, and that is another reason not to reduce the duration of application of this instrument. i thank the european parliament for its cooperation on this sensitive issue. the commission stands ready to work closely with parliament in order to have this proposal adopted and show the eu’s determination to act responsibly towards countries in need.
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on foreign affairs. - i think it's appropriate that we discuss this moreira report. why would you do that? because we are currently waiting for a decision on the derogation requested by the european union to the world trade organization on the very subject under discussion. for my part, i think it is important in this context to send a clear message to the other trading partners of the union: the union must remain committed to complementing the generous emergency humanitarian aid it has initially provided to pakistan with trade measures aimed at a sustainable economic recovery. the diplomatic consultations at the world trade organisation certainly require time, because the concerns of the union's trading partners must be taken into account. the outcome of these consultations is currently uncertain, but as recent events have reminded us, what is clear is that we need a stable and prosperous pakistan that does not slide into extremism and that can be a partner in the fight against terrorism. as an opinion rapporteur in afet, i would like to thank my colleagues in inta for taking up the main elements that i developed in the opinion. i shall stress two such elements here. the first, and perhaps the most important for the afet commission, was the need not to decouple conditionality linked to respect for human rights, including basic labour law standards, from the granting of trade preferences. i think we have a difference of opinion here. as human rights are an essential element of the agreement linking the union to pakistan, the proposed autonomous trade preferences must be conditional on respect for human rights in that country. on the other hand, a full impact assessment of the proposed measures was not carried out in advance by the commission. i think it would have been important, in particular, the effect on the population of pakistan and the effect on the budgetary resources of that country.
as some of our colleagues have said, you have noticed that they argue that granting special trade preferences to pakistan would not be a suitable solution to help the flood victims, because they do not consider trade to be a suitable tool to respond to such emergencies. i agree, trade preferences may not directly help the people who suffered from the floods, but by complementing humanitarian aid measures, we can help pakistan's economic recovery. and international trade and humanitarian aid are not two completely opposite fields. there is virtually complementarity between all the policies of the european union, and when we give trade preferences to developing countries, we do not do so for purely pragmatic, commercial reasons, but to show solidarity with these countries.
the free trade agreement with india will become the most important agreement of its kind if the negotiations are concluded in a satisfactory manner for both sides. the european union is india's largest trading partner, and the gsp is one of the eu's instruments for promoting india's economic development. although india has an emerging economy, social inequalities persist. more than 800 million people live on less than two dollars a day. india's efforts to build a strong economy must be matched by the political will to improve the human rights, social and environmental situation. the european commission must therefore advocate in the negotiations for the introduction of legally binding clauses in these areas. india can be not only an economic example for the rest of the developing world, but also a model of democratization.
india is a country on the rise, with enviable economic growth and one of our most important trading partners. the free trade agreement with india is extremely important for the future of our trade relations, which is why i am in favour of concluding this agreement as soon as possible. an important aspect is the liberalisation of services, especially in modes 3 and 4. services are particularly important for economic growth, both in india and in the european union, and this needs to be reflected in the free trade agreement. as regards module 4, the problems of recognition of professional qualifications need to be solved, which is, however, a rather difficult matter, given that we have problems of mutual recognition of professional qualifications even between the member states of the european union. i would ask the commission to tell us what the state of play is on this subject. the second aspect is related to reciprocity in access to public procurement markets. access for european companies to the public procurement markets in india can help our businesses develop. and there is a need for india to develop and implement transparent and clear rules on public procurement and to allow european companies access to it.
as a member of the eu-india delegation, i am in favour of a free trade agreement between the eu and india. india is an important developing country and an important trading partner of the european union. however, it is important to know in detail what the content of this agreement will be. i would remind you that the european parliament will ratify this agreement and we therefore ask to be kept informed of the state of the negotiations. i would like to ask the commission how this agreement will reflect both the future industrial policy of the european union and the industrial policy of india? particular attention should be paid to the respect and protection of intellectual property rights and patents. last but not least, i would like to know whether this agreement will ensure a convergence of the positions of the european union and india on the fight against climate change and the reduction of polluting emissions.
the european union and japan account for 35% of the world's gdp. i believe that a free trade agreement between these two economic powers could bring benefits to both, but it first needs to remove the underlying difficulties and, in practice, prepare the way for a truly mutually beneficial agreement. the japanese market is currently subject to barriers, as my colleagues have said, non-tariff barriers which restrict access to imports, affecting trade and investment as a whole. in the negotiations led by the european commission, it should seek to promote a more transparent regulatory policy, which would enable european companies to fully understand the rules for doing business with japanese partners, as well as liberalizing access to public procurement. finally, i believe that an impact study should be carried out to analyse the effects of a possible agreement, particularly in the area of vulnerable european industries such as the automotive, electronics and aerospace industries.
since 2009, trade policy has become an exclusive competence of the european union, and for foreign investment policy, for a significant part of it, we now need to find a common denominator. there will thus be a transitional period during which the competences relating to bilateral investment agreements between member states and third countries will be transferred to the european level. in this context, i consider that the adoption of a community-type procedure for the verification and review of bilateral investment agreements is preferable to an intergovernmental formality. the role of bringing the changes to fruition must be that of the european commission, not the member states, in order to ensure that the common interest is protected. the european executive must therefore guarantee both legal certainty for investors who will be affected by the transitional process and equivalent investment conditions for companies from all eu member states.
the investment policy of the member states must be harmonised at european level as part of the common commercial policy. member states should ensure that bilateral investment treaties are compatible with union development policies. the commission must gradually replace existing agreements with new ones that provide an optimal system of investment protection. due to the risky nature of foreign direct investments, it is necessary to ensure a high level of legal certainty during the transition period. in this respect, i welcome the commission's and the rapporteur's approach based on coexistence. it is essential that bilateral treaties remain in force and that member states are able to conclude or open new negotiations. finally, i support the establishment of a timetable with a deadline for the transition from the bilateral treaties of the member states to the eu's international treaties.

in writing. − illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing is one of the main threats to the resources of the fisheries market, where the european union is a major player internationally. the development of a common european fisheries policy to protect the sustainable exploitation of living aquatic resources is therefore a natural concern. the agreement proposed for adoption by the council is designed to meet this international requirement to prevent, deter and eliminate illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing by means of effective measures by the port state. measures which, upon adoption of the agreement, should evolve from an optional model to a package of mandatory minimum standards for port states for the monitoring, control and inspection of foreign flagged fishing vessels using ports. the fact that the set of measures, the implementation of which falls under the responsibility of the port states, is, however, developed by an international instrument is a plus. the global view of the phenomenon of iuu fishing can lead to better monitoring of fishing activities at the level of the whole and is more cost-effective in terms of organisation and implementation.

in writing. − this report is important in the context of the expansion of the single market for crossborder lending. it is currently partially blocked because of the reluctance of creditors in one member state to grant loans to debtors resident in another member state. a concrete example is where a resident of one member state wants to take out a mortgage loan from a bank resident in another member state. this is currently not possible, which in effect results in the non-existence of a consumer's right to buy products (banking, in this case) in any eu member state. the reason why a bank only grants mortgage loans to residents of the same country (even if the bank - a multinational bank - has a presence in several member states, in the form of subsidiaries or branches) is that, in the event of default, the bank is obliged to follow a forced execution procedure according to the lex rei sitae (the law of the country where the property on which the mortgage was established by the lending bank is located) and not the law of the country where the creditor is established. if a 28th regime were to be established, according to this report, this would facilitate cross-border credit-based transactions.
in writing. − in the eu, many companies do business within the internal market and european citizens enjoy the right to settle, work and travel freely within the eu. as i also stressed when we discussed the single market act, in order to deepen the internal market and promote crossborder transactions, including electronic commerce, we need guarantees for the recovery of any crossborder debts. i fully support the idea in this report of asking the commission to propose more effective enforcement instruments to complement those already in place for crossborder claims, such as the brussels i regulation or the procedure for small claims. the courts should have the tools to act quickly to freeze the assets of the debtor or alleged debtor, but not under all circumstances. we have to strike a balance between protecting creditors and protecting debtors' rights, to avoid arbitrariness. the possibility of obtaining an aeo without prior notification and hearing of the interested party is an infringement of the debtor's rights and is contrary to the current case-law of the cjeu. the report therefore fails to strike the necessary balance, and better protection of debtors' rights is needed.

in writing. − making the allocation of radio spectrum in the eu more efficient is a prerequisite for keeping pace with other developed countries in moving towards the digital society. the elements of this report are also fully consistent with the eu digital agenda. both consumers and businesses in the eu are increasingly using broadband and mobile internet via smartphones or tablets, which requires fast connections. this implies the release of the 800 mhz band for mobile broadband internet services as soon as possible and even the band below 790 mhz if it proves necessary to cope with the growth of data traffic. the measures envisaged in the first radio spectrum policy programme are indispensable to reduce the digital divide and provide fast and reliable telecommunications services in rural and remote areas with a view to revitalising them. last but not least, they support innovation and the wider use of new technologies, which is absolutely necessary for the competitiveness of the european economy, as was also underlined in the single market act.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the radio spectrum report today. it will ultimately create employment in this sector, aid the completion of the digital agenda and lend itself to achieving wireless frequency targets by 2013. in romania, we have one of the fastest internet speeds in europe. by enhancing european broadband, this will increase our competitiveness. it is noteworthy that the international telecommunications union argues that capacity has to be opened up and preferably harmonised at a global level. we all use radio spectrum in our daily lives for listening to radio programmes, for using our mobile telephones, for remotely locking our cars and for using satellite navigation systems. this report will aim to coordinate the eu approach for the management of spectrum across the union. it is important that member states continue to engage in bilateral communications and negotiations with third countries in order to achieve their union frequency targets.
in writing. − the creation of a common transparency register is undoubtedly an important step forward, which european citizens have been waiting for. the european institutions, whether elected or not, take decisions that affect the daily lives of citizens, and in a democratic system, which the eu is striving towards, it is quite normal for there to be a high degree of transparency in the decision-making process. this common transparency register also simplifies things for lobbyists, as there will be one single registration instead of two as at present. on the other hand, it is very true that this register will not be a sufficient tool to solve the problem of corruption. i do not think that its primary purpose is exclusively to fight corruption, since cases of corruption have been very rare.
in writing. − the establishment of a common transparency register, as well as the improvement of all transparency-related rules in the european parliament, are necessary to increase citizens' confidence in parliamentary activities and to ensure the necessary transparency of these activities. i voted in favour of both casini reports and i am awaiting the strongest possible proposals from the working group on transparency and the regulation of lobbying in the ep.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr fox's report. as the shadow rapporteur of the epp group, i would point out that the very good result of the final vote once again demonstrates the close cooperation between the political groups. we have thus succeeded in preventing the european parliament from taking an excessively binding stance on corporate governance rules. it is very important that our group promote a balanced approach in solving the global financial crisis. that is why we must avoid introducing barriers to financial institutions. the final report gives greater importance and empowerment to the role of the european supervisory authorities. the most important compromise concerns the equality between the principle of 'compliance or otherwise justification' and the mandatory rules. i think that the introduction of rules should only be done when codes of good practice fail. the 'compliance or otherwise justification' approach is proportionate and can be applied to a large number of financial institutions. at the same time, however, it must be complemented by regular external evaluations and adequate regulatory oversight.
in writing. − the financial crisis has highlighted the ineffectiveness of current corporate governance principles and it is now essential to learn from the past to avoid a repeat of a similar situation in the future. the area of corporate governance is constantly evolving and the financial sector has a particular responsibility for sustainable and sound strategies in the economic environment. it is necessary to maintain the sound, stable and competitive character of financial institutions so that they can contribute to economic growth. in this respect, i consider that effective corporate governance must take account in a fair way of the interests of all parties involved and, at the same time, of the stability of the financial system. this will ensure the smooth functioning of the internal market and increase consumer confidence in financial institutions and transactions.
