in writing. − forests are the main carbon store and play a key role in combating climate change. 42% of the european union's land area is covered by forests and woodlands. forests form carbon-storing biospheres and are particularly important for environmental conservation and protection against natural disasters. all these elements are essential for the quality of life of european citizens, but also for agriculture and rural development. i would like to stress that sustainable forest management is a key component in achieving the european union's climate objectives and in capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. the forest industries also provide two million jobs, contributing to economic growth, to employment. i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is essential that the european union reinforces its strategy to improve the sustainable management and conservation of the forestry sector.
in writing. − the forest action plan adopted in 2006 set four important objectives, which, however, were not given equal attention, as intermediate evaluations of its implementation have shown. the main shortcomings are in enhancing protection and conservation of biodiversity and show that 66% of forest habitats are in a poor state. in practice, the findings show that while attention has been paid to improving long-term competitiveness, the objectives of improving the environment, contributing to improving the quality of life and promoting coordination and communication have been rather poorly implemented. forests provide livelihoods for millions of workers, entrepreneurs and 16 million forest owners. the eu's forest industries provide over 2 million jobs, mostly in smes, and have a turnover of €300 billion. forest management, in turn, employs more than 350,000 people. from these perspectives, it is important to pursue the objectives set out in the forestry strategies. this, combined with climate change, is reason enough to mobilise all eu member states and make equal and united efforts to manage the union's forests. this must be coupled with the adaptation of energy, industry, trade, research and cohesion policies, including regional policy and the solidarity fund.
in writing. − the economic, social and environmental importance of forests in the international, european, regional and national context is generally well known and is partly legitimised in relevant international agreements and cooperation and funding programmes. climate change is having a very big impact on forests in all regions of europe, but with different intensities. a reform of the eu's approach to forest policies must not be limited to the challenges of climate change, but must take into account all aspects of the contribution of forests to sustainable development at regional, european and international level. another aspect is the support instruments and schemes for the forestry sector at union level, and these are far below those applicable to other sectors of activity and the current and prospective contribution of forests to the achievement of the sustainable development goals. however, a reform of the eu's approach to forest policies must not be limited to the challenges of climate change, but must take into account all aspects of the contribution of forests to sustainable development (environment, rural economies, etc.) at regional, european and international levels.
in writing. − due to the important contribution of forests to solving the climate crisis, sustainable forest management is of major importance for the eu to achieve its climate goals. the eu needs to strengthen its strategy to tackle the factors that cause forest degradation, such as uncontrolled deforestation, fires and air pollution. at the same time, ensuring biodiversity, protection against natural disasters and capture of co2 from the atmosphere are vital to improving the quality of life of our citizens and preserving the environment. i therefore believe that the protection of forests in the eu must aim at providing a guarantee that forests will continue to fulfil all their productive, socio-economic and ecological functions in the future.
in writing. - i voted against part of paragraph 36 because the provision is at least unrealistic. i don't think we should ban building on forest land that has been affected by fires, because some of that land is effectively unusable for other purposes. i do not think we should present some cases of abuse as a general rule and affect the property rights of forest owners who have already been affected by a forest fire. however, the idea in paragraph 37 is acceptable, which proposes the introduction of a ban in the event of a proven arson. but in this case, i think we can face the negative consequences that would result: the arsonist does not have to be the owner of the property and i do not see why the latter should be punished.
in writing. − forests provide us with many essential eco-services, ranging from regulating the water cycle to preventing soil erosion and sequestering carbon. the environmental and economic benefits of forests require that they be afforded urgent, continuing and long-term protection, and this is especially important in the context of climate change, in terms of both mitigation and adaptation. this report covers a wide range of issues and is the result of much hard work and fruitful negotiation involving all the main political groups. i sincerely hope the commission and the member states will act on its constructive suggestions.
in writing. − in a time of economic and financial crisis, the european union is called upon to strengthen its strategic autonomy to uphold its values and protect its citizens by developing a common vision of the main challenges and threats and by aligning its resources and capabilities to provide an adequate response. i consider that the new provisions on the common security and defence policy introduced by the treaty of lisbon represent a firm political expression of the union's intention to act as a stabilising force in the world and provide a clear legal framework for strengthening its capacity to pursue its foreign and security policy, through a comprehensive approach based on all the instruments at the disposal of the union and the member states, to prevent and manage crises and conflicts and to build lasting peace. i voted in favour of this report. i believe that the european union needs a strong and effective security and defence policy to prevent conflicts, to protect the security of its citizens, to assert its fundamental values, to contribute to the support of international law, to the promotion of respect for human rights and democratic values throughout the world.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it represents an important step towards implementing the lisbon treaty. the changes proposed in this document will improve the flexibility of european military capabilities. i would remind you that the diversification of global threats requires an adaptation of the common security and defence policy. cyberattacks, illegal immigration, and terrorism are just some of these. and the union has become a preferred target of international crime. i would also like to stress the importance of the financial resources that support this policy. i believe that the revision of the athena mechanism by the polish presidency will clarify the budgetary issue. this will make it easier to determine the member states' contribution to the common costs of european military operations. the dissolution of the western european union and the introduction of the mutual defence clause in the treaty marked a development in the common defence policy.
in writing. − i voted in support of our common foreign and security policy report, with the hope that such a policy would take shape at last. up to now our common foreign and security policy is a collection of disagreements and misguided initiatives. the recent euro-row over action in libya and the subsequent german opt-out made it clear to the rest of the world that the eu is still not able to project a real common foreign and security policy. moreover, the french initiative aiming at consolidating the financing of the southern neighbourhood at the expense of the eastern neighbourhood sent a disastrous message to our eastern partners. this is even more sensitive at a time when other quintessential european projects are in doubt, if not in crisis. the euro is under constant pressure and the problem is, in part, generated by the same lack of european ambition and coherence. the schengen area is rolled back on a daily basis and national barriers re-emerge as the european spirit and legislation are ignored or broken by fellow member states. a non-existent common foreign and security policy assisted by a huge external action service would seriously undermine european credibility in the world.
in writing. − the lisbon treaty strengthens the eu's capacity to join various international organisations, giving it a wider range of powers in the field of external action and giving it the opportunity to adopt a single, clearer and stronger position globally. the treaty also encourages cooperation with relevant international and regional organisations and groups of states and enables the union to become an effective global player. the eu's commitment to effective multilateralism is the guiding principle of european external action. i believe that the european union, based on its internal experience of cooperation between nations and institutions, has a global responsibility which it should continue to uphold. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mrs maría muñiz de urquiza because the union's presence in multilateral organisations is one of the main directions of its external policy. today, the eu has a legal personality, which gives it greater visibility on the world stage. moreover, the union has become by treaty a full participant in international politics. the lisbon treaty has improved instruments for external action, particularly in the un. in this connection, i would like to draw attention to article 12 of the report - the first step towards coordinated and effective action by the member states in the security council. i would like to stress that the un is currently in the process of reforming its structures, which also allows for a reorganisation of the eu's representation in this area.
in writing. − the eu's mechanisms for reaching consensus and taking concerted action make it a model for a rules-based international order. the eu must therefore cooperate with the major regional powers and actively participate in building and improving an international environment that allows it to promote its values and interests. the timing is all the more opportune given the sharp increase in the number of political and humanitarian crises worldwide, which means that the european union must make use of its foreign policy instruments to better exert its influence in international organisations and effectively take a leading role in resolving current and future international crises. on the other hand, globalisation processes also present a wide range of opportunities, challenges and threats to global governance, revealing social gaps and failures, including in the areas of financial markets, energy security, poverty reduction, climate change policy and human rights violations. and the eu must strengthen its role as a global actor and be a global decision-maker.
in writing. −the european union's commitment to effective multilateralism is of paramount importance. the union should take into account the enhanced representation of itself and of its member states in multilateral organisations. the rapid increase in the number of political and humanitarian crises today is worrying, indicating the need for such a strategy to be implemented in the eu. the union is not yet adequately fulfilling its role as a global actor and i consider that the strengthening and increasing importance of its role in multilateral organisations is real progress in stabilising its importance in the world.

general population. improving the business environment and access to finance, as well as facilitating smes' access to structural funds, will encourage the development of entrepreneurship. smes need legal and fiscal stability. repeated changes in tax legislation or in the conditions for access to different types of funds make their work more difficult. also, especially in times of crisis, smes are affected by the delay in paying their bills by public institutions. all of this affects smes' forecasts of the realisation of their business plans, their activity and, above all, their capacity to innovate. in the period 2006-2008, smes were able to obtain only 33% of the total value of public procurement contracts. given that public procurement represents 17% of the european union's gdp, we believe that the participation of smes in the public procurement market needs to increase. we therefore call on the commission and the member states to take the necessary measures to ensure that by 2015 at least 50% of public procurement is carried out by electronic means, as the member states' governments committed themselves to in manchester in 2005. i would point out that the single market in services is not yet operational and this is having a negative impact on the activities of smes in the european union. in 2008, the commission presented, as part of the european economic recovery plan, the programme in which the european investment bank participates with an overall package of €30 billion for loans to smes. the eib was to add €1 billion per year to its lending to medium-sized companies. i would like to ask the commission what the state of implementation of this programme is, whether it is considering supplementary funding and whether this funding is being distributed to improve the regulatory environment that is favourable to the needs of smes, the small business act needs to be aligned with the priorities of the europe 2020 strategy. the full and rapid implementation of the actions presented is therefore required, in particular the 'think small first' principle. i believe that special attention should be paid to large-scale financing of innovative companies. according to the commission's assessment, romania is an example of good practice in applying the principle of 'promoting entrepreneurship through the start business programme'. the programme has a budget of eur 21.2 million and aims to develop management skills among young people. we have also made progress in implementing the principle of 'access to finance for smes'. the government supports the creation and development of at least 1100 youth smes.
i start by welcoming the european commission's proposals for a revision of the small business act for europe. in fact, in its communication of 23 february 2011, the european commission notes the far-reaching progress that has been made since the adoption of the 'small business act' in june 2008, but draws attention to the remaining challenges. smes thus continue to face problems in expanding their activities, improving their capacity to innovate, accessing markets, obtaining financing and facing excessive bureaucracy. in many cases, when transposing directives into national law, the bureaucratic requirements set by the european union are practically exceeded. in order to ensure greater transparency, each member state should draw up comparative tables between bureaucratic measures at national level and those required by european directives. an assessment of the impact that new european legislative proposals could have on smes is also needed.

member of the commission. − mr president, i will focus on one issue only because i need my five minutes for that. in recent weeks, and today in this house, many voices have spoken in favour of debt restructuring in greece. it sounds very easy and neat. however, i must say that the proponents of sovereign debt restructuring seem to ignore the potentially devastating implications for financial stability in the country itself and in the euro area as a whole, and the consequences and ramifications for economic growth and employment. let us think about what the consequences of debt restructuring could be. of course, we are talking about a counterfactual situation, as are the proponents of debt restructuring, but we have enough understanding of the channels of impact on financial stability and economic activity to make a likely and most possible scenario. this is how it could very likely turn out. bondholders would take a big hit – i.e. households through their savings instruments like pension savings, as well as institutional investors such as pension funds and insurance companies. banks would also bear the cost. from last year’s bank stress-test exercise, we know that the greek banks hold eur 48 billion of government securities, greek government bonds. what would happen? a restructuring of sovereign securities would seriously erode their capital base. for instance, even a 30% haircut would mean that a large part of the banking system would end up under-capitalised, while a 50% haircut, which many have advocated, would imply that a large part of the greek banking system would simply become insolvent. thus, a debt restructuring in greece would have major consequences on the soundness of the banking sector in greece, as well as on any banks having exposure to greek securities. now, i do not love banks, nor do i do my job in the first place in order to save them, but it is a fact that such a major banking crisis would lead to a massive credit crunch. it is not a kind of theoretical virtuality. it is a very likely result. a massive credit crunch. moreover, through rating actions, the collateral pool at the disposal of the greek banks would most likely be wiped out. it would melt down. a massive credit crunch, possible bank runs, a deposit freeze and/or capital controls could well be part of the consequences. what is absolutely sure is that the contraction of the economy would be unprecedented in greece. let me recall that argentinian gdp collapsed by almost half over five years. would that help greece or europe? i doubt it. even such a severe haircut as 50% would not reduce the debt ratio below 100% of gdp, assuming that the international creditors like the euro area member states or the imf were excluded from this haircut. greece still has a large fiscal deficit which it has to finance. who would be ready to lend to greece the morning after it wiped out 70% or 50% or 30% of previous investors’ financial wealth? who would be ready to lend to greece the morning after? debt restructuring would cut greece’s access to financial markets for a very long time, and the goal of the eu/imf programme is indeed a relatively rapid return to the markets to finance the greek sovereign debt so that european taxpayers do not have to guarantee loans to do that. that is the goal of this exercise. let us recall that in the final analysis fiscal solvency requires stabilising and then reducing the government debt ratio – i.e. achieving a primary structural surplus and achieving a debt-stabilising level. greece is still living beyond its means, and the key is that greece has to start earning more than it consumes and also be able to pay the interest rates on its debt burden. that is the primary structural surplus that greece needs, and debt restructuring would not solve this very fundamental fact. therefore, at the end of the day, the main determinants over the solvency of greece are of a political and social nature – the consistent rigour to keep the primary surplus stable at a high level of around 5% of gdp for a long period of time. we have examples of this. belgium successfully did so in the 1990s for almost a decade. moreover, six eu member states have been able to maintain a primary surplus of over 4% for at least four years, so it is not impossible. it is certainly very challenging, but it has been done before and it is doable also for greece if there is the political will and unity in the country. this is the only way for greece to avoid much worse alternatives. we really are at a critical juncture concerning the future of europe. this debate is about the sovereign debt crisis. it has implications for the euro, for the future of europe. you know this very well. i must say that i am extremely concerned about the divergence in the national political debates we have heard recently, which have also been reflected in this house. there is political fatigue in central and northern europe about supporting the countries in trouble; there is reform fatigue in southern europe about carrying out the necessary reforms. we need to find the energy together to beat this fatigue. we need to build bridges over these divergences in order to save europe, and we need to make the necessary decisions to avoid another, even worse crisis and to enable the whole of europe to recover from this extremely serious financial crisis that we have experienced in the last years.

research and innovation are currently the preserve of the most developed member states, and this is detrimental to the union. the european union must take this into account and promote the balancing of innovation potential across its territory. it is necessary to support the new member states in developing their research infrastructure by allocating additional resources, as commissioner quinn promised not so long ago. only in this way can we be sure that the gap between the east and the west of the european union in terms of research and innovation will not be widened and that the goal of creating a real innovation union will be achieved. the idea of using the structural or agricultural funds to finance innovation and research is being floated. i believe that this is neither feasible nor fair. the realistic solution is to create specific tools that are dedicated solely to research and innovation.
meeting the europe 2020 strategy target of increasing investment in r&d to 3% of gdp could lead to the creation of 3.7 million jobs and an increase in annual gdp of up to eur 795 billion by 2025. but to do that, we will need an extra million researchers, as many of them are currently attracted to non-european countries where there are mechanisms to remove the bottlenecks that keep ideas from reaching the market. fragmentation of research systems and markets, under-use of public procurement to stimulate innovation, funding insecurity and the slow process of standardisation are issues that eu countries are still facing but which we hope will be taken seriously if we want the 'innovation union' programme to be one of the successes of the 'europe 2020' strategy. only then will we be able to achieve sustainable growth in europe and withstand the increasing pressure of globalisation.

romania's accession to the schengen area is a project that has involved major efforts from the financial, institutional and human point of view and represents one of the most important political objectives for romania. romania has invested over eur 1 billion and the results have been clearly positive in all evaluation reports. all the conditions imposed by the schengen acquis have been fulfilled. romania administers one of the longest external borders in the union and has therefore developed the most modern integrated security system to the standards required by the schengen acquis. romania and frontex have intensified their partnership relations. romania is the second largest contributor of equipment and human resources to frontex operations in greece, after germany. in the event of a massive influx of migrants at the border, specialised immigration and asylum mechanisms have been implemented in partnership with similar institutions in other member states, germany and the netherlands. the fight against illegal trafficking uses all modern methods of investigation and intelligence gathering. a single application has been developed in europe which allows data to be processed in both sis i and sis ii. the maritime border surveillance system was given as an example of good practice. in parallel, the authorities have given special attention to the fight against corruption. the permanent collaboration within the special mechanism set up by the european commission has led to results that prove that romania has the necessary institutional capacity and political will to achieve its justice objectives. i believe that accession to the schengen area is not a gift to romania, but a recognition of its merits and efforts and will bring a clear addition to the security of the union's external borders. mr. coelho, i thank you and congratulate you on the way you handled this case.

in writing. - of course, i voted for romania and bulgaria to join the schengen area. as all romanian and european citizens, i want the judicial reforms in my country to continue, corruption and fraud to be reduced, cases to be tried fairly and quickly, and the guilty to be punished severely. we joined the european union because we wanted to adopt its internal rules and it seems natural to me to respect them and to keep the promises we made when we joined. i thank the union and the member states for helping us make the judicial reforms and anti-corruption measures irreversible, because that is also the wish of the romanian citizens.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the coehlo report on the application of the schengen acquis to romania and bulgaria and i welcome the realism and good faith of all colleagues who also voted in favour of this report. romania and bulgaria have fulfilled the technical conditions for accession to the schengen area and this should be the sole criterion for the adoption of this decision. romania and bulgaria have demonstrated the capacity to adopt the necessary domestic legislation and secure their borders. significant progress has also been made in the fight against corruption - a subject that has often been wrongly and exaggeratedly associated with accession to the schengen area.
in writing. − based on the results of the evaluations and additional visits undertaken by the expert teams, it appears that romania is in a position to fully implement the schengen acquis and all points that needed special attention or re-examination have been resolved (improving risk assessment, updating building security features, improving the visa application submission and processing process, etc.), and it can be considered, in some respects, as an example of best practice. according to the evaluation reports, romania has demonstrated that it is sufficiently prepared to implement satisfactorily both the non-sis and sis provisions of the schengen acquis. the conditions for the adoption by the council of the decision referred to in article 4 (2) of the act of accession allowing for the abolition of internal border controls at air, land and sea borders have been fulfilled. the abolition of internal border controls thus requires a high level of mutual trust between member states as regards the existence of effective external border controls, as the security of the schengen area depends on the strictness and effectiveness with which each member state carries out its external border controls.
in writing. − in 2007, when they joined the eu, romania and bulgaria adopted the schengen acquis. in accordance with article 4 (2) of the act of accession, the verification, by means of evaluation procedures, of the fulfilment by the new member states of the conditions necessary for the application of all parts of the schengen acquis (data protection, sis, air borders, land borders, maritime borders, police cooperation and visas) is conditional on the adoption of a council decision abolishing checks at the internal borders with the member states concerned . according to the expert assessment reports, both romania and bulgaria have demonstrated that they are ready to apply the provisions of the schengen acquis in a satisfactory manner. that is why we are asking the council to approve the entry of romania and bulgaria into the schengen area. the union must apply the same criteria to all member states, including as regards accession to the schengen area. the cooperation and judicial verification mechanism is not part of the criteria for accession to the schengen area and cannot be invoked in the context of the accession of romania and bulgaria to the schengen area. as romania and bulgaria meet the technical conditions for accession to the schengen area, on behalf of the romanian and bulgarian citizens, european citizens, we ask the council to approve the accession of romania and bulgaria to the schengen area.
in writing. − i welcome the majority of over 80% with which the ep voted to adopt the report on the fulfilment of the schengen acquis by romania and bulgaria. this vote is a powerful political signal. the ep's view is that romania and bulgaria are ready to join the schengen area. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu. i believe that the rules should not be changed during the game, and the decision on joining the schengen area should take into account the achievements under the schengen agreement and not political assessments. the situation created around the accession of romania and bulgaria to the schengen area denotes the weakening of solidarity within the eu. the fact that some member states are ready to give up one of the freedoms which underpin the construction of europe, freedom of movement, is a wake-up call and at the same time a wrong response to the tensions generated by the economic crisis and its social consequences. the udmr believes that we need a strong europe that can be materialized through more solidarity and a firm rejection of domestic protectionism and populism.
in writing. − in a rapidly changing world, the european union is facing numerous challenges that require a concerted international response. all these substantial changes mean that the european union is actively engaged with other partners to promote effective solutions to problems affecting both european citizens and humanity as a whole. the european union is the world's largest provider of development aid and the united nations' main partner in its efforts at the level of its work. the european union must play a proactive role in building a united nations that contributes effectively to global solutions, peace and security, democracy and an international order based on the rule of law. in accordance with article 21 of the treaty on european union, the european union is formally committed to effective multilateralism centred on a strong united nations, which is vital for addressing global challenges.
in writing. - i voted for the report by mr lambsdorff because i believe that the eu is now creating a new identity on the international scene. i would remind you of the long-standing cooperation between the two international organisations, as well as the eu's involvement in numerous un-initiated projects. i am referring here to the commitment made by european leaders to achieve the millennium development goals. eradicating global poverty is now one of the union's foreign policy priorities. i welcome the initiative to strengthen cooperation in the stabilisation of crisis zones and the development of new nuclear safety standards. the development of events in japan demonstrates the need for this partnership. in the context of the social movements in the mediterranean area, i believe that coordinated eu and un action would guarantee a peaceful democratic transition. in this respect, the intensification of relations with regional organisations is welcome.
in writing. − the seventh framework programme of the european union for research, technological development and demonstration activities is the largest instrument of support for research worldwide and constitutes the main instrument of the european union's research policy. research is the process of converting economic power into knowledge, and innovation is the reverse process of converting knowledge into economic power. the european union and its member states must build the means to provide a common response to the major social, economic, environmental, demographic and ethical challenges facing european states, such as population ageing, citizens' health, food supply, sustainable development and major environmental issues. to enable the more efficient transformation of research results into products and services that generate economic growth and benefits for society at large, a better relationship between academia, research and industry is needed. member states should also step up their communication efforts on the use of new technologies, such as smart research information services, announcing future research challenges and disseminating the results of research activities. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − this report considers whether the review of the 7th framework programme for research and technological development (fp7) may offer an opportunity to consolidate the golden triangle of knowledge, education and research that is the key to europeans’ destiny. i welcome the level of participation and excellence in project selection but regret, however, that the success rate under this programme generally remains quite low and is a disincentive, particularly for smes. i support, within the framework of the ‘people’ chapter, the marie curie actions, which are of great value to researchers in their career and acknowledge that ‘joint technological initiatives’ (jtis) assist the competitiveness of european industry.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on eu-canada trade relations because it drew attention to the need to include social and environmental issues in the future eu-canada economic and trade agreement. as far as environmental protection is concerned, i think it is important that the european union should refuse to import oil extracted from oil sands.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on credit rating agencies because i believe that a new european rating agency is needed, which would introduce an alternative working method and more competition in this sector. the financial crisis has shown us that we cannot continue to accept the oligopolistic structure and lack of transparency and accountability of the current credit rating agencies.
in writing. − the external dimension of social policy includes european union activities and initiatives aimed at promoting social and labour standards in third countries. the protection of economic and social rights is an obligation for all states under the un universal declaration of human rights. the attitude of all member states of the european union must therefore clearly reflect the principles of the european social model when social issues and cooperation between member states are at stake. i would like to stress that the european social model offers equal opportunities in education, training and the labour market, as well as equal access to social services, as basic pillars of economic success. i therefore encourage member states to support freedom of association and collective bargaining, the elimination of forced and compulsory labour, the elimination of discrimination in employment and placement and the abolition of child labour. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution which supports dignity, well-being and personal development as values that should be the main objectives of economic development
in writing. − the external dimension of social policy includes eu activities and initiatives aimed at promoting social and labour standards in third countries. although both the lisbon strategy and the eu 2020 strategy place greater emphasis than ever on social policy, the competitiveness and economic factors aspect is still given priority over the social aspects. fundamental labour standards are included in the eight ilo conventions, which focus on freedom of association and collective bargaining, the elimination of forced and compulsory labour, the elimination of discrimination in employment and placement, and the abolition of child labour. for the eu to negotiate with third countries, they must meet all the requirements mentioned above. this is a mandatory condition for negotiations with third countries. trade policy cannot ignore violations of workers' rights and therefore the development of society can only continue after these drawbacks have been removed. the eu has a good reputation for international social dialogue. in this respect, the eu is considered a sensitive and reliable partner. this must be used to meet the more ambitious objectives set by the eu.
in writing. − according to the report, the eu has a unique combination of economic dynamism with a social model. it creates equal opportunities in education, training and the labour market and equal access to social services. the report stresses the fact that there is a need for implementation of decent work programmes that reflect national needs and priorities regarding employment and social policy, and are based on agreement between employers, workers and governments. this aspect is very important in the actual context. these are several of the reasons why i endorse this report.
in writing. − the core labour standards included in the eight ilo conventions focus on freedom of association and collective bargaining, the elimination of forced and compulsory labour, the elimination of discrimination in employment and placement, and the abolition of child labour. therefore, more attention should be paid to the protection of workers' rights and labour law. significant strengthening of the legal and social position of women is needed to prevent discrimination and to harness the potential contribution of women to economic and social development. i call on the commission and the member states to implement the right to non-discrimination, i.e. the right to work and equal treatment, regardless of gender, ethnic origin, age and disability, as a key principle in the fight against poverty. i call on the commission and the member states to work with partner countries to put more emphasis on combating the exploitation of child labour with a view to creating instead decent jobs for adults and allowing children to receive an appropriate education. freedom of association and the right to collective bargaining must be implemented without exception in order to improve and defend decent working conditions for workers.
in writing. - the economic crisis has completely disrupted the labour market in the european union. no major field of activity has been spared its harmful consequences, translated at the citizen level into job insecurity, unemployment, and harsh conditions or chances of re-employment. in this context, vocational education and training is proving to be a new opportunity, a new way for european citizens to get their lives back to normal. i am concerned about the high rate of unemployment among young people and believe that with the right education and continuing training, many young europeans will be able to find a well-paid job that is worth training or retraining. i congratulate the rapporteur on this dossier and conclude, with nadja hirsch, that if this wish is to be realised, vocational education and training must be clearly result-oriented. the goal for 2020 must be one: every young person has a job.
in writing. − the europe 2020 strategy states that the key drivers for smart growth are the promotion of knowledge, innovation and education, the digital society, but also sustainable and inclusive growth. the key here is education and training, which all member states must assume to the same standards. despite the drastic effects of the economic crisis on the european labour market, it can be assumed that employment in europe will increase over the next ten years, at least gradually. the forecasts suggest that the demand for qualifications will continue to grow. industrial and technological change brings with it a growing demand for medium and high-skilled workers, leaving behind the low-skilled. it is becoming increasingly important that learning be clearly result-oriented. reforms of the vocational training systems of some member states have already been put into practice. with regard to the comparability of education and training systems in the member states, the priority should be to remove barriers, increase transparency and facilitate comparison within and between different systems.
in writing. − measures in the field of education and training are absolutely indispensable for the transformation of the european economy into a knowledge-based economy, in line with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. i therefore fully support the recommendations of this report, which underline the importance of investment in education and training for the future competitiveness of the european economy. to achieve our objectives, effective, complementary measures are needed at national and european level. the unemployment rate among young people in the eu has risen alarmingly. the report sends a clear message: education and training are key factors in tackling youth unemployment. clear strategies are needed to integrate them into the labour market, and to link education programmes to labour market demands so that the latter can absorb graduates. a focus on concrete skills is needed to facilitate integration into the labour market. moreover, because of the constant changes in technology, employers have increasingly high expectations of the qualifications of their employees. continuing training therefore plays a key role in continuously adapting vocational qualifications to the requirements of the economy. this can help to avoid exclusion from the labour market at some point in their working lives.
in writing. − the europe 2020 strategy identifies the key drivers for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth (increasing employment, training and poverty eradication). concrete action at union and member state level is needed to implement the strategy in the field of education and training. european workers must be able to adapt to the demands of the economy. policy makers need to enable people to hone and expand their skills. it calls on the member states to monitor the facilitation of the transition from school to working life by developing integrated career guidance and counselling programmes, to create better opportunities for the qualification of trainers and to lay the foundations for a learning partnership to be promoted in particular at regional and local level. member states must take into account in vocational education and training the individual needs of low-skilled people, learners from migrant backgrounds, people belonging to an ethnic minority, women, the unemployed and people with disabilities. calls on the member states to support innovative activities, doctoral and post-doctoral programmes that support competitiveness and sustainable economic growth.
in writing. − the development cooperation instrument (dci) is one of the european union's profoundly altruistic projects, designed to help developing countries without any other conditions or interests. the absence of any utilitarianism on the european side should force the institutions on the continent to focus their funding much better and to focus on poverty eradication and the achievement of the millennium development goals (mdgs). i stress the need for increased transparency for all funds dedicated to this purpose and, more importantly, increased impact assessments of the icd among the populations of those countries. because these funds must be matched by effective social policies, implemented at the level of developing countries. these funds should be the medium- and long-term 'leash' for these peoples to learn how to fish and become self-sufficient. we must not forget that 2010 was the european year for combating poverty and social exclusion. the development cooperation instrument must therefore continue this fight in developing countries too, making a significant contribution to ensuring a decent living for as many citizens as possible.
in writing. − i have several reasons why i support this resolution. first of all it underlines that impact assessment can never be a substitute for political debate and the legislator’s decision-making process but should only help the technical preparation of political decisions. this would certainly improve the decision-making process. secondly, the impact assessments have to take a large number of criteria into account in order to provide the legislator with as comprehensive picture. only in this way can the legislator do his job efficiently.
in writing. − impact assessments (ias) are a key instrument for the legislative process, and one of which european legislators should make greater use in future. the benefits of ias are obvious. they show legislators the possible consequences of their policy options and help them in making a decision. ias can thus make a significant contribution to better lawmaking. however, they can in no way be a substitute for political debate and the legislator’s democratically legitimated decision-making process. they merely permit the technical, substantive preparation of a political decision. the ias used by the european institutions should comply with certain principles. first of all they should be completely independent and transparent, cover all categories of legislative proposal and employ a clear methodology. the policy options listed should also include the option of taking no action. the specific consequences for small and medium-sized enterprises should be taken into account where appropriate and they must always be kept up to date with current developments in the legislative process. parliament’s key demand is the creation of an autonomous structure for carrying out impact assessments within parliament, with a view to further enhancing the quality of its lawmaking and creating synergies with the possibility of a common mechanism for all eu institutions.
in writing. − the most obvious obstacles faced by consumers and smes in the single market are the complexity of contractual relationships, abusive terms and conditions in contracts, inadequate and insufficient information, lengthy procedures, language barriers, differences in taxation systems, the credibility of online traders, the demographic structure of the population of each member state, privacy considerations, complaint handling and intellectual property rights. european contract law establishes and regulates transactions in the internal market and seeks to solve problems in the single market caused, inter alia, by divergent contract law legislation. ensuring a coherent contract law regime is thus essential to realise the full potential of the internal market and to support the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives. choosing the right path in contract law can make a significant contribution to improving the functioning of the internal market and unlocking its full potential for businesses, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises, and for consumers. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i want to support the adoption of a clearly defined measurement system that goes beyond gdp in order to complement it in the context of decision-making and its evaluation. gdp is an indicator of market economic activity, which has become a standard reference for policymakers. all international institutions increasingly recognise the need to improve the data and indicators that complement gdp in assessing the overall development of society. this report highlights the need to measure the quality of life in societies. achieving and maintaining a quality of life involves factors such as health, education, culture, employment, housing and environmental conditions. i am in favour of establishing a sound legal framework for european economic and environmental accounts and encourage the need for reliable and harmonised statistics.
in writing. − i voted for this report because i believe that indicators must be found that are complementary to gdp and that help us measure factors such as climate change, biodiversity or resource efficiency. as joseph stiglitz rightly points out, gdp is not a sufficient instrument to reflect the well-being of citizens, but merely measures economic activity in the market. i hope that the european executive will come up with concrete proposals for additional, more comprehensive and more sustainable indicators to address the current shortcomings.
in writing. − gdp is the most eloquent measure of macroeconomic activity and is also an indirect indicator of the development and progress of society. however, it cannot provide information on all topics that are the subject of policy debates, such as the environment or social inclusion. this indicator underpins many of the european union's policy decisions and instruments, and i believe that we need to step up our efforts to make indicators available that meet the needs of all citizens, namely to measure progress towards economic, social and environmental objectives in a sustainable way. in conclusion, future european policies must be based on complete, up-to-date data covering all the essentials.
in writing. − the commission communication 'beyond gdp - measuring progress in a changing world' focuses on developing more comprehensive indicators to complement gdp and provide a more reliable knowledge base. gdp has come to take on the role of a comprehensive indicator of society's overall development and progress, but it does not provide a reliable basis for all the issues that are the subject of policy debate. in particular, gdp does not measure either environmental sustainability or social inclusion. i voted for this report because it is important to develop a tool that can complement gdp, given that this needs to be done in a way that has practical use, based on clearly defined indicators and high-quality data. this report asks the commission to present a sequential strategy on the 'beyond gdp' approach, explaining how the new approach can be applied pragmatically in everyday policy work.

the european arrest warrant is an effective tool for combating and controlling cross-border crime at community level. it has proved effective in speeding up the transfer of persons suspected of committing serious crimes, including terrorism and organised crime, between union countries. but too often this tool has been used for petty crime. it's about equal treatment of deeply unequal cases. the warrant was issued when its use was neither necessary nor proportionate. this has not only led to unfair situations for the accused but also to an unjustified burden on the resources of the executing state. the disproportionate use of this instrument, which is essential for the fight against cross-border crime, leads to an erosion of trust and will lead some states to conduct proportionality checks under their own rules when deciding to execute a european arrest warrant. the effect will be inconsistent and uneven application and consequently distrust of the concept of mutual recognition. the right to legal aid must be ensured in both the issuing and the executing states in order for the right of defence to be properly exercised. that is why we wanted to put these questions to the commission and the council. we need to be sure that the standards of criminal justice and prison conditions in the european union are not a source of distrust among the judicial systems of the member states. in conclusion, i would also like to thank commissioner reding for all the actions she has taken to strengthen procedural rights in criminal proceedings.

in writing. we are all aware of the potential and crucial role of the common agricultural policy in achieving the environmental and climate objectives, in providing public goods and, equally, in achieving the food security objectives of the eu. but it is very important that when we talk about agriculture and the future of the cap, the keywords are simplification and innovation. we need to focus on those policy measures that do not impose new administrative burdens because we do not want to make life more difficult for our farmers. the common agricultural policy needs to become fairer and simpler and i think we need to find the right balance between the policy objectives we propose and the administrative burden. we need to ensure the welfare of farmers and strengthen local economies, we need to ensure the protection of the environment and we need to be concerned about producing quality, safe and healthy food. when it comes to agriculture, we don't have to focus exclusively on technological solutions or on discussions about technological solutions, but we have to consider consumption patterns, and the waste problem, and the complex relationship that exists between the environment, biodiversity and health.
in writing. i consider the report by mr dess to be essential in the context of the global food crisis and environmental risks today. the common agricultural policy in its new form includes values such as consumer protection and regional cohesion. i believe that long-term productivity depends largely on the sustainable management of natural resources, another goal on the agenda. i welcome the initiative to involve farmers more actively in rural development programmes, which will lead to an increase in local competitiveness. food security is another priority under the new common agricultural policy. cooperation between member states is vital, as was shown in the e. coli crisis this summer. to avoid food price fluctuations, i support additional risk prevention measures that are available to all farmers in the eu. i also believe that it is important to ensure that the funds for agriculture are distributed fairly. here i highlight, for example, the impact of direct aid on increasing the profitability and competitiveness of small farms. it is also necessary to program special payments for areas marked by natural handicaps, which have special needs.
in writing. the common agricultural policy is facing a number of challenges, which call for a strategic decision by the european union and the member states on the future of agriculture. to be effective in addressing these challenges, the cap needs to act in the context of sound economic policies and sustainable public finances that contribute to the achievement of the union's objectives in the context of the 2020 strategy. i believe that the european union must continue to have sufficient instruments to combat market crises, supply crises, price and market fluctuations in the agricultural sector. i believe that the cap funds for the first and second pillars should be distributed equitably between member states and between farmers within a member state, thus reducing the large discrepancies in the distribution of these funds between member states. the second pillar of the cap is very important in the field of rural development and i believe that special attention should be paid to stimulating and encouraging young farmers. i therefore support the introduction of targeted measures in this pillar, to be set by the member states, to achieve the eu's priority targets so as to maintain compensation payments for the less-favoured areas in the second pillar.
in writing. food security is and will remain the main challenge for eu agriculture and beyond, as highlighted in the oecd-fao report agricultural outlook 2011-2020. i believe that we need to pay particular attention to the demographic challenges that affect the rural environment in particular. if we fail to manage demographic change and increase the attractiveness of rural areas for young farmers, we risk that this will become a real obstacle to sound and quality agricultural production over time. to do this, we are obliged to offer young people new attractive measures, substantial financial support, increased access to innovative services and infrastructure. in addition, there is a need for better coordination between financial support for rural development and other regional policies, and for cap funding to be maintained at a level that ensures that all the tasks proposed are fulfilled. in this way, we will facilitate a stronger economic, social and cultural involvement of young people in european union agriculture.
i shall vote tomorrow on the legislative package on european economic governance and i too would like to thank the rapporteurs, the hungarian presidency and the commission in particular for the really great efforts they have made to bring this legislative package to fruition. this european economic governance package has to be seen in conjunction with the other legislative package, which has already been adopted, on the financial sector, including the european financial supervisory architecture. i am convinced that by effectively implementing this legislation, no other member state will be left unarmed in the face of a future crisis and we will be able to prevent and correct fiscal imbalances, economic imbalances, and this is one of the best guarantees for economic growth and jobs. but i am concerned that the european institutions are unwilling to recognise an economic reality that we are facing today, namely that a member state that has a debt that it cannot pay can not be helped by adding new debt to the existing one, and even at higher costs. experience shows, and common sense tells us, that the solution is for the debtor country to get its house in order, and for the creditors to understand that the debt to be paid must be matched to the actual payment capacity of that country. if we do not do this, we will not save time but, on the contrary, we will waste time and the problem will become worse.
a unified eu strategy is needed to ensure a high level of competitiveness, sustainable growth and job creation. a strong, effective stability and growth pact is the key instrument. further efforts should therefore be made to prevent the adoption of unsustainable budgetary policies. the improved economic governance framework will be based on different interlinked policies. the package of proposals will encourage member states to pursue a prudent budgetary policy and, where appropriate, to take early adjustment measures to limit the application of sanctions. prevention is easier than cure.
in writing. at a time when the recession and the sovereign debt crisis are making themselves felt, we need strong economic governance at european level. however, the economic governance package, in its current form, would not allow the european union's economy to recover, but would instead bring it to a state where high unemployment and poverty would be pervasive. i think that the proposals in this package are not ambitious enough, they go exclusively in the direction of austerity and reduction of social rights of citizens. it does not mention elements that could underpin a revival of the european economy, such as investments in key areas of infrastructure, education, research and innovation. we are able to propose an alternative to this austerity model which, as we see in the case of greece, is proving to be severely limited. the creation of bonds for the joint issuance of part of the european public debt would automatically lower the cost of financing in the european union and allow for the resumption of investments. following the new deal model in the united states, the solution to the current economic and financial crisis will be a return to growth based on investment and job creation.
in writing. the economic crisis and its consequences have shown us that it is not national solutions but european solutions that are the basis on which the future of the eu must be built. a viable response to the sovereign debt crisis, the need to strengthen the euro and to return to a path of sustainable growth and job creation depends on effective coordination between member states, the strengthening of the stability and growth pact, in short, a strong europe, a goal also formulated in the slogan of the hungarian presidency of the european council. the european economic governance package on the european parliament's agenda is able to create the necessary mechanisms for the future of the eu as envisioned by its architects. the adoption of the economic governance package will mean close coordination, fiscal discipline, economic surveillance, effective rules for decision-making, strong european institutions, thus laying the foundations for the new eu. the economic crisis has irreversibly changed the world, and the need for a new financial architecture is becoming increasingly evident in the eu. we are at a turning point. the weakening of the ambition of the member states to complete the reforms triggered by the crisis, too much leniency, too many exceptions to the commonly accepted rules and a return to a new form of internal protectionism will be fatal.
the directive establishes the legal framework for the responsible management of spent fuel and radioactive waste, which is a much-needed regulation. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the aid is compatible with the internal market. germany has already announced that it will shut down a number of power plants. in the near future there will be other plants in other member states which will have to be shut down because they are reaching their final operational deadline. the national approach of the directive will result in the creation of radioactive waste sites throughout the union. it's a waste of resources and a source of public concern. it is the case now in romania, in my own region, with regard to the radioactive waste dump at kozloduy. i believe that a long-term approach, a truly european one, is needed, leading to the use of common technologies, to the saving of resources, to european funding mechanisms. a global approach and adequate information can win the trust and confidence of european citizens.
the issue of spent fuel and radioactive waste management is an important and pressing one, which has been given even greater prominence following the fukushima tragedy. the problem is a growing challenge, despite technological innovations and solutions, and waste management programmes. the management and disposal of radioactive waste is an existing problem and will remain so in the future. in europe, we are striving for energy security, environmentally friendly and stable energy production, but at the same time we must put increasing emphasis on a number of problems, such as the processing, transformation and disposal of the rapidly increasing amount of radioactive waste. this requires not only the technical conditions but also the rigorous political, legal and social structures. it would be worthwhile to consider, assess and plan pan-european cooperation in this field. all those responsible shall be involved in the establishment and development of the safe process. measures must be taken to protect future generations as well.

in writing. – the european union produces more that 40 000 m3 of radioactive waste each year, 80% is short-lived low-level radioactive waste and about 5% is long-lived low-level radioactive waste. it is important that the union will implement a directive on the management of spent fuel and radioactive waste. romania is among those member states which are in favour of having the possibility to export radioactive waste to third countries. spent fuel from research reactors in romania needs to be either repatriated to the country of origin, russia or the united states or exported to third countries in special cases. for this reason i cannot support the export ban proposal in this report. as nuclear energy will remain part of the member states’ energy mix in the future it is important that such a report is adopted successfully in the plenary session of this parliament. spent fuels should be moved out of pools and into dry storage as soon as possible and high priority should be placed on the oldest radioactive wastes. furthermore, it is important that citizens have confidence in the principles governing the safety of repositories and in waste management programmes.

crossborder cooperation in a borderless europe is beneficial for local and regional authorities as it is an important element for the further development of the union's single market. but crossborder areas have an important characteristic, that of shared multicultural traditions and ethnic diversity, which usually provide a solid basis for people-to-people and community-to-community action in various fields. we all know that crossborder areas are often characterised by medium to high unemployment, with significant differences between regions, and by a high level of hidden unemployment, caused by the lack of registration of unemployed persons. as such, i believe that an integrated approach to the labour market in crossborder areas can be beneficial in finding solutions to structural problems and would bring demand and supply closer together. therefore, as the rapporteur has argued, objective 3 needs to be strongly strengthened.

in writing. − the european commission's proposal for a consumer rights directive brings together four existing directives into a single legislative instrument, with the aim of simplifying and complementing the existing regulatory framework for consumer protection. the dual objective of the proposal is to ensure that all consumers in the eu-27 can rely on a high level of consumer protection and that businesses of all sizes are able to offer their goods and services to consumers in the eu-27. the new consumer rights rules cover almost all types of sales, whether in-store, by telephone or online, but strengthen in particular the provisions on international sales. the new legislation sets out what information the buyer must receive from the seller, the delivery conditions and rules that apply when the risk is borne by the buyer, and the buyer's right to cancel or refuse purchases or the right to have a good repaired or replaced. i support the proposal to introduce a combination of the principle of maximum harmonization and that of minimum harmonization, thus making it possible to maintain the rights acquired by consumers through national provisions.

rapporteur. − madam president, i would first like to express my gratitude to my colleagues, shadow rapporteurs, the rapporteur for the opinion and to other members of this parliament who contributed to this report. i would also like to express my thanks to the council and commission for all the successful cooperation during the trialogue meetings led by ms sharon bowles. i would also like thank mr van es, our adviser in the committee on economic and monetary affairs, for his support. with regard to financial conglomerates, there are potential risks arising from multiple uses of capital, management complexity, concentration, conflicts of interest and other so-called group risks when several licences for different financial services are combined. therefore, financial conglomerates must be placed under supplementary supervision, consolidated at group level. the commission intends to improve european legislation on supplementary supervision in two steps. the first step is to address the most urgent issues through amending the current directive and updating several sectoral directives. the second step, probably in 2012, is to present a proposal for a new directive on this supplementary supervision of financial conglomerates, based on a more fundamental debate on this issue. through our joint efforts we, the european parliament, council and commission, now have a good consensus on how to change the current directive at this first step. our main proposals refer to defining mixed financial holding companies and placing them under supplementary supervision – which includes bringing alternative investment fund managers under the scope of this current directive – introducing the possibility of stress-testing at the level of each financial conglomerate, ensuring that the new european supervisory authorities issue general guidelines regarding supervision of financial conglomerates through the joint committee, amending the solvency ii directive and improving the transparency of supplementary supervision. in view of the second step, our report includes a review clause. we ask the commission to look into the possibility of placing under supplementary supervision non-regulated entities, in particular special-purpose vehicles. the identification criteria of financial conglomerates owned by wider non-financial groups active in the banking, insurance and investment services sector are materially relevant in the internal market for financial services. the possibility of introducing mandatory stress-testing at a group level must also be considered.

we're going to apply them to 8,230 banks here in europe. in the united states, it will be about 20 banks. there is a third difference: the existence of the subject we are dealing with here in europe - reached on the ficod proposal and would like to thank all those of you who have been committed to bringing this process to a successful conclusion, and first of all you, mr stolojan, the rapporteur, financial conglomerates and insurance groups are, as i have said, a specific feature of the european banking landscape. it's a business model that works well. however, the crisis has shown that, again, certain aspects of the directive on financial conglomerates need to be strengthened. that is why the commission made this proposal in august 2010 to amend the directive. the agreement between parliament and the council on these amendments will significantly improve the supervision of financial conglomerates by closing a regulatory loophole. the inclusion of financial companies known as mixed holdings in the sectoral directives, i.e. in the capital requirements directive for banks and in solvency ii for insurers, will now monitor the highest level of conglomerates more effectively and i believe this will help to strengthen financial stability. i am particularly grateful to your rapporteur, mr stolojan, for his decisive role in improving the directive in several important areas which were not covered by the commission's original proposal. i am thinking of the stress testing, which he mentioned just now, and the strengthening of the role of the joint committee of the european supervisory authorities. all these improvements are in line with the "supervision" package. the agreement will also extend the scope of supplementary supervision to portfolio management companies and alternative funds controlled by a conglomerate. finally, i would also like to welcome the agreement reached on the transparency of group structures. i would also like to say a word about the correlation tables, which are a controversial subject, difficult at the time of the trilogues. i very much appreciate, ladies and gentlemen, the importance which parliament attaches to this subject. i sometimes find it difficult to understand the difficulties of the council in communicating to the commission, with the traditional transposition measures, these tables showing how the directive in question has been transposed into national law. i think that this should normally be part of the transposition work carried out by the member states. i am very pleased with the support of parliament on this point. the commission considers such tables to be an integral part of our efforts to improve legislation, and i would like to thank you for including them in the final text, as you propose, and as the commission also suggested initially.
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on legal affairs. − madam president, the functioning of the investor compensation schemes has been improved and brought into line with banking scheme standards. i would like to mention that we cannot send a signal of equivalence of treatment between capital market investors and depositors in commercial banks. although both categories have to be protected, with regard to protection for investors in securities it should be considered that the risk of the latter is taken by choice. i welcome the introduction of the lending system between the schemes and i hope that parliament in plenary will maintain my own amendment regarding the postponement of reaching the guarantee ceiling by romania and bulgaria, in order to respect the terms of the accession treaties.
i'd like to start by congratulating my colleague, mr. stolojan. this proposal for a directive is part of the developments in supplementary supervision with a view to making risk management practices more efficient. the review of the supplementary supervision framework for financial entities belonging to a financial conglomerate is dictated by the globalisation that has impacted the european financial market. the financial crisis has exposed major weaknesses in the supervision of the financial sector. i would point out that the purpose of the review of this framework is to oversee the activities of the largest european financial groups. certain financial groups cannot be subject to supplementary supervision because of their legal structure. at the same time, it is sometimes difficult to separate banking from insurance. finally, i would stress that it is very important that financial groups be subject to identical, harmonised supervision, which would strengthen european supervisory mechanisms.
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on legal affairs. − mr president, supplementary supervision of a financial conglomerate should lead to a reduction in the systemic risk that such conglomerates pose to the market. supervision at group level will be added and will not replace the supervision of each member of the conglomerate under the applicable arrangements for supervision in the banking market, the capital market or the insurance market. therefore we will have supervision at group-member level, over which we will overlap the supervision at group level to which the member belongs. this supplementary supervision will not produce extra bureaucracy as long as there is cooperation between the european and national authorities with regulatory responsibilities.
