rapporteur. − mr president, i thank all the speakers who raised several issues in this debate, some of which we had a long discussion on during the trialogue meetings. my colleagues proposed some issues as amendments, and the main obstacle we had in agreeing on these issues was the lack of impact assessments. we should not forget that we are discussing the financial sector, which is very sensitive to all kinds of regulation, and each regulation has a cost. therefore we should be very careful when we propose different regulation for entities operating in this sector. i very much hope that the commission will be able – maybe next year – to come up, as they proposed, with a new proposal for a directive on supplementary supervision of financial conglomerates. once again i want to thank mr barnier the commissioner, and his staff, who worked very hard with the hungarian presidency and with our colleagues, in order to arrive at this consensus, which i hope will be voted on tomorrow.
i also welcome the commission's initiative to create a legal framework on short selling and cdss, relating to situations where market operations would become a threat to financial stability or to market confidence. i agree with the proposal to introduce a transparency regime, which involves the notification to the competent authority of significant net short positions in shares, subject to specific thresholds. under normal circumstances, short selling favours market liquidity and contributes to efficient price setting. however, in markets in difficulty, this can amplify the price decline. this would lead to disorderly markets and systemic risks. regulators must be given clear powers to restrict or prohibit short selling in exceptional circumstances. they will be exercised in cooperation with esma.
in writing. unlike long sales, where the risk is reduced to the price difference between the purchase and resale, short sales are unlimited in risk, with theoretical infinite loss. in view of the unlimited risks that a seller and short seller assume, it was considered necessary to adopt this regulation. however, certain notifications or procedures may have slightly more relaxed deadlines. in addition, speculative transactions, alongside hedging, are part of this market and should be reported to esma. speculative transactions are not harmful in themselves, but their uncontrolled development is dangerous.
member of the commission. - madam president, i would first like to warmly thank mr olle schmidt, and also the econ committee and its chairman, mrs sharon bowles, for the very ambitious signal - mr schmidt, unequivocal - that parliament is sending on this important matter. the strengthening of investor compensation schemes is one piece in a coherent package which also includes - i remind you - the deposit guarantee and the white paper on insurance guarantee funds. it is a comprehensive package which was adopted by the commission a year ago. this is an important proposal in our response to the crisis. users, retail investors, are among the most vulnerable actors in the financial system and they are also the first victims of the crisis. it is not only right to protect them - our fellow citizens would not understand failure in this area - but also logical. a sound investment requires the assurance that one will be well compensated in the event of an extreme situation, such as fraud or operational errors that would result in the disappearance of securities. investor compensation therefore contributes to restoring confidence in the financial system - this is one of the lessons of the crisis - but also to the creation of a genuine internal market for financial services. it was this logic that was to lead the co-legislators to adopt, on the basis of a commission proposal in 1997, the very first directive on investor compensation. this directive has been useful, but it needs to be improved; that's what we're doing together today. ladies and gentlemen, i have long been a supporter of a policy of prevention, as we say in french, de prévention. it is always cheaper than repairing it, and i have, in other areas such as ecology, devised mechanisms for the provision of care in my own country. that is why i want this guarantee fund mechanism here. first of all, mr schmidt, i share the ambitious approach that characterizes your report. the agreement of parliament on the principle of prefinancing is a very positive point. for us - and for the commission - this is a sine qua non for the system to be credible. what is the point of providing a high level of cover if there is not enough money available? to say that we could raise money as and when we need it is quite delusional in times of stress. secondly, mr schmidt, i am also in favour of aligning the level of cover on the deposit guarantee to eur 100 000, as you have proposed. we in the commission had proposed eur 50 000, i.e. a lower level than for deposit guarantee in the banking sector because the risks to financial stability seem to us to be higher in the latter sector and lower in the other. i am thinking in particular of the phenomenon of bank runs as we experienced with the northern rock bank in 2008. but i'm willing to consider your proposal, which is more ambitious. finally, i welcome the fact that parliament is preserving the mechanism of mutual borrowing between funds. i see this as a further demonstration of your commitment to the emergence of a more harmonized, more shared economic approach, which is essential to overcome the challenges of the crisis. of course, mr schmidt, there are a few points here and there which are subject to debate or to divergence from the commission's original proposal. for example - as you mentioned in your speech - it seems to me that the extension of cover to ucits is natural, given the attractiveness of this product to retail investors. you requested that this measure be postponed. that said, i note your wish to review it in the context of the revision of the ucits directive in a few months' time. you can count on the commission to do more, mr schmidt. moreover, the reduction of the pre-financing to 0.3% will have to be carefully evaluated if you really want to increase the coverage to eur 100 000. it is no secret, ladies and gentlemen, that increasing coverage while reducing funding risks potentially putting the system in a difficult or stressful situation. finally, i have some reservations about the introduction of an amendment which seeks to cover what is known as 'bad advice'. i share your objective: finance is a complex discipline and there are a number of charlatans who have been quick to exploit the less-informed consumers. however, this situation is rather governed by the rules of conduct of the mifid directive, the violation of which gives rise to liability actions. the idea is also difficult to implement. it could lead to a substantial increase in the number of situations in which we would have to use the compensation funds without the funding being revised accordingly. so, mr schmidt, quite frankly, the concept of bad advice is quite uncertain in our view, and it could lead to significant differences of interpretation between countries and to further fragmentation of the market. that is why we find it difficult to accept the introduction of this concept in the text. but overall, mr schmidt, in thanking you again for the excellent work done by you, the fictitious rapporteurs and the coordinators, i can say that parliament and the commission - that is what is important to me - clearly share a common vision on this matter. it is an ambitious solution, it is a european solution and the council will have to take it into account. this is the signal you send to the member states so that they can quickly agree on a general approach. i am counting on the polish presidency to make every effort to convince those countries which have not yet done so to adopt this more european approach, which is more favourable to retail investors. in total, any credible agreement must provide for a sufficiently high coverage, a credible level of pre-financing and easy access to compensation. that is what we are working towards, mr schmidt, and i would like to thank you for that.

the rapporteur for the opinion, the committee on budgetary control. − the operational management of sis ii, vis, eurodac and other large-scale information technology systems is vital for the future of the european area of freedom, security and justice. it is therefore essential to establish a single authority to ensure the operational management of these information systems. we are in a period of budgetary constraints which must be reflected in the work of the european bodies. i support the proposal that the agency's strategy be based on a multiannual staff policy plan and a draft annual work programme with clear objectives and performance indicators. i regret that the budgetary control committee's proposal to reduce the number of members of the management board was not accepted. i respect the right of member states to be involved in decision-making at agency level, but i believe that a 29-member management board is a costly and burdensome structure that does not contribute to efficiency. i believe that the first priority of the agency should be to clarify the situation in sis ii. an analysis and decision on the timetable and costs of completing this system is required.
and i would like, first of all, to acknowledge the excellent work done by my colleague carlos, who has once again demonstrated his exceptional expertise in this field. i would like to make two comments on the establishment of this new agency, which i also consider to be very useful. first, in the current context, where cyberattacks have become a threat of the highest global importance, we need to ensure that the security of the databases managed by this agency is of the highest standard. secondly, at least at this stage, the new agency, if it were to function, would be without part of its scope of activity, as the sis ii system is still far from being operational. i therefore take this opportunity to ask the commission and the commissioner to honour their commitment to complete the sis ii system in due time.
the proposal to set up this agency is a natural one, since the commission does not have to be the manager of these large-scale information systems, precisely to ensure total transparency and to remove any conflict of interest. please note the scale of this system composed of three parts - sis ii, vis and eurodac - which, due to its major importance and the interconnectedness between them, requires the protection of a single well-defined entity. i believe that fragmented and uncorrelated administration would lead to a desynchronisation between these systems, which could have devastating effects on the protection of personal data, visa-related information and asylum applications. i therefore fully support the establishment of this specific agency for the operational management of large-scale information systems as a measure to protect security and integrity in the european union.

in writing. increased mobility at european level has also necessitated the idea of a single number for emergency calls, precisely to increase the efficiency of the services offered to citizens. the number 112, part of the obligations member states have assumed for eu accession, serves this purpose, although only 26% of europeans can identify it as an emergency number, according to the latest eurobarometer. we therefore see the need to promote the single 112 number more so that it does not lose its usefulness in the member states, while giving up the promotion of other national numbers. due to the mobility of european citizens, we need to consider the efficient handling of emergency calls in foreign languages, as well as alternatives to voice calls: sms, e-mail or fax, especially for the hearing impaired. at the technical level, it is essential to reduce missed emergency calls, to reduce response times and to reduce the number of false calls, which can far exceed the number of real calls. as a romanian, where the 112 number has been working effectively for several years, i believe it is important to support the exchange of experience between the emergency services of the member states, as well as joint training programmes for experts and non-governmental organisations.

genetically modified organisms have not provided the miracle solutions that the biotech industry originally claimed. the promises were for high yields and high drought resistance crops that required less chemical treatment. in reality, we have reached a situation where a few companies own a growing share of the seeds and crops used to produce food and make huge profits from selling the chemicals needed to grow these crops. this is gradually evolving into a monopoly of food resources and at the same time has serious consequences for biodiversity. in addition, we do not yet fully understand the effects of genetic manipulation. national governments must have the right to stop the cultivation of these crops if they pose a danger to the environment or on socioeconomic grounds, and the legal right to restrict cultivation also implies responsibility.

in writing. − the dock dues scheme approved on 5 july 2011 by the european parliament authorises france to adopt, for the four french overseas departments, a differentiated dock dues scheme for certain products manufactured in the octs by 1 july 2014. the anchorage fee is vital to support the outermost regions which are economically and socially disadvantaged by certain permanent factors such as small size and insularity, remoteness from large markets, deficient topography and climate or dependence on a small number of marketed products. the aim of the dock levy is to stabilise the economies of the outermost regions, helping to maintain jobs in regimes where unemployment is close to 30% and, by implication, supporting local production. moreover, the revenue from the application of this dockage tax, which represents between 37 and 48% of the budget of the local authorities of the overseas departments, is intended to be and must be a major support for investment policies on local development. the european parliament therefore supports the necessary perpetuation from 2014 of the exemptions or reductions of the duties in the context of the dock dues granted to french sacs.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal to amend directive 2001/18/ec as regards the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory. the directive and regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 of the european parliament and of the council of 22 september 2003 on genetically modified food and feed establish a very rigorous framework which, if properly applied, allows for a high level of protection of human life and health, animal health and welfare, the environment and consumer interests, while ensuring the effective functioning of the internal market. the directive allows gmos to be authorised for placing on the market only if a specific environmental risk assessment has been carried out. annex ii, which sets out the principles applicable to environmental risk assessment, requires consideration of direct and indirect, immediate and delayed effects, as well as an analysis of cumulative long-term effects on flora and fauna, soil fertility, degradation of soil organic matter, the human or animal food chain, biological diversity, animal health and problems of antibiotic resistance.

in writing. the use of body scanners should be allowed in the eu only if there is conclusive evidence that the risk to human health is minimal. their use must also be without prejudice to the right to privacy. there is evidence that at the current state of technology, body scanners may not meet all the requirements for health safety. these scans, especially those using ionizing radiation, can seriously affect the human body even with low levels of radiation because of their cumulative effect. this is all the more dangerous for frequent airline passengers who must endure hundreds of scanner exposures each year, plus in-flight solar radiation that is several hundred times greater than at ground level. in addition, certain categories of people, such as pregnant women, children, and the elderly, may be even more sensitive to radiation exposure. i therefore believe that the decision on the use of body scanners in eu countries must be made with great caution in order to protect the fundamental rights and health of european citizens.
in writing. the report we are voting on is an important step towards ensuring aviation safety. the danger of recent terrorist attacks has brought to the fore the need to improve aviation safety standards. in 2008, parliament rejected the use of security scanners because they did not meet a number of requirements, such as respect for fundamental rights, protection of the dignity, privacy and health of individuals. meanwhile, technology has evolved and allowed the development of scanners that provide the necessary safety without endangering the health and privacy of individuals. we considered it very important that the report should state the need to inform passengers about the new types of scans and the process they will undergo during the scans in order to avoid any confusion. it was also essential to clarify that the scanners do not show the human body but standard images which only indicate whether the passenger is carrying dangerous objects or not. last but not least, i wanted to mention the need to increase the number of checkpoints and security staff, in order to avoid as much as possible the increase in the time allocated to security checks. as regards the issue of the ban on liquids, aerosols and gels, i ask the commission to take the necessary measures to lift the restriction by 2013 and to introduce mandatory scanning of these products.
i would also like to congratulate mrs rodi kratsa on this report which she has produced and which is a first step in making this problem more visible. the outcome of these debates can provide long-term solutions. this report highlights a phenomenon that is having a significant impact on the european business environment. promoting women to management positions in companies is difficult and discriminatory. there is a marked difference between the number of women who graduate from college and those who enter companies in a leadership position. unfortunately, despite adapted social and economic policies, the european union still faces this problem. theoretically, equality in the labour market is supported in absolutely all areas. in practice, however, the figures show otherwise. the labour potential of women is, in this case, under-exploited and undervalued. i would point out that various studies have shown the positive impact of the work of women managers on the competitiveness rate of companies. even so, discrimination and prejudice hinder their advancement in their careers. another regrettable aspect is the persistence of the gender pay gap in management positions. i welcome the setting of target percentages for increasing women's participation in business management by 2015 and 2020 respectively. this allows a concrete assessment of the progress of the implementation of these measures. finally, i believe it is the responsibility of the european institutions to initiate a reform in this respect, involving all decision-makers. at the same time, joint action by national authorities, trade unions and employers is needed to eliminate this type of hidden discrimination.
i would like to congratulate you on the strong message you have conveyed today to the whole of the european union, to congratulate you on your pro-european attitude, because today we need more europe than ever, we need to lift all restrictions on the internal market, we need solidarity, and i am referring to schengen, i know and understand your position on schengen, but not only the restrictions imposed on the danish borders, but also the postponement of romania and bulgaria's accession to the schengen area is a barrier, and i would like you to make it clear what your position is on romania and bulgaria's accession to the schengen area. i am counting heavily on your capacity for dialogue, on the positive energy you are giving off, and i am confident that you will send a clear message to the council that romania and bulgaria's accession to the schengen area is not in the interests of the two countries, but of the whole european union. good luck with that.
in writing. - mr prime minister. i congratulate you on your achievements at home despite the economic crisis, but also on the pragmatic, optimistic speech you have just delivered. he mentioned the past, which is the only thing that can make you think about the future. poland has - as in the current economic crisis - shown throughout history how to manage difficult situations. as a transylvanian hungarian, i would like to highlight the role of our common ruler, istván báthory in stabilizing the region. i was pleased to read that among the polish priorities, poland wants to pursue the enlargement process in an 'open european spirit'; wants to help with the democratic transition in relation to the north african states; stresses the need to accelerate economic growth; considers it important to ensure the application of fundamental rights and the protection of minorities and to allow the free movement of people. i am convinced that europe must show this open face, not a closed, rejecting europe, looking out from behind the schengen borders in fear. as a minority, you should not forget the poles in lithuania, but also the other european minorities. good luck to poland in achieving the tasks of the presidency.
mr president, i would like to join the line of those welcoming this report, especially its practical recommendations. with this report, our parliament shows vision and provides concrete policy tools to address challenges to come. it provides a focus for the eu 2020 strategy by addressing the new job creation objectives. this is just one of the many important contributions of the epp group to this report. it calls for a new generation of eu funding programmes to support innovative and job-creating smes. education and youth are core elements of the eu 2020 strategy. they will remain a foundation of our efforts to promote innovation, growth and sustainability. without the implementation of the educational policy tools, the eu 2020 strategy will fail. this report paves the way for a new eu internship programme involving both the private sector and smes, and proposes the introduction of a european innovation scholarship, which should contribute to the fostering of the knowledge and skills of those employed in innovative sectors. i am confident that this house will support the crisis report with a large majority. therefore, i urge the european commission and the member states to consider the rapid implementation of the specific programmes in the field of smes and education strategy.
in writing. recently, a third member state was forced to ask for help from the european union, unable to obtain funding. in the current context of the sovereign debt crisis and the fragility of the european economy, we need greater integration at political and economic level. in this respect, i welcome the report on the financial, economic and social crisis, which stresses the importance of relaunching the european project. to break the deadlock, the european union needs to make long-term investments in key areas such as education, research, and road and information infrastructure. they would both increase competitiveness and counter job losses. we need a single taxation policy at european level to encourage these investments. the creation of bonds for the joint issuance of part of the european public debt would also automatically lower the cost of financing in the european union.
the report of the special committee on the financial, economic and social crisis underlines that both agricultural and cohesion policies should play a key role in the europe 2020 strategy. the reform of the common agricultural policy must be designed to meet global challenges and cohesion policy must be designed with clear objectives to promote competitiveness. in most of the new member states, farmers rely on the current system of the cap and expect cohesion policy to focus on basic infrastructure investments, where we are far behind the old member states. the eu 2020 strategy must serve the development of the eu as a whole, which is unthinkable without the development of the lagging regions, the preservation of the original objectives of the agricultural policy and the cohesion policy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on a comprehensive approach to the protection of personal data in the european union. the eu needs to equip itself, after an in-depth impact assessment, with a comprehensive, coherent, modern and high-level framework capable of effectively protecting the fundamental rights of individuals, in particular the right to privacy, with regard to the processing of personal data, in order to be able to meet the many challenges posed by globalisation, technological development, the intensification of online activities and the fight against terrorism. such a data protection framework can increase legal certainty, minimise administrative burden, ensure a level playing field for all economic operators, stimulate the digital single market and boost confidence in the behaviour of data controllers and law enforcement authorities.
in writing. − this european parliament motion for a resolution on a comprehensive approach to the protection of personal data in the european union is important because data protection in the eu is guaranteed as a fundamental human right by article 8 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. a global approach to data protection is also required by technological developments, which have created new threats to the protection of personal data and led to a large increase in the use of information technology for normal, everyday purposes. full harmonisation at the highest level is therefore required to guarantee legal certainty and a uniformly high level of protection of persons in all situations. last but not least, this motion for a resolution provides further clarification of the rules on applicable law in order to provide the same degree of protection for individuals regardless of the geographical location of the data controller, including in the case of the application of data protection law by authorities or in court.
in writing. − the introduction of new rules for consumer information on food marketed in the community is primarily aimed at enabling consumers to make healthier and more informed choices when buying food. it is not enough, however, for the european citizen to be able to choose freely between the various products. it is essential that he make a conscious choice based on the health benefits or harms that a food product may have. i therefore believe that the fight in the future must be directed towards informing european citizens of the importance which consulting all the information elements on food labels can have in maintaining and guaranteeing a healthy lifestyle. at the same time, the new regulations will also make life easier for food producers by providing legal certainty, less red tape and much improved legislation.
in writing. − consumers will be able to make more informed and healthier choices when buying food as a result of the implementation of new food labelling rules. at a time when food-borne illnesses are one of the leading causes of death, it is important to shop with information and to know the exact amounts of fats, fatty acids, carbohydrates, carbohydrates, proteins, and salt. in addition, consumers will know exactly where certain foods come from, which are not required to be specified at present. this is important, since product labels can often be misleading. the new food labelling rules will help educate the european consumer, who, while spending more time on the shelves, will learn what is healthy and what is not and should only be eaten occasionally. in time, there will likely be a discouragement of those manufacturers of profoundly unhealthy products whose sales could be reduced by detailed ingredient listings. it is true that it will be at least five years before the european market is uniform and the new rules are implemented. but it is never too late.
in writing. − while the original objectives and main components of the current labelling legislation are still valid, it needs to be streamlined to ensure that it is easier for stakeholders to comply with and to benefit from greater clarity to take account of new developments in food information. this regulation will serve both the interests of the internal market by simplifying legislation, ensuring legal certainty and reducing red tape, and the interests of citizens by imposing mandatory labelling of foodstuffs in a clear, legible and understandable manner.
in writing. − the text voted by parliament is a very good compromise, as it is the consumers who will benefit from choosing healthier food. in the future, consumers will be able to identify details such as energy value, amounts of lipids, saturated fatty acids, carbohydrates, carbohydrates, proteins and salt on food packaging much more quickly. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a directive on the protection of consumers in the event of a fire, and that the council adopt a directive on the protection of consumers in the event of a fire.
in writing. − under the new labelling rules, the energy value, amounts of lipids, saturated fatty acids, carbohydrates, carbohydrates, proteins and salt will have to be clearly visible on food packaging. allergens will have to be highlighted in the list of ingredients. country of origin will become mandatory for fresh meat from pigs, sheep, goats and poultry, and not only for beef as was the case until now. consumers will be informed about the specific source of origin of vegetable oils used in various products, such as palm oil. in addition, there will be strict rules to prevent consumers from being misled by the way food is packaged and rules for the labelling of 'counterfeit foods' such as cheese or ham. the compromise reached between the ep and the council will ensure better legibility of labels, thus allowing consumers to find the information they need more easily when shopping, thus allowing them to make informed and healthier choices when purchasing food. the new rules will modernise, simplify and clarify food labelling across the eu. the new law will also reduce red tape for producers and food business operators and strengthen the single market.
in writing. − road safety in the european union will only benefit from the implementation of the directive institutionalizing the exchange of vehicle registration information between member states. it will allow serious road accidents to be traced throughout the union and will ensure equality before the law for european citizens, regardless of the member state in which they live. the union will have safer roads when the directive is implemented. it's a very important first step towards increased road safety and, considering that it's being done after three years of negotiations, it's all the more important. we are moving towards the ideal situation where no perpetrator of a crime or misdemeanour will ever get away with it because he does not live in the state where he committed the crime. the authorities of the country where the offence was committed will then send the offender a registered letter informing him of the type of offence committed and the applicable sanction, possible remedies and legal consequences. the fine and the conditions of its application shall be determined in accordance with the rules of the state in which the offence was committed. i hope that the directive will be adopted by the council of ministers soon and that it will enter into force on the date set.
in writing. − the commission has to deliver a 2012 work programme primarily oriented towards growth, job creation, a rise in living standards, mobility, guaranteeing a good level of security and social protection for citizens, while promoting europe’s competitiveness and capacity as a global actor. the main priority of the 2012 programme and the years after should be the exit process out of the crisis, for the benefit of our citizens, with a fair share of responsibility to be borne by those who caused or amplified it. it is necessary to develop and implement a strategy to halve child poverty by 2020, to mainstream individual children’s rights in all eu policies and to promote measures to monitor and evaluate steps undertaken to end child poverty at national level. moreover, the revision of the directive on maternity leave must be adopted as a matter of urgency. the commission should develop specific policies to ensure the transition towards a green and smart growth, especially as regards worker re-skilling for green jobs and assistance for greening european industry in the context of global markets, as well as encouraging the private sector to invest in low-emissions technologies that are favourable to innovation and job creation.
in writing. − in the european union, the number of cases of transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (tses) has decreased dramatically in recent years. it is important evidence that the community measures to eradicate the std have worked. however, this downward trend should not lead to less stringent supervision and control measures in the future. the primary objective of any measures in this area must continue to be to ensure the highest level of consumer protection and food safety. i therefore encourage member states to continue to exercise vigilance and to closely monitor the evolution of transmissible spongiform encephalopathies in the event of a recurrence in animals or humans.
in writing. − the number of positive bse cases in the eu fell from 2 167 cases in 2001 to 67 cases in 2009. therefore, the tse legislation may be amended in the future, while ensuring and maintaining a high level of animal and public health standards in the european union. these changes could include measures related to the disposal of specified risk material (srs), the revision of the provisions on the total ban on animal meal, the eradication of scrapie, the slaughter of cohorts and the monitoring of the evolution/involution of the ets by correlating member states' reports. i call on the commission and the member states to take measures to ensure that the requirements of the legislation in force in this area are respected and that the possibility of illegal diversion in the feed chain is excluded. i call on the commission and the member states to continue to be vigilant and to closely monitor the evolution of tse in the event of a recurrence of tse/bse. i would stress that consumer protection, animal health and the eradication of tses must always be the overriding objectives and have priority importance when considering changes to the current rules.
in writing. - i voted for the report by mr de grandes pascual because i believe it deals with a subject of great importance in the context of the international fight against terrorism. i consider that the measure prohibiting the access of liquids on board aircraft was justified at the time it was adopted. technology did not yet allow for rapid scanning, and prevention was the most effective way to reduce the risk of an attack. with a view to lifting this restriction in 2013, cooperation between the european and national institutions needs to be stepped up. therefore, there is a need to review the control mechanisms at airports to ensure the same level of safety as at present. at the same time, it is important that passenger rights are respected, regardless of the nature of the new aviation security measures. the proportionality of the actions taken by states towards their citizens must therefore remain a priority in all circumstances.
in writing. − the european parliament has given an important signal by voting on the report on airport body scanners. security is very important but you cannot pay any price for it. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of personal data. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be given the right to adopt a decision on the application of the principle of proportionality. body scanners are currently not included in the list of control methods and technologies that have the capability to detect hidden objects in clothing - a list established in the eu aviation security legal framework. the european commission is to propose a set of rules that will add body scanners to the list of authorised eu-wide search methods. but this does not mean that parliament will not be able to reject the commission's proposal. the fact that they could affect the health of passengers is an important detail that needs to be resolved before approving one or the other of these technologies.
in writing. − the whole analysis leads to the conclusion that promoting greater representation of women must in future be an unconditional necessity for enterprises. indeed, they must implement arrangements that encourage women to aspire to management positions, in particular by increasing career opportunities, prospects within the company. it is essential that enterprises set targets for increased female participation, in parallel with the recruitment of women to top positions in the enterprise hierarchy, so as to promote equality and diversity. increased representation of women in decision-making positions would also ensure that discrimination against employees is tackled, as statistics show that 53% of women worldwide are in a vulnerable position in the workplace.
in writing. − an equal participation of women and men in decision-making is a democratic and economic necessity and all the more important in the current economic situation, where all talent needs to be mobilised. although many structural barriers have been removed through legislation in order to promote gender equality in corporate management, men continue to predominate in leadership positions. today, only one out of 10 board members of the largest companies listed on the national stock exchanges of eu member states is a woman, and progress has been slow in recent years. the disparity is widest at the very top, where only 3% of such companies have a woman directing the highest decision-making body. member states and the commission should consider introducing new policies enabling more women to become involved in managing companies, in particular by: initiating a dialogue with the management of large companies about ways of increasing female representation; supporting initiatives to assess male-female equality on recruitment committees and in other areas, e.g. with regard to wage differentials and career patterns and developing women’s individual capabilities in-house, by means of specific further training courses and other forms of professional support, in order to prepare them effectively for management duties.
in writing. − although signs suggest that the wave of negative effects generated by the economic and financial crisis has passed, social reality and the global macroeconomic landscape show that a return to normalcy is a difficult process. in the context of rising sovereign debts and the inability of some states to rebalance their public spending, the concept of democracy on credit or government on borrowing, which characterises some eu member states, is increasingly being discussed. the critical moment for these member states has not passed, and that is why i agree with the rapporteur that the competent institutions must monitor present or future systemic risks very closely. to take firm steps to get out of the grey area of the effects of the crisis, we need an intra-european balance. the high potential that the coordination of fiscal policies can have in rebalancing european budgets is, in my view, one of the solutions that must be considered in the medium and long term.

in writing. - the crisis is far from over and we can expect the economic situation to worsen at any time, both in europe and globally. the current situation of young people in the european union, where the unemployment rate is 21%, and in some member states even exceeds the 40% threshold, is worrying and makes them the main category affected by the economic crisis. i believe that the main efforts to create jobs must focus on youth employment. to do this, we need to integrate the needs of young people into community employment strategies, develop programmes to equip young people with the skills needed in the real economy, promote their opportunities to specialise or work in another member state and support the development of entrepreneurship among young people through specific vocational training, access to european funds and business advice.

mr president, i want to congratulate the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy on the work that has been done during this period of very complex events in the arab world and north africa. i also want today to raise concerns about the repression of children in syria, which reached a new level of horror with the release at the end of may of a video showing the body of hamza al-khatib. hamza was only 13 years old. he was arrested among other protestors in saida on 29 april 2011. a month later, his body was returned to his family, and it was obvious that the boy had been through severe torture during his detention. it was reported that he had injuries and burns consistent with the use of electric-shock devices. his eyes were swollen and black. he had been shot through both arms. his neck was broken. he had suffered genital mutilation. the case of hamza is not isolated. alarming reports, testimonies and footage reveal that a significant number of children in syria are being arrested, detained and subjected to various forms of torture and degrading treatment. we ask – through this resolution here today – for the urgent release of all the children arrested and detained in syria, and we must also give urgent consideration to ways of supporting these children and their families in the near future.

madam president, ‘europe has never been so prosperous, so secure nor so free’ is the opening phrase of the european security strategy of 2003. that is only eight, not 50, years ago. we were wrong to ignore the fact that stabilising our neighbourhood – something on which that happy condition depended – is a relentless task in need of constant monitoring. from that standpoint, it has to be said that we failed. despite our extensive set of programmes and policies undertaken over years, the region, rather than being stabilised, exploded, because we committed two strategic mistakes. we approached the entire effort mainly bureaucratically and we talked only to the people in power, avoiding deeper probing into those societies. then, how did we react when all was suddenly in flames? with a lot of effort and some luck – the new reality coinciding with our neighbourhood policy review – we managed to put in extra money, directed more effectively towards the real needs of these societies in profound transformation, while establishing contact with the emerging leaderships there. however, let us not fool ourselves: we are in for a huge, long-term effort of supporting state-building, which requires a strategic rather than a bureaucratic approach, and the end of which, we hope, will be a more balanced and intimate relationship with these regions, without our customary arrogance of appearing to know best what others really need.
the failure of nato operations in libya and the european union's inability to bring about an end to the bloody reprisals in syria and bahrain and to stop the situation in yemen from degenerating into civil conflict demonstrate the limited scope for action and influence of the european union and nato in a region shaken by conflicts with major implications for europe. i believe that a un resolution is needed on the rapidly worsening situation in syria and that european sanctions against the assad regime, which is itself at war with its own people, should be tightened. i believe that without a more effective european engagement in the region, we risk destroying the credibility of nato and the european union, against the backdrop of the deteriorating situation of civilians, both in syria and yemen, and in libya, where human lives are lost every day and civilians are not protected from attacks by the gaddafi regime.
written. – after months of intervention and non-action, wishful thinking and short-sightedness, strategic confusion and tactical opportunism, an assessment of the spring 2011 developments in the arab world and north africa shows the following: 1. the events are a replica of the geostrategic quake which took place in eastern and central europe in 1989; 2. notwithstanding the specificity of each country concerned, the general refusal of the people to accept authority (in whatever form) any longer constitutes the common triggering factor; 3. similarly to 1989, the transformation was not prepared or initiated by the euro-atlantic democracies; 4. the euro-atlantic players are trying, again as with 1989, to become protagonists by exporting their democratic model post-factum; 5. as usual, the euro-atlantic players, desirous to externalise their internal crises or to fulfil their national geopolitical ambitions, apply multiple standards, thus undermining the coherence of any future regional policy; 6. external military intervention can only undermine the equilibrium and complicate the situation. against this background, one can understand why, after unwisely trying to behave like an international cop, the eu, too divided to be strong and too nervous to be prudent, has no perspective; but one can only hope that things will eventually end well. unfortunately, hope is not a policy!

madam president, i would like to thank the high representative for her detailed statement. the russian decision to block the registration of a credible political party prior to the elections is not an aberration, it is yet another example of russia’s refusal to play by the rules while claiming to be a genuinely democratic post-soviet entity. but politically motivated killings, kidnappings and jailings, sanctioned by a corrupt justice system or ignored by the judicial authorities, are a common feature of the russian democracy. indeed one can say that the russian authorities perfected democracy to the point where opposition is not necessary any more and the voters are no longer essential. but if russia is not willing to be honest with its own people we should not expect honesty in russia’s relations with the eu. it might take one to kozachok, but it surely takes two to tango. so i call on you and the commission to make any further negotiations with russia conditional on the fair preparation and conduct of the elections in december. human rights and democracy should be at the centre of our relationship with russia, and if we are ready to reset our relations with russia then russia should reset its own relations with democracy.
