vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − madam president, honourable members, thank you again. i found that a very interesting and stimulating debate. as we think about how to address some of the areas of concern that honourable members have quite rightly raised, i just want to make three very straightforward points. first of all we have to continue to articulate our expectations to russia as far as free and fair elections are concerned, and we will recall the international commitments that russia has taken in this regard. i think it is very important as we move towards the elections that we continue to send that strong message: that we want to see these elections be fair and free; that we want to see the international commitments fully followed. secondly, we want as well to offer our election observation. i said earlier that consultations between russia and osce/odihr are ongoing; they seem keen to cooperate; i hope that will happen and that this will also help in the light of some of the comments that honourable members have made about the need to look at the long-term nature of observation. thirdly we also need, and again members made this clear, to make sure that at the level of the modernisation partnership we are working closely to help support that process. we currently have 16 bilateral partnerships, and these look at issues like foreign investment, know-how, technology as well as the rule of law of modern democratic institutions and civil society involvement. because i think it is also clear from what honourable members have said that we want to send a very clear message to the people of russia that we are a supportive friend, that we want to see progress, we want to see modernisation and we want also to be source of inspiration when it comes to the democratic values we hold and our absolute passion for human rights.
in writing. i welcome the high representative's statement at such an important moment for any democracy in the world. i believe that a genuine eu-russia partnership must be based not only on common interests but also on shared principles and values. respect for the rule of law and fundamental rights and freedoms is necessarily one of them. it is essential that russia live up to expectations of democratic standards in the preparation and conduct of the elections in december 2011. political pluralism is a defining characteristic of modern societies. by organising free and fair elections, a diversity of opinions, views and options is ensured. in this way, the russian authorities can make a significant contribution not only to strengthening the democratic character of the state but also to providing a viable model for neighbouring countries.
in writing. russia is one of our main partners. it is also a member state of the council of europe and the osce. we therefore give it special attention in the discussions in the european parliament. five months ago, we passed a resolution expressing doubts about the rule of law in russia. last month, in paragraph 12 of the resolution on the eu-russia summit, i stressed the need for free and fair elections, by implementing the standards set by the council of europe and the osce. we are forced to return to this subject, in the context of the fact that the parnas party has been denied the right to participate in the next parliamentary elections. it's an unfortunate decision. some of the procedures for the registration of political parties and lists of candidates used in russia have been found to be unjustified. they have become an obstacle to free and fair elections. it is essential for the credibility of the december elections that the russian authorities allow the osce/council of europe to conduct long-term election observation missions. in this way, the international community will be able to see whether there is progress in russia's democratization or whether it is a sham democracy.
on behalf of the alde group. – madam president, over the last few months the european union has been confronted with several challenges. as if the economic crisis and the efforts to overcome it were not enough, some member states have added another sensitive point to the agenda. instead of welcoming the switch to democratic regimes in some countries in northern africa, and instead of putting more energy and imagination into assisting the peoples there, a couple of governments – ironically, eu founder-members – afraid that 25 000 people entering the eu would affect their stability, considered that the best way to protect their own borders would be to close them. they had the idea that a new mechanism, profoundly affecting the schengen area and free movement, should be allowed. other governments consider that reinstating border controls is an efficient way to fight organised crime, as if criminals follow rules. the alde group has been very firm and vocal from the very beginning. we do not want – and we will not accept – any new mechanism that may affect the schengen acquis, the very spirit of eu integration. instead, we are ready and have already started working towards better schengen governance for better protection of the eu external borders – while fully respecting the human rights of those trying to reach them – and towards full implementation of the principle of solidarity among member states. politicians who believe that european citizens will like them as a result of this initiative are very wrong. they may get some votes in their own countries in the next elections as politicians, but they will not be forgiven for not acting as great statesmen in the interest of all european citizens, including their own. only the preservation of schengen and its acquis is a win-win situation.
the changes recently proposed in the european council to improve the so-called schengen governance are inconsistent and endanger the free movement of european citizens. the proposal is a serious attack on the integrity of the schengen area, which should be based on mutual trust and solidarity between member states. we cannot accept that situations currently defined as exceptional should be multiplied by a new mechanism, because we would give the possibility to governments with populist nationalist tendencies to use this to promote their anti-unionist policies. we already have the example of denmark, which is violating both the schengen acquis and the principles of the single market, under the closed eyes of the commission, the guarantor of the treaties. finally, i would draw the council's attention to the fact that its lack of transparency and its intention to exclude parliament from adopting the new mechanism or any other legislative proposal is unacceptable and constitutes a serious breach of the treaties.
what is happening now with internal border controls cannot be accepted. the schengen credibility is undermined by the fact that the union does not have a mechanism that can be triggered if a member state fails to properly fulfil its responsibilities at the external border of the union. the solution is to change the intergovernmental approach to a coordinated mechanism at union level. in the event of problems at the external borders, measures should be taken to support the member states concerned, in particular through the intervention of frontex. the reintroduction of controls should apply as a last resort and only if, even after granting the support, the member state is not able to remedy the deficiency within 6 months. in this case, i think it is right to establish financial compensatory measures to support the member states affected by the reintroduction of internal border controls. such a mechanism would avoid situations where a member state unilaterally introduces controls at its borders.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, on behalf of the commission i would also like to congratulate you and i wish you lots of success in your new position. as you will see, you will often have your hands full handling debates as lively and important as today’s. i would also like to thank all the members of the european parliament who supported schengen and who made it absolutely clear that schengen represents freedom and reunification of europe, openness and also togetherness of european nations and european citizens in the european union. this debate also confirmed that it is true that the schengen system has come under pressure recently. we must do everything possible to upgrade it and make it stronger than before. we need to start by restoring trust. we need to maintain mutual trust in our capacity, the capacity of us all, to fully comply with the obligations imposed on us to preserve an area without internal border controls. therefore schengen needs a stronger monitoring and evaluation system. the commission is looking into the possibilities for further strengthening this new mechanism aiming to bring an adequate response to a situation where a member state fails to fulfil its obligations at the external borders. a series of measures could be envisaged at eu level to assist a member state facing heavy pressure at the external borders. it would include inspection visits, technical and financial support, including the participation of frontex. i think we all agree that we need a complex and comprehensive approach to this problem. we are therefore talking about a complete set of measures including an eu-based mechanism, strengthened schengen governance, evaluation and reinforcement of frontex and further guidelines and recommendations to better explain the existing rules. this has to be seen in parallel with the completion of a common asylum system in 2012, where – as we know – we also very often have big divergences in how the asylum system is applied and how asylum status is granted to refugees. i would reiterate once again that we are fully aware in the commission of the crucial importance of free movement for the eu and its future. therefore the commission strongly believes that the proposal for the mechanism should be based on article 77 of the tfeu. this means that the proposal will be subject to ordinary legislative procedure, thus ensuring full involvement of parliament on an equal footing with the council. if you allow me, i should like to conclude on denmark, because several of you have referred to the recent and current developments in denmark. i would like to inform you that on 28 june the commission received a reply from denmark to our questions. the reply is now being carefully evaluated by all the commission services concerned in order to decide if all the commission questions have been answered and if all relevant information has been provided. as i said in my introductory remarks, we are fully aware of our important role as a guardian of the treaties, and we will do our utmost to ensure that all rules, all acquis, and the schengen acquis in this particular context, are fully respected.
in writing. the proposal to amend the schengen system comes at a time when the eu is facing an unprecedented wave of immigration. the message we must convey, the message of a united europe, is confronted by a reality that cannot leave us indifferent. the solutions we need to pursue are those that reconcile european values and current challenges. so we cannot encourage the reintroduction of border controls, especially because there is a risk that certain states will use this opportunity to exacerbate xenophobic tendencies, but we cannot remain passive either. we can only accept the reintroduction of border controls with clear criteria of conditionality, which do not affect the schengen acquis and which are already provided for in regulation 562/2006. the problems caused by the influx of migrants must be solved by sharing responsibility between the signatory states of the acquis. moreover, we must not forget that these problems stem from the reluctance to implement common european policies in other areas, firstly a common european asylum and immigration system (including an approach to illegal immigration and to fight organised crime). but this deadlock must not be reinforced by even more drastic measures that undermine the eu's core values.
in writing. membership of schengen entails the full freedom of movement of nationals of a member state within this area and the total abolition of border controls between member states. the security of the schengen area depends on the rigour and effectiveness with which each schengen member state carries out controls at the eu's external borders. the free movement of persons is one of the fundamental principles of the union and the completion of the internal market is based on the free movement of goods, services and persons. the schengen area is one of the eu's main achievements and it is therefore important to promote and defend the principles that govern it. the economic and financial crisis should not be invoked as a justification for the introduction by certain member states of restrictions on the free movement of persons. i reiterate my firm opposition to any new schengen mechanism having other objectives than the strengthening of the free movement of persons. we cannot have double standards in the schengen area and i regret the attempt by some member states to unilaterally reintroduce checks at the internal borders of the union. i ask the commission to assess as a matter of urgency the respect of the community and schengen acquis in the event of the decision taken by the united kingdom of denmark to re-introduce border controls at its borders.
the programme for the most deprived persons is one of the best known and most appreciated european programmes by the citizens of the european union, as it supports the provision of food to particularly vulnerable individuals or families who are in a difficult situation. in the european union, 43 million people cannot afford to eat a full meal every two days, and the economic and financial crisis has increased the number. in 2009, 18 million citizens in 19 member states benefited from 440 000 tonnes of food. we support continuing the programme and returning to the budget of 500 million euros a year. i believe it is urgent to find sources of funding for the programme for the period 2011-2013 and then to establish a sustainable solution, including from a legal point of view, for the period 2014-2020. the un report on the food crisis requires us to act immediately and responsibly.
although europe has the highest standard of living in the world, millions of people are unable to obtain the food they need. by reducing the total funding for the programme to provide food to the most deprived people in the european union, many people will be deprived of a fundamental right, the right to food. the court of justice's ruling must be matched by the need to find solutions for the continuation of the programme in the medium and long term, on a permanent basis and in line with the legal situation. the common agricultural policy is a social policy, in which not only farmers but all european citizens, as taxpayers, must be represented. supporting people in need is therefore a responsibility that must demonstrate unity in diversity at european level.
we are more than 30 years away from the first direct elections for members of the european parliament and i welcome mr duff's report. however, i do not support the idea of transnational lists, because that would mean creating two categories of members of the european parliament: some who are elected in national constituencies, and others who should be elected on the basis of a european-level constituency. i wanted to stress this, because it is important that the members of the european parliament be equal, and therefore that they can represent the citizens of the member states.
i believe that mr van orden's report brings into question one of the security risks that still plagues europe. antipersonnel mines have been used extensively in conflicts such as the one in the balkans, continuing to cause civilian casualties. demining former conflict zones is costly and time-consuming. not all affected states have the necessary funds for such an activity. for this reason, the return of the inhabitants is difficult and there is a risk of accidents. i believe that better coordination between international donors would ensure legal support for the gradual demining of conflict zones. it is also important to involve local authorities in this process, which will be beneficial to them. in this context, i also call on the specialized non-governmental organizations to concentrate their efforts and put an end to this problem.
in writing. − the percentage of the european population aged over 60 will increase at a much faster rate than before. this is a consequence of improved health care services and quality of life. however, the eu is facing a sharp decline in population in some regions, with severe pressure on pension funds and problems with financial resources for health care and public services. a key way to address these challenges is to promote the creation of a sustainable culture of active ageing, thus ensuring that the population segment of people approaching or over 60 years of age has appropriate opportunities for active participation in social life, cultural expression and sport, taking into account the positive contribution of these activities to mental and physical health. ageing is a challenge for society as a whole and for all generations, but it is also about solidarity between generations and the role of the family. promoting a culture of active ageing therefore requires a multidimensional approach throughout the life course and solidarity between generations.
in writing. − i was the virtual rapporteur of the socialists and democrats in the european parliament for the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the european year of active ageing (2012). the proposed initiative aims to support and encourage the efforts of member states, local authorities, social partners and civil society to promote active ageing and to make more efforts to exploit the potential of the population over 50 years of age. the european year should therefore serve as a framework for raising awareness, identifying and disseminating good practices and, most importantly, encouraging decision-makers and stakeholders at all levels to promote active ageing, social inclusion and the effective use of the experience of older workers.
in writing. − to promote active ageing, it is of the utmost importance to strengthen solidarity and cooperation between generations. this solidarity should not be approached from a purely financial perspective but should also be seen in a broader context that includes promoting mutual cooperation and exchanges between generations, so that each generation can find its place in society and contribute to european society as best it can. european society must become a society for all ages. governments and public policies need to respond to this challenge in several areas, in particular by establishing framework conditions to deal with the consequences of population ageing. the private sector, social partners and civil society, as well as individual citizens, must each contribute in their own way. all these stakeholders are key factors in providing solutions to the challenge of an ageing european society. the commission and the member states should consider mainstreaming the principle of equality between women and men, persons with disabilities, persons belonging to ethnic minorities, in particular those belonging to the roma minority, in the implementation of the european year. it is also important to promote good health and a high quality of life, including by ensuring access to high-quality health care services.
in writing. - i support this resolution and express the hope that the violent repression in syria and yemen will end. the moment a leader or a ruling class chooses violence to maintain power, the legitimacy of their decisions suffers greatly. when innocent women and children are among the victims, the situation must be condemned in unison by all who believe in the values of democracy, freedom of expression and the right of a citizen to challenge his own rulers.
in writing. − firstly, the report stresses the importance of eu external policies by underlining the fact that partnerships based on dialogue and consultation on the protection of human rights must constitute a real priority in its policy towards third countries. secondly, i believe that the democratisation process has to go hand-in-hand with social and economic development in third countries. thirdly, the report gives a special place to civil society, which has proven to be a pillar of democracy. this is why i voted in favour of véronique de keyser’s report.
in writing. − the eu needs to shift from a stability to a democracy paradigm. in the area of human rights and democracy, it needs to establish greater consistency between its values and democracy as it is actually practised, between its internal and its external policies, and between the institutions. the eu consequently has a duty, through its different programmes, to strengthen its support for civil society and social movements (trade unions, mutual societies, women’s networks and youth networks), supporting the spread of those movements. however, it must also take steps to promote the freedom of expression of independent media and the protection of journalists and human rights defenders. it is important to emphasise the need for a gender perspective in the implementation of the guidelines, with targeted actions in favour of female human rights defenders and other particularly vulnerable groups, such as journalists and defenders working to promote economic, social and cultural rights, children's rights, and minority rights. i underline the necessity for women's full participation in all areas of peace and security in order to enhance conflict prevention, ensure sustainable peace and develop specific training programs allowing female entrepreneurs to increase their participation in world trade.
in writing. − i consider the european council's initiative to amend the schengen rules to be unacceptable. i regret that the leaders of some member states want to punctuate elections with the risk of diluting one of the eu's most important achievements and one of the most visible positive aspects for european citizens. these proposed amendments denote a dual attitude of the eu. on the one hand, european leaders are speaking in solidarity with arab peoples who aspire to democracy, while on the other, refugees are being denied access to the eu on the grounds that migration flows would be excessive. i do not dispute that when all refugees arrive in one member state, such a situation can present difficulties. but it is precisely for this reason that we need more solidarity between member states and the finalisation of a common european asylum system and a genuine common immigration policy. the solution to making schengen more efficient is not to reintroduce controls, which would amount to destroying the schengen area, but to introduce complementary mechanisms for jointly managing migration flows. i refuse to subscribe to these proposals and hope that we can concentrate on the real problems of the schengen area, leaving aside such diversions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the adoption of the european parliament resolution on the amendments to the schengen system, as the creation of the schengen area and the integration of the schengen acquis within the eu is one of the greatest achievements of the european integration process, meaning the absence of internal border controls and unprecedented freedom of movement within the european union. freedom of movement has become one of the basic elements of european citizenship and one of the cornerstones of the eu as an area of freedom, security and justice, enshrining the right to free movement and residence in all member states under conditions of equal rights, guarantees and protections, including the prohibition of all forms of discrimination based on nationality. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to apply the schengen acquis to all third-country nationals who are not nationals of the member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the amendments to the schengen system. it has a positive impact on the lives of hundreds of thousands of eu citizens, not only by making it easier to cross borders, but also by boosting the economy. support the strengthening of schengen governance to ensure that each member state can effectively control its own part of the eu's external borders, to build confidence in the effectiveness of the eu migration management system. i would stress that the correct and proper implementation of the schengen rules by the member states must be guaranteed, even after their accession. the conditions for the temporary reintroduction of internal border controls in exceptional situations are already clearly laid down in regulation 562/2006 (schengen borders code). i consider that the influx of migrants and asylum seekers at the external borders cannot in any case be considered as an additional reason for reintroducing border controls. we call on the commission to present an initiative aimed at defining the strict application of articles 23, 24 and 25 of the schengen borders code. i consider that any new additional derogations from the current rules, such as new grounds for reintroducing border controls for 'exceptional' situations, will in no way strengthen the schengen system.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the ep resolution because interparliamentary cooperation is given a central role in the new eu treaty in order to build genuine democratic legitimacy. the contribution of national parliaments to shaping the common foreign and security policy is particularly useful. articles 9 and 10 provide for specialised committees as a working instrument, which gives greater flexibility to the procedure. i believe that the exchange of good practice between delegations contributes to improving the consultation process and to a faster adaptation to the other union mechanisms. i welcome the creation of an initiative by the conference of parliamentary bodies to bring relevant issues to the attention of the european institutions. communication with national authorities in this way will facilitate foreign policy decision-making at european level. interparliamentary cooperation is also a way of increasing the representation of citizens in the political processes of the union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the programme for the distribution of food to the most deprived persons in the union, as the european commission estimates that 80 million people in the eu are at risk of poverty and that, because of the financial and economic crisis, their number could increase, and one of the five priorities of the eu 2020 strategy is to reduce poverty and social exclusion in the european union. it is an essential form of solidarity at a time when conservative policies, national egos and social disparities are putting the most deprived of our fellow citizens at a disadvantage.
i join those who condemn the killings in south kivu province and sexual violence as a weapon of war. local sources indicate that about 40 rapes are committed daily, and often the perpetrators are members of the military or armed groups. during this time, medical, social, and legal assistance for victims is lacking, and perpetrators go unpunished and uninvestigated. the protection of the 170 victims and witnesses is necessary to allow for an urgent, independent and impartial investigation to punish the perpetrators of the june violence. we insist on ending this situation and the culture of impunity. i call on the commission to urgently release additional funds to combat sexual violence and provide assistance to victims. the financial pressure of the european union must be used for this cause.
it is not the first time that we have drawn attention to the situation in the congo and we condemn in the strongest possible terms not only the atrocities committed with a frightening rhythm in that country but also the passivity of the congolese authorities. in the last five months, only 11 military personnel have appeared in court charged with rape. but reports from non-governmental organizations say that 400,000 women have been raped in the congo in the last decade, and according to statistics, 48 women are raped every hour. this humanitarian crisis is amplified by impunity and prejudice that turn rape into a taboo, otherwise, victims risk exclusion from their families and communities. this is the case for many of the 121 women who reported being raped in june in south kivu province. i call on the commission to devote more funds and attention to the creation of care centres for victims and to actions for their family and social reintegration. i also renew the call for the creation of an international criminal tribunal for the congo, the only viable solution against impunity. i also call on the authorities of european countries to facilitate the obtaining of residence permits for rape victims seeking refuge in the european union.
i am deeply outraged by the mass rapes that took place in june in south kivu province. unfortunately, the democratic republic of congo has been, for the past 20 years, the scene of some of the most deadly conflicts since world war ii, over 5 million, and already has a sad tradition of atrocities and grave human rights violations. i believe that the european union must show solidarity, support the victims of these atrocities and, as far as possible, help to find a lasting solution to the extremely difficult situation in the democratic republic of congo. but now, as soon as possible, the european union must provide financial assistance to combat sexual violence and to assist victims of such violence. the number one priority must be to provide adequate medical care and support for the integration of these victims into congolese society. we'll have to make sure that the money actually reaches the victims and is used for assistance.
of course, i have read a number of studies that show how many rapes are taking place in the republic of congo at this time, but i think it is worse what my colleague veronique de keyser told me, who was there and saw how much suffering there is among the population, how much terror, especially among women and children. this situation must end and we, the institutions of the european union, must firmly demand here in parliament that the congolese authorities carry out all the necessary investigations and punish the guilty, and also provide medical, legal and psychological counselling to all the victims, who must be included in a protection programme, and also that the entire international community, especially women's organisations, react, put an end to this situation in congo.
the author. - indonesia, as we know, is an important partner of the european union in the muslim world, and it must be said that in recent years there has been progress in this country towards democracy and the protection of human rights. it is sufficient to mention, for example, the ratification of important international instruments. the situation of minorities, and particularly religious minorities, whether ahmadis, christians or buddhists, has worsened considerably. the proliferation of laws that restrict the rights of religious minorities and the increasingly violent attacks on them are evidence of the spread of intolerance in indonesia. the jakarta authorities should develop a clear strategy to ensure respect for religious freedom and promote tolerance. of course, we also need to abolish discriminatory legislation and punish those who are guilty of violence. i believe that the partnership and cooperation agreement we have with indonesia is a privileged framework to address the situation of religious freedom and minorities.
on behalf of the ppe group. the vast majority of the population of the european union is christian. the former configuration of the member states involved in integration is inseparable from christian culture, but the main reason why we must speak out against attacks on christians in indonesia and elsewhere in the world is that european states have committed themselves to a high level of protection of fundamental human rights and want to uphold this principle with their important trading partners. this courageous stand also presupposes that eu member states respect the rights of minorities living on their territory, including the recognition of the special status of indigenous national minorities. as the world's most populous predominantly muslim country, indonesia has a special responsibility for the treatment of religious and ethnic minorities on its territory. similarly, the european union has a huge responsibility to deal with its own minorities and to pay greater attention to their problems.
the recent tensions in indonesia contradict the concept of a multicultural society promoted by the authorities in recent years. i draw attention to the increasing number of attacks against religious minorities, in particular the ahmadiyya and christian communities. the indonesian authorities have a duty to take the necessary measures to protect their citizens, regardless of religion or opinion. these include investigating and adequately punishing acts of violence, including those of 6 february 2011, and combating intolerance. i call on the government in jakarta to give priority to these matters. civil society also has an important role to play in restoring social cohesion at this time. the eu, in turn, can make a concrete contribution to promoting a higher level of human rights protection through dialogue and cooperation with the indonesian authorities.
indonesia is the world's largest muslim country and a consolidated democracy. sadly, in recent years, as in more and more parts of the world, there have been acts of violence against religious minorities. religious fundamentalism is on the rise, and indonesia is one of the countries affected by this scourge. the resolution refers to a series of discriminatory acts against several minorities, which cause tensions between different communities, victims of religious intolerance. extreme cases of sharia law enforcement have also been reported, in contravention of indonesian law. i believe that we need to work more closely with the indonesian government to support the improvement of respect for the rights of all minorities in this country.
member of the commission. − madam president, the vice-president/high representative shares parliament’s concerns about discrimination against religious minorities, in particular the ahmadi and christian communities. she also shares the concerns about the impact of introduction of sharia-based laws on human rights, in particular the rights of women. i would, though, like to underline that we have good long-standing relations with indonesia, with whom we signed the first partnership and cooperation agreement in asia. the eu has raised the matter of violence against religious minorities through established channels. we have made it clear to indonesia that this problem has to be tackled seriously, based on respect and protection of beliefs, without discrimination. following the attacks last february against the ahmadiyyah, the european union issued a statement expressing strong concern, and emphasising the need for an effective response by the government. the eu delegation in jakarta met with representatives of the ahmadi community. the eu also raised this issue in the official human rights dialogue that we established with indonesia in 2010, at the meeting which took place in march in brussels. we emphasised the government’s obligation to protect all religious communities and stressed that the police should be trained, including on human rights, to respond to threats and violence against religious minorities. we are delivering practical assistance in these areas. since 2002, the eu has funded, for an amount of eur 750 000, eight projects carried out by civil society organisations. these projects are aimed at enhancing tolerance and peace and promoting pluralism and multiculturalism. we are also working with the indonesian government to foster inter-faith dialogue. last year we organised together a seminar on islam and a globalising world, which brought together ngos, government representatives, european academics and islamic religious scholars. looking ahead, we are preparing a major conference with eu and indonesian civil society in jakarta this october, on freedom of religion and protection of minorities. its recommendations will be fed into the next session of the human rights dialogue. we follow closely developments concerning the implementation of sharia-based laws, in particular in the province of aceh. we raised this question in the human rights dialogue last march. the indonesian government informed us that aceh has agreed to abide by international obligations and is in dialogue with local authorities and civil society to harmonise local by-laws with human right standards. i would also like to mention the case of the torture of papuan prisoners and the lenient sentences imposed on the soldiers convicted by a military tribunal in relation to recent cases. we discussed this issue in the human rights dialogue and underscored the need for dissuasive punishment for those who commit torture. the indonesian government is committed to ratifying the optional protocol of the convention against torture and is pursuing initiatives to build better community relations in papua. i would like to conclude by mentioning that we are also supporting indonesia in addressing the underlying causes of religious violence, such as the spread of islamic extremism in schools and in society generally. in this regard, we plan to fund a cooperation programme with indonesia aimed at deradicalisation in the context of the fight against terrorism.
written. – violence against the ahmadis (who consider themselves muslims) and other religious minorities – such as christians, bahá'ís and buddhists – as well as progressive civil society organisations has increased in indonesia. the government is lagging far behind in addressing the underlying causes. investigations have not revealed who was behind the attacks against ahmadis in february 2011. two weeks ago, a 22-year-old female pentecostal pastor was abducted by three islamic radicals. islamic extremism has spread in schools and other public areas. combating discrimination and securing the human rights of all, including minorities, should be a prerequisite for good relations between the eu and indonesia. i urge the indonesian authorities to take effective action to protect the life and personal integrity of all members of religious minorities. i call for the commission to include a binding human rights clause in the comprehensive economic partnership, insist on a moratorium on the application of blasphemy laws, and persuade the indonesian government to repeal a 2008 ban on ahmadi muslim teachings, which encourages such attacks and infringes upon the freedom of religion.
the author. − an article published in the international press on 13 june reported that the indian state of assam has no executioner available to carry out the death sentence of mahendra nath das, whose request for pardon was rejected by the country's president. another death row inmate whose request for clemency was denied is davinder pal singh. we would like such an important partner of the european union as india to respect the moratorium requested by the united nations general assembly and not execute the two men mentioned. fortunately, as you know, india has not carried out the death penalty since 2007. but we would welcome india's view, as the eu does, that the abolition of the death penalty is a factor in the promotion of human dignity. perhaps the fact that no one is found willing to carry out the death penalty is a sign that the time has come for india to ban the death penalty.

the laudable initiative to promote development as the central pillar of the multilateral trading system through the doha round is today proving to be a chimera. the opening of the doha round was necessary to address the inequalities produced by the uruguay round, which focused on the interests of rich countries to the detriment of developing and least developed countries. however, even in the current negotiations, the level of development of the participating countries has not always been taken into account. thus, in order to grant concessions on agricultural subsidies, industrialized countries have asked developing countries to reciprocate in other areas. for development to be more than a decorative principle of the doha round, there is a need for duty-free and quota-free market access for products from ldcs, as agreed at the 2005 hong kong conference, special and differential treatment for developing countries, the elimination of export subsidies for cotton by developed countries, improved preferential certificates of origin for imports from ldcs, and greater financial effort by the united states and the european union in the area of trade support. the success of the doha round depends on the credibility of the world trade organisation itself in managing global governance. the wto risks being reduced to a mere forum of inefficiency. the challenges we face, the sovereign debt crisis, the alarming unemployment rate, the volatility of food prices, illicit trade, climate change, all require global management. i therefore believe that there is a need for a rethinking of the multilateral trading system, which will enable the development objectives proposed by the doha agenda to be achieved through the wto and a more effective approach to the links between trade and global challenges. furthermore, enhanced cooperation between the wto and other international organisations and bodies, such as the food and agriculture organisation of the united nations, the international labour organisation or the united nations environment and development programmes, could lead to the creation of international standards addressing trade, social, development and environmental concerns. last but not least, i would like to draw attention to the need for more democracy and transparency in the work of the wto. if we really want free trade and economic globalisation on a level playing field, then we have to take into account more than a few factors essential to economic equilibrium, such as the need to encourage trade, especially in technology and innovation, and to avoid causes of harm to the quality of life of citizens and the environment. (the president agreed to answer a question put under the 'blue card' procedure (rule 149 (8) of the rules of procedure). )
of course we can talk. i have presented a point of view in which i have expressed my opinion, in view of what is happening after ten years in the doha programme. i think we are at the stage where we must take urgent action and we must take the most correct stance in support of the world trade organization. i don't want you to get that impression. i merely said that i think that if we continue at this rate, the wto will become a forum for discussion, a forum in which no decision is taken in favour of the development of multilateral trade.
i believe that we need a stimulating stance on the doha development agenda, which so far represents only a global attempt to put the development process at the heart of the multilateral trading system. i therefore believe that developed countries must take greater account of the needs and imbalances of developing countries and ensure that they are given special and differential treatment in accordance with previous agreements, including a derogation on services and a different monitoring mechanism. new investment is needed to boost economic recovery and stability in developing countries, many of which are affected by internal crises and disastrous conflicts. i therefore call on the european commission to continue to support the ambitious goals set out in the 2001 doha ministerial declaration, as well as the commitments made at the 2005 hong kong wto ministerial conference, by promoting development as a central objective of the doha agenda. i also believe that in the current context the european union can and must play a more active role as a mediator between the different positions of the members of the world trade organisation. in this context, i would like to recall that article 208 of the treaty of lisbon on policy coherence for development obliges the european union to take account of the impact of trade and other policies on developing countries. with a view to the 8th world trade organisation meeting in geneva, the most appropriate solutions to address the main challenges facing these countries must be identified so that trade can drive sustainable development. in particular, restrictions on exports of natural resources require comprehensive regulation at the level of international trade rules. these riches are the main source of income for many developing countries. i would also like to draw attention to the impact of emerging economies and i think it is appropriate to reiterate the call on these countries to assume their responsibility as significant global actors and to report their concessions to their own level of development and sectoral competitiveness. the changes in the last decade, stimulated and influenced by the economic crisis, may have negative effects on the doha round, which needs to be adapted in a more dynamic manner to the new global circumstances. food insecurity, caused by massive price increases and climate change, is one of the key elements to be considered in this regard. in turn, agricultural subsidies to developing countries and export subsidies to developed countries have negative effects, requiring remedies that do not affect economic balances within and between these countries.
vice-president of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the commission will remain firmly committed to a successful outcome of the doha negotiations and we are also pleased with the expressions of support in the chamber. we would obviously have preferred a much stronger multilateral commitment than the present one and to conclude these negotiations in a positive way is certainly good news, not only for us in europe but also for the rest of the world economy. i can assure you that over the next ten weeks commissioner de gucht and his staff will be stepping up their efforts and contacts and the commissioner has asked me to tell you that he will be pleased to have further discussions on the future of doha in the committee on international trade. unfortunately, as the presidency has said, commissioner de gucht had to leave the house against his will because he had to take a flight to south africa for the summit and the bilateral trade talks. we can only stress the importance of doha in keeping world markets open, in improving the functioning of markets that are already open and in opening up the market even more in accordance with the needs of a world economy in the era of globalisation, with an ever-increasing number of players, and where not all have the same economic weight; but, i repeat, the commission will do everything possible to ensure that the economy benefits from the conclusion of the doha agreements.
in writing. i would like to remind the commission that the european parliament has called for strict compliance with the negotiating mandate given by the council in the doha development agenda since last year. i also remind the commission that it is necessary to complete the debate on the future of the common agricultural policy post 2013 before making new proposals to our trading partners. i believe that the european union has already made enough concessions in the field of agriculture, including reducing support for farmers; unfortunately, the same concessions were not adopted by other negotiating states, and the situation is similar with regard to the applicable quality and food safety rules - which puts european producers at a disadvantage worldwide. the doha negotiations are a serious responsibility for the commission, and i call on it once again to give the agriculture sector the attention it needs.

i thank the rapporteur for his cooperation and for the inclusion of the amendments in the final text of the report. the european union is entirely dependent on imports of raw materials, and demand for raw materials will be driven by future developments in emerging economies and the rapid spread of related technologies. rare materials and rare earths are traded globally, with markets for certain rare materials and rare earths being less transparent and trading volumes very low compared to other materials. rare earths are used in the manufacture of watches, mobile phones and other everyday appliances. they're essential for making the permanent magnets used in wind turbines, they're essential for electric vehicles, catalytic converters for cars, electronic circuits, fiber optics and high-temperature superconductors. so rare earths are essential for the european union economy to become an eco-efficient economy. i call on the commission and the member states to develop a research and innovation programme in the future research framework programme for new materials and materials that could replace the current raw materials whose resources are scarce in the future. i also stress the need to invest in the recycling of raw materials and rare earths, as their mining, refining and recycling have serious environmental consequences if not managed properly. it is also important for resource-rich developing countries such as india and brazil. as a member of the eu-mercosur delegation, i draw attention to the 5th eu-brazil summit, which will take place on 4 october in brussels. into concrete action by the commission and the member states. finally, we ask the commission to update the list of raw materials regularly in order to keep abreast of market and technological developments.
european firms are facing intensified competition for resources, raw materials. this competition will become increasingly aggressive because, on the one hand, we are seeing population growth, especially concentrated in emerging countries, and, on the other hand, the sustained economic growth taking place in these emerging countries and intensifying the global demand for resources. in addition, the geographical location of resources in certain countries creates and complicates this competition, because some countries are inclined to use politically these resources that they have. so it's no coincidence that governments in some countries are intervening with industrial policies to support, to create advantages for firms in this global competition. we cannot help but see that some countries are using public funds to create such advantages. the european union cannot stand idly by and i appreciate the direction given in this strategy. obviously, the main effort must be made to decouple economic growth in european countries from resource consumption through innovation, through saving. at the same time, at the level of the european union, we need to support european companies more through policies that, on the one hand, encourage strategic alliances, as well as private investment in resource-rich countries and, of course, fair trade conditions in the raw materials markets.
europe faces both challenges and opportunities in raw materials. the challenge must be turned into an opportunity to reinvigorate europe's industrial power. a european industrial innovation strategy is needed to address the efficient use of raw materials in europe. the intensification of innovation in the means of using raw materials by european industries will contribute significantly to european competitiveness, sustainability and security of supply. the union must develop partnerships with third countries, strengthen negotiations on raw materials. this could create an international regulatory platform to ensure that the union is supplied with the necessary raw materials from third countries. the commission should draw up a study identifying the import dependency of european industries and the threats to raw material supply and assessing current and future prices. the study will enable industries and research institutions to engage in long-term projects and investments.
we all know that europe faces both significant challenges and opportunities in terms of raw materials. raw materials policies are also of particular importance to the european union, both in terms of industrial policy and international trade and in terms of cross-cutting policies in relation to different areas of internal policy as well as foreign and security policy. in this context, i believe that effective monitoring of agricultural raw materials policies is essential for an effective strategy. i believe that there is a need for closer coordination between the european commission and the member states and for regular information to the european parliament on the progress of the initiative on agricultural raw materials, by means of an annual activity report. last but not least, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on the work he has done on this report.
i believe that the european union needs an effective raw materials strategy if it is to remain competitive in the industrial sector. a coherent and effective resource diplomacy is also essential to achieve this. this is all the more important as the supply of raw materials has an impact on a wide range of union policies. i welcome the fact that the report stresses the importance of diplomatic instruments and makes concrete suggestions for cooperation with external partners, for example support for developing countries, including through the transfer of scientific and legal knowledge. i also recall the importance of coordination between the eu's external policy in this area and that of the member states. i therefore express the hope that the eeas will prove to be an important additional instrument in the eu's dialogue with other actors on the issue of raw materials.
in writing. the european industry is facing a delicate situation with regard to the supply of raw materials. we are now heavily dependent on imports, especially of rare earths. these resources are crucial to the eu's transition to a sustainable, low-carbon economy. i believe that the proposal to set up a european working group on raw materials, covering all the directorates-general concerned, can have a positive impact and is an effective measure. this working group should develop priority actions on the management of the key elements and ensure strategic cohesion. i also believe that special attention should be paid to the recovery of useful materials from waste in urban areas. the challenge we face today must be turned into an opportunity to reinvigorate europe's industrial power by harnessing our research, development and innovation potential. we need to maintain a leading global position in terms of competitiveness and adopt an industrial innovation strategy to make efficient use of resources and recycling processes. last but not least, we must ensure that the european union develops sustainable and mutually beneficial partnerships with resource-rich countries and strategies based on them.

the report by my colleague simon busuttil points to the improvement of the functioning of frontex in line with the european commission's proposal. i particularly welcome the intention to strengthen the provisions on fundamental human rights, since no european measure, not even the strengthening of the protection of external borders, can take this into account. i also agree with my colleague that the agency should pay particular attention to member states facing specific and disproportionate burdens. not only because recent events have brought to light more clearly than ever the difficulties faced by member states in this situation, but also because this is what the idea of european solidarity demands. this is what is required for the success of the plan to create a common area of freedom, security and justice. i would like to stress that the abolition of internal borders and the protection of the common external borders are in the interests of all european citizens. i therefore hope that the romanian and bulgarian citizens will soon be able to enjoy the benefits of the schengen area.
recent events have shown us that we urgently need a european approach to the management of schengen borders. in this respect, the reform of frontex is fundamental and must be supported. one of the areas where frontex has suffered the most is the protection of fundamental rights, security guarantees and the protection of migrants. i believe that the compromise text brings substantial improvements in this area. the most important thing is that these new rules are correctly applied and hence the need for transparency on the part of frontex towards the european parliament. i also think it is important that frontex will be responsible for carrying out risk analyses at the external borders. in practice, these risk analyses will enable us to have objective and accurate data on the real problems that exist in the schengen area. in this way, we will avoid the strictly political and subjective assessments that are currently taking place in the case of romania and bulgaria's accession to the schengen area.
madam president, one merit of the report is that it underlines the need for solidarity with the frontier countries of the eu. better management is provided by strengthening the external borders of the eu through solidarity and trust, rather than by carving into those borders by denying access to schengen. the main handicap of this instrument seems to be its total dependence on the means provided by the member states when needed, making it a prisoner to their scarcity, political calculus or simply goodwill. rather, to be fully operational, frontex would need a minimal permanent capacity to intervene, like a rapid reaction force supplied by the member states through rotation. finally, with regard to involving frontex in the processing of personal data, while linking frontex up with other relevant institutions is inevitable, its role should be limited, strictly regulated and properly monitored.
in writing. the new frontex regulation is the most important reform of the legislation that created frontex in 2004 and a step forward for the future of the eu's external borders. the consolidation of the eu's external borders cannot be done at the level of the member states. through frontex, all member states will be able to participate in external border operations and actively promote the principle of burden-sharing on immigration and asylum. we must not lose sight of the importance of showing solidarity with those member states that are under migratory pressure. the creation of european border guard teams is another important step. this new external border service will mobilise border guards designated by the member states for joint operations. i hope that frontex's actions will be more visible in the future and i stress the importance of increasing frontex's budget for 2012 in view of the new tasks arising from this new regulation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the reform of frontex is very important in order to correct the shortcomings identified in its work so far, but also to give it new powers and resources. one of the most important aspects of this new regulation is to improve the agency's protection of the fundamental rights of immigrants. from this point of view, the most important issues are the introduction of special training for agents, the establishment of a code of conduct, but also the obligation for frontex agents to comply with european rules when undertaking operations outside the eu territory. i also think that it is a very important step forward that frontex will be entrusted with carrying out risk analyses at the external borders, as these risk analyses will allow an objective assessment of the real problems that exist in the schengen states. finally, i believe that the next logical step in the evolution of frontex should be the creation of an eu border surveillance system, the implementation of which should not be delayed.
in writing. - new rules for the european border protection agency, frontex, are a necessity in the new context of the arab spring, with the immigration problem becoming increasingly serious. as with all other external action, we decided in the ep that respect for human rights, one of the eu's basic principles, was essential. that's why i've listed the conditions for violating that principle. the question of efficiency was also a major part of our negotiations. the new rules therefore require frontex to have its own logistical resources, which it can lease or purchase, without being dependent on the involvement of the member states. i consider the frontex review to be an important step in protecting the union's borders, but also a guarantee that our actions will be under the aegis of respect for human rights.

in writing. − the european union's environmental policy is based on the precautionary principle and the principle of preventive action, the principle of priority of remediation of environmental damage at source and the 'polluter pays' principle. environmental effects must be taken into account as early as possible in all technical planning and decision-making processes. i believe that the authorisation of public and private projects which may have significant effects on the environment should be granted only after a prior assessment of the possible effects of these projects on the environment has been carried out. the evaluation should be carried out on the basis of appropriate information provided by the project initiator, which may be supplemented by the authorities and by persons who may be involved in the project. certain types of projects have significant effects on the environment and should generally be the subject of systematic evaluations. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the modalities of access to the regulated public service (prs) provided by the global satellite navigation system built under the galileo programme because i believe that a detailed legal framework is needed for the regulations on access to the prs and for the management and monitoring of users, in order to guarantee the security of the system and the protection of information. the prs service is one of the cornerstones of the galileo programme and will guarantee continuity of service and security, even in severe crisis situations. they also agree that the security mechanism proposed by the commission provides the necessary balance between the definition of common minimum standards and enforcement at eu level on the one hand and the decentralisation of the oversight function currently carried out by the member states on the other. last but not least, i support the introduction of a precise procedure for cases where a competent prs authority does not comply with the common minimum standards and i believe that this procedure should aim at ensuring compliance with these standards throughout the eu.
in writing. − satellite navigation applications are increasingly used by individuals, businesses and the public sector. the services offered go beyond the familiar realm of driving cars: police, emergency services, transport, electricity supply, etc. the eu certainly needs an independent satellite navigation infrastructure to ensure the continuous and secure provision of such services. of the five components of the european satellite navigation system, the prs - or regulated public service - is the key. it requires a high level of accuracy and reliability. it is therefore appropriate to prepare the framework for the entry into force of the prs in 2014 by implementing early monitoring mechanisms to ensure compliance with the safety standards specific to sensitive areas. in addition to the issue of compliance with security rules, member states have to solve another problem, namely whether or not users have to pay for using the prs, since member states will bear the operational costs of the prs.
in writing. - illegal logging is a widespread phenomenon, with an area of original forest the size of greece disappearing every year. the european regulation lays down the obligations of operators placing timber and timber products on the market. suppliers must be identifiable throughout the production or marketing chain, and sanctions imposed by member states must go as far as confiscation of the timber or products and even immediate suspension of the marketing authorisation.
in writing. − the european union and switzerland have defined their relations in bilateral treaties in various fields. switzerland is thus the eu's fourth largest trading partner, with significant exports and imports of agricultural products between the two partners. although the agriculture agreement was concluded in 1999 and entered into force on 1 june 2002, it did not allow for complete free trade in agricultural products, but only partial liberalisation of certain agricultural sectors. both parties agreed to adopt a harmonised procedure for the designation and effective protection of registered designations of origin and geographical indications. as a result of a common understanding and convergence of their domestic legislation, the two sides have mutually recognised a number of protected agricultural products. this represents a substantial improvement over the trading conditions of the past.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that auditors have an important role to play in improving the supervision of financial institutions, especially in the context of the financial crisis. at the same time, situations where auditors provide different services to the same company should be avoided in order to prevent conflicts of interest. i also believe that the european commission's carrying out of a detailed audit market analysis and the integration of the european group of auditors' supervisory bodies into the european system of financial supervision are two proposals that could hold european auditors accountable.
in writing. - auditors play a particularly important role in the economy. their task is to provide an opinion on the veracity and accuracy of the audited entities' financial statements. in this respect, the independence of auditors is the overriding element of the audit environment. i believe that the rules governing auditing at european level must be simplified and we must also ensure a level playing field for all firms operating in the audit market. it is essential that significant economic operators benefit from audit services on an ongoing basis to ensure financial stability. i also believe that it is necessary to examine the possibilities of reducing the entry conditions to the audit market. this will attract as many participants as possible to the audit market and create an effective competitive environment.
in writing. − the persistence of gender stereotypes, amplified by age discrimination faced by older people in the labour market, significantly reduces older women's employment, training and promotion opportunities and is partly responsible for the increased risk of poverty among older people. in europe, economic competitiveness, prosperity and inclusion depend on its ability to concretely improve the use of its labour force, not only by extending working life, but also by creating working conditions and social security systems that support improved working and living conditions and are profitable for the economy. equal opportunities education from an early age, career guidance policies and policies to promote women's employment are also effective ways of tackling this type of discrimination once and for all. i believe that the situation of women approaching retirement age can be tackled more effectively in the open method of coordination on pensions, social inclusion, employment, changing gender stereotypes and the inclusion of women in political and economic decision-making bodies.
