in writing. − europe has the highest proportion of older women in the world, and the employment rate for women aged 55-64 was 37.8% in 2009, compared with 54.8% for men of the same age. member states should include older women in lifelong learning, develop and support on an ongoing basis flexible retraining programmes tailored to older women and pass on the experience and knowledge gained to younger generations. the commission and the member states should ensure that disadvantages faced by women in the labour market, in particular those arising from caring responsibilities, do not lead to women being penalised in terms of pension or other social security rights. member states should encourage the active participation of older women in business, support women starting a new business and facilitate women's access to finance, in particular through microcredit, as well as equal representation of women and men in economic decision-making bodies.
in writing. − the objective of this report is to promote the amicable settlement of disputes by encouraging the use of mediation and ensuring a balanced relationship between mediation and judicial proceedings. to facilitate access to mediation as a viable alternative to the traditional adversarial approach and to ensure that parties who have resorted to mediation in the eu benefit from a predictable framework legislation, this report introduces common principles that address civil procedure issues in particular. i voted in favour of this report because i recognise the importance of establishing common standards for access to the profession of mediator, with a view to promoting better quality mediation and ensuring high standards of professional training and accreditation in the european union.
in writing. − i voted in favour because one of the key objectives of european union policy is to ensure improved access to justice, with a view to establishing an area of freedom, security and justice. the objective of directive 2008/52/ec is to promote the amicable settlement of disputes by encouraging the use of mediation and ensuring a balanced relationship between mediation and judicial proceedings. to facilitate access to mediation as a viable alternative to the traditional adversarial approach and to ensure that parties who have resorted to mediation in the european union benefit from a predictable framework legislation, the directive introduces common principles addressing in particular civil procedural issues. as demonstrated by the positive results in the union countries that have encouraged this out-of-court dispute settlement, such as italy, bulgaria and romania, mediation adapts processes to the needs of the parties, is characterised by a cost-effectiveness advantage and, above all, by speed - a key advantage especially in member states whose judicial systems are overburdened.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal amending council regulation no 378/2007 by adding a provision on implementing acts. the treaty of lisbon abolished the former comitology system, based on the classical comitology procedures and the regulatory procedure with scrutiny. this system is now replaced by a two-tier structure comprising delegated and implementing acts (the first category includes parliament's veto) which allows the commission to exercise its implementing powers. the current body of legislation must therefore be aligned with this new legal reality. i hope that the amendments concerning the assistance of the commission by the committee on rural development and the committee on agricultural funds will prove stimulating for ec work in this area.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by reinhard butikofer on an effective raw materials strategy for europe because it is clear that european industry is currently facing a delicate situation with regard to the supply of raw materials. these resources are crucial to the eu's transition to a sustainable, low-carbon economy. i believe that the rapporteur's proposal to set up a european working group on raw materials, comprising all the directorates-general concerned, can have a positive impact and is an effective measure, and that this working group should develop priority actions on the management of essential elements and ensure strategic cohesion. i believe that the challenge we face today must be turned into an opportunity to reinvigorate europe's industrial power by harnessing our research, development and innovation potential. it is therefore essential to maintain a leading global competitiveness position and to adopt an industrial innovation strategy to make resource use and recycling processes more efficient.
in writing. − recently, commodity markets have been characterised by increased volatility and large price variations. prices of raw materials have increased significantly in recent years and have reached historical highs for some products, putting european industries in a difficult situation. i believe that the european raw materials strategy must aim at ensuring the supremacy and competitiveness of the european union's economies. unfortunately, the european union is heavily dependent on imports and in the coming period we will have to focus on intensifying innovation in the means of using raw materials. by harnessing our innovation, research and development potential, the raw materials challenge can be turned into an opportunity to reinvigorate europe's industrial power.
in writing. − financial and commodity markets are closely interdependent, both in the european and international context, with increasing numbers of participants pursuing risk-mitigation instruments and new investment objectives. the increase in the flow of financial investment in recent years has influenced, among other things, the prices of raw materials, electricity and foodstuffs at european level. we face limited transparency in the areas concerned, and therefore cannot present a clear analysis of the links between commodity prices and financial instrument markets. increasing the level of transparency and access to information in physical markets would allow investors to better understand the areas concerned and would lead to a limitation of abuses. in agriculture, better coordination between local, regional and national authorities can help improve the quality of food stock information, production and consumption capacity forecasts. i would like to draw attention to the importance of investing in agriculture in less developed regions, so as not to lose control of the unjustified food price developments.
in writing. − the report supports raw materials diplomacy through the european external action service (eeas) to ensure europe’s industry can maintain access to vital raw materials such as those used in the hi-tech sector. a strong focus is also placed on reducing our reliance on imports by stepping up exploration and production within the eu (including research into better clean technologies) where possible- it also calls for recycling and re-use and a gradual ban on waste landfill, while at the same time advocating reopening old landfill sites to extract valuable scrap metal and raw materials. the eu’s raw materials strategy must be efficient and fair, respecting the right of developing countries to benefit from their natural resources. it is also an opportunity for the eu to boost its internal industry, recycle more and be more efficient. the report adopted also makes clear that trade and development policies should go hand in hand and old colonialist approaches are unacceptable; agreements with third countries and the eu should include clauses on human rights, labour standards and corporate and social responsibility.
in writing. − managing fisheries in the black sea is extremely difficult because only two of the six countries that have access to the black sea are eu member states. much of the black sea's problems are due to the lack of an appropriate institutional structure to coordinate and ensure fisheries management at a professional and specialised level. i encourage the creation of a common political mechanism for the six countries bordering the black sea, to ensure, among other things, environmental protection and to facilitate the economic and social development of coastal areas. this new policy mechanism for the black sea should aim to preserve and enhance biodiversity, as well as the prosperity of people working in the fisheries sector in the area. i voted in favour of this report because the black sea should take its rightful place among the main marine areas in europe, given that it is the youngest and most dynamic of the semi-enclosed seas.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs iotova's report because i consider it extremely important to institutionalize the coordination of fisheries in the black sea basin. an integrated maritime policy will ensure effective cooperation in order to improve the situation of fisheries resources in this area. the management of fisheries in the black sea is currently particularly difficult. of the six countries that have an outlet to this basin, only romania and bulgaria are eu member states, often at a disadvantage compared to their neighbours, russia and turkey. in this context, the eu needs to make the most efficient use of both diplomatic and financial instruments to strengthen cooperation between all those involved in fisheries. i support the idea of the black sea basin being given an appropriate status in community policies. they also support the creation of a regional body for the management of fisheries in the black sea.
in writing. - i supported and voted in favour of this report. the situation in the black sea fisheries was to be regulated in the interests of coordination. it's not just the ecological balance, it's the livelihood of the fishermen. i agree that, given the concrete situation that the resources of the black sea are shared between six states, the best formulas are partnership and joint long-term management plans. it should be borne in mind that romania and bulgaria have a relatively small share of the fishing fleet and catches compared to russia and turkey. in addition, illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing should be covered by the new framework. it is the commission's role to involve turkey, georgia, the russian federation and ukraine in this process.
in writing. − the decision to vote in favour of the resolution containing a new strategy for the maintenance of the black sea fish stocks came naturally, given that the improvement of the marine ecosystem is of direct concern to us as a country bordering the black sea. the european union, the world's second-largest fisheries power, needs to maintain this status by better addressing pollution and the effects of climate change on fish stocks. as the report also states, this goal can only be achieved through good cooperation between the black sea basin states, despite the fact that many of them are not eu members. if we are to prosper from the resources of the black sea, the european community will have to allocate funds to help develop the fisheries sector, but also to promote cooperation at diplomatic and scientific level to achieve favourable results. the proposal to create a body to synchronise the fisheries policies of countries with an opening to the black sea can open the way to better promoting the european community's attitude on this subject.
in writing. − many of the problems in the black sea are caused by the lack of an appropriate institutional structure to manage black sea fisheries at a professional and specialised level. according to the european parliament, a separate regional organisation for the management of fisheries in the black sea could promote long-term communication between scientific institutes and professional organisations of fishermen, producers and processors to solve problems and develop cooperation in the black sea. the resolution adopted today welcomes the european commission's efforts to set up working groups with russia and turkey, but stresses the need to involve countries such as ukraine and georgia.
in writing. - i welcome the report drawn up by mrs iotova and would like to highlight a number of very important points which deserve the full attention of the european parliament. in any discussion of fishing in the black sea, the interests of all the coastal countries, not just the interests of the eu member states, must be taken into account. it is the only way to bring all these countries together at the negotiating table, which is imperative to identify the most appropriate solutions to the problems we face. the report rightly points out that there is a need to create a separate body for the management of fisheries in the black sea and to improve bilateral dialogue with countries such as russia and turkey.
in writing. − domestic oil and gas sources make a significant contribution to meeting europe's current energy needs and are now essential for our energy security and diversity. offshore activity is increasing in areas adjacent to the eu territory, which are not subject to the provisions of eu legislation, but where any incident could have consequences for the eu territory. this is to ensure, at the highest level, the safety and integrity of oil and gas exploration operations and the protection of citizens. different regulatory mechanisms in the member states create serious difficulties in ensuring the integrity of safety measures on a consistent basis, impose an additional financial burden on undertakings and hamper the proper functioning of the internal market. finally, the effectiveness of legislation depends on how well it is implemented by the national and european authorities and bodies responsible for the application, management and implementation of the relevant legislation.
in writing. - i support our colleague's proposals without being an expert in this field. i support them because if over 90% of european oil and over 60% of european gas is produced by offshore operations - most of it in the north sea - there is clearly a need for risk assessment before any drilling is undertaken. i support and voted in favour of the idea of a forum of the mediterranean, the baltic and the black seas to carry out multinational audit projects.
in writing. − the report emphasises very strongly the need to implement in the national legislation of each member state a package of laws to monitor the exploitation of gas and oil resources in the seas of the european union. these measures are necessary to ensure both the smooth running of the fuel market, which continues to thrive even in times of crisis, and the safety and well-being of european citizens. i believe that the provisions of this report are of major importance in instructing member states on the measures to be taken, both individually and collectively, in the event of ecological disasters which do not take account of the land or sea borders of a state. the need for an independent body to monitor regularly the efficiency and proper functioning of oil companies and the preventive measures taken by them has strengthened my conviction that this report is a comprehensive one that addresses and clarifies issues related to the transport of oil and the exploitation of gas fields in the marine domain. i also welcome both the report's initiative to create a safer environment for the worker who is constantly exposed to environmental factors harmful to his health and the plan proposed for the arrangements for financial compensation in the event of an accident at work.
in writing. − this report has been drafted in the light of a commission communication and in anticipation of a legislative proposal expected in late 2011 looking at how, following the major bp oil spill in the us last year, the eu should best react to ensure that no such incident can affect eu waters. the regional groupings which are already working well, such as the north sea offshore authorities forum, should be replicated in other areas such as the mediterranean. the report also calls for regular, vigorous and independent third-party verification of safety procedures, including before drilling can start. it calls for all information on safety incidents to be made public and transparent, for the european maritime safety agency to be given a greater coordinating role in the event of an accident. it shies away from backing a new eu agency to oversee offshore oil and gas safety, but instead suggests that a body bringing together national regulators could provide added value at eu level. i support the specific point on ensuring that elected safety representatives should be elected and involved at all levels of operation and decision-making, as well as the paragraph calling on eu companies to respect at least minimum eu standards when operating in third countries, with the commission examining which mechanisms might help implement this.
in writing. − female entrepreneurship provides a key source of increased female employment and is a way to make better use of women's educational level and to ensure that they are not automatically reserved for precarious jobs. i encourage member states to implement policies that enable women to achieve an appropriate work-life balance and to create appropriate childcare structures, as the high level of their rates, the lack of available places and the low quality create additional obstacles for women who intend to become entrepreneurs. the potential of female entrepreneurship is far from being exploited to a sufficient level in the european union, given that the increase in the number of women entrepreneurs has positive consequences for the economy as a whole and an immediate contribution to it.

in writing. − there are discrepancies between member states in the number of women entrepreneurs, with a lower tendency to consider entrepreneurship as a viable career option. despite the increase in the number of female entrepreneurs leading smes in the eu, only one in 10 women is an entrepreneur, compared to one in 4 men. women represent about 60% of the total number of university graduates, but in the labour market they are underrepresented among full-time workers, especially in the entrepreneurial field. it is essential to provide incentives and means to enable women to start entrepreneurial projects in order to reduce the existing inequalities between women and men. the european commission and member states need to make better use of the funding opportunities available to women entrepreneurs through special subsidies, social security provisions and interest rate reductions, allowing for fair and equal access to finance. member states should encourage banking and financial institutions to consider setting up 'women-friendly' business support services, to pay particular attention to the situation of women over 50 and to help them set up their own companies.
energy market integrity and transparency is a key instrument for the completion of the internal energy market by 2014. we must bear in mind that the emergence of abuses in the energy market in a particular member state can have consequences for the whole of the european union. i reiterate that energy liberalisation must first and foremost benefit consumers, stimulate investment and not generate wealth overnight, as has happened in some member states, such as romania. it should be borne in mind that the fundamental purpose of the european energy market is to offer consumers lower prices by stimulating competition. the european regulatory agency must play an important role in preventing market abuse and manipulation that causes the consumer market to grow and in helping to inform european citizens about their rights in a competitive market. i would stress that the national regulatory authorities must accept communication and cooperation with acer.
the energy market is not only trans-european but also regional. energy markets in the european union are increasingly crossing national borders and this is likely to increase strongly in the coming period. unfortunately, the system governing energy market transparency and market abuse has created significant gaps in the applicable rules and the level of transparency. i believe we need consistent rules at european level and a mechanism that allows the authorities to access information from across the union in order to understand in depth the evolution of the market. i would, however, recommend that account be taken of the fact that european energy markets are organised in regional groupings and i believe that we must continue to pay greater attention to the specificities of national and regional markets in order to ensure the proper application of legislative rules.
member of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the commission has already made a number of proposals. firstly, the regulation is a step forward. i am not going to say that everything in the regulation has proved to be 100% practical in ten years. we're about to start a real-life test. we believe that we have proposed the right measures and will report to you acer with the respective progress reports, we as the commission if and where any improvements, any amendment of this law, the regulation, and the instruments still need to be improved and the measures optimized. the question was asked: why do you need your own agency? we have not deliberately proposed an agency of our own, but we have entrusted this complementary competence to the agency for cooperation with national regulators, which was set up in march, acer , because there is a lot of overlap between acer's previous activities and the new tasks. if we did not give acer the task, it would either have to be done by national regulators alone - then the bundling and also the harmonization of sanctions and so on would be done away with - or the commission would have to work with the directorate-general. but the directorates-general have a management function, a control function, but not the function of day-to-day processing. thirdly, i am as sensitive as you are to the question: what staffing levels are needed to achieve full employment? what material resources do we need to operate? what it equipment do we need? i want the agency to get to work. as soon as we know more about the workload, we will be happy to approach parliament to ensure that the agency can meet all its workloads and control densities in a few years' time, either by reshuffling or by re-approving posts. the question of setting up branches, liaison offices, was raised. we have told the agency - its boards, its director, its supervisory bodies - that you should decide how you organise yourselves. i cannot imagine that we have a branch in every capital city of a member state. we shall be happy to report on whether and where to do so at the next opportunity. but i'm very reluctant to suggest outposts. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. the question can be asked again: has the internal market with competition and transparency been useful for electricity and gas? it was created in this parliament 15 years ago. europe is built on the basic principle of a market economy. the internal market, alongside the union of peace, is a principle of the european idea, without barriers to trade, without frontiers, with competition and transparency: an internal market for food, for vehicles, for white goods, for brown goods, for goods, goods and services in every respect. europe has benefited from the single market and its trade agreements with third countries. i believe that the single market is the right basis for economic activity. it is therefore logical in principle that not only coal and oil, which have been products of the internal market for many decades, but also electricity and gas should be subject to the rules of the internal market. i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter. it would be a bureaucratic event, a monster. in addition, it is only within the internal market that we can tackle common targets for co2 reduction or renewable energy. and solidarity can only take place in the internal market, through the member states. so it is not a question of whether the single market is right - it is right - but of whether it can be applied and not abused. i therefore believe that today is a decisive step towards putting the internal market on a sound, trustworthy footing and to eliminate market abuse and thus, in effect, attacks on the internal market and the advantages of market participants as far as possible, as is also being done successfully with other services in europe. i would like to thank you again for your constructive comments and cooperation over the last six months. if you decide in parliament tomorrow, we will implement what you have decided immediately.

report and they do not concern only the fact that european law is too often violated, just as we too often have to deal with delays in the transposition process. it should also be borne in mind that legislation at european level is perhaps more often the result of a compromise than national legislation. a compromise does not always guarantee that the resulting result will be as clear and concise as desired. if we are to respect the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, if we are to take account of the principle of 'think small first', if we want our work to lead to a reduction in lisbon and the charter of fundamental rights, access to documents has become a fundamental right of every citizen of the union and of every person residing or established in a member state. what is the situation in the council (since various types of complaints are often made against the council)? by the end of 2010, the council's public register of documents contained more than 1.5 million documents. over 75% of these documents could have been made public. this represents an increase of around 12% in the number of documents directly made available by the register compared to 2009. as regards requests for public access, the council secretariat examined more than 9 000 documents in 2010. in over 70% of cases, a decision was taken to allow access to the entire document. two behalf of the polish presidency. first, i would like to state my clear appreciation of the three reports that we are debating today. it is important that the institutions work together on these topics, which are so important if we want to make eu legislative and political action more transparent, more accessible and more useful for citizens. as for better legislation, subsidiarity and proportionality, and smart regulation, i am very happy to learn that mr karim’s report supports our agenda and underlines the shared responsibility of the eu institutions in this area. smart regulation is a key priority for the commission and we have an ambitious smart regulation agenda with clearly defined priorities. the commission remains committed to further improving the quality of its initiatives and to evaluating existing legislation, as well as continuing to reduce administrative burdens and simplifying wherever possible. for example, the commission is on track to exceed its target of 25% of administrative burden reductions by 2012. we now need to ensure that this translates into concrete benefits for businesses through the adoption of relevant legislation by the council and parliament and by effective implementation in the member states. the delivery of this target by 2012 must be our common priority within a broader approach to legislation to make it more efficient and effective. to this end, we also make thorough use of impact assessments in the commission. another key tool in this new approach will be the systematic ex-post evaluation of the legislation. the commission has therefore merged its efforts to reduce administrative burdens with those to simplify and to evaluate legislation. finally, the commission welcomes an open discussion on the responsibility of the three institutions in delivering smart regulation. we need to ensure that all three institutions show a commitment to making real progress. they should start by making the best use of existing instruments. therefore, the commission calls for the full implementation of the current interinstitutional agreement on better lawmaking. turning now to the application of eu law, i would first like to thank members for the preparatory work on our annual report on the monitoring of the application of eu law. as the current interinstitutional talks on correlation tables demonstrate, the commission and parliament attach great importance to the current application of eu law. i appreciate the opportunity to have an exchange of views on a regular basis on this subject. i would also like to use this opportunity to thank the polish presidency and mr szpunar for his personal involvement and commitment to resolving the issue we are discussing now concerning correlation tables and explanatory information from the member states to the commission so that we can do our work better in the future. with regard to the issues raised in ms lichtenberger’s report, i would like to highlight the following points. in 2007, we announced that we would improve and intensify our collaboration with the member states. therefore, in 2008, we introduced the eu pilot project and i am happy to say that nearly all member states are participating. this instrument is an early-warning and problem-solving tool vis-à-vis member states in many cases. it does not replace the infringement procedure but helps to resolve a lot of cases. those that cannot be resolved are of course put into the infringement procedure. the eu pilot gives full and quick effect to union law for the benefit of citizens and businesses. as i am sure we will discuss later today, petitions to parliament are key in identifying citizens’ concerns. the annual report analyses in detail the nature of petitions and gives concrete examples where they have also triggered infringement procedures. in order to improve the follow-up to complaints, we have set up an effective complaint registration system. i am confident that the system meets the concerns previously spelled out by parliament and the ombudsman. it allows the rapid treatment of incoming complaints and gives swift information to the complainants about any major step decided by the commission. the lisbon treaty has strengthened the role of the commission with regard to the late transposition of directives by the member states. in 2010, the commission explained publicly the concrete ways in which it will apply these new powers. this was communicated to the other institutions as well. we are confident that this contributes to putting further pressure on member states to improve their performance in this field. last but not least, ms sargentini’s report clearly shows the importance of public access to documents as a central element of the transparency of the work of the institutions. the report contains useful suggestions which the commission will duly take into consideration. in particular, the commission agrees that the information should be made available to the public in a proactive manner whenever possible. the commission has already made significant efforts in this respect. for example, information and documents on comitology committees and on expert groups are available through dedicated websites. the commission also provides information on beneficiaries of eu funds, both under central and shared management, and for the latter information on beneficiaries of funds is accessible through a portal providing links with national websites. of course, the commission shares parliament’s wish to improve the interoperability of the public registers, and we still have a lot of work to do on this, but the commission takes note of the rapporteur’s comments concerning the ongoing legislative procedure on a recast of the access to documents regulation. however, this debate cannot replace the ongoing legislative process. in this regard let me underline that our proposal for a recast does not reduce the level of transparency. our estimation is that the same number of requests for access would be granted. our proposal merely aims at clarifying a number of provisions and at facilitating the application of the regulation. the commission agrees with the rapporteur that some changes to the regulation are made necessary by the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, most importantly the extension of the citizen’s right to access the documents of all eu institutions and bodies. this would include, for example, the european council and the eas. for this reason, the commission decided last march to submit a second proposal to align the existing regulation to the treaty. our objective with the second proposal is to give citizens the rights the treaty has created for them, and to do so as quickly as possible without waiting for the conclusion of the discussions on the wider recast proposal. the commission therefore invites parliament and the council to adopt quickly the proposal aligning the regulations to the treaty and, in parallel, we will continue our discussions on the wider recast proposal. we look forward to relaunching the legislative process. in this context, debate should focus on the core issues, such as the definition of the ‘space to think’ within the institutions and the balance between the protection of personal data and the right of access to documents, which have been rightly highlighted by the rapporteur. other issues such as classification rules or historical archives should not be addressed in this context, but rather in specific fora. to conclude, i would like to repeat the commission’s appreciation of these three reports, which contain very useful observations and suggestions. i now look forward to deepening this debate with you and i thank you in advance for your remarks.
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection. − mr president, a few months ago this house endorsed a set of key measures to relaunch the single market, and i strongly believe that the ambitious goals we have set will be impossible to achieve without ensuring proper application of eu law. i would like to congratulate ms lichtenberger on the good work that she has done. the committee on the internal market and consumer protection was happy to see that some progress has been made in some areas, such as late transposition of directives or the improvement in the functioning of solvit. however, a lot more remains to be done to ensure that businesses and citizens fully benefit from the single market. member states should incentivise their responsible government departments to ensure timely transposition. correlation tables are another useful tool that would contribute to a better transposition process, and i really hope that member states will show their commitment to proper implementation by accepting to draw up such tables. infringement procedures need to be shorter and more transparent so that citizens remain fully informed about the follow-up to their requests, and we should continue to support and develop problem-solving tools like solvit and eu pilot.
on behalf of the epp group. this report focuses on the commission's fundamental role as guardian of the treaties and points out that, despite a decline in the number of infringement cases opened by the commission, the committee on petitions had to deal with some 2 900 complaints and infringement cases at the end of 2009, and member states still experienced delays in transposing directives in more than half of the cases. the commission should make the procedures for infringements of existing union law more transparent and inform citizens of the measures taken following their request as quickly and appropriately as possible. the rapporteur's approach of asking the commission to propose a procedural code in the form of a regulation, on the basis of the new legal basis of article 298 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, is correct and i support it. it is regrettable that too many infringement procedures of union law take a long time to close or to be brought before the court. for this reason, member states and the commission should step up their efforts to resolve cases of infringement. the commission's establishment of a hierarchy of priority for infringements of union law in different sectors would be welcomed. we note that there is still a high number of cases of infringements of union law due to the delayed transposition of directives. timely transposition of eu directives is essential for the smooth functioning of the single market, to the benefit of consumers and businesses across the union. in this context, i welcome the request made by the commission, by the rapporteur, to continue promoting best practice in the transposition of legislation in the field of the single market.
i will begin by stressing once again the importance and the special role of the committee on petitions in guaranteeing and defending the rights of european citizens when they are infringed by an authority of a member state or a european authority. and we, the meps elected by the citizens of our union, have the right and the duty to defend them. i would like to highlight two important aspects of the debate on the meyer report. firstly, i regret that, despite a large number of petitions concerning serious violations of the human rights enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights, the european commission either refuses or explains, on the pretext of lack of instruments, that it cannot act. i quote from the report of the venice commission on the hungarian constitution: once ratified, the charter of fundamental rights is a legal, binding piece of legislation, which is not yet obvious to the european commission. secondly, as regards european environmental legislation, the european commission should monitor more closely and act accordingly to ensure that all european acts and legislation are respected and implemented, and this must be done at all stages of project development, not just when they have been implemented. i would like to draw the attention of the european commission to the gigantic project under development in romania, roşia montană. i take this opportunity to thank once again my colleague meyer for his excellent cooperation, as well as all the members of the committee on petitions.

there is a direct link between internationalisation and the performance of smes. international activities strengthen growth and competitiveness and support the long-term viability of companies. however, european smes still rely heavily on internal markets, despite the opportunities brought by the expanded single market and globalisation in general. internationalisation is not limited to exports. for example, cross-border cooperation, participation in profitable networks, the search for competitive means or new technologies are important elements in the motivation of modern smes to go international. smes also need to combine different approaches in their internationalisation strategies, which are mutually supportive, both internally and internationally. i therefore stress the importance of doing business in partnership with third countries, thus ensuring access to domestic and international markets.

madam president, i fully support this oral question and this resolution, because we are faced with a problem unworthy of europe, unworthy of the values we defend and unworthy of the average standard of living in europe. the crisis has considerably increased the problem of homelessness, but i think we must realize that today everyone is threatened: any european can become homeless tomorrow. the first lever we can use is, of course, the european social fund, which enables integration or reintegration into the workforce, entry into employment, adaptation to new jobs, and the return of the unemployed to employment. but beyond that - and as chair of the working group on the european social fund and progress - i would like to stress that the progress programme can and must also help us to move faster in solving this problem: firstly, preventing, but also defining indicators together to give us a real policy or approach, effective access to housing. there are good practices at european level to achieve these objectives. i believe that we all together - at the level of the commission and our working party, and in the committee on employment and social affairs with our chair, mrs berès - must know what is being done and what is working in the member states, what are the strategies that are really promising for the future and whether individual coaching, individual approach and personal monitoring can really be important elements that enable us to solve these problems unworthy of europe.
homelessness continues to be a problem across europe, with a negative impact on both homeless people and society. it is known that during the winter, large cities in the member states are faced with a shortage of places in the shelters specifically designed for homeless people. combating homelessness has become a priority, being a major part of the european strategy on social protection and social inclusion and, in particular, in the new post-lisbon strategy, europe 2020. despite progress in many member states to combat the phenomenon, support and policy coordination at european level is needed. not only does the definition of homelessness vary widely between member states, but the collection and reporting of data is also very different. the european union needs to develop a common framework to support and monitor member states in developing policies to combat homelessness. i consider prevention to be the most cost-effective way to combat homelessness. emphasis should also be placed on the integration into employment of disadvantaged groups: young people, the elderly, women, people with disabilities and minority groups. integration must also take into account aspects of family life, with special attention to disadvantaged regions and the use of the european regional development fund for the construction of social housing for disadvantaged people.
the problem of homelessness is undoubtedly a serious one which needs to be brought to the attention of national and european institutions. but i think the discussion is incomplete if we ignore another problem that is at least as serious - i am talking about the poor living conditions. according to eurostat, one in six europeans lives in overcrowded housing or faces inherent housing problems. housing problems are present in all member states. millions of europeans do not have indoor toilets or bathrooms and showers. according to a study by the french abbé pierre foundation on poverty and housing, more than 8 million french people live in precarious conditions. in these circumstances, together with a european union strategy on homelessness, i believe that a long-term policy is needed to improve the living conditions of european citizens.
the problem of homelessness has become more acute in recent years, with homeless women, families living on the streets, homeless youth and children, and workers who have lost their homes to credit default as a result of the economic and financial crisis. i would like to make a few suggestions to the commission which could provide solutions to this problem. firstly, i believe that the establishment of a european agency for persons or the supervision of homeless people could be a solution that would pursue the problem of homeless people in a european manner and with common solutions throughout europe. then, the extension and use of structural funds, such as the european social fund and the european regional development fund, to address the phenomenon of homelessness and, in particular, to build permanent housing where it is needed, following the finnish 'housing first' model, which has proven to reduce costs by eur 14 000 per assisted beneficiary. and last but not least, i suggest consulting with the homeless and the associations they belong to to work out what to do next.
over the last decade, the alarming increase in the number of homeless people and the social polarization in housing conditions have posed major challenges for european states. a prerequisite for mitigating the effects of homelessness is the coordination of strategies to address exclusion due to lack of shelter, involving national, regional and local levels, so that decisions are taken as closely as possible to the people affected. equally important is the efficient use of european funds for housing construction and their directing to social housing. campaigns such as the 'european year for combating poverty and social exclusion', which encourage the exchange of good practice, can play a key role in raising public awareness and responsibility. i would also like to draw attention to the need for national strategies for vulnerable people to improve living conditions by removing barriers to labour market participation, improving the quality of social services and increasing the supply of affordable housing.
the problem of homelessness has become more acute and diversified in recent times as a result of the economic crisis. they're particularly vulnerable. the absence of a european policy on the social integration of this category is a violation of fundamental human rights. i support the idea of adopting a strategy to improve the situation of homeless people. the eu must protect the right of all citizens to a life of dignity and to full participation in society. i would point out that exclusion generates discrimination on grounds of social belonging. it can have a strong impact on the physical and mental integrity of those affected. i believe that the allocation of structural funds at eu level is necessary to help solve this problem. the funds may be used in particular for the construction of permanent social housing.
from a strictly biological standpoint, health is not a possession of the rich, just as illness is not a possession of the poor. socially, however, this claim tends to prove untrue. of course, there are european institutions and bodies that provide healthcare to disadvantaged groups, including the homeless. sadly, however, both the quality of the medical record and the quality of the programs are not on par with those on the other side of the atlantic. perhaps this european homelessness strategy should now be reconsidered in this respect, namely the provision of health care to homeless people.
in writing. in response to the oral question put by my colleagues, i would ask the commission to give priority to prevention in the forthcoming development of an eu strategy on homelessness. homelessness is now a growing concern across europe, a phenomenon that is a consequence of the atomization of society and the breakdown of traditional small communities, in addition to obvious economic causes. the problem today is not limited to those who are confined to the margins of society because of their use of alcohol or drugs. in several eu countries, the phenomenon affects a growing middle class, many of whom have or have had a university degree or even a permanent job. they are the ones who, with a detailed strategy, with relatively small, targeted assistance, could avoid homelessness and the degradation that it causes. it is sad to say that the kind of social networking that was typical of small communities with a strong sense of solidarity a few decades ago is no longer there or has become very limited. this is why it is important that member states pay greater attention to those on the periphery.
the climate change that we are all experiencing has ecological and social consequences that ultimately affect human health through changes in the quality and quantity of water, air and food, but also through altered weather patterns, agriculture and ecosystems. it has been scientifically demonstrated that the benefits of reducing anthropogenic non-co2 emissions are felt immediately and directly in the areas where measures are taken. i'm glad that we've moved past the phase where carbon dioxide emissions were the cause of all the evils in the earth's atmosphere, and that it's finally time to act on the other factors that are as bad as carbon dioxide. as an example, the total global warming impact of the use of hydrofluorocarbons (hfcs) is currently estimated to be about 2% of total greenhouse gas emissions. however, it is expected that an increase in demand for hfcs could lead to a contribution of 7-13% of total greenhouse gases by 2050. as such, if we are to take the bull by the horns, the industry would need a stable legal framework quickly to encourage manufacturers to develop alternatives to hfcs. as i said, this is just one example of many possible actions in the case of reducing anthropogenic emissions. i wanted the commission's answer to the question on this subject to be concrete and firm, so that action could be taken in a relatively short time. also, because the montreal protocol has succeeded in demonstrating that it is possible to successfully reduce greenhouse gas emissions, i believe it is the most appropriate forum to regulate and reduce the production and consumption of hydrofluorocarbons internationally.
the promotion of a resource-efficient, green and competitive economy is a central element of the europe 2020 strategy. eu action over the past decades has resulted in a considerable reduction in emissions of air pollutants, including sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, volatile organic compounds, ammonia and particulate matter. the quality guidelines for fuels used in both road and maritime transport have made a major contribution to this reduction. directive 32/99 on the reduction of the sulphur content of certain liquid fuels sets the maximum permissible sulphur content for heavy fuel oil, diesel fuel and marine engines used in the union. measures on energy efficiency of buildings and waste recycling will also contribute significantly to reducing pollutant emissions. commissioner, i would like to ask you what measures you intend to take to ensure that the emissions generated by the industrial sectors are reduced, especially in the context of the economic and financial crisis.
a paradox of our times is the need to control emissions and the trend towards increased consumption in an era of globalization. we see the devastating effects of climate change, but we hesitate to take action. the reservations in the copenhagen and cancun agreements are conclusive. we remain hopeful that future conferences will take a firm stand on this. europe is an example of initiative in the fight against climate change. i believe that the commission's role at this point is to initiate a concrete strategy for the gradual reduction of the production and consumption of pollutants. the framework programmes for research and innovation could help identify alternative solutions for the gradual replacement of current technologies with innovative clean technologies. i'm a chemical engineer; chemistry helps us a lot in our daily lives today, but it can also kill us. with discernment, we must move beyond the stage of wonderful declarations of intent and move urgently to concrete action.

in writing. most euro area countries were not in difficulty before the financial crisis, with public debt and deficits falling. on the other hand, the euro area's public debt to gdp ratio is still well below that of the united states or japan. the european union suffers not so much from a public debt problem as from a lack of fiscal and political integration. this crisis requires a european response and a common economic governance based on the community method rather than the intergovernmental method, which is deficient in terms of democracy and decision-making. in this context, i welcome the fact that the european executive is preparing a proposal for a common market in public debt, which will facilitate debt financing and ensure the liquidity of the european currency. at the same time, proposals on fiscal harmonisation, european economic governance, growth and job creation are still needed. the importance of the euro in the international arena is indisputable. the united states has called for european unity these days, and the union must live up to expectations.
in writing. the eu is not just under the pressure of the sovereign debt crisis, under the pressure of the crisis of confidence. the union is at a crossroads, faced with a choice between deepening integration and retrogression. we are living in crucial moments when we must decide whether we will continue the european project of economic integration, the expansion of the single market and the consolidation of the emu, or allow the single european construction to sink into the swamp of populism, extremism and isolationism. the crisis facing the eu requires a european response, not a sum of national responses. it is not enough to say and repeat this, but the european solidarity response must be put into practice. we need the implementation of the measures and the establishment of the european institutions proposed in the european economic governance package now. but we also need a european government, first at the level of the eurozone. last but not least, we need a european parliament with broad powers to manage the process of deepening european integration, because the continuation of the transfer of sovereignty must be guaranteed by the only european institution directly elected by the 500 million citizens of the eu. the beneficiaries of deeper european integration will thus be the citizens of europe.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the energy market integrity and transparency regulation is a key instrument for the completion of the internal energy market by 2014. it will create a framework defining coherent rules, adapted to the specificities of energy markets and designed to detect and discourage market abuse. we must bear in mind that market abuse in a particular member state will not be limited to that member state but can have consequences at eu level and we must not forget that the fundamental purpose of the european energy market is to offer consumers lower prices by stimulating competition. the regulation gives national authorities the lead role in the investigation procedures in the event of suspected abuses and i believe that member states should give them the necessary powers to investigate market abuse and lay down appropriate rules on applicable sanctions. last but not least, i argue that acer must play an instrumental role in preventing market abuse and manipulation that causes consumer prices to rise, and that nras must accept communication and collaboration with acer, because only then will the agency be able to fulfil its assigned role.
in writing. − the regulation aims to prohibit market manipulation and insider trading in the eu’s energy markets and defines them and puts in place monitoring mechanisms and penalties to dissuade from such forms of market abuse. acer (agency for the cooperation of european energy regulators) is given a strong role to play: to monitor and help enforce the regulation with national regulatory authorities, a registration scheme for market participants (with the possibility for a licensing scheme should this not prove sufficient), ensuring that penalties take into account the consumer damage caused by market abuse, that acer will be allocated sufficient funds in a review in order to take into account the extra tasks assigned to it. the commission should consider presenting a proposal to harmonise minimum standards for penalties and member states have to work to harmonise sanctions, so as to avoid competition or loopholes. voting this report we act to curtail market abuse and speculation in the wholesale energy markets, to protect the consumer, as it is ultimately consumers who pay more for their electricity and gas when these abuses occur.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on public access to documents for 2009-2010 because i consider transparency to be a fundamental right of citizens, legally binding as well as a general rule. i argue that any decision to deny access to documents must be based on clear, precisely defined, reasoned and clearly explained exceptions, so that citizens can understand the situation and use other available legal remedies. the european union must be a model of institutional transparency and modern democracy for both its member states and third countries. we also need a proactive approach to information availability and we need to make efforts to make as many categories of documents as possible available to the public through all communication channels. last but not least, i believe that there is a need for harmonisation of access to information legislation at eu level and that member states should be encouraged to adopt legislation that is as transparent as possible on access to documents.

in writing. − in an effort to mitigate the consequences of climate change, the european climate policy has been focused on long-term reductions of co2 emissions. scientific data prove that the eu policy is lacking a comprehensive approach towards the reduction of the non-co2 climate-relevant anthropogenic emissions, namely the hfcs, black carbon and pollutant gases that lead to formation of tropospheric ozone. the same data indicate that it is important to complement our efforts against climate change, by firmly and timely addressing the non-co2 pollutants, while taking advantage of existing technologies and institutions. relevant policy options include: (a) phasing down the production and consumption of hfcs with global warming potential, to accelerate the phase-out of hcfcs, and recover and destroy stratospheric ozone-depleting ghgs in discarded products and equipment, (b) reduction of emissions of black carbon, giving priority to emissions that affect regions of snow and ice, including the arctic glaciers; (c) reduction of pollutant gases that lead to formation of tropospheric ozone, a significant ghg. the eu needs to develop a broader, more comprehensive climate change policy which would address the harmful effects of non-co2 climate-related anthropogenic emissions, such as hfcs, black carbon and other pollutant gases which are particularly damaging to the lower ozone layer.
in writing. − i very much welcome this initiative and the attention which is now being paid to addressing non-co2 emissions. given the disproportionately large influence on climate change of some of these gases, it is clear that any effective emission reduction strategy cannot focus solely on carbon dioxide. we must, however, ensure that emission reduction policies apply fairly across different sectors. i could not support some colleagues earlier this year when they voted for measures which would have disproportionately and negatively affected the agricultural sector, particularly small-scale farms. agriculture can and should make a big contribution to emission reduction, but it must be done fairly, which means avoiding harming the most vulnerable farmers.

the s&d group welcomes the fact that the european parliament has adopted a resolution on the situation in eritrea, which is currently in the process of being revised. dawit isaak, a swedish citizen, returned to his native country after obtaining citizenship to work at the first independent newspaper in eritrea. his abusive detention without trial and without a lawyer is all the more outrageous because the conditions in which he is held are inhumane. i believe that concrete measures are needed to compel the asmara authorities to provide medical and legal assistance to the prisoners, to release prisoners of conscience, to hold democratic elections, which have been scheduled and cancelled periodically, and to respect the freedom of the press. i believe that there is a need for a suspension of development assistance and direct sanctions against the leadership of the state, including travel restrictions and asset freezes. the eu is also committed to the development of a common approach to the fight against poverty and social exclusion.
reporters without borders said that isaak dawit chose to write freely and encouraged others to do the same. according to his relatives, he decided to return to his native country to help build democracy. for this, he has been imprisoned for almost 10 years without trial and without being formally charged. the eu cannot accept that one of its citizens is treated like this. we must use all legal and political means to obtain isaak's release. i ask the council to consider applying sanctions against the asmara regime, as proposed by the epp. i also draw attention to the fact that we must not forget the other political activists and journalists imprisoned in eritrean prisons for the crime of free thought.
the proposed new common strategic framework can facilitate, through simplified procedures and the increased transparency it brings, a wider opening up of funding programmes. i would like to draw attention to a less discussed aspect - and i am glad that mr reul, president of the itre commission, has mentioned it here - namely that in the european union, at member state level, there are important gaps in research and innovation capacity, research infrastructure and industrial structure. i believe that the current funding framework programme favours the more advanced countries and that the gap will therefore be widened permanently. i therefore believe that at european level, cooperation in research and innovation between member states must be stepped up and cohesion funding must be complementary to the future framework programme. in this way, the lagging countries will have increased access to available funds and will be able to develop effective projects themselves.
we are currently facing an economic, social and environmental crisis, and fundamental and applied research, education and innovation are crucial tools for economic recovery and job creation. we call for simplification of the procedures for accessing european research and innovation funds and programmes. the common strategic framework for research and innovation funding must be based on the coordination of the european union's and member states' research programmes and address global societal challenges such as demographic change, sustainable resource management and a sound, stable and equitable economic base. the participation of smes in cdi collaboration projects should exceed 15%, and therefore simplification and removal of bureaucratic barriers are essential to achieve this and to the participation of industry as a whole. i call for increased funding for the development of gnss-specific applications, without which the galileo project will not be able to be used to its full capacity.
i would also like to congratulate marisa matias on her excellent report. despite the economic crisis, trends in research and innovation are promising. however, much remains to be done, particularly in those member states classified as moderately innovative. significant inequalities in financing capacity persist and are becoming more pronounced in the union. this difference is reflected in participation in the union's seventh framework programme and i believe that we need a balancing mechanism in the common strategic framework to boost the research and innovation capacities of all member states. we need new approaches to help the less-performing regions and member states, as education and innovation are crucial tools for both economic recovery and job creation. therefore, flexibility and simplification in all research and innovation programmes must be the priority of the new programming period.
research, education and innovation are the building blocks of a competitive and sound economy. in a difficult context they are essential for a sustainable economic recovery. that is why i welcome the commission's green paper, which is all the more timely in the present circumstances. i also appreciate the attention paid to reducing disparities between member states in this area. for my country, this is important, because romania is significantly below the eu average for most indicators. for example, the aggregate innovation score is less than half the european average. at the same time, i would like to underline the importance of regional cooperation, which favours the exchange of good practice. in this context, i would like to highlight romania's proposal to create an international centre for advanced studies for the danube-delta-black sea system within the framework of the eu strategy for the danube region.
increasing the efficiency of research and innovation funding is the key condition for increasing allocations to this area in line with the 3% growth target set in the eu 2020 strategy. we face a number of obstacles in the implementation of research and innovation results due to the fact that national and regional governments pursue separate strategies, which lead to a lot of duplication and fragmentation. the common strategic framework for research and innovation could therefore regulate eu funding in these areas by creating a simplified and efficient structure. the csf would allow for the implementation of an appropriate set of funding instruments through which eu objectives can be found in the member states at both local and regional level. research and innovation funding should aim to attract private investment and smes should play an important role in product initiation and development in the sectors in which they operate.
we all know that the european union has set itself the objective of increasing spending on research and innovation to 3% of the union's gdp by 2020. however, as not all member states will be able to achieve this, i believe that a strategic and integrated approach to research and innovation in the context of strategy 2020 is needed to ensure that increased public and private investment in this area is realised. as a member of the committee on agriculture and rural development, i believe that the european commission's approach should be one that maximises synergies within the common strategic framework for research and innovation, the european agricultural fund for rural development and the structural funds, and adopts a strategy based on as many additional funds as possible, targeting research and innovation at regional level and supporting the development of the institutional capacity of regions targeting research and innovation policies.
