on behalf of the s&d group. first of all, i would like to congratulate maria koppa on her work and express on behalf of my political group my support for her position in favour of the agreement between the european union and the palestinian authority of the west bank and the gaza strip on the liberalisation of trade in agricultural and fisheries products. our discussion comes at a time when developments are being recorded in a process which has been blocked by decades of bloodshed. in this context, the decision to allow palestinian exports to enter the internal market more easily expresses the european union's determination to actively contribute to the process of building a functioning economy. the economic and political dimensions are interdependent in the eu's relationship with the palestinian authority. a fragile economy, extreme poverty and massive unemployment are factors fuelling the potential for conflict in the region. by encouraging trade, we are not only helping to reduce poverty, but also to strengthen political institutions. the economic development of the palestinian territories also depends on access to the european market for products from the gaza strip and the west bank. it is important that, in the application of this agreement, particular attention be paid to the rules of origin. the european court of justice's ruling in brita of 25 february 2010 is relevant in this respect, whereby the palestinian authorities are considered to be the only ones able to provide the documents attesting to the origin of the products manufactured in the gaza strip and the west bank.
rapporteur for opinion, committee on agriculture and rural development. − i was rapporteur for the opinion expressed by the committee on agriculture on this subject and i consider it important that the final report takes up our references to rural tourism and agro-tourism. rural tourism is an asset for europe and must be exploited. this sector plays a key role in keeping rural areas alive, in increasing incomes in these areas, in generating jobs. support for investment in rural tourism must continue to receive adequate funding under the future common agricultural policy, under the second pillar, where adequate funding for rural infrastructure must also be maintained, for investments that can make european villages more easily accessible and attractive. in conclusion, i would also stress the importance of the commission's call to promote eco-tourism.
tomorrow is international tourism day and the danube forum of the european parliament will organise a debate on 'tourism in the danube region' to highlight the tourism potential of this region. the development of inland waterway transport and tourism can contribute to the sustainable development of cultural, nature and leisure tourism. an effective european tourism policy requires a strategy, an action plan and adequate financial resources. the relaunch of tourism, an integral part of the european industrial policy, is a strategic objective for employment. recognising the close link between tourism and transport, we call on the commission and the member states to modernise national, regional and cross-border infrastructure for the various modes of transport. we support the promotion of integrated electronic ticketing systems for different modes of transport and call for a charter of tourist rights and responsibilities, including principles on accessibility, provision of information, price transparency and compensation. last but not least, working conditions are essential for the quality of tourist services.
the report proposes the development of a book of rights and responsibilities for tourists, including the principles of accessibility, providing information on prices and compensation in a transparent manner. the protection of tourists' rights is necessary and the drafting of a book covering all existing european consumer rights legislation is a first step in this direction. the introduction of the standard contract between tourist and operator at european level would, in my view, be the next logical step towards harmonising and protecting the rights of european tourists. the need to harmonise hotel classification by identifying common minimum standards is also very important. this harmonisation, together with other factors, forms the basis for ensuring the rights of tourists.
in writing. recent economic developments have highlighted the need for a coherent european strategy in the field of tourism. it should address social, territorial cohesion and protection of natural and cultural heritage. at the same time, it is important to develop regional policy in support of this area. the eu strategy for the danube region, a romanian-austrian initiative, is a model in this regard. one of the first results of its implementation in our country is the inauguration of the mini-port of st. george just last weekend. at the same time, europe needs to harness the resources of eco-tourism. romania, for example, is planning to set up a national network of cycling routes in areas with scenic landscapes. promoting romania's country brand provides for diversification of services so that the number of foreign tourists doubles by 2015.
in writing. in a recent ranking of the 50 most admired countries in the world, seven eu countries are among the top 10 destinations. it is clear evidence that europe has significant tourist and cultural potential, but that it still has room for development despite the economic crisis. i believe that the eu and the member states can identify new ways to attract foreign tourists to europe and encourage better mobility of tourists within the european union, especially in the context of major cultural or sporting events. multicultural europe still has many places with traditions to see, but also monuments and places less included in the classic tourist circuits, which must be visited in the context of such events. in addition, tourism operators must be encouraged and supported in attracting tourists from non-eu countries, if tourism is to continue to be a major contributor to the gross domestic product of european countries.
as other colleagues will probably wish to do this evening, i wish to express my disappointment at the populist temptations which led two european states last week to block romania's accession to the schengen area. romania and bulgaria were promised, on the date of accession to the european union, that if they met the necessary conditions, they would be admitted to schengen, but the promise was broken. i hope that the two countries will reconsider this decision as soon as possible in the near future, proving their objectivity. romania and bulgaria have met all the technical criteria for accession to the schengen area, and our citizens have the right to fully enjoy freedom of movement.
last week, the european union gave up, hopefully for a short time, one of the principles on which it was founded: equality among its members. the jha council has suspended the accession of romania and bulgaria to the schengen area, although the two countries have met all the technical criteria, according to the expert assessments. the refusal of a dutch minister to honour a promise made by the union in the accession treaties seems to me to be an exaggerated measure. this is because i believe that the dutch citizens have confidence in romania, while dutch investors rank first in my country with subscribed capital of 5.37 billion euros in almost four thousand majority-controlled companies. the question of additional criteria for accession to schengen is deeply unfair and discredits the community's construction, especially when the rules agreed upon are changed during the game.
the failure of romania's entry into schengen is one that, although explainable by the lack of capacity of romania's representatives to plead this case with conviction, unfortunately has negative effects on the entire population of romania, not only on the governors who, once again, have demonstrated that they are not up to the task entrusted to them. unfortunately, this was overlooked in the vote on romania's accession to the schengen area, with the states openly opposing it without taking into account the profound implications that a negative vote could have for romania. i hope that in the future this hostile and slightly simplistic attitude will be replaced by one that truly corresponds to the spirit of the european union, in which we do not have to punish a member state with its entire population just because it has stupid leaders.
the new education law adopted this year in romania defines the university of medicine and pharmacy in marosvásárhely, where half of the students were already of hungarian nationality, as a multicultural higher education institution. although the adopted law provides for the establishment of a separate hungarian faculty, the university's leadership, belonging to the majority nation, refuses to allow this. half of the universities attended by hungarian students and officially recognized as multicultural, obstruct medical education in hungarian by all means. this is the policy of multiculturalism and anti-minorityism that characterises the attitude towards this issue in some member states. the copenhagen criteria have examined the treatment of minorities in the candidate countries. but it must be possible to take account of the copenhagen criteria after accession. in europe, particularly in the eastern half, interethnic relations were tense. ignoring this is a huge mistake that could backfire in the future.
romania and bulgaria's accession to schengen was postponed last week for an unspecified date. two member states, the netherlands and finland, objected without giving reasons under community law. these member states have not only blocked access to the schengen area - they have blocked the fulfilment by the two states of their obligations under the treaty. i believe that the use of domestic policy considerations in european decision-making is incorrect and unproductive. the european parliament has already voted its agreement on this subject. i think that it must come back and speak very clearly, once again, particularly with regard to respect for community rules and respect between member states. we must remember a rule of good conduct: keep your word. i think it is necessary to prove at the european council in october that the union still exists. the decision must be taken that the two member states join schengen.
the current proposal for an energy efficiency directive proposes measures to reduce energy consumption by 20% by 2020, including improving technologies and reducing losses in energy systems. the romanian government has found an original solution to achieve this mandatory objective much earlier and without investment. instead of proposing measures to eliminate the heat losses of over 40% of romania's district heating system, the boc government cut the heating subsidy for low-income families. next winter, a million families will be unable to pay their heating bills and will have to relinquish their heat energy and live in the cold. thus, at national level, the 20% reduction target will be reached quickly. i call on the european commission to take action against this decision which violates the fundamental human right to a decent life.
i would like to congratulate mr koch on his report and also welcome the recent adoption of the directive on the crossborder prosecution of road traffic offences. this directive will certainly help to increase road safety at european level. given the link between high road accidents and the quality of transport infrastructure, we call on the member states to ensure the development of road transport infrastructure and compliance with the rules on road signalling and, in particular, those on signalling of road infrastructure works. we also call on the commission to adopt as soon as possible the specifications for intelligent transport systems mentioned in the intelligent transport systems directive, namely: the provision at union level of real-time traffic information services, data and procedures for the provision to users, free of charge, where possible, of minimum universal traffic information, the implementation of an interoperable system at european union level and the provision of services and information on safe parking spaces for trucks. last but not least, i would stress the importance of developing and improving road safety education programmes, especially for children and young people.
water is a scarce resource, even though it covers over 70% of the earth's surface. it is essential for life, but it can also cause major natural disasters, either through drought or flooding. we see this paradox again when we approach the subject of dams. in many cases, dams are the only way to supply power to communities isolated by mountains or rugged terrain. these systems are also a clean source of electricity. but if the construction is faulty, the impact becomes negative from an ecological and social point of view. i stress the need for any new projects in this area to be based on comprehensive impact assessments, starting with the recommendations of the world commission on dams. i therefore ask the commission to promote these issues in its dialogue with other countries.
the global food crisis is not only a growing humanitarian problem but also a major threat to world peace and security. the growing danger of food speculation, climate change, biofuels, biodiversity loss, soil degradation and pressure on water resources are the main causes of hunger, malnutrition and food insecurity. i welcome the unambiguous policy option of proposing that the right to food become a cornerstone of the european union's policy framework. ensuring food security requires the coherence and coordination of the various sectoral policies at eu level, namely development policy, the common agricultural policy, the common trade policy, energy policy and research programmes. in addition, the european union and partner countries should establish transparent monitoring mechanisms, including the participation of civil society organisations and local authorities, to ensure the proper implementation of right to food policies.

the rapporteur. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, at this late hour of the day, the pupils are sleeping, i hope, the teachers will soon be sleeping too, but we are watching. the report is based on the commission's last report on the european schools system and aims to improve the concept of european schools, which must be adapted to new economic requirements and changes in society. this concept must remain an inspirational model for national school systems, valuing european citizenship and promoting the development of mobility, as well as the learning of the languages of the member states, the languages of the countries of europe. the report's main points are: firstly, it contains a series of political priorities for improving this model of education in europe, in particular by establishing it on an adequate legal basis, as provided for in the merger treaty. the current legal status has reached its limits and requires a profound change which would enable the union to take action to support, coordinate or supplement the action of the member states, without, of course, substituting itself for their powers, but also to adopt legally binding acts within the meaning of articles 2 and 6 of the merger treaty. i believe that article 165 of the treaty could be a very appropriate legal basis. the european schools must serve as an example of teaching based on the dissemination of culture, values, european integration and european languages. it is therefore essential that member states cooperate in the development of their national school curricula, taking advantage of the simple example, which has worked wonderfully so far, of the european schools in terms of teaching. the opening of type 2 and type 3 schools must be strongly encouraged. it is in this spirit that the report stresses that holders of the european baccalaureate may apply for admission to any university in the union once and for all, with the same rights as nationals of that state with equivalent qualifications, since it is essential that this baccalaureate be automatically recognised in all the member states of the union. in this difficult period, i wanted to stress the absolute need to rationalise the costs of running these schools, without questioning the fundamental principles on which this concept is based, and in particular teaching in the mother tongue by native speakers, in order to preserve the quality of this education. i also believe it is essential to maintain equal and equivalent conditions of education for children of all the language communities in european schools. it is therefore in the interests of fairness that the report stresses, in accordance with article 4 of the convention on the status of european schools, that it is envisaged to generalize the use of so-called 'vehicular languages' for the teaching of all non-basic subjects, without this, of course, being to the detriment of pupils whose mother tongue is not one of these 'vehicular languages'. the lack of seconded staff also needs to be taken very seriously in order to ensure good governance of the european schools. this should be compensated by the local recruitment of lecturers whose salaries should be borne by the schools. the higher council must therefore ensure that those member states which do not contribute financially by posting teachers make an equivalent contribution to the school budget, as they are obliged to do. i also wanted to reiterate that, especially in these difficult times, the care of pupils with special educational needs remains a priority, and in this regard i asked the higher council to ensure that the coefficients are applied to this category of pupils when calculating class sizes in order to preserve their full integration. finally, madam president, commissioner, i repeat my request to the higher council to look for alternatives to enable students who are unable to remain in the sector to find vocational courses. i would not like to end this report without thanking the commission, my colleagues, the fictitious rapporteurs and rapporteurs, but also the parents' unions in particular, who have enabled us to reach a consensus to move this matter forward. sorry i stole 45 seconds from you.

the objective of absorbing as much financial support as possible requires ongoing efforts by the member states, and the involvement of local and regional government at every stage of the process is essential. the rules on these funds are complex, making it difficult to implement them in national law and to comply with them, which can lead to difficulties, and member states and regions spend too much time trying to manage and control these difficulties. there is a need for simpler and more flexible rules and procedures, both at union and national level, to facilitate access to european funds and to promote their sound management by the administrative services without creating major difficulties for the beneficiaries. this simplification should contribute to the rapid allocation of funds, higher absorption rates, increased efficiency and transparency, fewer errors in implementation and shorter payment deadlines. proposals in future framework documents and operational programmes must respond as closely as possible to the needs of the relevant actors.
the european union's regional policy helps to reduce disparities between regions and stimulate development and job creation. the rate at which eu funds are absorbed by the member states varies. romania has a very low absorption rate, but this should not diminish the eu funds that romania can access and needs in the 2014-2020 period. increasing the absorption of european funds requires the timely adoption of the multiannual financial framework, greater flexibility in the organisation of operational programmes, their preparation and timely adoption. we believe that more european funds are needed to develop energy infrastructure and energy efficiency measures for housing. the commission will allocate €10 billion from the cohesion fund for the period 2014-2020 to transport infrastructure in countries under the convergence criterion. this money will be managed by the trans-european transport executive agency. i ask that the national allocations be retained, even though the project applications will be released by the tnt executive agency.

the european union solidarity fund is generally functioning well, but experience gained during the first years of implementation shows that there are important limitations and weaknesses in the functioning of the fund. these are related to the lack of speed with which funding from the fund is made available, the degree of transparency of the criteria for mobilising the fund in the event of regional disasters and the delimitation of natural disasters. i would remind you that several member states have received financial support from the european union for projects in areas affected by various disasters, but the funds were not released in time to be most effective. to this end, i believe that the possibility of providing assistance in the form of an advance payment system based on the initial estimate of the damage of a country affected by a disaster, upon its request, would be a facility that would be greatly appreciated by the affected areas immediately after a disaster has occurred.
the european union and its citizens are facing an alarming increase in the number and severity of disasters. the disasters that have struck all the countries of the world demonstrate the need to strengthen a european force for rapid response to emergencies. disaster-generating events cannot be avoided, but they can be managed and their effects reduced. reducing the risk associated with natural phenomena requires a series of measures and actions embodied in policies to prevent the impact of disasters. the financial assistance of over eur 2 billion provided over the period 2002-2010 through the solidarity fund confirms the eu's key role in supporting disaster-stricken states. the money allocated, however, is hard to reach the people affected, and it is necessary to create an efficient mechanism for the immediate mobilisation of the amounts allocated from the solidarity fund, which can find a correspondent in each of the member states as quickly. thank you and congratulations to mrs. gardini.
madam president, the multiplication of natural disasters and human-produced disasters is a fact. at the same time, there is more and more strain on the national means available for response, not least because the rest of the world expects the eu to respond to their disasters, too. until now that response has been ad hoc and too bureaucratic. therefore, a complete overhaul of the entire system is indispensable, and this very detailed report provides the necessary orientation. in essence, we have to eliminate redundancies and increase the efficiency of what we want to keep. in that respect, we need to shift the emphasis from reaction to prevention, stressing monitoring, scenario preparation and education. we need to create a permanent pool of the national means placed at our disposal for such purposes and increase the flexibility of our procedures to make the entire system more operative. the main conditionality would be subsidiarity, then availability of means – both material and financial. finally, let us not forget that civil protection is entirely in line with the eu philosophy of intervention, and let us stress the civilian element over the military which, even if not entirely eliminated, will not be central.
in writing. – the 2010 floods in romania brought sudden disaster and tragic loss of life to many communities. since then, we have seen many natural disasters unfold around the world, with significant human, environmental, and economic costs. the costs of both the immediate emergency response and long-term reconstruction are considerable. so i welcome this report’s emphasis on improving the flexibility and efficiency of the solidarity fund, which can provide valuable assistance to member states and the assurance they need to release funds in the aftermath of a disaster. i also support the calls for a response capacity based on the european civil protection mechanism, which pools capabilities and expertise from across the eu so as to provide the best and most efficient expert help during times of crises. many disasters happen despite being entirely preventable. last year, the european parliament adopted a resolution calling for a complete ban on the use of cyanide technology in mining projects, because of the potential for cross-border environmental catastrophe in the event of an accident. yet despite this, the romanian government is about to approve such a mining project, which poses a grave threat to the environment and valuable cultural heritage of a whole region.
in writing. we live in an interconnected world, where damage to one element can have unintended consequences elsewhere. the lessons learned from many disasters show the important role that information and its exchange between actors play, not only in preventing but also in responding effectively to critical situations. for this reason, i consider it imperative and i support the creation of a european emergency response centre. as cooperation has enabled us to prosper at continental level and to be an economic leader for a long time, it is necessary to create a reserve of means, capacities and resources for union interventions in crisis situations, but also to act unitedly on the world stage. we must bear in mind that our environmental footprint extends far beyond the union's borders and we must therefore be solidarity-oriented not only in sharing the benefits of our actions but also in sharing the costs.
the volatility of food and commodity prices has become a major problem, adding to the poverty of millions of people and threatening the functioning of the global financial system. trade imbalances and speculative activity are at the root of this volatility, and climate change will continue to exacerbate it. a european trade policy strategy must address the central role of the union in the multilateral trading system. this long-term strategy must have clear objectives, take account of developments in the international trading system and emphasise elements consistent with union principles, such as the importance of access to generic medicines for the poorest, or the need to include fair trade, human rights and social and environmental standards automatically in all trade agreements.
in writing. although the european economy is the largest in the world, with the eu being both the main exporter and the main supplier and recipient of foreign direct investment, it is estimated that by 2015, 90% of global growth will be generated outside europe. in the years ahead, the european union must seize the opportunities offered by high levels of growth abroad. in this respect, i would like to refer to public procurement, which is an area where foreign markets are largely closed to union companies. representing on average more than 10% of gdp in these countries, public procurement constitutes significant business opportunities in sectors where eu industry is highly competitive. given that our market is already wide open, i believe that the clear priority in reciprocal access is not to close european markets but to open foreign public procurement markets. i therefore strongly urge the eu to step up its efforts to facilitate access to public procurement abroad for european companies and to eliminate discriminatory practices.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i consider the absorption of the structural and cohesion funds to be one of the main priorities in the implementation of eu cohesion policy. the absorption capacity is essential to make the maximum contribution to the eu's economic and social cohesion using the resources available from the funds. the objective of absorbing this much-needed financial support requires both ongoing efforts by the member states and the involvement of local and regional government at every stage of the process. i support the rapporteur's position on the need to simplify rules and procedures in order to achieve higher absorption rates, reduce errors and increase efficiency. i agree that a balance should be struck between simplification and the stability of rules and procedures. last but not least, a very important aspect highlighted in this report is the existence of large differences in the absorption capacity of the member states. therefore, increased attention should be paid to the establishment of cooperation programmes between member states for the exchange of good practice.
in writing. − we have all had to learn during this programming period and it is clear that the management and control system raises serious operational problems for some member states that need to make the most of the lessons learned. the first proof will be the involvement of all local and regional stakeholders in the programming phase. it is essential that potential applicants or beneficiaries are involved in the preparation of operational programmes, which will thus become more relevant and better suited to their needs. we also need to pay more attention to administrative capacity, i.e. human resources at both local and regional and national levels. i believe that the attraction and retention of qualified staff can be improved. it is therefore useful for the member states to understand that even technical assistance or esf funds can be used for this and i am confident that this will happen.
in writing. − the european union and its member states face many risks, such as earthquakes, fires, floods, landslides, industrial and nuclear accidents, terrorist attacks, natural disasters and major pandemics. recently, there has been a dramatic increase in the number and severity of these natural and man-made disasters, affecting citizens worldwide with corresponding increases in loss of life, economic, social and environmental damage and damage to cultural heritage. we cannot exclude the possibility of such extreme events of unpredictable magnitude occurring at any time, in which case the european response to disasters would prove extremely useful, as national capacities could be tested to the limit. i therefore believe that scientific research in this area needs to be developed with a view to improving risk assessment mechanisms, prevention systems and the means of combating these phenomena. the most effective disaster management strategy is an integrated approach to crisis response at all stages, taking into account all risks and linking disaster prevention with preparedness, response and recovery in the broader context of sustainable development.
in writing. − i would like to remind you that romania was financially supported by the european union for projects in the flood-stricken areas, but the release of funds was delayed compared to the time when it would have been most effective. to this end, i consider that the possibility of providing assistance, in the form of an advance payment system based on the initial estimate of direct damage, to a country affected by a disaster, upon its request, would be a facility that would be highly appreciated by the affected areas immediately after a disaster.
in writing. − in my view, as i have already argued in numerous interventions, the european commission should take steps to allow the eu solidarity fund to be more flexible and to simplify its administrative rules, as such a simplification of administrative procedures would speed up the payments made and ensure that those in need of support receive payments immediately. another observation made over time in the regi commission is that european regions on the eu's borders can be affected by disasters in regions in third countries, in which case intervention is even more difficult. it is therefore imperative to develop specific measures to support these regions, taking into account man-made disasters and industrial accidents, which require different strategies. last but not least, the commission must ensure in the future that member states involve regional and local authorities in disaster response from the outset, based on the multi-level governance model applied in the field of cohesion policy, through a communication strategy that benefits all actors involved in the response mechanism.
in writing. - we live in a time of increasing disasters. the annual number of recorded disasters worldwide has increased fivefold in the last 35 years, to nearly 400 today. disasters in europe over the past 20 years have killed nearly 90 000 people, affected more than 29 million people and caused economic losses of eur 211 billion. we voted for this report to create the mechanism for increasing efficiency at all stages of the european disaster management cycle, including prevention, preparedness, response and recovery, while optimising economic resources during times of austerity. this approach enjoys overwhelming support from around 90% of european citizens, who expect the eu to do more to help their country when it is hit by a disaster, with a similar percentage supporting eu humanitarian action outside the eu. i stress the importance of all member states contributing, in a spirit of european solidarity, to the european response to disasters.
in writing. − although euro banknotes and coins were put into circulation in 2002, the market for the transport of euro cash by road remains highly fragmented due to the wide differences between national rules in this area, which make it significantly difficult for professional cash handlers to provide crossborder services. the purpose of this regulation is therefore to simplify those regulatory constraints in order to allow for a better circulation of euro banknotes and coins between euro area member states. given the particular dangers of transporting funds, this regulation should contribute to strengthening public security requirements both for the security staff providing transport and for the general public. as regards the various methods of transporting funds, member states should be able to choose as many options as they wish from the five transport modes for banknotes and the two transport modes for coins provided for by the regulation. i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is important that there are sufficiently clear and operational rules for cash carriers in and for the state authorities.
in writing. − tourism contributes to the enrichment of the human spirit, to the achievement of exchanges, to well-being, to the development of culture, and to social cohesion. the aim of the project is to promote the development of tourism in the european union by promoting the development of tourism-related activities and activities, and by promoting the development of tourism-related activities. the diversity, variety and multiculturalism of europe enhance any form of thematic tourism, and the development and promotion of diversified forms of tourism can be the only effective solution against the distortions, problems and deterioration caused by the unregulated and undifferentiated mass tourism model. the development of tourism plays a key role in enhancing the regional dimension within the european union. tourism is a very important economic resource and the main calling card that europe presents to the world. at the same time, i believe that european tourism is not being exploited to its true potential. europe has a lot to offer both its own citizens and the rest of the world. i therefore urge the member states to facilitate and promote the training of tourism operators, to support the diversification and specialisation of european tourism and to encourage tourism organisations to exchange good practice.
in writing. − in its strategy for promoting european tourism, i believe that the union should consider and stimulate cooperation between regions in the framework of interregional projects, which will allow the promotion of their specific traditions, especially those of regions in different member states with common traditions, as well as the promotion of sites important to the history of the european union, especially those not included in traditional tourist circuits.
in writing. − there is now a growing talk about increasing the eu's global competitiveness, and tourism is one of the most important socioeconomic activities, generating a good part of the european union's gdp. i believe that the strategy presented by the commission represents a concrete starting point for the development of sustainable, competitive, modern, high-quality and accessible tourism. we must do everything we can to remain the world's number one tourist destination and to do that we must make the most of all possible funding opportunities. in this context, i call on the european executive to develop and mobilise specific community support instruments and programmes for the development of european tourism, in line with the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. − talking about road safety is a duty of the authorities of any state. just like they have to talk about a great health care system to save lives and good schools to educate. romania is trying to have safer roads. we're still far from ideal, but statistics show that each year the number of accidents with casualties is decreasing. romania ranks 24th out of 27 member states in the criterion that measures safety on public roads. it's a place that does not honor us and that forces us to take serious action. road fatalities have dropped by 11% since 2001. but we know that people are not numbers and behind every accident is the drama of many families and the drama of loss of human life. romania is aware that it needs to learn from the experience of other member states that have managed to significantly reduce the number of fatal road accidents. romania has a chance to achieve this goal faster by learning from and benefiting from the experience of other eu member states. romania has committed itself to the european union's goal of reducing the number of serious accidents on romanian roads by at least half by 2020.
in writing. − water is a scarce natural resource, which requires an analysis of the fairness of its allocation. it should therefore be stressed that rethinking the management of freshwater resources in the context of climate change is undoubtedly a key challenge for the whole world. on the other hand, no other natural phenomenon has proved more destructive in terms of damage or loss of life than floods in the last century, despite billions of dollars spent on flood management. i believe that balanced investment in management measures and improvements in water collection and storage methods is needed to increase efficient and sustainable water uses, to mitigate the effect of floods and recurrent droughts and to achieve minimum water security. i urge priority to be given to investments that reduce rural poverty, strengthen climate resilience and adaptation and stimulate cooperation in the international watershed.
in writing. − global demand for agricultural products is estimated to increase by around 70% by 2050 and the world population is also estimated to reach 9 billion by then. as food insecurity is aggravated by many factors, but particularly climate change, i believe it is necessary and urgent for the european union to take action to restore food stocks which have fallen to record levels in recent years, which has implicitly led to speculation on the prices of agricultural products on the market. as a women's rights advocate, i strongly believe that women, as smallholder farmers, play a fundamental role in food and nutrition security for themselves and their children. in this context, i believe that the european union must adopt a strategy to encourage and secure livelihoods for women and to improve knowledge of proper nutrition. last but not least, i should mention that the european commission should focus on implementing a set of measures so that women, as small farmers, benefit from agricultural training opportunities, nutrition education, good health and working conditions, and food safety measures.
in writing. - i voted against paragraph 63 of the zimmer report on an eu policy framework to support developing countries in their efforts to meet the challenges of food security. the claims in this paragraph are not supported by the facts and i do not believe that we should, in these circumstances, advocate either the 'elimination of export subsidies' or the elimination of all other 'incentives in the cap which have the effect of distorting trade'.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on supporting developing countries in their efforts to meet food security challenges. access to decent food is a universal right. according to fao, in 2010, 925 million people were affected by hunger. globally, 26% of children under five years of age are malnourished, and over a third of deaths among children under five years of age are due to malnutrition. i emphasize the role of smallholder farmers in developing countries and in particular the role of women in ensuring nutritional security for themselves and their children. small farmers must use sustainable agricultural practices and have access to microcredit. in view of the growing population and the increasing pressure on natural resources, it is essential to ensure sustainable and efficient agricultural production on a global scale. the fao reported in february 2011 that food prices have reached an all-time high and will continue to rise. i call on the commission and the member states to invest in agriculture so that the eu can improve its production capacity to help meet both its own needs and to export agricultural products to third countries.
in writing. − economic growth, prosperity, jobs and the maintenance of the european social model are closely linked and mutually supportive. this report sets out how trade and investment policy should contribute to these objectives, as well as to foreign policy objectives in general. in addition, trade policy is one of the main tools available to the eu to support progress in reform and democratisation. trade stimulates efficiency and the spirit of innovation. europe must reap the benefits of greater openness to trade and investment, while remaining vigilant to the costs of adjustment: stronger growth, more jobs and lower consumer prices. trade should also bring improvements in social inclusion, both globally and in the eu. developing countries that have entered into world trade and global production chains have benefited from rapidly growing incomes and labour markets, as well as significant poverty reduction. the rapporteur gives greater transparency and legitimacy to the european union's trade policy. i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. - i voted for the report by mr caspary because i believe that the eu needs a coherent trade strategy to strengthen european competitiveness in world trade. as a result of changing areas of economic influence, europe is faced with international challenges. trade needs to be based on fair global competition and full reciprocity. the fragmentation of the production system at european and international level has highlighted the need for liberalisation of the services sector. the quality and price of services play a crucial role in the efficiency of firms. to have a competitive and sustainable economy, the eu needs an internal services policy. attention should also be paid to the development of information technologies. this sector has brought about fundamental changes in the world trading system.
in writing. − europe needs to rethink its trade policies because the evolution of trade policies in recent years shows that the focus is beginning to shift towards developing countries. exports are a prerequisite for economic growth and job creation or growth. international trade in the european union faces several challenges. in 2000, the eu and the us together accounted for 48% of world gdp. but estimates show that by 2020 they will only be 35 percent. while in 1999 eu exports accounted for 19% of the global total, in 2009 the percentage dropped to 17%. the center of gravity of the world economy is shifting to the developing world. in the eu, 36 million jobs (18% of the total) are directly linked to international trade. it is estimated that by 2015, 90% of global economic growth will be generated outside the eu, leading to increased dependence on the union's trade. in these circumstances, the european parliament's call to the european commission to consider policies to boost trade policies in the long term is welcome. we have a duty to think of the future as well as the present.
in writing. - i fully agree with this report because it raises a key issue in the difficult period we are currently living through: the decline of the european union's global trading power. despite the urgent need for action, i support the idea of a long-term economic strategy that will lead to economic growth and stability. in this respect, the european union must aim, both internally and internationally, at harmonising standards and removing the various barriers to trade and investment. that said, as a member of the committee on the internal market, i am pleased to see that the report stresses the importance of balancing these objectives on the one hand and maintaining high technical standards and economic balance within the european union on the other. last but not least, given the social mission of the european union, i fully support the commitment expressed in this report to fight poverty and to respect fundamental values such as the protection of human rights or the rule of law in the implementation of these measures.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on 'a new trade policy for europe in line with the europa 2020 strategy', as economic growth, prosperity, jobs and the european social model also depend to a large extent on the eu's trade policy. the commission estimates that 18% of the union workforce (36 million jobs) is dependent on the union's trade performance. european industry is facing increasing global competition from industrialised and emerging countries such as china, india and the states of the mercosur region in terms of access to resources, technological innovation, skilled labour as well as industrial and innovation policies. the eu is today india's most important source of foreign direct investment (fdi), accounting for 27% of total fdi in 2009, and trade between the eu and mercosur amounts to around eur 100 billion annually. the development of the eu's industrial policy depends on the availability of resources and raw materials. the eu's future trade policy must therefore aim to secure raw materials and resources so that industrial production and jobs are kept within the eu.
last month, the gaddafi regime collapsed after rebels took the capital. today, pro-ntc forces control the port of sirte, which means that very soon libya will be able to engage in a transition to democracy. in syria, the regime of bashar al-assad will very likely soon meet the same fate. while tunisians, egyptians, libyans and, hopefully, all of us, soon, syrians, are discovering the taste of freedom, the landscape is very different in the middle east. if north africa is on the agenda for democratization and will succeed if it establishes a policy based on compromise, we see something quite different in the middle east peace process. it is not the consensus construct that seems to prevail here, but a one-sided vision. that, in my opinion, is the meaning of the application for membership of the united nations submitted by president abbas on friday. instead of trying to build genuine internal autonomy before imposing it internationally, president abbas has chosen, as president obama said, an illusory shortcut. the palestinian accession request is in fact going beyond the negotiating framework defined by the oslo accords and specified in the roadmap presented by the quartet in 2003. peace is built through negotiation, not unilateral action. the lesson of the arab spring for the peace process should be that democracy means seeking consensus and not unilateralism.
on the basis of the good bilateral relations it has developed with both israel and the palestinian national authority, romania has always encouraged the parties to sit down at the negotiating table without preconditions. my position on this subject is a principled one. resuming negotiations is the best course of action to achieve a two-state solution that will allow for peace and security. i believe that unilateral action is not conducive to the establishment of a lasting peace, which is the fundamental objective of the entire international community. i strongly believe that the only way to fulfill the palestinian ideals is through direct negotiations. i will support any initiative that might serve that purpose, as i have done so far. there can be no viable long-term solution unless there is an agreement between the palestinians and the israelis. any recognition of palestine as a state must be based on a mutually acceptable solution with which both sides can go to the un. finally, i welcome the quartet statement calling on both sides to resume direct bilateral negotiations immediately and without preconditions. it is not too late for diplomatic efforts, on the contrary it is time to step them up.

vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − madam president, can i just say to honourable members that we have seen the debate laid out before us? if you add up all the different views expressed in this house, you will find that they reflect, and are reflected in, many of the conversations that i have had, not just in the european union, but with many other countries as well. let us start where we agree. we agree that there should be a palestinian state. everybody supports that, including israel. i agree with all of you who have said that it is important to see a palestinian state come into being as soon as possible. the question is how to support the palestinian state into being in a way that will bring long-term peace and security to its people and to the people of israel, who will be its neighbours next door. i would argue that we are discussing the question of how – not if, not whether, not any other question, but how – to make sure that is achieved. it has been the view of the european union, the view of this house and the view of member states for a long time that the most effective way to ensure long-term stability and security for the people of israel and the people of palestine is through an agreement between the two on borders, on security, on the rights of refugees, on the issue of jerusalem, on all of the issues that are very familiar to everybody here. that is what i am determined upon. i am determined upon reality. i am determined upon making sure that the desire of the people, the desire of president abbas and prime minister fayyad, is achieved and is achieved in a way that they can be sure is going to bring that peace and security to them and to the region. that is what drives me and what motivates me to work with the member states, to work with you, to work with my colleagues in the commission, and to work internationally with the quartet and – way beyond the quartet – with many countries with whom i have discussed this issue, not just in new york last week, but over the past two years. i want to be clear about one thing, namely about settlements. i have condemned it every time a settlement announcement has been made – six times this year from me, plus one local one and one quartet one. i have checked the numbers. the announcement that was made today is an announcement of the continuation of a series of legal moves following on from an announcement that was made in 2009. i said earlier on that i deeply regretted that, having condemned that original announcement, we have now seen a move further forward. we have made that position clear, not just in this house, but also to the israeli government. can i also say that, instead of shouting about it – which is very easy to do, perhaps without listening for the response that you get – i say this to prime minister netanyahu directly. each time i have met him – and i have met him many times – i have made it clear that we consider settlements to be illegal under international law, and that he should stop announcing them and, more importantly, stop building them. i do not accept, i am afraid, what is said to me that somehow, by not using a particular word, i have moved away from my commitment, because i am the one who, on your behalf, is saying it to the person who has the power to make the difference. i will continue to do so in every conversation, not just because it is wrong. i think that it is wrong to get people to live in a place from which, when you look at a negotiated settlement, they are probably going to have to move. that does not make any sense, to me, for the people who are moving in to that area. it is not a good move if you believe – as i do – that we have to reach a conclusion and a settlement for this conflict that is going to be based upon – as we have said consistently – the 1967 borders, with agreements on moving bits of land around, but which give the palestinians a viable contiguous state. that is going to mean that there will have to be changes. it is therefore in the interests of all the people of israel and palestine to get there and make sure that where people move and where people live is somewhere they can live for the rest of their lives if they choose to. i also want to make it clear that i have said to israel that i do believe in president abbas and prime minister fayyad. they have people with whom they can be proud to negotiate. i believe that president abbas and prime minister fayyad, who i have had the privilege to get to know over the last two years, are people who hold the values that we hold dear in their heart. i believe that they want to see a democratic palestine, based on the rule of law and the values of human rights. i believe that israel could do no better than to negotiate with them. i have also said that directly to prime minister netanyahu, to foreign minister lieberman and to other members inside and outside the israeli government and in the knesset. i will continue to keep saying that, because i believe it to be true. i have said many times that i think that the work that prime minister fayyad has done has been remarkable in that, according not to me but to the world bank and other institutions, he has completed the building of the institutions that will create the state of palestine and will enable them to be able to function as a state – an important element if they are going to become a country, in the very near future i hope. i was fortunate enough to go with prime minister fayyad privileged to be able to fund. i said in the un when i met with the ad hoc liaison committee under the chairmanship of norway – to whom i pay great tribute – that i felt this was a good investment of our resources, because you can see what our money and our support has actually built and achieved. i think that we should be proud to be investing in the work of prime minister fayyad. as i say, i pay tribute to him. we have to make sure that everything that we are doing on this is actually going to help to lead to the results. that is why i have been working with the israeli government, the palestinian authority, the arab league, the united states, canada, russia, and the un especially – because i agree with what has been said about the value and importance of the un in all this. i could not agree more. i think the united nations are critical to all this, but what matters is what we are actually able to achieve. the point about what we did in the quartet statement was that we laid out quartet envoys will need to discuss, which is why they will pre-meet with the parties, but the objective is to get this thing moving. i understand the frustration in this house. i have only been doing happening in the north of kosovo, as you would expect me to be. it is really important that whatever we do finds a conclusion that is really going to last. i am not going to do something that is just in writing. – ever since the arab spring began, one question imposed itself: would those revolutionary developments speed up or delay resolution of the middle east conflict, which is one that has the potential to ignite an international conflagration? well, now, many months after, although things are no clearer, one can detect a slight tilt of the balance towards the latter. in that respect, i am particularly concerned at the possibility that the new revolutionary authorities in those countries, faced with the impossibility of fulfilling the high expectations of their populations, might try to deflect popular energy towards israel. this might be true even for the palestinian authorities, which probably saw in the recent request for un state recognition a way to escape possible contestation from ordinary palestinians, emboldened by the example of their other arab brothers. it looks as if, recently, both hamas and fatah have been losing ground. irrespective of whether these suppositions are true or not, the potential implications of a worsening of the middle east conflict would only underline the crucial importance of eu involvement and support in the region.
mr president, the warsaw summit will acknowledge the european aspirations of our east european partners. that is true, but is it enough or is it a ritual phrase unfit for the political realities developing along our eastern borders? at a time when tymoshenko is subjected to a stalinist trial, at a time when putin and medvedev swap places like interchangeable tsars, our message should reaffirm the democratic alternative, as a counterweight to the putinist contagion that threatens the whole area. and yet our messages are not exactly convincing. membership prospects are almost taboo. liberalisation and trade agreements are moving forward, but at a slow pace. the focus on the events in the south has generated frustration in the east. our partners have reason to believe that they have been downgraded. the nabucco project is less visible than it used to be. the mediation capacity of the union cannot properly deal with so-called frozen conflicts. as a result, the frozen conflicts are ready to ignite. to sum it up, all is quiet on the eastern front. this deficit of political will does not encourage our partners to pursue democratic reforms. this could add a strategic and an energy crisis, which would multiply the economic crisis that we already know. the eastern dimension of our policies is ours to develop.
mr president, the eastern partnership has been our response to the interruption of gas supply from russia and to the conflict in georgia. we wanted to reassure the eastern countries that they were not forgotten and their hope to get closer to the eu is a tangible expectation. the fact that all these countries belong to the former soviet space has inevitably brought russia into the equation, complicating it from the very beginning. moreover, since then, the current problems in the eu created by the crisis, and the unexpected developments in north africa, have complicated matters even further, while not deterring russia from taking advantage of these difficulties. i would only hope that when the negotiations on the association agreements are completed, there will not be any last-minute political change of heart, on our part, in honouring them.
the eastern partnership represents a great opportunity for the countries of the european union's eastern neighbourhood and can become a real engine for political and economic stability, security and prosperity in these countries. i therefore believe that this initiative launched in 2009 should not only be continued but also strengthened. i am pleased that the polish presidency is making the eastern partnership a priority and i am confident that thursday's summit will give a new impetus to cooperation with these countries. we need to take into account the findings of the implementation report and the various country reports and thus come up with solutions that match the progress and specific needs of each country. the future actions of this cooperation must also bring the most tangible benefits to the citizens of these countries, which will encourage them in their efforts towards democratisation and economic development. last but not least, we need adequate financial resources, and it will be important to allocate an ambitious percentage to the eastern partnership for the period 2014-2020.
in writing. i believe that improving relations with our neighbours in the east is very important and we must support the consolidation of democracy in these countries. the prague declaration, followed by the launch of the eastern partnership, includes an initiative containing the following phrase 'we will take steps towards visa liberalisation'. we cannot talk about a rapprochement with the eastern partnership countries without taking this important step seriously. a positive note was noted in chisinau, where the latest developments in the implementation of the visa liberalisation action plan, as well as the european commission's first progress report, recently published, were presented at the expanded meeting of the working group on the coordination of the visa liberalisation process with the eu. the eu should remove the 'long-term objective' from all relevant visa liberalisation documents, including from the draft association agreements with moldova as well as with other eastern partnership countries. by promoting citizens' mobility and contacts with the eu, we are also supporting the development of countries in europe's neighbourhood, such as the republic of moldova. visa liberalisation promotes good understanding, links with civil society and intercultural exchanges. this would be a first sign that the eastern partnership's intentions are open and serious.
in writing. the eastern partnership summit is an important opportunity to strengthen and refine the union's relationship with the countries of the east. welcomes the approach of the commission and the high representative catherine ashton, set out in communication com ((2011) 303), to treat each country in the union's neighbourhood policy on its merits (the principle of differentiation/'more for more') and on the basis of clear criteria; the republic of moldova is a model for the eastern partnership. over the past two years, the alliance for european integration has initiated important reforms in constant consultation with the union. i welcome the explicit reference by the european parliament to the prospect of the republic of moldova's accession to the eu, in accordance with article 49 of the treaty (the recent resolution on the association agreement). the accession perspective is important for reformers in this country, it is the motivation and the stimulus for efforts to continue and implement the necessary reforms. the european parliament also called for the opening of negotiations with the republic of moldova on the free trade agreement by the end of 2011 and for increased efforts to be made to resolve the conflict in the transnistrian region, while respecting the territorial integrity of the republic of moldova. i welcome prime minister vlad filat's recent announcement of the resumption of formal negotiations in the 5+2 format and i consider relevant his vision of replacing troops in the transnistrian region with a civilian mission. it is important that the eu has a greater role in these negotiations.
in writing. the warsaw summit is an important moment to analyse the progress made in the union's eastern neighbourhood as a basis for developing concrete policies for a common future. the european union must support the democratic transition in the eastern partnership countries. i therefore believe that a key step in this direction is to set out a clear perspective for the accession of partner countries and to implement the structural reforms needed to align with european policies and rules. i would like to stress the need for concrete commitments by the union in the area of the conclusion of association and free trade agreements, and the importance of visa liberalisation for eastern european partners. we should also not forget the role of local and regional authorities in harmonising relations within the eastern partnership. their contribution is essential and should be focused in particular on territorial development, supporting mutual contacts and improving economic relations. eastern partnership countries also need to take important steps to increase respect for human rights, fundamental freedoms, and the rule of law. the union's objective in the eastern neighbourhood must be centred around the creation of a democratic and stable region, guaranteeing respect for freedom, dignity and fundamental rights.
in writing. – i would like to underline three main ideas. first of all, i consider that the perspective of membership should be the silver thread that guides our relations with the eastern neighbours. not only do these countries belong geographically to our continent, but they are deeply interlinked with the eu through both history and culture. enlargement has been the most successful foreign policy tool of the eu and can serve as a strong incentive for internal reforms aiming to reach deep democracy in these countries. nevertheless, we all understand that membership of the eu will not be accomplished tomorrow. not only because of the enlargement fatigue, but also because these internal reforms take time and sometimes steps forward can be followed by steps backwards, as the case of ukraine proves it so clearly. this is why we should pursue firmly the objective of visa liberalisation, in order to provide people-to-people contacts. a democratic evolution of these countries through emulation of already set standards can only come along in this way. finally, we should apply the principle more for more, encouraging countries such as georgia or moldova, that have made significant progress lately and whose willingness for reform must be wholeheartedly welcomed.
in writing. the turkish-cypriot conflict - frozen by the international community's inability to get the parties to reach a negotiated solution - is re-emerging in a highly tense international context, particularly in the mediterranean. and turkey has its share of responsibility in escalating tensions in the region. after deteriorating relations with israel, the turkish government - faithful to the aggressive policy of recent years - decided to counter the cypriot government's intention to explore gas fields off the island, launching its own exploitation in the eastern mediterranean. this policy of force threatens the negotiations between the turkish and greek communities for the reunification of cyprus. it also risks blowing up a region already affected by political change and economic problems. i believe it is the duty of the european union to firmly reject these challenges and to show full solidarity with a member state that is the victim of threats from a third country. we strongly urge turkey to refrain from any hostile action if it wishes to remain a respected partner. the threat of a freeze on relations with the eu if cyprus takes over the union's presidency next year calls into question both turkey's european perspective and the future of bilateral relations.
there have been a number of concerns expressed here today about the future of the european union, but we also had a promising speech from the executive on the way out of the crisis and the future of the european union. unfortunately, the measures implemented by some governments in the european union have proven to be ineffective, and that is why now, more than ever, we need a total mobilization to revitalize the european union's economy. in this respect, i believe that the european union must act as one entity, must acquire powers to coordinate fiscal policies at european union level and, where appropriate, implement a common economic governance, but with a well-funded budget. it must be able to respond promptly to needs at european level and must implement appropriate arrangements for crisis management as quickly as possible. in writing. the union is, first and foremost, the 500 million european citizens united by a desire for peace and prosperity and by a belief in the european social model. today, in the union, 23 million european citizens are unemployed and 80 million european citizens are at risk of poverty. one in five young europeans is unemployed. european citizens fear for their future and that of their children. european families are facing rising prices, especially for energy, transport and food, and declining incomes, which are driving down living standards. due to the economic crisis, member state governments have cut budgets for education and health, thousands of schools and hospitals have been closed and specialist staff laid off. member states undergoing fiscal consolidation also have difficulties in securing co-financing for european projects, with a low absorption rate of european funds. this is the state of the union today. the union and the member states must invest as a priority in education and health, but must also ensure the development of transport, energy and communications infrastructure, and not least agriculture. only through bold programmes and policies can we create jobs and fulfil the aspirations of european citizens.
i voted in favour of the economic governance reform package because we are facing a difficult time and this set of measures is a very important step in the process of strengthening macroeconomic surveillance and financial discipline. to achieve future goals such as increasing competitiveness, promoting employment, strengthening financial stability or improving public finances, we need to make much more ambitious and concrete commitments. the experience gained in the first decade of the functioning of the economic and monetary union has highlighted the urgent need for improved economic governance, which implies both a real national ownership and a much stronger framework for the supervision of national economic policies at union level. by setting a set of minimum requirements for national staff, we will thus encourage both budgetary accountability and the effectiveness of the deficit procedure. last but not least, member states' budgetary planning must be based on realistic forecasts, while paying due attention to the sustainability of their social protection systems.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the request for mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) submitted by germany for the automotive industry in the regions of arnsberg and dusseldorf. the request concerns 778 redundancies in 5 enterprises in the automotive industry in the regions of arnsberg and dusseldorf in germany between march and december 2010. the 778 redundancies will increase the unemployment rate in the arnsberg and dusseldorf regions, which are already severely affected by the nokia redundancies in bochum and the closure of general motors. the german authorities argue that these redundancies were caused by the sharp decline in demand for new cars in europe, with dramatic consequences for the german car industry. eu car production in the first three quarters of 2010 was 14% lower than in the same period of 2008, and in 2009 german car production decreased by 13,8% compared to 2008 and by 16,1% compared to 2007. i call on the commission and the member states to make the necessary efforts to improve the procedural and budgetary mechanisms with a view to accelerating the mobilisation of the egf. i also ask the commission to collect and publish data on egf beneficiaries who have been reintegrated into the labour market.
in writing. − the adoption of the six-pack of economic governance legislation will fill a legislative gap in the functioning of the european union. the current budget deficit crisis has shown that the union cannot function properly on the basis of trust alone, and solidarity without supervisory and control mechanisms can destroy the confidence of citizens in some member states in the european project. the balance found between the financial correction mechanisms and the social aspects should have led to a consensual vote by all the political groups, but this did not happen, with the socialists abstaining or voting against some of the articles - this after they tried to return the laws to the parliamentary special committee (econ). the compromise reached by the epp, alde and ecr, however, prevailed and allowed the package to be sent to and adopted by the plenary. i hope that this package and the mechanisms it contains will work so that no one can say in the future that they did not have the appropriate instruments to stop a member state going wrong. the legislative package of course addresses future challenges, with the eu still having to find or implement a solution to the current crisis.
in writing. − today, the european parliament held its final vote on the economic governance package, a package of six proposals concerning the coordination of economic policies within the european union. i have chosen to oppose most of these proposals, believing that the solution to the current economic crisis cannot be one of austerity alone. the european union needs fiscal adjustment measures, but these must be combined equally with elements to promote investment, job creation and growth. the austerity package voted on today in the european parliament could fuel economic stagnation and accentuate the precarious situation of many citizens of the european union. however, i welcome the announcement made today by mr barroso, and reinforced by mr olli rehn, european commissioner for economic affairs, on the proposals the european executive is preparing to introduce a financial transaction tax and issue common european bonds. the implementation of the second initiative would allow a reduction in member states' debts and increase liquidity in the european market, fostering the long-awaited prospect of economic recovery.
