in writing. - i voted against this report because i think it is against economic logic to call for such measures in a period of recession which will certainly further impede economic growth. furthermore, i consider that this report is clearly opposed to the europe 2020 strategy. there are alternatives and the social democratic group in the european parliament has proposed a much more coherent policy, with growth and job creation as its main objective.
in writing. − i voted against the report on strengthening the surveillance of budgetary positions and the surveillance and coordination of economic policies as the whole economic governance package only introduces austerity measures and does not give member states the opportunity to invest in measures for growth and job creation. as proposed by the commission, each member state shall present its national reform programme by 30 april each year. the council shall, on a recommendation from the commission, assess whether the planned policy measures and economic assumptions of the national reform programmes are realistic. for non-euro area member states, the commission and the council shall monitor the implementation of convergence programmes to identify significant differences between the budgetary position and the medium-term budgetary objective. in the event of a significant deviation from the adjustment path towards the medium-term objective, the commission shall address a warning to the member state concerned and the council shall, within one month, adopt a policy recommendation setting a deadline of five months for correcting the deviation. i consider that these austerity measures limit the flexibility of member states to define their own set of measures to ensure economic and social development and thus contribute to the achievement of the medium-term objective.
in writing. − budgetary surveillance allows member states to benefit from prompt coordination at eu level and enables enhanced surveillance and simultaneous evaluation of both budgetary measures and structural reforms promoting growth and employment. the budgetary surveillance framework should be accompanied, in particular in times of economic downturn, by effective efforts to stimulate sustainable growth, protect social cohesion and create jobs, while respecting the priorities and needs of each member state. i consider that additional incentives and penalties are necessary to make the application of budgetary supervision more effective. those penalties should enhance the credibility of the budgetary surveillance framework in the european union and the incentives should enhance compliance. this regulation establishes a system of incentives and penalties for better implementation of the preventive and corrective components of the stability and growth pact and for strengthening the coordination and surveillance of budgetary discipline in the euro area and for maintaining financial stability in the euro area. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the euro area is going through a period of deep crisis because of weaknesses in the foundations on which the euro area was built. the stability pact is a very useful instrument for budgetary discipline, but it has been applied incorrectly, allowing the current macroeconomic imbalances to emerge. to avoid such situations in the future, but also to regain the confidence of financial markets in the single currency, a series of structural reforms are needed to address weaknesses in the budgetary surveillance system in the euro area. i believe that the agreement reached brings such improvements. one of the most important developments is the use of reverse qualified majority voting when imposing sanctions for non-compliance with the stability pact. this will strengthen the position of the european commission, which is the independent body that should be responsible for the application of sanctions, as it is unlikely that member states will apply sanctions to each other by qualified majority, as has been seen from previous experiences. the reference to eurobonds is welcome, as they can be a solution to the sovereign debt crisis by facilitating financing on financial markets at lower interest rates. obviously, eurobonds should only cover part of the public debt and contain elements that discourage 'free-rider' behaviour.
in writing. - i voted against the economic package because it is aimed exclusively at a radicalisation of austerity measures, completely ignoring the social effects. without a stimulus to growth, to investment, the stalemate risks continuing. austerity is not a panacea, and the dramatic case of greece shows this. fiscal discipline must be matched by measures against economic stagnation. without boosting consumption, job creation and strong public investment we will not have economic recovery.
in writing. − i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on the following provisions of the document resulting from the negotiations: the fine (of 0.2% of gdp) in the event of fraudulent presentation of deficit and debt statistics; increased powers granted to the commission, which will be able to request more information than previously provided for and by setting up surveillance missions in the member states; the regular and thorough evaluation by the commission of the economic governance system, in particular the effectiveness and appropriateness of sanctions; the opportunity for the competent committee of the european parliament to invite the commission, the president of the council and, where appropriate, the president of the european council or the president of the eurogroup to discuss the decisions adopted. the opportunity for the competent committee of the european parliament to invite the member state concerned by the decisions in question to participate in an exchange of views is also welcome.
in writing. − i voted against the report on the proposal for a regulation on the effective application of budgetary surveillance in the euro area as the whole economic governance package only introduces austerity measures and does not give member states the opportunity to invest in measures for growth and job creation. the commission should have a more important coordinating role in enhanced surveillance procedures, but i believe that we cannot stipulate in the text of a regulation that countries with a weaker economic or budgetary position pay a higher interest rate or have the right to borrow up to a lower proportion of gdp in euro-securities. i also believe that forcing a member state with an excessive deficit to make a non-interest bearing deposit of 0.2% of its gdp and imposing a fine of 0.2% of gdp on a member state with an excessive deficit where the council considers that it has not taken effective action in response to its recommendations within the time-limit are only very harsh austerity measures that will not foster economic development and job creation in that member state.
in writing. − the euro area needs the confidence of financial markets now more than ever, and to do this we need to adopt measures to oblige member states to respect their commitments under the stability pact. as previous experiences have shown, member states have failed to enforce budgetary discipline effectively, contributing to the public debt crisis that has seriously damaged the credibility of the single currency. reliable statistical information is needed for effective surveillance and timely detection of macroeconomic imbalances. the possibility of applying fines for the provision of false macroeconomic data, especially when the purpose is to conceal the exceeding of the targets set out in the stability pact, will discourage unfair practices. as with the other reports in the legislative package, the major qualitative contribution to the implementation of measures to correct excessive macroeconomic imbalances is the possibility of adopting sanctions by reverse qualified majority, as well as the publicity of the council's deliberations on sanctions. this will avoid the obscure agreements between member states which lead to sanctions relief and to crises like the one we are currently experiencing.
in writing. − this report puts into practice the measures to correct the macroeconomic imbalances identified by the mechanisms set out in the ferreira report, but i believe that an intermediate step was necessary by providing an interest-bearing guarantee before the 0.1% of gdp penalty was imposed. if these measures had been taken into account, the union would have had a number of more flexible measures at its disposal.
in writing. − the improved economic governance framework must be based on a european union strategy for growth and employment, an effective framework for preventing and correcting excessive budgetary positions, a robust framework for preventing and correcting macroeconomic imbalances, and strengthened financial market regulation and supervision. coordination of the economic policies of the member states must take place in the context of the broad economic policy guidelines and the employment guidelines and must involve respect for guiding principles such as price stability, the soundness and sustainability of public finances and monetary conditions. the objective of enhanced economic coordination must be to establish a stable economic and social union based on the principles of the community procedure. the internal market must contribute to the sustainable development of the union, based on balanced economic growth and price stability, a highly competitive social market economy, aiming at achieving full employment and social cohesion, and ensuring a high level of environmental protection and improving the quality of the environment. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i voted for the prevention and correction of macroeconomic imbalances because we need a strong instrument, such as the proposed regulation, to address the problem of the precarious balance, which is generated in particular by medium and long-term structural trends, by the increasingly pronounced discrepancies within the union (and in particular the euro area), and by the spill-over effects of individual member states' policies.
in writing. - of all the six-pack, mrs ferreira's report is the only one that takes account of social realities and sets out measures that will allow us in the future to detect any economic imbalances in the member states as soon as possible. if these measures had been in place, the problem of greece would have been noticed much earlier and we could have taken much easier measures to save the economy, both the greek and the european economy.
in writing. − in september 2010, the commission presented a legislative package aimed at strengthening economic governance in the eu and the euro area, calling for the development of a new structured procedure to prevent and correct adverse macroeconomic imbalances in all member states. in order to develop a coordinated strategy for employment, member states and the union should act in accordance with the guiding principles of promoting a skilled and trained workforce and labour markets responsive to economic change. the internal market should contribute to the sustainable development of the union, based on balanced economic growth and price stability, a highly competitive social market economy, aiming at full employment and social cohesion, and a high level of environmental protection and improvement. measures proposed to a given member state to correct imbalances should take into account the objectives of a union strategy for growth and jobs and the need to use such a strategy as a tool for ensuring sustainable internal cohesion.
in writing. − i supported this report as it establishes a system for detecting and correcting macroeconomic imbalances, while, at the same time, protecting social rights and having a symmetrical approach in monitoring both surplus and deficit countries. furthermore, the regulation ensures the monitoring of a wide range of potential sources of imbalances, including the monitoring of social indicators such as unemployment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that preventing and correcting macroeconomic imbalances is a powerful tool to address the delicate balance problem, generated in particular by medium and long-term structural trends, by the increasing discrepancies within the union, and by the spill-over effects of the policies of individual member states. the current strengthening of economic governance must be accompanied by strengthening the democratic legitimacy of decisions taken, which requires the direct involvement of not only relevant stakeholders but also national parliaments and the european parliament throughout the process. the experience of economic and monetary union in its first decade of operation has shown the clear need for an improved economic governance framework, which should be based on a stronger national ownership of commonly agreed rules and policies and a more robust system of european oversight of national economic policies.
in writing. − this report is essentially a continuation and extension of the faulty logic of the wortmann-kool report on the surveillance of budgetary positions and the surveillance and coordination of economic policies. that is why i have voted against this report.
in writing. − i voted against the report on the application of the excessive deficit procedure as the economic governance package only introduces austerity measures and does not give member states the possibility to invest in measures for growth and job creation. the purpose of the excessive deficit procedure is to prevent excessive government deficits and to encourage their correction. compliance with budgetary discipline shall be examined on the basis of the government deficit criterion and the government debt criterion. the council shall decide within two months whether an excessive deficit exists and shall make recommendations to the member state concerned. the council recommendation sets a deadline of six months for the state concerned to take concrete action and a deadline for the correction of the excessive deficit, which must be achieved in the year following its establishment. the council invites the member state to achieve annual budgetary targets allowing the deficit to be reduced by at least 0,5% of gdp as a reference value, in order to ensure that the excessive deficit is corrected within the deadline set by the council. i consider that these austerity measures limit the flexibility of member states in defining their own set of measures to ensure economic and social development and thus contribute, in the medium and long term, to the reduction of the excessive deficit.
in writing. − in several countries, the apparently strong budgetary positions of the pre-crisis period masked a strong dependence on exceptional revenue to finance expenditure; the decline in this revenue contributed to the sharp increase in budget deficits. to address these shortcomings, budgetary policy coordination and surveillance aimed at strengthening the stability and growth pact by providing it with more effective enforcement tools and by supplementing the pact with provisions on national budgetary frameworks is needed. the budgetary framework is intended to ensure that member states apply prudent budgetary policies so that stricter forms of coordination are not necessary to avoid jeopardising the sustainability of public finances and potential negative consequences for the whole of economic and monetary union. member states are therefore invited to present stability and convergence programmes setting out their plans to achieve their medium-term budgetary objectives, which are defined as a percentage of gdp in structural terms.
in writing. − i voted against the report on the proposal for a directive on the requirements for member states' budgetary frameworks as the whole economic governance package only introduces austerity measures and does not give member states the opportunity to invest in measures for growth and job creation. the public availability of fiscal data, official macroeconomic and budgetary forecasts and the methodologies, assumptions and parameters on which those forecasts are based is important for the proper functioning of the union budgetary surveillance framework. it is also necessary to adopt international accounting standards for the public sector and the professional independence of national statistical authorities and national courts of auditors. it is important that the methodologies, assumptions and parameters underlying the commission's macroeconomic and budgetary forecasts are published and that the level of the debt and deficit of the member states, as well as their evolution, are published by eurostat at least on a quarterly basis. however, i believe that the role of the commission is to coordinate the macroeconomic and budgetary policies of the member states in order to comply with the stability and growth pact. the commission can, through the levers it has, impose improvements in the work of the national statistical authorities, but it does not have to replace them.
in writing. − the eu's primary tasks in terms of economic and monetary stability are to curb national waste and to protect economic growth against macroeconomic shocks. these are the questions addressed by the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1466/97 on the strengthening of the surveillance of budgetary positions and the surveillance and coordination of economic policies. the compromise reached between the eu institutions and the member states after long and difficult negotiations, as reflected in this report, is welcome for the following reasons: first, the emphasis is not only on controlling the government budget deficit but also on controlling the public debt, with a strictly substantial limit of 3% of gdp deficit and 60% of gdp public debt. secondly, the introduction of a six-monthly european economic policy coordination framework with individual medium-term budgetary objectives for the member states and stronger supervisory functions for the commission. the report also sets out the main objectives of the reforms and the new approaches to be taken by the commission in the field of statistics.

producers will of course have consequences for the price of energy, which will have repercussions on the competitiveness of energy-intensive industries, as well as the steel industry. it is clear that the member states and the industry are affected differently, depending on the mode of electricity production and the type of furnace, as mr pirillo has also mentioned, whether fuel-based or electric. states. i would like to stress that the steel market is a global market and that the emission reduction targets risk introducing distortions of competition between producers. in the absence of a global agreement on emission reduction targets, eu industry is under pressure that is not being experienced by companies in countries that have not set such ambitious targets, and the risk of relocation is therefore real and must be treated as such. in order to offset this risk, the commission should clearly state in the future state aid guidelines that all industries on the list adopted by the decision of 24 december 2009 are eligible for indirect emission cost compensation. it is also necessary that those compensations are proportionate to the level of indirect costs generated by european union and a failure to reduce carbon emissions globally.

vice-president of the commission. − madam president, i would like to thank the honourable member for these questions because it gives me the opportunity to present the commission’s overall assessment of the implementation of protocol no 2 of the treaty of lisbon, also known as the subsidiarity control mechanism. the subsidiarity control mechanism is up and running, and its implementation has so far been very smooth, thanks not only to thorough preparation by both the commission and the national parliaments before the treaty entered into force, but also to the excellent cooperation and constructive contacts between the commission and the national parliaments. the experience gained so far has clearly shown that national parliaments are well prepared and ready to assume their new role and powers under the new treaty. by the end of september 2011, the commission had sent to national parliaments 139 draft legislative proposals falling within the scope of the subsidiarity control mechanism, and had received a total of 61 reasoned opinions stating that the respective legislative drafts did not observe the principle of subsidiarity. however, in no case have the thresholds provided for in protocol no 2, triggering the so-called yellow or orange cards, been reached. the commission is convinced that relations with national parliaments should not be confined merely to questions of subsidiarity, and it supports a deepening of the political dialogue with national parliaments, of which the subsidiarity control mechanism is only one aspect. in the context of the political dialogue, the commission currently receives and replies to more than 600 opinions per year from national parliaments, including their opinions on the content of commission proposals. one of the questions put to the commission was about how we are staffed. a unit in the secretariat-general is dedicated to relations with national parliaments and, in addition, every dg has designated coordinators for relations with national parliaments, who contribute to smooth implementation of the subsidiarity control mechanism and political dialogue, as do the offices of the relevant commissioners. turning to the overall assessment, the question of the subsidiarity control mechanism and political dialogue is an item regularly discussed at the cosac meetings, where the commission meets with members of the national parliaments who work in the european committees. i agree with the honourable member who pointed out that it is very important that national mps be more involved in discussions on european legislation. we can see that debate on these issues is much more frequent and more detailed, and that the quality of the opinions coming from the national parliaments is much higher. we are trying to take the same approach on the commission side because one of the matters raised at recent cosac meetings concerned comments from national parliaments suggesting that, on some issues, we should be more precise. the national parliaments would like to see more thorough explanation of the subsidiarity clauses in our legislative proposals, and therefore it is a mutual learning process. in the next phase we should ensure that sectoral proposals – for example, on the environment and transport – are discussed by the national parliaments not only in the european committees but in the relevant sectoral committees. i believe this would increase interest among national mps in european legislation, and they would also gain greater ownership and be much more careful when it comes to transposition, which, as we all know, depends heavily on national authorities. i think that the mechanism is working very well. the political dialogue is important because it gives us at the commission the chance to receive not only reasoned – i.e. negative – opinions, but also a great deal of encouragement and positive opinions from the national parliaments. i am sure that the dialogue will evolve and that the number and quality of both the national parliaments’ opinions and the commission responses will gradually improve in the coming months and years.
i welcome the re-examination of the application of this principle, particularly in the light of protocol 2 to the lisbon treaty. i welcome the development of a control mechanism for compliance with article 5 of the eu treaty. the delimitation of the allocation of competences at community and national level in the new text clarifies the functioning of the subsidiarity mechanism. in practice, its application must take account of the characteristics of each member state and its sub-units. i would point out the limited control exercised by the european court of justice on the application of this principle. the court may only annul an act which has been unlawfully adopted without verifying that subsidiarity has been observed. in this context, the exercise of control at legislative level is the way to complete the court's work.
the crisis has led many member states to increase vat rates, so that it has become an even more important revenue source for member states' budgets. every year, whenever i discuss with my students the information and actual circuits generated by the european vat regime, there is always a heated debate about the complexity, burden and evasion that this european vat regime favours. that is why i very much support the proposals in my colleague mr casa's report, which seek to reduce and eliminate, as far as possible by each member state, the vat exemptions, exemptions and reduced rates which only increase the complexity and administrative burden of this tax. i obviously support measures that reduce the bureaucratic red tape required to enforce this regime. i have serious reservations about proposals for a general exemption for the activities of non-governmental non-profit organisations, because in many cases, and i do not want to give examples now, these organisations are merely covering up tax evasion generated by some of their activities.
value added tax is an indispensable source of revenue for national budgets and in many member states is even the main source of revenue. while at the beginning of the economic crisis vat revenue represented around 8% of member states' gdp, its share has subsequently increased significantly due to the need for member states to increase the vat rate. given that the vat system represents around 60% of the administrative burden on businesses, i believe that simplifying and modernising the vat system is essential for the economy to function well, especially in times of crisis. i call for the issues of liability, deductibility and rates to be regulated as soon as possible, as these are the main concerns of economic operators. their complexity makes it difficult for economic agents to operate, increases costs and often reduces the attractiveness of european schemes for foreign investors, thus hampering regional development.
in the context of economic crisis and excessive government deficits, vat has proved to be an important source of revenue for national budgets. but raising it does not guarantee economic growth, especially when the consumption of staple foods is affected. in romania, vat on essential foodstuffs was maintained at 24%, which did not favour consumption but accentuated poverty. i therefore believe that alternative sources of income that are much more equitable must be found. on the other hand, it is not just consumers who have suffered from high vat, but also small and medium-sized enterprises, the economic engine of the european union. i therefore welcome the rapporteur's proposal to consider the adoption at european level of a vat exemption threshold for smes, with the aim of facilitating their access to the internal market and reducing administrative costs and burdens.
i would also like to congratulate my colleague, mr casa, on the excellent report he has produced. vat revenue is a major source of revenue for national budgets. in times of crisis, however, it is preferable to avoid raising vat and other taxes when there is an alternative. for example, in romania, the five-point increase in vat from 19% to 24% had a negative impact on the business environment, generating pressures. initially considered as a way of economic recovery, it delayed, according to the analyses, romania's exit from recession and would have been appropriate to operate in two stages. today, romania is one of the highest vat-paying member states and needs measures to stimulate investment and absorb european funds.
in writing. i join my colleagues in supporting the need to reform the vat system, which puts member states in a difficult situation as it is now regulated and defined. in my country, romania, the vat rate is among the highest in the union and no differentiation has yet been accepted for certain categories of goods or products. i therefore support the commission's request to submit to parliament and the council a mandatory list of goods and services which may be subject to a reduced rate or exemption under the vat directive. equally important, in my view, is the harmonisation of administrative practices and the reduction of red tape, i.e. the elimination of some of the annual returns, the reduction in the frequency of the periodic returns, the simplification of the evidence required for exemption from vat on exports and the future european standard invoice. i hope that we will consult seriously, in this whole process, with businesses and entrepreneurs and that we will get results. god help you!
financial investment to create new jobs plays a key role in economic recovery. the plan to boost the u.s. labor market, blocked yesterday by the u.s. senate, provides tax incentives for small businesses and employers. it offers a tax break for companies that hire new workers, while also lowering taxes on wages. at the same time, the american jobs act proposes an investment of over $100 billion in public works, using only materials made or available in the united states. the provisions in question could thus restrict european companies from participating in infrastructure projects in the usa. i should mention that, despite their commitment not to impose protectionist measures, the world's major economies continue to take measures to protect their own industries from international competition.

i wanted to stress that i voted against the two amendments tabled by the committee on economic and monetary affairs and industrial policy because it is unacceptable to change the rules in the middle of the game by promoting double standards with the member states. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' in the context of the directive. the debate yesterday once again confirmed that parliament remains committed to the great emblematic projects of european construction, such as the free movement of citizens and the schengen area, the euro area. i condemn the fact that political decisions in some member states give priority to populist approaches rather than to facts and realities. every country has the right to make its own decisions. but the european spirit demands that those countries which are currently opposed to romania and bulgaria joining the schengen area urgently identify a solution acceptable to us all.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because insurance guarantee schemes are a valuable tool in reducing the risks faced by policyholders in the event of the failure of an insurance company. i believe that there should be a coherent and consistent cross-border framework at community level for the national insurance guarantee schemes in the member states, the role of which is to provide consumers with protection of last resort in the event that insurance companies are unable to meet their contractual obligations. the exposure of taxpayers to the failure of financial institutions should be kept to a minimum by effective and balanced supervision by national and european supervisory authorities.
in writing. − insurance guarantee schemes are a fundamental tool in reducing the risks of policyholders in the event of bankruptcy. they are important and we voted for the idea that all types of insurance products that european consumers buy are covered by the sga and that the sga will guarantee 100% reimbursement within a fixed period of time, valid throughout the eu.
in writing. − a directive on the harmonisation of conditions for the protection of insurance consumers is intended to protect all europeans in the event of the bankruptcy of an insurer from the complications that may arise, depending on the country of origin of the insurer, from fraud or mis-selling or from the failure of guarantee schemes. the scheme of supplementary and uniform protection for those who use the insurance instrument must be designed in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity. insurance guarantee schemes are considered as a risk reduction tool for policyholders in the event of the bankruptcy of an insurance company. the european parliament has repeatedly demonstrated its support for a common approach at eu level. it is clear that the issue of gms is complex due to the wide variety of systems existing in eu member states as well as the interaction between gms and other issues currently under consideration at eu level, the most important of which is the imminent introduction of the solvency ii directive. this will radically change the european insurance industry. statistically, the risk-based economic requirements will reduce the risk of an insurer going bankrupt at a 200-year event.
in writing. − insurance guarantee schemes (igs) are a last resort for consumers in cases where insurance companies are unable to meet their contractual obligations. it is tragic that only 12 of the 30 eu-eea countries have at least one general insurance scheme. this means that in the event of the bankruptcy of an insurance company, one third of the entire insurance market in the eu-eea is not covered by any guarantee. given that it represents 26% of life insurance policies and 56% of general insurance policies, i believe that european citizens should benefit from igs to protect them against the risk of their claims not being honoured by insolvent insurance companies.
in writing. - i voted for the report on insurance guarantee schemes because european consumers need protection in the event of the bankruptcy of the insurer. in order to ensure a high level of consumer protection in the event of the insolvency of the insurer, it is necessary to establish a european framework allowing for a choice between financial compensation for the investment made in the insurance policy and the maintenance of insurance contracts by means of a portfolio transfer. i stress the importance of improving consumer knowledge and awareness of financial services and the risks associated with them. it is necessary to establish a mechanism for insurance policies that include clear warnings about the risks associated with them and the options available to consumers in such cases. we call on the commission to take action to establish a common, coherent and consistent insurance guarantee framework, which guarantees full and continuous protection of insurance policyholders throughout the eu. in the case of insurance, it is also necessary for the authorities responsible for consumer protection to give their opinion on the framework contracts offered by insurers so that consumers are protected and informed of their rights and obligations and can have bargaining power when taking out an insurance policy.
in writing. − value added tax is a main collection instrument, alongside tax, which has made a significant contribution to reducing budget deficits in the current crisis period. member states have had to raise vat ceilings, which has affected the business environment and slowed economic growth. the most vulnerable to the increase in the vat rate were certainly smes. the ec should therefore consider establishing a support mechanism for them, by reducing obligations and costs and by supporting access to the internal market. it is necessary that the future establishment of the vat regime takes account of the objectives of cohesion policy. i consider that the facilities for the payment of vat on non-repayable loans would be an important support for the beneficiaries and would, by implication, stimulate the absorption of european funds. member states should establish clear and simplified rules by consulting the beneficiaries of grants with a view to identifying measures to support them. i support this report in order to intensify cooperation between member states in the future, with a view to facilitating the exchange of information between tax authorities in the member states through online tax information and assistance portals.
in writing. - i voted for the report on the future of value added tax because the proposed measures contribute to making the internal market more efficient. the report calls on member states to coordinate and harmonise their administrative practices on vat and to implement measures to reduce the administrative burden of vat, to reduce the frequency of periodic vat returns, to simplify the evidence needed for export vat exemption. electronic invoicing facilitates the reduction of payment delays, reduces the risk of errors, fraud and administrative costs. directive 2010/45/eu on the common system of vat as regards rules on invoicing establishes new vat rules on electronic invoicing, ensuring equal treatment of paper invoices and electronic invoices. according to com ((2009) 15) on the reduction of administrative burdens, applying the same vat rules to both paper and electronic invoices will reduce the administrative burden on businesses by up to eur 18 million in the medium term. in the field of transport, harmonised rules or a reduced vat rate for crossborder transport within the eu have been called for, as has the accessibility of information on the different vat rates applicable in the passenger transport sector, in order to inform travellers of the exact cost of the crossborder journey.

in writing. − the european bank for reconstruction and development (ebrd) needs to respond effectively to the crisis and reorient its strategy, given the particularly significant impact of the crisis on the area in which the bank operates. i consider the capital increase proposed by the ebrd to be absolutely necessary to mitigate the impact of the crisis. this will enable the ebrd to maintain a high level of activity and contribute, together with other european or national organisations and institutions, to the economic recovery in its area of operation. the estimates show that the capital increase will generate an annual ebrd business volume of around eur 9 billion in 2011 and 2012 and around eur 8,5 billion per year until 2015. i therefore believe that the eu's role in the governance of the ebrd requires it to underwrite new actions to achieve the community's objectives.

member of the commission. - madam president, i would like to make a few comments and reply to certain points. first of all, i would like to recall what i said in my introduction, namely that the european commission is preparing a european legislative act on accessibility, which will be preceded by an impact study on the degree of accessibility that currently exists in the european union, in the different member states, as well as an analysis of the costs and benefits of accessibility measures of an economic nature. i think that, in parallel with the legal measures, the legislative measures, we must also be able to stimulate industry, services and the production of goods that can appeal to this category of people, to ensure that accessibility does not exist only on paper but that it is also a reality in practice. i believe that this cost-benefit analysis will also enable us, including through european instruments, to identify and stimulate opportunities to make available to disabled people the different instruments they need. i would also like to point out that many powers and responsibilities in matters such as employment, education and social protection are the responsibility of the member states, but that does not mean that everything should be left to the member states and that we should do nothing at european level. on the one hand, the commission supports the member states in their approaches and in their national accountability by providing them with data, indicators on the situation of disabled people and by organising exchanges of good practice, and on the other hand, we have the europe 2020 strategy which, through various flagship initiatives, deals directly and indirectly with this issue. i would first mention the flagship initiative on innovation, which provides for the respect of accessibility standards in the context of public procurement provided for in the member states. secondly, i would mention inclusive growth, i.e. access to work for people with disabilities, through initiatives which must come from the member states and which are supported by specific programmes. finally, i would mention the flagship initiative on social innovation for vulnerable people, which is specifically devoted to this issue. i would also like to point out that the anti-discrimination directive, which has been on the council's table since 2008, is still under discussion within this institution. i can assure you that the commission is actively supporting the negotiations taking place in the council with a view to adopting this directive. i would like to conclude by recalling that the european commission considers that parliament's committee on petitions will always play an important role in keeping these issues in the public and political spotlight, rather than only occasionally being brought to mind, and also in keeping in touch with reality in the preparation of the various legislative proposals.
in writing. statistics show that one in six people in the european union has a disability; in total, some 80 million people are prevented from participating fully in social and economic life because of physical and behavioural barriers. the poverty level of people with disabilities is also about 70% above the average recorded, which partly leads to their limited access to employment. i believe that all member states must review and improve their social policies for disabled people so that their social and economic situation becomes normal. i believe that the european commission, in collaboration with the member states, must act and develop strategies to remove the obstacles and the various problems faced by men, women and children with disabilities and to ensure their effective participation in society on an equal basis of dignity.
member of the commission. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank mrs rühle and the members of the imco committee very sincerely for this report, which is indeed an important contribution. you said, "i hope we have leverage". i, for my part, - and i have been following your debates since i became commissioner - have found that parliament has a real lever in many areas and this report is certainly an essential element for us, for me, as i have been working in recent weeks to modernise european public procurement. what you write and say together will be extremely helpful. public procurement accounts for 17% of the european gdp. so we are talking about economies, we are talking about jobs and we are talking about growth. i am very pleased to see the convergence between the report you are about to vote on and the work i am currently conducting for the coming legislative procedures. the revision of the public procurement directives is part of an overall programme for the thorough modernization of public procurement throughout europe. this programme, on which i am working with my colleagues, includes, apart from the revision of the directives, a directive on concessions - which has specific features, as we know - which justifies a separate text, while ensuring that it is consistent with the overall reform. this package also includes an external aspect of our policy, for which i will propose, in agreement with my colleague, mr karel de gucht, an instrument to ensure reciprocity in access to public procurement worldwide. these three initiatives will together form the legislative package which i will be proposing to the college in december, that is to say in a few weeks' time. where are we and what do we want to do in the extension and in the very spirit of the light you give with this report? we're working on the options that i'll briefly describe to you: firstly, simplification of the procedures. that's the number one goal. to this end, we are working on the generalization of the negotiated procedure with prior publication. it is a good way for public authorities to buy goods and services that are really tailored to their specific needs. this procedure could be accompanied by the safeguards necessary to ensure compliance with the principles of non-discrimination and equal treatment. we are also considering a drastic reduction in documentation. i think it is quite frankly excessive and i had the opportunity in my previous life to launch many calls for tenders as chairman of a local authority in my country that companies have to provide, sometimes and we see this in practice very regularly more than twenty documents, from various authorities and often paid, for a single call for tenders. this discourages many companies, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, from participating in tenders. that is why we could replace this documentation with solemn declarations by the contractors. only the successful tenderer would be required to provide certificates in due form. finally, we are working on strengthening and developing the digitalisation of public procurement. this is another essential vector of simplification. we could make the use of electronic means mandatory in some cases, so that electronic instead of paper is the standard or default method, such as email for personal written communications. all these measures will help to reduce the administrative burden for both contracting authorities and firms, and in particular for small and medium-sized enterprises. i come now to my second objective, which is also in line with your report, namely: how can we improve access to public procurement for small and mediumsized enterprises, which - i would remind you - make up 80 to 90% of the european economic fabric and which themselves have a very high potential for job creation, growth and innovation? to this end, we are in favour of a ban on disproportionate requirements on economic operators in terms of financial capacity. i therefore want to set a maximum level of turnover which may be required of a firm as proof of its ability to execute a contract. we are also considering a possible obligation to allocate, namely to divide public contracts into lots to facilitate access, through smaller lots, to small and mediumsized enterprises. ladies and gentlemen, after simplification, we will seek, in this package, to improve the current legal framework in order to facilitate the pursuit of societal objectives, which are also included in the europe 2020 strategy: the environment, social inclusion and innovation. we must of course be careful not to increase the administrative burden on contracting authorities. i have noted the strong opposition, particularly in the public consultation, to certain ideas, including the idea of imposing 'what to buy' obligations which could run counter to this simplification objective. in this package we are considering some concrete measures to facilitate the taking into account, through public procurement, of transversal objectives which correspond to the new requirements of our society. this is why we are working to strengthen life-cycle cost assessment, which encourages public authorities to assess the full life cycle of products in their purchases. we are considering clarifying the possibility for contracting authorities to take into account the production process. this should enable member states and contracting authorities to take account, in particular, of the working conditions of staff, compliance with the minimum wage, collective agreements and conventions of the international labour organisation. furthermore, with regard to innovation in particular - this is a subject on which chairman malcolm harbour regularly informs me and on which he is very vigilant, as are the other members of the committee - i would like to see more support for this objective of fostering innovation. we therefore envisage the introduction of a new partnership procedure specifically for the purchase of innovative products by contracting authorities. another aspect which is particularly close to my heart, as you know, is that of social services of general economic interest. in this area, i would like to see the rules further relaxed, giving member states even more freedom in the organisation of their tendering procedures for social services of general economic interest, naturally respecting the principles of transparency and non-discrimination. finally, we in writing. the main purpose of public procurement must remain the procurement of goods, works and services by public authorities, which is adapted to the needs of citizens and which ensures the efficient use of public funds. we need simplified procedures, flexibility and better information. we need legal certainty and less bureaucracy. a properly functioning public procurement market is a key factor for growth and a cornerstone of the single market. in addition, it is essential for stimulating competition and innovation and for addressing rapidly social and environmental challenges arising from public policies, as well as the issue of quality of work, including adequate remuneration, equality, cohesion and social inclusion. i believe that european public procurement rules should make a significant contribution to increasing transparency and guaranteeing equal treatment, to combating corruption and to professionalising public procurement procedures. it is also important that public procurement legislation returns to its essence, namely the guarantee of transparency, non-discrimination and competition.
in writing. the revision of the public procurement directive is one of the most important projects commissioner barnier has launched and will have a major impact on the whole economy and not just on contracting authorities. smes are the engine of economic growth in the eu and therefore their growth must be supported including through public procurement. in its current form, the procedures are far too complex to allow smes to participate in tenders. that is why i support the division into lots, so that the procedures are more accessible to smes. at the same time, i believe that the rules should provide flexibility for public authorities. using price as the sole criterion has in many cases led to suboptimal results. it seems to me more reasonable to take the whole life cycle of the product into account when estimating the cost, and where appropriate, the environmental impact. i believe that, as long as the link between the subject of the contract and the criteria imposed is maintained, public procurement can be used in a pragmatic way to achieve synergies with other european policies and to achieve other objectives, such as those relating to the environment or the encouragement of innovation.
in writing. public procurement in the european union is a strategic segment of the single market and at the same time a key element in achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. local and regional authorities are among the most important purchasers in europe and therefore play a key role in the application of the rules for the award of public contracts. i believe that these authorities should be given more attention and included in the process of reviewing eu public procurement rules, which should give them more autonomy. increased attention should also be paid to smes, as they are the backbone of the eu economy with huge potential for job creation, growth and innovation. a balance must also be struck between the desire to simplify procedures and the need to ensure fair competition in public procurement and to achieve optimal results. i believe that improving and simplifying procedures will contribute to faster allocation of funds, higher absorption rates, increased efficiency in the use of funds and reduced errors.
the economic and financial crisis has severely affected the activity of european smes, while discouraging the development of innovative enterprises. in romania, 55% of smes recorded lower financial results in 2010 compared to 2009, and the overall economic situation was perceived as unfavourable for business by 70% of smes. given the importance of the work carried out by smes in supporting the european economy and employment, and given that 67% of jobs in the european union are created by smes, we need to ensure that their development is encouraged, that access to finance is facilitated and that their work in the single market is not constrained by one-off bureaucratic measures. i believe that we have invested too much in saving the european banking system when productive and sustainable jobs are generated by small and medium-sized economic actors.
as the main source of job creation, smes are directly involved in the economic recovery and development of the european union. adopted in june 2008, the small business act aims to improve entrepreneurship in independent companies to strengthen competitiveness. i support the development of education in this field by applying the best practices in europe. in my country, the start program aims to develop the entrepreneurial skills of young people. the eu needs to encourage smes by facilitating access to finance, and i welcome the provision of european advertising funds. the new government programmes to stimulate the activity of romanian smes have created or saved over 300 thousand jobs. at the same time, romania is among the member states that have adopted measures to facilitate sme financing through public support for guarantee schemes.
as the adoption of the small business act in 2008 has been beneficial for the entrepreneurial environment in europe, making the process of setting up a company easier and simpler, but also cheaper, i want to bring european private companies, so-called spes, into the discussion at this point on the agenda. we all know that in practice, the seps would mean that smes could carry out a professional activity wherever they were in the european union, as well as in their own country. if they opt for the spe, entrepreneurs will save time and money on legal, management and administrative assistance. i believe that at this moment, in order to ensure the development of such companies with european support, governments must agree on a new legislative act allowing small businesses to register as european private companies. this possibility, together with the adoption of the european purchase agreement, would, i believe, represent a real leap for smes in the european union.
in writing. one third of smes in romania achieved lower results in 2010 than in the previous year, and two thirds of romanian smes consider the overall economic situation to be hostile. one of the main causes of the decline in this sector is the decline in domestic demand, against the background of the reduction in population consumption. the romanian government's austerity policy is equivalent to turning off the engine of a car on a hill to save gas. but we risk the brakes turning out to be faulty and catastrophe closer than the fanatics of excessive taxation and inhumane cuts in the population's sources of income can comprehend. inflation, government bill delays and high cost of credit are some of the other obstacles to sme development. this is the reality in many eu countries, despite the fact that smes have been placed at the heart of the lisbon strategy for growth and jobs since 2005. in this context, a joint programme to stimulate entrepreneurship is needed, as the private initiative can be a lifeline for investors who have gone bankrupt and for workers who have lost their jobs as a result of the economic crisis.
europe is home to 25% of the world's forests. europe is home to primary forests, natural treasures of unprecedented diversity that must be protected. unfortunately, many of europe's forests are suffering from excessive deforestation. in romania, in retezat national park, one of the last intact forests on the planet, massive deforestation has been carried out, with the approval of the authorities, right within the protected perimeter. in effect, deforestation is causing forest fragmentation, soil degradation, and the extinction of plant and animal species. the european union unfortunately has a lax system of monitoring its forests, which lacks mandatory, regular and comprehensive assessments of afforestation, deforestation and reforestation. this is why we need to improve and i also believe that we need to improve the protection and management of forest land in the european union in order to be able to leave these riches to future generations.

rapporteur. − madam president, the free movement of workers is a very sensitive problem indeed. ultimately it is going to shape the economic and social future of the european union. as rapporteur i have to stress that we face a situation that is politically untenable and economically irrational. the free movement of workers cannot be accidental. it is a right that all the member states have agreed upon. yet we are witnessing a situation in which member states are deciding to introduce or to re-introduce restrictions and are even suggesting that they could introduce more later on. this is pure politics: national and electoral politics. the economics tell a very different story. for years, official figures – some of them from the commission – proved that east european migrant workers did not generate unemployment and did not put under stress the welfare systems in their countries of destination. on the contrary, this european influx brought economic growth, which is generally accepted and evaluated at around 1% of gdp. the idea of more europe has been fashionable lately. should we mean by this more europe for fewer europeans? because we do have a single market for capital and goods, but we do not have a single market for labour. what does this mean? this means that western companies can operate in the east, sometimes successfully, sometimes generating thousands of unemployed, while east european workers cannot seek a job in the west. and this is not all. the same countries that restrict east european workers, romanians and bulgarians in this case, are happy to hunt for the best of the best in eastern europe: medical doctors, engineers, it specialists. this should be stopped. it is economically, politically and morally wrong. people will seek jobs as it is their right to do so. we have granted them this right. that is what my report supports. that is what the committee supported in its vote, and this is what i hope this house will support tomorrow.
in writing. we cannot have a common internal market without the free movement of labour. romania and bulgaria continue to face restrictions on the european labour market. these restrictions have a legal basis and all the new member states have had restrictions. at the end of 2011 we will see how many member states will express their desire to extend restrictions on their labour market for romanians and bulgarians. i believe that the reasons for these extensions in the various member states are unfounded and promote in a populist style, which is not economically justified, the protection of their own labour market. but member states can fill in because they have certain professional gaps in certain sectors. at the same time, there is a black market in eu labour which is maintained by certain member states. if national legislation were applied more strictly and more rigorously, the need for restrictions on the labour market would disappear. and last but not least, with regard to the various directives, such as the blue card or the seasonal workers directive, which regulate the european labour market for workers from third countries, i believe that a primary condition for those member states wishing to bring in workers from third countries is to first remove restrictions for workers from within the eu.
in writing. i would like to congratulate my colleague mr ungureanu on his excellent report. the free movement of workers is a fundamental right of the european union. this requires coordinated action between the institutions at national and european level to remove all existing barriers to the mobility of workers. given the vital role that smes play in the european economy and their contribution to boosting economic growth, employment and social cohesion, we need to have concrete actions for the development of smes so that they can absorb labour, especially from the younger generations. the increase in youth unemployment is alarming. according to eurostat, the number of unemployed people under 25 years of age in the european union is 5 139 000. the union must support these young people, including by multiplying projects such as the european employment mobility portal (eures) or the 'european jobs days'. labour mobility within the european union is a key element in achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy for reform and economic recovery. in this context, the removal of labour market restrictions for romanian and bulgarian nationals is essential. i consider these restrictions to be discriminatory and excessive.
full implementation of the services directive plays a key role in maintaining the eu's global competitiveness. at the same time, a truly integrated single market for services will help to stimulate economic growth. i would point out that services account for more than two thirds of gdp and jobs at european level. the eu needs to encourage member states to identify and address legislative gaps that could constitute unjustified obstacles to the proper functioning of the services market. in romania, for example, performance tests will be carried out in the tourism, business and construction sectors. the single electronic contact point also aims to facilitate access to information on entering the romanian services market.
as the rapporteur said, nine out of ten jobs in the european union are in the service sector. this is clearly the driving force of the european union's economy, generating around two thirds of the community's gross domestic product. we need a truly functioning single market for services that functions as a key tool for generating growth and jobs and improving the union's global competitiveness. unfortunately, much remains to be done to ensure the proper functioning of the single market in services and i believe that the role of national, regional and local administrations in the states must be strengthened. the dialogue with them must also be intensified and, at the same time, the dialogue with the regions and local public authorities must be intensified. the peer review process is a valuable tool for identifying remaining obstacles. this is a shared responsibility and the success of the proposed actions will depend on the involvement of all relevant institutions and parties in this process.
i would also like to congratulate mrs diana wallis on the preparation of this report in the context of the europe 2020 strategy. i believe that access for consumers and smes to alternative dispute resolution mechanisms is essential for strengthening the single market. these courts provide confidentiality and speed of dispute resolution at better financial conditions than the judicial system. i would point out that, although commercial arbitration tribunals are fully functional in the member states, they primarily settle disputes of national law. the reason for this is the lack of legislative harmonisation at european level. thus, it is difficult to resolve a dispute within multiple legal systems. i therefore support the development of a code of good practice on standard contracts. they would facilitate the use of alternative mechanisms, in particular for international disputes of low value.
i too would like to first of all congratulate my colleague mr hökmark on this report. this crisis has highlighted the need to strengthen global economic governance, particularly in the financial area. the lack of a common framework could lead to macroeconomic imbalances and missed opportunities to exit the recession. the existing system needs to be improved by introducing new levels of regulation and control bodies. unfortunately, the international monetary fund or the informal meetings of the g20 are bodies with limited powers. the eu needs to find an integrated solution to the euro area debt crisis. the piecemeal approach has not worked so far. my country has already adopted austerity measures to maintain financial stability. the current account deficit in romania is below 5% of gdp, with a deficit target of below 3% of gdp for 2012.
in writing. unfortunately, single mothers are often a neglected demographic category, although five per cent of women in the european union currently fall into this category. in the context of the current economic crisis, these women have been particularly affected. often, in order to provide the financial support needed to raise their children, they must forego rest or medical services. we cannot be indifferent to our citizens who are experiencing hardship. i would like to stress the need for additional unemployment benefits for each child, but also priority access to affordable housing. i also believe that at eu, national and local level, single mothers should be offered flexible employment opportunities to enable them to reconcile their working and family lives.
the rapporteur. − madam president, the fourth high level forum on aid effectiveness, to be held in busan at the end of november, provides an opportunity for the international community to reaffirm, by coordinating the economic and social policies of the member states, the european semester is an important step towards establishing sound european economic governance. tax policy must henceforth be a common area of action at european level. the reform programmes and the stability and convergence programmes must also include the requirements of stimulating economic growth and investment, guaranteeing a high level of education for all european citizens, ensuring social protection and creating jobs. in this regard, the annual recommendations addressed to both the member states and the union should be sufficiently ambitious to allow the achievement of the objectives set through the europe 2020 strategy. as a result of this first implementation exercise of the european semester, the commission will have to analyse the main problems facing the union and the member states and propose clear directions for reducing macroeconomic imbalances and stimulating balanced economic growth. i also believe, as do other colleagues, that the improvement of the european semester can only be achieved in full compliance with the powers granted to the european parliament, in accordance with the treaty on the functioning of the european union, by fully involving parliament in the process of formulating recommendations.
the question of how to prevent mismanagement of public finances, of macroeconomic balances, we already have two answers. the financial market that gave a very strong response, in that it removed the mirage of relatively equal interest rates at which the euro area member states were borrowing. each member state is now judged on its own financial situation and pays interest accordingly. the second answer is provided by the new regulations on economic governance in the european union and under these new regulations, the european semester is the main instrument for structured analysis of the economic situations of each member state. we therefore have a responsibility to make this semester as effective as possible and we strongly emphasise the council's responsibility to explain publicly, with reasons, why it rejects some of the recommendations made by the european commission.
madam president, the council stated that parliament concluded the 2009 discharge procedure when it granted discharge and closure of accounts to the commission. this is wrong. i cannot believe that the council wants to spend money without scrutiny. however, this is what i see. this is neither responsible nor an example of good governance, transparency or accountability and is even more appalling during this time of financial crisis and a crisis of trust, when every euro must be accounted for and transparency and accountability enhanced. in democratic regimes, parliaments have the right to scrutinise the executive and its expenditures. the european union should not depart from this practice, and this is why i fully support the position of the rapporteur in not granting the discharge to the council.

currently very high - cost of patents, for them and for all others, who are the first victims of the current situation. parliament has suggested, at your instigation, an alternative solution which would offer additional advantages for small and mediumsized enterprises. it would allow for additional reimbursement to these companies for translation costs related to the patent operation. i think this is a good proposal, which would be in line with the policy we want to implement on simplifying the patent system, reducing costs and special offers we want to make in all areas for small and mediumsized enterprises. as regards going further, as some national governments have done, with a national patent fund, which could become a european fund, we are working on this, as you know, with my colleague tajani. i personally think it is a good idea to go further, beyond reimbursement of the costs of registration and translation, with a european fund, but we need to look into this idea in the context of the next financial perspective.
