among the many valid findings in my colleague adam kos, i would like to highlight the ideas on equal opportunities. the report concludes that equality of opportunity does not mean that we provide equal opportunities for all, because equal opportunities are created when the same effort for all leads to the same result. for example, in the case of indigenous national minorities whose mother tongue is different from the official language of their member state , genuine equality of opportunity is achieved when they are able to study and to make a living in their mother tongue under the same conditions as members of the majority nation. disabled women, elderly people are more disadvantaged, but disabled people belonging to an indigenous national minority are also in the same situation. equal opportunities therefore also constitute positive discrimination against those who would suffer disadvantages under the same conditions.
i very much supported the report by mr ungureanu and voted in favour because, as i said in the hearing on this subject last week, the free movement of workers from the member states that joined in 2004 and 2007 did not produce imbalances in the labour market at the end of the first stage of the transition, as the european commission's 2008 communication states. therefore, the maintenance of restrictions by some member states has no economic basis but is based solely on political reasons. the current obstacles to mobility range from psychological and cultural barriers, sometimes generated by stereotypes, to bureaucracy. if the former are more difficult to manage, the latter can be re-analyzed and resolved. another barrier to mobility is the recognition of professional qualifications.
in writing. − there were serious irregularities in the implementation of the european police college budget for the financial year 2009. however, i voted in favour of granting it the discharge, primarily due to the new management and governance of the college, which displayed a commitment to tackle its deficiencies and to implement measures required by the european parliament, in particular the revision of the financial regulation of the college, the application of the procurement manual and the decision of its governing board to grant voting rights to the commission. the fulfilment of these commitments will be closely monitored during the 2010 discharge procedure. i call for cepol to be merged into europol in order to reduce expenditure and increase efficiency. this is why i called on the court of auditors to prepare a special report, during 2012, setting out the costs and benefits in financial and operational terms of merging the college’s responsibilities with those of europol. as rapporteur for the 2010 discharge of the eu agencies, i strongly believe that the rationalisation of eu agencies is both necessary and relevant.
in writing. − the discharge for 2009 was granted today to the european medicines agency. however, i would like to point out that the agency failed to provide the parliament with the action plan on public procurement, its timetable for implementation and the updated documents on the management and prevention of conflicts of interests, as requested in may 2011 when the discharge was postponed. these areas will be closely monitored. these were part of the amendments which i tabled and were adopted during the vote in the committee on budgetary control and integrated in the final report voted on today by the plenary. as parliament’s rapporteur for the 2010 discharge of the eu agencies’ budgets i will closely monitor the european medicines agency and look in particular at conflicts of interests and cost-efficiency criteria in each and every eu agency. these issues will bear considerable weight in the decision on discharge.
in writing. − alternative dispute resolution is an out-of-court settlement mechanism whereby consumers and traders are helped to settle their disagreements through a mediator or arbitrator. i welcome the commission's intention to encourage the use of alternative dispute resolution methods which are accessible, not costly, fast, efficient and offer the possibility of establishing and maintaining good commercial, economic, social and neighbourly relations, based on mutual trust, and which can contribute to raising the level of consumer protection in mutually advantageous situations, which offer more benefits to all parties than the current case law. i consider it essential to urgently address the existing shortcomings in the geographical coverage of alternative dispute resolution in europe and i encourage the existence of an effective system of out-of-court dispute resolution for consumer contracts that is functional throughout the european union.
in writing. − the availability of alternative dispute resolution mechanisms is one of the key elements to increase the confidence of european consumers and businesses in the single market. at present, many consumers and businesses are reluctant to transact cross-border for fear of not being able to resolve disputes properly. but this reluctance to engage in crossborder transactions deprives consumers and businesses of the benefits of a competitive internal market. we need dispute resolution mechanisms that are fast, efficient, independent and, above all, as low-cost as possible. this would have a real advantage over judicial procedures which are long and costly. furthermore, the promotion of adr will also lead to a smoother functioning of the judicial system, as some cases will be resolved through mediation or arbitration. the essential condition is, of course, that these alternative mechanisms are properly promoted by informing consumers and businesses so that they are used more widely. i therefore believe that it is desirable to have a legislative proposal from the commission as soon as possible, which follows the guidelines of this report, so that all eu citizens have access to alternative dispute resolution mechanisms.
in writing. − as in some member states, such as romania, courts are overwhelmed by the volume of files on file, i support the european commission's intention to encourage the use of alternative dispute resolution. the romanian courts have over 138 500 cases older than one year, according to the monitoring report of the judicial inspectorate attached to the plenum of the superior council of magistracy. of these, 4001 files are between 5 and 10 years old and 586 are over 10 years old. so i think we need a set of rules to govern the resolution of disagreements through mediation or arbitration. however, their appointment must avoid potential conflicts of interest and must be based on professional competence and impartiality. it is also necessary to increase the information of citizens on the functioning and advantages of the use of alternative dispute resolution. last but not least, this mechanism of out-of-court amicable settlement must remain optional, in order not to prejudice access to justice.
in writing. − directive 2000/25/25/ec reduces the permissible levels of exhaust (gaseous and particle) emissions from engines in agricultural and forestry tractors. an amendment in 2005 introducing ambitious reduction targets in pm and nox values provided for a possibility for the commission to conduct a technical review in order to examine the available technology, with a view to confirming stage iii b and iv limit values, and evaluate the possible need for additional flexibilities, exemptions or later introduction dates for certain types of equipment or engines. the commission conducted this review and came to the conclusion that for engine categories t2, c2, and t4.1 it was appropriate to postpone for 3 years the introduction of category iiib and iv for narrow-track tractors with a maximum width of 1.15 m, as relevant data confirmed that more time is required to enable manufacturers to develop stage iiib-compliant systems. i strongly support the proposal, which asks the commission to present the ep, on a yearly basis, with a progress report on the development of technical solutions for stage iv.
in writing. − the non-road mobile machinery (nrmm) directive (97/68/ec) aims to control carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides, hydrocarbons and particulates emissions (co2 emissions are not covered by this legislation) from a variety of engines such as excavators, bulldozers, front loaders, back loaders and compressors. the directive was amended in 2004 to introduce new emission limits and, with that, the flexibility scheme. the flexibility scheme allows manufacturers to place on the market a limited number of engines belonging to the older category (with higher maximum permitted exhaust emissions). i support the following compromises: the flexibility scheme to be increased to 37.5% of the annual quantity of equipment placed on the market for the duration of the stage iiib or up to three years when no subsequent stage exists; 16 engines for locomotives to be compliant with the previous stage standards and additionally 10 engines for locomotives that can be used in the uk due to specific rail conditions. environmental legislation should always be consistent with our medium-term and long-term environmental goals, but in the short run we are making efforts to support the recovery of smes from the economic crisis.
in writing. − i supported this report as it is an important part of eu legislation on the environment and public health. the report provides for the protection of human health, in particular of workers and persons who are often exposed to emissions from engines installed in non-road mobile machinery.
in writing. − people with disabilities must have the right to community-based services that promote independent living, the right to personal assistance, the right to economic and social independence and full participation in society and the labour market. as full citizens, persons with disabilities have equal rights, including the right to unquestioned dignity, equal treatment, independent living and full participation in society. i would like to draw attention to the fact that many persons with disabilities continue to be discriminated against in terms of equal recognition before the law and the judiciary, and i encourage member states to address these shortcomings, including effective access to justice for persons with disabilities and adequate training of judicial administrative staff. i also stress the importance of guaranteeing and ensuring equal conditions for participation in political and public life.
in writing. − i voted for this report because i believe it is essential that the obstacles preventing people with disabilities from exercising their fundamental rights are removed. europe needs to provide people with disabilities with the ability to enjoy full rights and to participate in european social and economic life. in this context, the eu should encourage member states to harmonise policies and strategies relating to persons with disabilities. i would like to mention that these people are one of the groups most affected by the financial crisis in europe. in my country, building an effective model of integration for people with disabilities is the main objective of the national organization of people with disabilities. currently, three projects funded by european funds are mainly aimed at integrating people with disabilities into the romanian labour market.
in writing. − one of the main objectives of the europe 2020 strategy is to increase the number of jobs for the nearly 80 million people with disabilities in the eu. the employment rate of disabled people and people with reduced working capacity is generally low across the eu, with only 30-40% of these people in employment. the situation is more dramatic in the newly admitted states. for example, the latest statistics show that in romania only 4% of the 631,000 people with disabilities are in employment. it is clear that for these people, a job means a chance at a normal life. romania's new labor law requires large firms with more than 50 employees to employ 4% of people with disabilities. in particular, for every 50 employees, 2 must be from the disabled population, for every 100 employees, 4 must be disabled, and so on. there is currently a functioning government programme in romania whereby any company that employs people with disabilities for at least 2 years receives 500 lei (approximately eur 120) per month for them.
in writing. − one in four europeans with disabilities is at risk of poverty, as many eu governments have resorted to shocking cuts in social assistance. people with disabilities also face severe discrimination, from low numbers attending high school or college to difficulties in obtaining employment and access to health services. one of the foreseeable consequences of not integrating the disabled into the labour force will be the failure of the europe 2020 strategy target of reaching an employment rate of 75% of the total working population aged 20-64. last but not least, i would like to stress that more than a third of europeans over 75 have a disability, and the proportion of the elderly is increasing. investments in adapting education systems and in preventing disability and its secondary consequences can lower social budgets and would ensure improved prospects for the integration of our fellow citizens with disabilities. on these grounds, i support the resolution.
in writing. − i believe that all member states must review and improve their social policies for people with disabilities so that their social and economic situation becomes normal. i believe that the european commission, in collaboration with the member states, must act and develop strategies to remove the obstacles and the various problems faced by men, women and children with disabilities and to ensure their effective participation in society on an equal basis of dignity.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the european parliament has a duty to focus on the situation of people with disabilities and that they must be included in all strategies for the future of the eu, with a view to respecting both the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and equal opportunities for all citizens. i believe that the situation of people with disabilities must be addressed in the long term, from the perspective of social investment, and i believe that the strengthening of their active participation in public life must be emphasised. as a member of the committee on industry, research and energy, i believe it is important to support research and development of technologies for people with disabilities to bridge social gaps and to give greater importance to the creation of accessible websites and effective communication channels for all european citizens with disabilities. last but not least, i support the rapporteur's position that education and training systems are not adequately prepared to take into account the needs of young people with disabilities and i believe that the europe 2020 strategy needs to take these issues into account and address them appropriately.
in writing. − people with disabilities are a vulnerable group, with a poverty rate 70% above average. this increased exposure to the risk of poverty is the result of often limited access to jobs, vocational training and healthcare. this is why it is important that more disabled people and workers with disabling illnesses are in employment. in this context, member states should be encouraged to introduce special employment quotas or measures to adapt jobs to the needs of disabled people. the european parliament and the european commission could start to employ people with disabilities, setting an example for other member states.
in writing. − as job accessibility, employer mentality and specific or related legislation in some eu countries disadvantage the employment of people with disabilities and little attention is paid to programmes to prevent the onset of disability in newborns or to prevent its lifelong acquisition by identifying the causes and eliminating or reducing them, i consider it essential to transfer good practice between eu member states and to intensify collaboration through working groups at european level. recall the importance of a relevant assessment of the situation of persons with disabilities and the establishment of national priorities on the avoidance of family transfers of persons with disabilities to residential centres on the grounds of poverty. i would stress the importance of access in all member states to the 112 emergency service or other services designed to save the life of the disabled person or his or her family members, including for the hearing-impaired/deaf-mutes. i draw attention to the importance of linking labour market demand with the development of new schools focused on vocational training and establishing the 16-18 years as the area of training and preparation for access to the labour market and increasing the chance of success in job retention and sustainability.
in writing. − the employment level for people with disabilities and whose work capacity has changed is generally low throughout the eu, with 30-40% of them working; the situation is even worse in the poorer member states, whilst the employment level needs to rise by approximately 1% per year if the 75% level set out in eu2020 is to be met. meanwhile, 12 million jobs suitable for low-qualified workers will disappear by 2020. in this respect, employers should allow people with disabilities to take up a position, if qualified, advance in it and to support them by training. the european commission and the member states should support the flexibility in the labour market combined with an adequate social security system by creating flexible and secure contractual arrangements and work organisations, effective active labour market policies and reliable and responsive lifelong learning systems. member states should review their provision of health services for people with disabilities, such as measures relating to physical accessibility to services, training and medical staff, information provided in accessible formats, customised counselling services, including translation into various languages, and health services customised to the needs of people with disabilities.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is imperative to increase equality of opportunity for people with disabilities. this means giving them the right to health and education, social protection, adequate means of communication, while ensuring their integration into society and facilitating their access to suitable jobs.
in writing. − i voted for the modernisation of eu public procurement policy. public procurement accounts for around 17% of eu gdp and can play an important role in ensuring sustainable employment, fostering innovation and sustainable working conditions, especially for businesses, and promoting social inclusion. the legislative framework on public procurement must also reflect the specific nature of social services, the economic and innovative potential of smes and, not least, ensure compliance with the applicable principles - competition, transparency, non-discrimination, efficiency.
in writing. − as europe seeks solutions to overcome the crisis and boost growth, i think it is good to propose a revision of public procurement criteria to take into account the life-cycle costs of the relevant goods, services or works, and not just the lowest price. it has been found that sometimes this criterion has led to additional downstream costs simply because the necessary post-contract services during the use of goods or services purchased at the lowest price have not been taken into account. this principle should be taken into account in particular in areas such as food or health, with a view to access based on value for money and not just the cheapest offer available to consumers, such as hospitals, care centres for the elderly, schools or kindergartens, with a view to equal access to healthy food.
in writing. − european public procurement legislation has mainly aimed at implementing transparent procurement arrangements by tackling irregularities, reducing red tape and simplifying enforcement procedures. current practice in this area indicates the need for better alignment of national criteria with european legislation. the new provisions can create a legislative framework favourable to increasing access to public procurement for smes by avoiding the introduction of additional bureaucratic procedures. i stress the importance of establishing additional criteria for the award of public contracts. the introduction of the 'most economically advantageous' criterion will take into account objectives that bring economic and social benefits and have a low environmental impact. only 50% of eu public procurement is conducted electronically, but even here there are many imperfections in the implementation of an effective e-procurement system. i consider that a common framework is necessary to establish the procedures for contesting the results of tenders. in some member states, litigation is the main obstacle to investment. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the future of public procurement can be an important source of job creation and skills development in research and innovation.
in writing. − the report on the modernisation of public procurement (pp) is based on the green paper preceding the imminent legislative proposals from the commission on pp (due to come in dec 2011), its content being relevant to the future legislative report. i voted for this report because pp could be a real driver in promoting quality jobs, wages and conditions, and equality, developing skills and training, promoting environmental policies, and providing incentives for research and innovation. i fully support the request to the commission to encourage governments and contracting authorities to increase the use of sustainable public procurement supporting and promoting good quality employment, and providing quality services and goods in europe. i consider there are good provisions relating to smes, to the fight against corruption and to e-public procurement.
in writing. − although the right to live and work in any country of the european union is a basic component of european citizenship, recognised by the treaties, statistics show that too few people are still exercising this right. in times of economic crisis, occupational and geographical mobility of workers can contribute to reducing unemployment by matching labour supply with demand, to job creation opportunities, to adapting the economy, society and demography to structural change, and to promoting economic growth and eu competitiveness. these obstacles and restrictions violate a fundamental worker's right, make it more difficult for eu economies to recover and can lead to counterproductive effects such as unlawful work and exploitation of workers. i believe that freedom of movement for workers should be encouraged, as it represents a positive socioeconomic example both for the european union and for the member states, constituting a landmark in integration that contributes to economic development, social cohesion, individual professional development, combating prejudice, racism and xenophobia and also helping to counterbalance the negative effects of the economic crisis.
in writing. − the call by the european legislator for member states to allow romanians and bulgarians access to the labour market by the end of 2011 is in fact a call for normality, especially as analyses clearly show that the integration of the two states in 2007 did not have a negative impact on the labour market in any of the member states. official figures, including those from the european commission, show that workers in eastern europe have not generated unemployment and put pressure on social protection systems. on the contrary, the influx brought economic growth in the destination countries, estimated at 1% of gdp. it is becoming imperative that all member states review their rules on transition periods before opening up access to the labour market. we hope that the countries that still impose restrictions on romanians and bulgarians will lift them by the end of 2011, i.e. before the 2013 deadline set in the eu accession treaty. in the long term, these restrictions may have a negative impact on the fundamental values and rights enshrined in the eu treaties, such as freedom of movement, non-discrimination, solidarity and equality of rights. europe has no first-class or second-class citizens. congratulations to your hungarian colleague on the report.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on promoting the mobility of workers within the european union in the hope of removing the discriminatory barriers imposed on romanians and bulgarians after eu accession. beyond the unfairness of these restrictions, it has been shown that the exercise of the right of free movement does not have adverse effects on the labour market. it is also of concern that gender differences in labour mobility within the eu are disadvantageous for women, which is why better monitoring is needed in this regard. many women who move abroad for work work work for private entities, often illegally, as baby-sitters, and therefore lack social security, healthcare and protection from abuse by employers. more attention and involvement is needed in this regard. last but not least, the removal of counterproductive restrictions within the european union can help kick-start economic recovery and achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. − in the context of an ageing european population, i believe that the mobility of workers in the eu labour market is a beneficial process, but it is necessary to remove all existing restrictions for workers from the new member states. in order for the union to achieve its growth targets and the europe 2020 targets for job creation, i believe it is useful to carry out periodic assessments of the professions in short supply and the sectors facing recruitment difficulties. these evaluations should be linked to european educational programmes and measures to use the experience of older people at the end of their careers to make the best possible transfer of skills to young people. last but not least, a link with vocational retraining programmes for the unemployed is needed to reduce the number of unemployed and to cover the labour needs for the shortage occupations.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the free movement of workers is an essential step towards the completion of the single market and the consolidation of a strong european identity. despite some member states maintaining restrictions on labour market opening to new member states, labour migration has had a positive effect on the eu as a whole. in its amendments to this report, we underlined that labour mobility within the european union is fundamental to economic recovery and the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives and called on member states that maintain labour market restrictions for romanian and bulgarian nationals to lift these restrictions by the end of 2011. furthermore, i believe that there is no sound socioeconomic argument to support the maintenance of these labour market restrictions.
in writing. − studies are well known that highlight the positive effect of labour mobility from the new member states on overall gdp, the moderate effects on gdp per capita, the minor impact of post-enlargement labour mobility on local workers' wages. i supported the resolution drafted by my colleague traian ungureanu, because the reasons for the restrictions introduced by some european states cannot be economic, as long as romanians are required for highly qualified professions - and here i mean engineers, doctors, teachers, it specialists. recent statistics reveal new trends in the mobility of highly qualified people, a phenomenon that is also increasing in the context of the economic crisis. in view of these aspects, i hope that by the end of this year the european commission will encourage member states to remove the barriers imposed on the labour market for romanian and bulgarian workers.
in writing. − labour migration within the eu has long been perceived as a potential problem, causing imbalances at national level in terms of shortages of labour supply and affecting collective bargaining and wages within host countries. it has, though, had a beneficial effect on the eu as a whole. according to the november 2008 commission communication, mobility flows have had a major positive impact on economic growth in the european union. however, if we focus on details, we notice problems related to changing cultures, adjusting to new languages and alienation from the family, to which there are also other barriers related to enjoying the full exercise of free movement. the member states should improve the situation of the children left behind by their parents and help them develop normally, benefiting from education and an appropriate social life. the member states should create mechanisms of cooperation aimed at preventing such devastating effects on families, especially on children, caused by separation from their parents and the distance between them. the member states and the european commission should determine the social partners and the ngos which will be more involved in such actions aimed at improving the situation of migrants’ children.
in writing. − i voted in favour, given the need to stimulate the peer review process provided for in the services directive. the experiences and results of peer evaluation are useful and valuable and the report therefore proposes to extend its use to other areas of action. the services directive was adopted in 2006 and remains a key instrument for creating a fully operational single market for services. member states have made substantial efforts to implement it. however, efforts should be stepped up to ensure full and correct implementation of the services directive and to establish fully operational single points of contact.
in writing. − i voted for this report because effective global economic governance would minimise the negative impacts and correct the harmful effects of globalisation, such as the deepening of inequalities or the destruction of the environment. global economic governance is needed as the us and the eu continue to face the worst effects of the worst international economic downturn since the great depression. at the same time, social and economic inequalities between and within countries need to be reduced. last but not least, the fight against poverty in europe must be one of the top priorities of the eu 2020 strategy.
in writing. − this financial and economic crisis has demonstrated that capital flows must be accompanied by a responsible monetary policy, adequate regulation and sound financial supervision. i believe that we need strong structural reforms from governments to ensure the sustainability of public finances and to boost economic growth. this means fully respecting the agreed fiscal targets and accelerating structural reforms. global imbalances pose a serious threat to financial and macroeconomic stability of states and can have long-term repercussions. so, leaders of states around the world must continue to find viable solutions to reform global economic governance. in this way, they will help to restore the global economy and avoid a similar situation in the future.
in writing. − in europe, a very high percentage of single parent cases are single mothers over the age of 25. member states must guarantee equal treatment and maintain a high quality of life for all children, regardless of the marital status of the parents or the family structure, by providing general allowances. as regards the encouragement of activities to help single mothers, i believe that these efforts should be directed towards strengthening the self-confidence and independence of single mothers, towards reducing their passive and isolating behaviours, towards improving social skills and parenting skills, by giving them better access to information on rights and employment opportunities.
in writing. − in the eu, on average, 85% of single parents are mothers aged 25-64, and in some member states single mothers represent as much as 9% of the total female population. statistics show that single-parent households are much more vulnerable to poverty risk and perpetuation than are two-parent households: according to the most recent data available in 2006, 32% of single-parent households in the eu-25 were at risk of poverty, compared with 12% of couples with children. in addition, the gender pay gap, which is on average 18% in the eu, increases when women become mothers and continues until retirement. i voted for the resolution in view of this hostile context for single mothers and the need to support them, particularly in countries where support for single-parent families is non-existent or worryingly diminished in the context of the crisis, such as romania.
in writing. − according to the latest statistics, the number of single mothers is increasing alarmingly across the union. in this context, member states should pay attention to this, as the main risk is the poverty into which these women may fall. it's not the same to be a single mother in the northern countries, where you're protected and helped, and to be a single mother in other countries, where you're subject to social exclusion. i strongly believe that the european union and the member states must design strategies that pay greater attention to gender issues and identify common policies based on and sharing good practices in europe, so that there is no longer discrimination against a single mother from one country to another at the level of the union.
in writing. − in a society where the concept of the family is changing, we need to pay due attention to the difficulties faced by single parents: both women and men. the pay gap, however, makes the situation of single mothers more difficult. in european societies, the ways in which this problem is tackled vary from the help received from the extended family to well-established national social protection systems. however, the danger of poverty persists, risking to perpetuate itself to the next generation and reducing the chances of success in life of children. furthermore, social stigma increases the risk of child abandonment. possible solutions call for health care for single mothers with incomes below the national average, affordable housing, and child care networks in day care centers and nurseries so that mothers can continue their careers. also, appropriate unemployment benefits for single mothers can contribute to a decent life for these single-parent families. equally useful to me is the concept of social entrepreneurship - a business that tackles a social problem, in diverse fields and with varied target groups. this is a personal and professional value addition to the vulnerable individuals employed and is also a profit generator for the company.
in writing. − single mothers are an often overlooked demographic category, with 5% of women in europe currently being single mothers. in the context of the negative effects of the economic and financial crisis, in addition to the high unemployment rate among single mothers, poverty has serious consequences for the children being raised and cared for by single mothers. member states should adopt public policies, including education, care, health, employment, social security systems, housing policies to support the needs of single-parent families. access (through esf and member state funding) to initial training, vocational training and scholarships for single mothers (unmarried, widowed or separated) must be facilitated, young pregnant women must be encouraged not to drop out of their studies, as education will enable them to gain qualifications and maximise their chances of decent working conditions, well-paid jobs and financial independence. member states must ensure that all allowances (maintenance) are paid regularly by the parent who does not have custody of the child and take into account the gender factor and in particular the situation of single mothers in the reform of their pension systems.
in writing. − organized crime has significant social costs, by draining and embezzling resources, distorting the free common market, corrupting legitimate businesses and economic activities, fostering corruption, polluting and destroying the environment, and violating human rights and democratic rules. the effects of this phenomenon have a profound impact on the duties of the european union towards its citizens and it is therefore necessary for the institutions to make a concrete political effort to combat organised crime that produces tangible and significant effects. organised crime, especially mafia-type crime, is taking advantage of globalisation, the disappearance of borders within the eu and the differences in legislation between member states to make increasingly important profits while ensuring impunity. this is possible because organised crime has created a network of consensus and support, with deep and solid infiltrations into the world of politics, public administration and the legal economy. in romania, a bill was recently passed that makes usury a crime punishable by imprisonment from six months to five years. also, money and property derived from this activity is confiscated. the clergy, especially in times of economic crisis, thrive and destroy lives.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report which aims to combat organised crime at eu level. organized crime entails not only the trampling on the fundamental rights of the many and the honest, but also significant social costs, by draining and misappropriating resources (financial, labour, etc.), by altering the common free market, by corrupting legitimate businesses and economic activities, by encouraging corruption, by polluting and destroying the environment, and by violating human rights and democratic rules. the report will improve the eu's legislative framework with specific measures to tackle the internationalisation of mafia-like criminal organisations. improving the functioning of european structures responsible for combating organised crime and relations with other international institutions such as unodc and interpol is of fundamental importance in this regard.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider organised crime to be one of the main threats to both the internal security of the european union and the freedom and security of citizens. such crime disrupts free trade and the common market, slows down the economy and business, promotes corruption and violates fundamental human rights, all of which pose a serious threat to democracy. i support the transnational and cross-border approach proposed by the rapporteur to combat this phenomenon and believe that the presence of the mafia in many eu member states requires an effective common response. i believe that the proposals to improve the eu's legislative framework are welcome and that the measures proposed to combat the internationalisation of criminal organisations can have positive results. last but not least, i believe that the european structures involved in the fight against organised crime are of key importance and must be strengthened, and their relations with other international bodies such as interpol must be enhanced.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on organised crime in the eu, which outlines the need for an eu strategy to fight organised crime, to include legislative and operational measures, allocation of funds, and a rigorous implementation timetable. the report also underlines the importance of promoting a culture of legality. i tabled amendments in the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs for (i) the consolidation of the legal and institutional framework regarding confiscation of assets (including civil confiscation), which result from organised crime, (ii) legislation on the re-use of crime proceeds for social purposes, (iii) proper protection of people agreeing to cooperate with the judiciary and of whistle blowers, (iv) transparency in the use of european funds, and (v) setting up the european prosecutor’s office with a robust mandate to investigate serious cross-border crimes, including organised crime and corruption.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on aid effectiveness for development, given that transparency and accountability are fundamental conditions for aid effectiveness, not only between donor and recipient governments, but also between the state and society. donors and partner countries agreed in the accra agenda for action to disseminate timely and detailed information on aid flows so that developing countries can budget and audit their accounts with greater precision. it is also of the utmost importance that donor countries - and the eu in particular, as the leading global actor in development aid - support the strengthening of the institution of national parliaments and the involvement of local authorities and civil society organisations in linking development policy with the process of democratisation, as many developing countries face major shortcomings not only in economic and social terms but also in the development and functioning of democratic institutions.
nokia's relocation in romania leaves thousands of people unemployed and severely affects the national economy at a difficult time. unfortunately, at the end of nokia's three years in our country, the company's motto could become 'disconnecting people', as a finnish newspaper proposed. it was clearly a specific investment for the third world, as is being attempted today in the case of rosia montana for the start of cyanide-based gold mining. the unscrupulous pursuit of profit only accentuates the precariousness of the many, national egos, and skepticism. nokia has taken full advantage of the facilities generously offered by the romanian authorities, benefiting from tax rewards without fulfilling its obligations. now he's decided to close the gates with a cynicism beyond compare. while the bochum unionists in germany received compensation of 60 minimum wages, romanian employees are offered only three compensatory wages, and their chances of reintegration are practically non-existent in the current economic context. i therefore call for the european commission to be involved urgently in order to ensure that staff made redundant receive decent treatment in order to support their professional conversion. the sharp drop in steel market transactions and prices is also likely to trigger further restructuring in the steel industry. there is a risk that 10 years after privatisation, the nearly 9000 romanian employees of the arcelor mittal combined company in galati will be affected. a common strategy is needed at all levels of decision-making to maintain productive capacities and ensure that workers' interests are effectively protected. in view of the prospect of increased unemployment, i believe that the european commission's priority must be to preserve jobs, not controls on electricity tariffs, which help to preserve production units. we need a proper order of priorities, and jobs must take precedence over other considerations in energy market agreements.
madam president, the so-called nokia incident is no accident. it tells us two very instructive things. first, helped by nokia, we have found out how we europeans lost our competitive edge. for too long, producers chose to relocate in order to reduce production costs. that was fine from a cost-reduction perspective, but it was not a guarantee of increased quality in a very competitive market. cheap is not enough. that is what companies like nokia found in romania. nokia closed up shop in romania because it was severely hit by its own lack of mobility in terms of innovation. so costs are important, but knowledge and innovation are vital. from this point of view nokia only has itself to blame. what about the 2 000 or so romanians made instantly unemployed by nokia? should they blame the smart phones that defeated nokia? that would not be very smart. the problem for romanian workers is that a unified european market allows nokia to operate successfully or unsuccessfully in romania, while romanians face a restricted labour market. in other words, romanians won the right to be made unemployed by nokia, only to then be denied a job anywhere else in europe. that is the second lesson that we can learn from the nokia fiasco in romania. of course, assistance from the globalisation adjustment fund could alleviate the problem, but only an unrestricted european labour market will solve it.
the transfer of nokia from romania certainly had negative effects at local and regional level. as was emphasised throughout the debate, access to the egf can help to reduce the social impact on people who have lost their jobs as a result of this decision. the romanian authorities are currently in talks with companies that could take over the industrial park at jucu. at the local level, a significant number of unemployed people must be managed and alternative sources of revenue for the budget found. it also requires the use of its own natural resources. romania has important gold, silver and copper deposits, the exploitation of which can produce new jobs, especially at roşia montană, certez and băiţa - crăciuneşti. but short-term solutions are not enough, measures are needed to make romania much more attractive to investors.
three years ago, nokia announced that it was abandoning mobile phone production at its bochum plant and moving to more cost-competitive areas. 2,300 employees were affected at the time. the relocation of production to romania cost nokia over 82 million euros, but a month ago, the finnish manufacturer's management announced the closure of the factory in cluj and the layoff of 2200 workers. it is worrying that this time nokia is leaving one of the most advantageous convergence regions of the eu for cheap and accessible labour and possibly leaving the eu, perhaps choosing more attractive asian markets for production and consumption. i would like to ask the commission what urgent measures can be taken in the fields of employment, research and innovation to save the relocations from the eu to third countries whose effects we are already feeling?
madam president! i want to make it clear in advance that i have two nokia phones and i will continue to buy nokia phones in the future, but we have to decide whether we are protecting the interests of banks, big corporations or citizens, profit or employment. then nokia will go to asia, and then we can speak under the banner of "human rights in the world" to protest against the fact that people in asia are forced to work for minimum wage or starvation wages. at the very least, if this company took a grant, it should pay it back. my question is the same as that of my colleague matula: what measures can the commission take to put an end to this unfortunate situation, which has not only been the case for nokia in eastern europe, but also for many other large companies, where we have not done enough to put an end to this unfortunate situation?
the relocation of companies from eu countries is not only an effect of the economic crisis but also of the wrong policies pursued by some member states. one example is romania, where, despite the government investing in infrastructure and providing facilities to ensure optimal operating conditions, nokia decided to close the factory. as a result of this decision, several thousand people lost their jobs. in the european union in particular, romanian citizens are in a worse situation, as jobs in romania are becoming fewer and fewer and, unfortunately, the european labour market is also becoming more restrictive for them. i am referring to the measure taken by spain to restrict access to the labour market in a discriminatory manner to romanian nationals only. i have put a written question to the commission on this subject a long time ago and have not yet received a reply, although the situation is serious. if i can't expect anything from the government in bucharest, i expect something from the comise in this area.
the eu 2020 strategy includes two important objectives, research and job creation, but there is a risk that we will not be able to achieve them in the way the european union wants, as long as actions such as those undertaken by nokia and arcelor mittal to suppress factories and relocate brand activities outside europe take place. we have discussed and approved in the european parliament proposals to make european industry more competitive, but we have not taken into account such actions which greatly affect the national and local budgets of the member states, which are obliged to intervene with social measures. i believe that the european union should impose a number of conditions on private companies wishing to relocate their activities, especially if they have announced significant benefits in the period preceding the closure of some locations and have received important facilities to create jobs, as happened in romania.
in writing. under the pressure of the economic crisis, political babble and unfinished projects, the eu risks becoming the big loser in global competition. we look with frustration at emerging economies and revolt when multinational companies like nokia or arcelor decide to move their businesses out of europe. but europe expects firm action, not complaints, and the power is in our hands, the europeans, to change what now seems to be an implacable destiny. one of the right answers is to return to our own resources. we must complete one of the most important projects, the european single market. we have enormous potential at our disposal which we are not exploiting because we do not have common legislation recognised by all the member states, we do not have common regulations in as many of the areas which are relevant to the common market, but we do have many barriers. in time, the ec now has the same duty to respond to nokia's layoffs in jucu, romania, as it did to those in bochum, germany, but these responses are only palliative. without a functioning single market, the eu will remain a mere spectator to the rise of its competitors.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the conclusion of the eu-norway satellite navigation cooperation agreement as the agreement contributes to the implementation of the eu's space policy. norway is the closest non-eu partner in the european gnss galileo and egnos systems and has contributed politically, technically and financially to all phases of the galileo programme as a member of the european space agency. norway will host two major land-based facilities that will contribute to the smooth functioning of the gnss system. in this context, norway commits itself politically to adhere to the future union policy on the protection of the european gnss systems. the agreement sets out the general principles of cooperation and norway's rights and obligations in relevant areas such as security. norway intends to adopt and implement measures in the territories under its jurisdiction to ensure a degree of security and safety equivalent to that provided by the measures applicable to gnss in the eu. the agreement provides for cooperation in the provision of satellite navigation services in the territories of the parties and the use of all galileo and egnos services, including the public regulated service (prs), subject to the fulfilment of the conditions governing their use.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report drawn up by mr reul because i consider the galileo programme to be one of the achievements of european integration. within the efforts and initiatives of the eu 2020 strategy, the development of gps and related applications plays a crucial role in strengthening innovation at european level. the agreement is the culmination of 12 years of discussions between the european and american sides, which have led to a consensus on the civilian and military use of such systems. respect for the principle of proportionality is essential in this case. thus, the necessary data must be provided to the population, while ensuring the adequate protection of military objectives. the geographical coverage of these systems is also important, as is the compatibility of different networks and reception modes. with all these elements harmonised, the balance between publicly available and confidential information will be clearer.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the conclusion of the eu-us agreement on the promotion, supply and use of galileo and gps satellite navigation systems and related applications. the agreement provides the framework for cooperation between the parties on the promotion, provision and use of gps and galileo civil navigation and timing signals and services, value-added services, complementary devices and global navigation and timing equipment. the us operates the global positioning system (gps), a dual-use system that provides accurate time, navigation services and positioning signals for civilian and military purposes. the us provides civilian gps free of charge to direct users and intends to continue to provide this service under the same conditions in the future. the eu is developing and planning the operation of galileo, a global civil satellite navigation, timing and positioning system that is radio frequency compatible with gps and interoperable with civil gps services at the user level. the civil gps and galileo services could increase the accuracy and accessibility of navigation signals for civil users worldwide. we call on the commission and the council to increase the budget for research related to gnss services and applications so that galileo can be used at its projected capacity once completed.
in writing. − the average eu corporate tax rate fell from 44% in 1980 to 35% in 1995 and finally to 23.2% in 2010. however, there are different tax regimes and double taxation of companies is addressed through bilateral agreements and community legislation. i support the proposal for a common european approach to halt and reverse the trend towards lower corporation tax rates. i also believe that stronger anti-abuse provisions and measures to limit the erosion of the tax base by eu corporations are needed.
in writing. − due to tax competition between eu member states, the average level of corporate taxation in the eu has fallen from 44% in 1980 to 23.2% in 2010. at the same time, some economic operators have increased access to capital and profit transfers, while others are deprived of this possibility. it is thus difficult to promote a socially and economically sustainable and integrated society. individuals and economic operators operating in the european union benefit from tax regimes that vary from one member state to another, and double taxation of companies is addressed through bilateral agreements and community legislation. i believe that we need a common european approach and at the same time we must prevent this tendency to reduce corporate tax rates too much. in addition, additional measures are necessary to address double taxation, to prevent misunderstandings or attempted fraud by member states. a thorough review of the community directives on the common tax system is therefore now required.

in writing. – the status of children has been the focus of international attention for a number of years, most notably in the drawing up of the un convention on the rights of the child. children are also increasingly affected by a whole range of eu policies and legislation. the commission has made an effort to define a so-called ‘eu agenda on the rights of the child’. however, its communication focuses mainly on legal dimensions, which – although of major importance in their own right – do not take proper account of the critical importance of appropriate socio-economic policies for children. we may not achieve the target of curbing the level of poverty by helping 20 million persons improve their standard of life by 2020, if we do not have a strategic approach on children and children-related components. we should develop and implement an eu strategy to halve child-poverty by 2020, and break the spiral of poverty in general. we consider necessary to mainstream individual children’s rights in all eu policies, monitoring and evaluating the steps undertaken to end child poverty, identifying and developing priority actions, aiming to enhance data collection and to further develop common indicators at eu level.

member of the commission. − mr president, we have indeed travelled a long way on this. it was in may last year that we started to discuss the renegotiations of the pnr agreement with australia and the usa. considerable efforts and contacts and a good cooperation, including with our australian counterparts, have been taking place during this time. today we have a proposed agreement that you will be voting on tomorrow. i think we can agree that we have worked hard on this. we have an agreement with very high standards which very much reflects the position taken by parliament in its resolution and the mandate given by the council. from the commission side, we consider that this is a further improvement of the 2008 agreement. it has clearer language, such as the definition of terrorism and serious transnational crime, it is a further strengthening of police cooperation, with high standards of data protection and it ensures freedom and safety for international air travel. it also recognises that information sharing is a fundamental component of the fight against terrorism and serious transnational crime. in this context, the use of pnr data is an essential tool but it recognises that such information sharing has to be undertaken in full respect of fundamental rights and freedoms. the data are transferred to the australia customs service for the purposes of preventing, detecting, investigating and prosecuting terrorist offences or serious transnational crime. in exceptional cases, pnr data may be processed for the prosecution of the vital interest of any individual, such as risk of death, serious injury or threat to health. the australian customs services will ensure that the relevant analytical information obtained from pnr is available to police and judicial authorities of member states or europol or eurojust as part of eu-australian security cooperation. the data is retained for five and a half years. after three years the data elements which could serve to identify the passenger to whom pnr data relate will be masked out. such depersonalised data will only be accessible to a very limited number of customs services officials. the data will, as the rapporteur said, be transferred to the australian customs service on the basis of the ‘push’ method only. the agreement applies without discrimination between passengers and prohibits all processing of sensitive data. it lays down provisions regulating rights of access, rectification, erasure and redress for any individual concerned. it prohibits decisions with adverse legal effects being taken exclusively on the basis of automatic processing of pnr data. all data processing is subject to oversight by the australian information commissioner, who has effective powers to investigate and monitor compliance with the terms of the agreement. all data processing is logged or documented for the purposes of oversight and auditing by the australian information commission. data may be shared with other government authorities of australia only on a case-by-case basis and only for the purposes of the agreement. onward transfer of data to authorities of third countries is allowed, subject to the same data protection safeguards as those applicable to transfers of data by air carriers to australian customs services under the agreement, only for the purposes set out in the agreement and only on a case-by-case basis. the competent authorities of the member states are also consulted when data concerning an eu citizen have been transferred to a country. the agreement will be reviewed one year after its entry into force. as regards suspension, in general suspension of agreements is regulated, as you know, by article 289 of the treaty. under that procedure, the council takes a decision on suspension on a proposal from the commission, but a parliamentary resolution calling for a suspension signals serious problems with the current agreement and would certainly be a very important element in this respect. i would like to thank the house, and especially the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs, for their very important cooperation. i think we can be proud of the result.
the committee on foreign affairs is the rapporteur for the opinion. − as rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on foreign affairs, i recommended to parliament that it give its consent to the signing of the new text of the agreement between the european union and australia on the processing and transfer of passenger name record data by air carriers to the australian customs and border protection service. the renegotiated draft agreement contains safeguards on the transfer and processing of passenger name record data, including: the right of access to and rectification of passenger data, the right of passengers to bring legal proceedings or sanctions for breaches of data security. this proposal will contribute to the effectiveness of measures against terrorism and crossborder organised crime, to international cooperation for the safety of citizens. passenger rights will be better protected with this agreement than without it. thank you to sophia and the pnr team for their work.

in writing. − antimicrobial resistance is a serious threat to public health worldwide, involving more complicated treatment protocols, higher risks of death and additional costs for health systems. this phenomenon clearly has cross-border implications and it cannot be excluded that exceptional situations may arise which are unlikely to be able to be managed with current resources and knowledge. i therefore call on member states to step up their global commitment to protecting the efficacy of antimicrobials for the benefit of future generations. i am also concerned that the level of access to information on antimicrobial resistance and the impact on citizens' consumption behaviour remains uneven across the european union, in particular with regard to the implementation of legislation on the use of antibiotics only on prescription. i believe that research on new antimicrobial agents and possible alternatives should be intensified in the framework of the european union's research programmes.

in writing. − antimicrobial resistance is an important and largely unresolved issue that has become a public health threat in europe and, globally, has led to longer and more complicated treatments, reduced quality of life, increased risk of death (every year in the eu, 25 000 patients die from an infection caused by resistant microorganisms), additional healthcare costs and lost productivity worth at least €1.5 billion/year. the special eurobarometer of april 2010 shows that there are many misconceptions about antibiotics and their effects and that 53% of europeans continue to believe that antibiotics kill viruses and 47% believe that antibiotics are effective against colds and flu. therefore, it is important to have a well-functioning monitoring and surveillance system in place to collect reliable and comparable data on the susceptibility of pathogens to microbial agents and the infections they cause, and the commission should propose without delay a harmonised surveillance system for antimicrobial resistance. research on new antimicrobial agents and possible alternatives needs to be intensified in the framework of the eu research programmes and cooperation with who needs to be strengthened.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on antimicrobial resistance, a public health threat, because it affects a growing number of people and implies high costs for public health systems. according to a 2009 report by the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc), more than 25 000 patients in the eu die each year from infections caused by multidrug-resistant bacteria. i voted for amendment no 1 because, although there is no clear link between the use of antibiotics in veterinary care and the development of resistance in humans, antimicrobial resistance affects both humans and animals and can potentially be transmitted both ways. therefore, further efforts are needed to improve agricultural practices in order to minimise the risks associated with the use of antibiotics for veterinary purposes and the development of resistance in humans. i voted for amendments 2 and 3 because i believe that restrictions should not be placed on existing treatment options that are effective and that the use of so-called 'antibiotics of last resort' targeting human pathogens should be allowed in the agricultural sector only under authorised conditions and in combination with resistance monitoring, preferably on a case-by-case basis.

in writing. the european union is recognised worldwide as an alliance of states that stand up for human rights, the rule of law and respect for human dignity. it has earned these honors for speaking out against human rights abuses in various parts of the world and for its trade relations being explicitly influenced by the attitudes of the state to the human rights regime in force. we know china is one of the most important trading partners of the western world. it is in the interest of the european states that this partnership should continue to be equally fruitful for both parties. the chinese government's policy on tibet, the systematic disregard for the rights of the tibetan people, is not new. the self-sacrifice and suicide of tibetan monks and nuns is a cry for help to the whole world. a cry for help, because it seems that the previous signals, the previous less drastic forms of protest, have not been heard by the world and its champion of human rights, the european union. we have heard it and we are hearing it now, but apart from debates like this here in parliament or in some national parliaments, there is not much that is actually being done to clarify the situation. i believe that the european states should take their responses to such cases more seriously, and the european union should take itself more seriously.
a report released monday by several human rights organizations points out that the wave of protests and regime change in the arab world has led to a tightening of repressive measures in many countries. bahrain is one of the most worrying examples of this, given the brutality with which the movement for political and social reform has been suppressed. the military intervention, including by gulf joint force troops, against the peaceful protesters has left dozens dead, hundreds injured and many arrested. the decrease in the intensity of the protests did not mean the easing of the repression. arrestations of human rights defenders, dismissals and abusive sentences of medical personnel who provided first aid to injured protesters, as well as the denial of legal and medical assistance to detainees and the imposition of censorship of the media and internet access continue to be reported. the european union has repeatedly condemned the violence and repression ordered by the bahraini government, but the situation has not changed. i believe it is necessary to continue to press for the release of political prisoners, the cessation of prosecution of doctors and the persecution on political and religious grounds. i also believe that the bahraini authorities must urgently commute the death sentences that have been handed down and abandon this barbaric practice. last but not least, i want to appreciate the delay in u.s. arms sales to bahrain until the inquiry report next week.

in writing. what happened in bahrain this spring must not become a forgotten revolution. the intervention of saudi troops has allowed perhaps temporarily the restoration of royal authority but, despite our repeated calls, a genuine dialogue with the opposition on political reforms has not yet been engaged. recent developments in this country are not encouraging. dozens of protesters arrested in february were brought before special national security courts and received record sentences (between 7 years and life imprisonment). doctors and medical staff at the manama hospital were also severely condemned for the simple fact that they acted ethically in treating the shia victims of the pearl square demonstrations. press freedom is also in danger as several journalists have been prosecuted and fined for spreading false news during the riots. we cannot have double standards in the way we approach events in north africa and the middle east. that is why i think it is time to be very firm with the bahraini authorities, who must urgently start a genuine process of democratic reform, which takes into account the aspirations of the protesters.

on behalf of the epp group. dictatorial regimes often take action against psychology and psychologists. hitler abolished the social science departments. in 1977, the romanian communist regime closed the psychology departments of the country's major university centers. specialists in the field have been prosecuted or forcibly transferred to unskilled labor. by improperly arresting psychoanalyst rafah nached, the syrian regime continues this sad tradition, proving once again its undemocratic character. it does not engage in political activities, yet its actions have been considered subversive because they concern the human soul, which naturally aspires to freedom. and for the syrian regime, this aspiration is a danger. rafah nached must be released immediately. not because she's a scientific personality or because of her health problems, but because she's done nothing but practice her profession.

the reform of the directive establishing the single european railway area consolidates and clarifies the requirements of the previous directives. i welcome the obligation for member states to adopt national rail infrastructure development strategies for a period of at least seven years. only by investing in rail transport can we increase its market share. conditions for access to railway infrastructure must not prevent passengers from receiving information and buying a ticket to get from one location to another, regardless of how many operators provide rail passenger services between the two locations. i consider that the separation of the provision of rail transport services from the management of railway infrastructure should not have negative consequences for social and working conditions in this sector. we call on the commission to cooperate with trade unions and trade union associations in the sector, as well as with user representatives, in monitoring technical and economic conditions and developments on the european rail transport market, including employment.
the development of the european railway sector is essential for the union to cope with the competition and challenges it faces, but also to meet the requirements of all beneficiaries. i believe that it is beneficial to link rail transport as closely as possible with inland waterway transport, in order to cover the whole of the european union as well as to meet the objectives of reducing carbon dioxide emissions. consultation with local and regional authorities is essential for the development of national rail infrastructure strategies, as is support for countries with less developed networks. i also believe that the eu countries should put more emphasis on using the structural funds for priority transport projects, including cross-border connections and urban mobility, and should participate as much as possible in the development of specialised networks, so as not to end up with a multi-speed europe in the field of transport networks. thank you, sir.
it is clear that rail transport has not developed at the same pace as other transport sectors. the proposal for the establishment of the single european railway area sought to improve this situation. he didn't quite make it, but he made strides. unfortunately, there are still member states, there are still railway companies that do not want the real liberalisation of railway activity. the package improves non-discriminatory access to service infrastructures such as maintenance and repair stations or refuelling stations and increases the transparency of the institutional framework of the railway market. national regulatory bodies are established to prevent discriminatory practices. these bodies must be completely independent of the railway industry and national governments in order to carry out their functions. full independence of railway transport operators from infrastructure managers has not been achieved, but the accounting separation of profit and loss accounts has been achieved.
the implementation of directive 2005/36/ec on the recognition of professional qualifications is essential for professional mobility, a key factor for the economic and social development of the union. since 2007, around 100 000 recognition decisions have been taken under the directive, facilitating the mobility of 85 000 professionals. however, over 16% of solvit cases in 2010 are related to the recognition of professional qualifications. the evolution of labour markets requires greater transparency, simplification and flexibility in the rules on the recognition of professional qualifications. the periodic updating of initial training, recognition of experience and continuing training requirements is essential for the harmonisation of training. the right to work or provide services in another member state is a fundamental right, conferred by the treaties, and is a concrete example of how citizens can benefit from the single market. i take this opportunity to call again for the removal of the barriers to the free movement of labour in romania and bulgaria.
in writing. modernising and streamlining the procedures for the recognition of professional qualifications is an indispensable element for increasing the mobility of european citizens. at the same time, making the labour market more flexible will also lead to a better functioning of the single market and the economic union as a whole. this report raises key issues for the future reform of the directive. an effort must be made to simplify procedures, in particular for the general recognition system. i also consider it appropriate to assess the application of compensatory measures and their relevance and to adopt optional guidelines for a more uniform approach to the application of these measures. temporary mobility should be supported by clarifying the concept and by eliminating the system of prior declaration in cases where service providers accompany the consumer in another member state without contacting local consumers. we can also explore the possibilities of coordinating our education systems so that we can achieve a higher degree of harmonisation in the future and we can extend the system of automatic recognition to other professions. lastly, voluntary professional cards can be an effective tool for faster recognition of qualifications, but they should only be implemented where they have real added value compared to the current system.
in writing. facilitating the recognition of professional qualifications at european level is a measure that will allow for a faster professional integration of young people into the eu labour market. i welcome the proposals to create networks of competent authorities and professional bodies for the most mobile professions, and to exchange information on educational programmes on a permanent basis, in order to increase the credibility of diplomas between member states, but also to improve the language skills of young people wishing to work in another member state. in addition, the introduction of the professional card, which recognises the professional qualifications of its holder at european level, will reduce bureaucratic obstacles and allow greater mobility of european citizens on the labour market. i also hope that cross-border mobility will be improved as a means of stimulating economic growth and competitiveness within the union.
in writing. the recognition of diplomas and professional qualifications at eu level, regulated by the 2005 directive (2005/36/ec), is particularly important for both the old member states and for citizens of new states, such as my country, romania. freedom of movement is one of the essential rights conferred by membership of the union, and demographic change will make mobility between eu countries increasingly important. at present, only a few professions are regulated at community level, while for the rest, costly and lengthy equivalence procedures are applied, ranging from testing to the imposition of additional studies. given that education reforms facilitate the process of recognition of european qualifications, through the european qualifications framework and the bologna process, i believe that the list of regulated professions at eu level should be extended. the procedures for the recognition of diplomas and professional qualifications must also be simplified and made more urgent, but greater transparency is also needed. in this context too, attention must be paid to the issue of recognition of the qualifications of third-country nationals, who must not be given priority over nationals of member states. i also believe that states should accept all categories of workers on the labour market, not just those with highly skilled professions, i.e. the so-called brain drain phenomenon.
