services of general economic interest contribute to the prosperity and economic competitiveness of the member states. these services are also essential in combating social inequalities. however, the compensation for their insurance must not distort competition and harm other undertakings. the principle of subsidiarity must be strictly respected. i draw your attention to protocol 26 to the treaty of lisbon. according to the court, the member states have competence to provide public services. i consider that the state aid rules should be clarified. in romania, these rules are to be simplified for small-scale public services of a local nature. the european union must also support member states' efforts to modernise services of general economic interest and to adapt them to the needs of the population. public services in romania are regulated by legislation specific to each sector.
member of the commission. − mr president, on behalf of vice-president almunia, i would first of all like to thank mr simon for his report on the reform of the eu state aid rules for services of general economic interest and would also like to thank the econ, itre and imco committees and all their members for their contributions to this report. we are convinced that public services play a key role in the european social model because they make an important contribution to social stability and territorial cohesion. this is why services of general economic interest are one of the key priorities in the state aid field during our mandate. we are glad that there is such an intense debate going on about this topic between parliament, other eu institutions and all stakeholders. we particularly welcome parliament’s contribution to this debate. it reflects the importance which parliament attaches to establishing a clear legal framework for services of general economic interest. let me recall that our reform is based on three objectives: clarification, simplification and a more diversified approach. we set out these objectives in detail in our communication in march. since then, we have published draft texts that show how we think the objectives should be translated into rules. the reply to the public consultation on the draft texts has been rich and fruitful. the direction of the reform is broadly shared by all, although stakeholders have different views on the details of the changes. this is why in the coming weeks we will work to further improve on the delivery of the three objectives. the report by the european parliament could not have come at a better time. it has been able to take account of our draft texts and thus to provide us suggestions on how to further improve our texts. it will prove a particularly valuable contribution to the reform. let me briefly focus on three points in mr simon’s report: a major tool for simplification in our reform is the new de minimis regulation. the report suggests that a threshold based on the size of the municipality is not necessary to restrict the de minimis regulation to small local services, and that a three-year approach would be more flexible than the current one-year threshold. as i have already emphasised, no decision has yet been taken as to what kind of thresholds are most appropriate. we are open to suggestions and appreciate the views of all stakeholders, in particular the european parliament’s opinion. secondly, the report requests that additional social services be covered by the decision. social services play a very important role in our society and there is less need for very strict scrutiny. this is why under the more diversified approach they benefit from exemption from notification and more lenient compatibility criteria of the decision. i am open to assessing evidence and arguments to improve the scope and treatment of social services where justified. thirdly, parliament considers that the commission cannot define efficiency criteria under state aid rules. let me underline that the current drafts do not require undertakings to be efficient, nor do they allow the commission to check for efficiency. the draft texts only require that undertakings be given incentives to improve their efficiency. i know that some of you are nevertheless afraid of such a change. however, those efficiency incentives only apply to large commercial sgeis that we assess under the framework. they are also largely supported by service providers and other stakeholders. let me recall again why we are so keen to improve our rules: in the present situation, given the tight budgetary constraints of all member states, we want everyone to be given the possibility to continue enjoying accessible, affordable and efficient public services. thank you very much once again for your contribution to this reform.
in writing. ensuring that public services are of quality and accessible to all citizens is an essential element of the european social model. public services meet the daily needs of europeans and play an important role in ensuring equal opportunities and respect for fundamental rights. the european commission is seeking to simplify the state aid rules applicable to services of general economic interest; services which include the management of public transport, the supply of water and heat, the construction of social housing and the provision of postal services. the introduction of simplified legislative rules in this area would reduce the administrative burden on local authorities. at the same time, the future reform must not, under the pretext of streamlining processes, jeopardise universal access to services that mitigate the social impact of the economic crisis by protecting the vulnerable. a narrow definition of the category of services of general economic interest and the setting of low thresholds for the volume of compensation allowed would facilitate the liberalisation of public services, and liberalisation of public services means sacrificing citizens' rights and deepening economic inequalities.
in writing. i think that the commission's lack of concern about the social implications of the anti-crisis programmes implemented in the european union is evident. the conservative right has other priorities than the 116 million people who face the risk of poverty and the 42 million people who live in conditions of extreme poverty and cannot afford the essentials for a decent life. it is shocking that the banking sector is so much more important to european decision-makers than the fact that more than a quarter of the eu population is facing the scourge of poverty. poverty and its implications including long-term unemployment, which affects one in three unemployed, lack of housing and access to health services, school dropouts, social exclusion of the elderly and people with disabilities are factors that destroy social cohesion between generations and between occupational categories. i am concerned that the platform proposed by the commission does not take into account the need to combat the increased vulnerability of women, especially single mothers and the elderly. i call on the commission to be more involved in helping european citizens to fight poverty and social exclusion and i believe that a realistic analysis of the possibility of reducing by 20 million the number of people at risk of poverty, in line with the europe 2020 strategy, is needed.
in writing. the existence of poverty in europe, which threatens some 8% of the active population, highlights the fact that further efforts are needed to achieve one of the main objectives of european integration - raising and maintaining a high standard of living for europeans. at the same time, looking at which region of europe is geographically most affected by poverty, it is very easy to turn our attention to the new member states, the region of central and eastern europe. i therefore believe that territorial cohesion, the reduction of disparities in development between the regions of europe, is one of the greatest challenges facing the union. solidarity is one of the european values enshrined in the treaties, and it is clear that this is the key to maintaining and further strengthening cohesion policy. support for economically disadvantaged regions not only benefits the economies of the member states but also brings the living standards of citizens in different regions of europe closer together, thus contributing to the construction of a common europe and to the strengthening of european identity. the achievement of the europe 2020 targets, including poverty reduction, requires the strengthening of national economies and the acceleration of their economic expansion. the european union can also contribute to this, for example through cohesion policy.
in writing. the poor suffer from hunger and disease and have a low life expectancy. hunger and malnutrition are the biggest public health threats in the world. of the 7 billion people on earth, some 925 million suffer from hunger, and children are the most affected. poverty is a major factor in the deaths of at least five million children every year around the world. in addition, poverty is also one of the biggest risk factors for diseases like hiv/aids, malaria and tuberculosis. i would like to encourage projects/initiatives aimed at increasing life expectancy in developing countries, addressing health care gaps in less developed countries, raising awareness of parasitic diseases worldwide, but also projects aiming at providing immediate help to disadvantaged families in the eu, and not just help that can consist of food, access to drinking water, clothing, shelter, sanitation, education and information. it is our role to do everything we can to eradicate poverty, reduce child mortality and increase life expectancy, and the european platform against poverty and social exclusion is a very good tool to achieve these goals.
i would like to say that i voted for this report because the decline in the active population and the ageing of the workforce will mark demographic developments in the eu in the coming decades. in this context, the lack of effective measures to preserve the quality of life and social inclusion can have a negative impact on social security systems. in the union, expenditure on pension funds represents on average 43% of gross expenditure on social protection benefits. the potential of older people must be exploited. i also believe that strategies to encourage birth and migration are needed. they must be tackled in a coordinated way by all european, national and regional authorities. romania has more pensioners than employees, which means that in the future the pension system will be in danger.
i voted in favour of adopting the report on demographic change in the context of the future cohesion policy, because issues such as depopulation, population ageing or labour migration represent real challenges for the member states, with a particularly strong impact on european regions. regional policy is a key instrument in tackling demographic change and that is why we must ensure that this dimension is included as a horizontal objective in future cohesion policy. the vote we have taken today is to give the regions most affected the resources and technical assistance needed to access the structural funds. they will ensure access to essential public services, but also the creation of new sources of employment, in particular by supporting small and medium-sized enterprises. one of the solutions at european level to reduce the negative effects of demographic change is to promote the exchange of good practice between member states. that is why i have asked the european commission to come up with concrete solutions to ensure the continuation of the 'erasmus for local and regional elected officials' programme. i believe that this programme must continue in a form appropriate to the needs and realities.

in writing. − the accession to the athens convention on the carriage of passengers and their luggage by sea has been a long-standing concern of the eu and, in particular, of parliament. the convention dates back to 1974 and deals in particular with the safety of passenger ships and the rights of passengers. however, it was considered that this convention does not sufficiently regulate several important aspects, such as the nature and limits of the liability of carriers and minimum insurance requirements. as it is a mixed agreement, which needs to be ratified by the member states in order to ensure a coherent legal framework throughout the union, both the member states and the union should prepare the simultaneous deposit of their instruments of ratification or accession by 31 december 2011.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution on the draft council decision on the eu's accession to the 2002 protocol to the athens convention of 1974 on the carriage of passengers and their luggage by sea, with the exception of articles 10 and 11. this protocol introduces clarifications on liability in the event of the fault or negligence of the carrier, compulsory insurance, limitation of liability in the event of death or personal injury or damage to luggage or vehicles. the adoption of regulation (ec) no 392/2009 on the liability of carriers of passengers by sea implies that the union now has exclusive competence to accede to the athens protocol as regards the matters covered by the regulation. all other aspects of the protocol which are not covered by the regulation are the responsibility of the member states. the athens protocol remains a mixed agreement to which each member state must become a contracting party. to that end, the member states and the union are to deposit their instruments of accession on the same day. i draw attention to the deadline of 31 december 2011 by which the union and the member states are to deposit their instruments of accession to the athens protocol or of ratification for those who have already signed it.
in writing. − the agreement put forth by the committee on transport and tourism establishing relations in the field of aviation between the eu’s 27 member states and georgia is an important step in streamlining operations between countries. in a field such as aviation where safety, security and air traffic management are paramount, it is important that the bilateral agreements that exist between individual member states and georgia be consolidated into an agreement of a common aviation area. additionally, the eu and georgia should form this agreement to solidify common framework conditions. moreover, reciprocal market opening will help broaden participation in the market which coincides with the objectives of the european neighbourhood policy. as a member of the delegation to the euronest parliamentary assembly, i see the eu-georgia common aviation area agreement as a logical step in increasing georgia’s involvement in activities that affect both georgia and the eu. the eu must ensure its commitment to passenger safety and the efficient operation of air services while encouraging the participation of its neighbours in market-boosting pursuits.
in writing. - i voted in favour of temporarily suspending common customs tariff duties on imports of certain industrial products into the canary islands, in order to support spain's efforts to strengthen the competitiveness of local economic operators and to stabilise employment in these outermost regions of the union. in order to ensure that goods imported duty-free do not distort competition, end-use controls are required to ensure that they are used by local companies on the islands. i believe that this type of measure, which favours local smes and farmers and encourages them to invest and create jobs, should also be considered in other outermost regions of the european union.
in writing. − i consider it beneficial that the european union has recognised the particular and specific problems of the canary islands and their implications for integration into the union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this motion for a decision because i believe it is important to ensure the continuity of eu-funded research in the two priority areas of the programme: fusion and nuclear fission research and radiation protection. i believe that it is important for the future energy mix of the union to develop the knowledge base for iter and to make iter the main step forward towards the creation of prototype power plant reactors that are safe, sustainable, environmentally friendly and economically viable. it is important that, under the second priority 'nuclear fission and radiation protection', practical developments towards safer management of long-lived radioactive waste are accelerated in order to increase in particular the safety and efficiency of resource use. i have called for special attention to be given to the development of contractual arrangements that reduce the risk of non-performance and the reallocation of risks over time. i consider it important that, in the composition of the committees on fission and fusion issues, a reasonable balance be ensured between the number of women and men and between the member states carrying out nuclear research and training.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that there is a need to harmonise insolvency procedures. the scope of the insolvency regulation should be extended. insolvency has negative consequences for the economy of the member states. it can lead to difficulties for businesses with cross-border activities. at the same time, disparities between national legislation in this area affect competitiveness. the insolvency of a group of undertakings may lead to multiple insolvency proceedings. however, i would point out that there are no legal provisions at eu level on the insolvency of groups of undertakings. this lack of transparency can have significant negative consequences. divergence of the main procedures should be avoided. it is necessary to provide for appropriate procedural safeguards. at the same time, the balance between the interest of the entrepreneur in seeking to save his company and the interest of creditors in protecting their claims must be strengthened. i welcome the idea of creating an eu-wide insolvency register.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. differences between national insolvency laws create major problems for companies, generate abuses and affect the economies of member states. i also support the recommendations in the annex to the report, in particular those concerning the timely opening of insolvency proceedings by all firms in the event of temporary insolvency, those concerning claims, actions for annulment, the powers of the liquidator, restructuring plans, etc.
in writing. − freedom of establishment and increased mobility of companies between member states have highlighted the need for better coordination and greater harmonisation of insolvency law to combat the negative effects of 'insolvency tourism' on employees. even though labour law is the responsibility of the member states, insolvency law can have an impact on labour law and, in the context of increased globalisation and even the economic crisis, the issue of insolvency needs to be examined from the perspective of labour law. i note with concern the increasing number of workers, especially women and those over 45 years of age, affected by insolvency proceedings, which can be attributed to the very serious economic and social effects of the financial and economic crisis, and the nature of systemically important cross-border financial institutions enhancing their role in this area. i welcome the fact that directive 2008/94/ec on the protection of employees in the event of the insolvency of their employer explicitly includes part-time workers, fixed-term workers and temporary agency workers in its scope. however, i believe that it is necessary to strengthen protection in the event of insolvency, even for workers with atypical contracts.
in writing. − europe has the oldest population in the world and the lowest rate of population growth. this is a reality that should concern us and make us aware that demographic change is affecting many sectors. through the implementation of community policies, common solutions and synergies can be found on the main vulnerabilities caused by demographic change. the structural funds must therefore be better adapted to the challenges of these changes, depopulation and social isolation of older people must be prevented and urban planning must be adapted. increasing the employment rate of women also plays a central role in combating this phenomenon. last but not least, better coordination between competent authorities at all levels is needed and exchanges of good practice should be encouraged. in this way, i invite member states to take into account the different levels of development of the regions in the allocation and distribution of eu structural funds and the definition of impact indicators.
in writing. − there are two important aspects of europe today: the ageing of the population and migration flows from within and outside the eu. in the current financial year, member states have allocated €30 billion from the structural funds to measures related to demographic change. it's an interesting idea to treat demographic change as an opportunity, not just a threat. this can be done by addressing the problem at the regional level. the commission proposed to support young families through high-quality childcare and education institutions, but also through solutions for the middle and older generation. as such, it is right to consider that the structural funds should be better adapted to these challenges. cities and villages need to be attractive to their inhabitants, have the infrastructure needed for children and families and homes for several generations. it is desirable to reduce youth unemployment through esf-funded projects.
in writing. − the european union needs to take account of current demographic changes in the member states to identify how european strategies in this area can be adapted to the problems identified by local and regional authorities. the current crisis should not affect urban and regional development projects, which should be linked to functional changes in infrastructure, including the revitalization and redevelopment of central urban areas, and the possibility of developing smaller or larger cities in the future that are better adapted to older people and their mobility.
in writing. − demographic change is a topical issue facing the eu, with irreversible effects on society. in order to achieve the eu 2020 goals of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, demographic change must be addressed as an opportunity, not a burden. 2012 is the 'european year of active ageing and solidarity between generations'. the decline in the number of people able to work and the ageing of the population will have a decisive effect on the labour market. at the same time, the rate of unemployment among young people is rising alarmingly, and the european union is virtually obliged to create a balance between the generations. a first step is to use the full potential of the european social fund to support training opportunities, retraining and social inclusion for women and young people. secondly, the training of the workforce must be encouraged, especially in developing regions, in countries that have recently joined the european union. the labour force in countries like romania and bulgaria is not being exploited to its full capacity. equal opportunities in the labour market will bring beneficial competition and ensure a dynamic, well-trained workforce. the elimination of discrimination in the labour force, its mobility, together with the creation of stable vocational training, are the key factors for the future of the european union.
in writing. − i voted for the report on demographic change and its consequences for the future eu cohesion policy because demographic change has very different effects from one region to another, has implications for both infrastructure and services and must be addressed in a coordinated way by european, national and regional authorities. the union's population is ageing and the birth rate is falling. an active and healthy population is critical to the development of european society. to cope with demographic change, the union needs to reduce health disparities and improve access to health services. member states should be encouraged to use the erdf and esf structural funds to adapt housing to the needs of older people, to guarantee the quality of life of an ageing society and to support young families. we call for the rules on the esf to be more manageable and to allow even small organisations to benefit from this source of funding, to develop and manage innovative social projects. we call on the commission to create more flexible conditions to stimulate combined erdf and esf funding by member states and local authorities when developing and implementing integrated urban development plans/strategies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on short selling and certain aspects of credit default swaps because i hope that it will ensure the proper functioning of the internal market and improve the conditions for its functioning, especially as regards financial markets. it is also necessary to ensure a high level of consumer and investor protection and to harmonise the framework for the conduct of short selling and certain aspects of credit default swaps in order to prevent the creation of obstacles to the proper functioning of the internal market, given the likelihood that member states will continue to adopt divergent measures.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution which aims to update the legal framework for european statistics on permanent crops by adapting it to the current needs of users and the market. in this respect and with a view to simplification, the commission is working to reduce the administrative burden on respondents and to ensure that statistical data on permanent crops are a viable basis for making sound decisions on european production and the market. it should be borne in mind that structural statistics on permanent crops are essential for the management of markets at union level.
in writing. − i consider it necessary to strengthen cooperation between the authorities producing european statistics on permanent crops at union level. i also believe that when european statistics are produced, best international practice should be taken into account.
in writing. − i voted in favour of implementing the framework programme (2012-2013), which should be based on the principles of simplicity, stability, transparency, legal certainty, consistency, excellence and trust, following the recommendations of the european parliament in its report on simplifying the implementation of the research framework programmes. to maintain and improve the safety level of both western and russian nuclear power plants, advanced and refined safety assessment methodologies and the corresponding analytical tools need to be extended and validated. to this end, the jrc will continue, in collaboration with its international partners, to develop networks for measuring radioactivity in the environment, making all collected data immediately available to the public.
in writing. − the euratom treaty limits the duration of all research programmes to five years. the current euratom framework programme, fp7 euratom (2007-2011), which consists of two specific programmes (one for 'indirect actions' and the other for 'direct actions' of the joint research centre (jrc), will expire at the end of 2011. i voted to extend the specific programme for 'direct actions' for 2012-13 to ensure the continuation of eu-funded research in the field of nuclear waste management and in the field of physical and radiological safety and security of nuclear systems. the implementation of the framework programme (2012-2013) should be based on the principles of simplicity, stability, transparency, legal certainty, consistency, excellence and trust. i support the need to increase budgets for initiatives ancillary to the core nuclear research activity, such as investments in human capital, as well as training and aid for nuclear researchers, to prevent possible shortages of skilled labour in the coming years. i believe that the joint research centre should contribute to the supervision of the quality and efficiency of training and to the coordination of existing educational programmes in the field of nuclear energy both within the union and in the candidate and neighbouring countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the framework programme (2012-2013), which should contribute to the realisation of the 'innovation union', one of the flagship initiatives of the europe 2020 strategy, by strengthening competition for scientific excellence and accelerating the implementation of key innovations in nuclear energy, in particular in nuclear fusion and safety, while also playing a role in addressing the challenges of the energy sector and climate change. the programme aims to complement other union actions in the field of research policy necessary for the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy, in particular those relating to education and training, competitiveness and innovation, industry, employment and the environment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european commission's proposals to continue nuclear research, because nuclear energy currently plays an important role in the energy mix of the member states and in ensuring energy security. i support the commission's approach, which recommends that great importance should be attached to current nuclear financing, as the european union is in a decision-making process on the future of nuclear that will be largely determined by the results of the technical risk and safety assessment of eu nuclear power plants. in addition, research in this area is also essential for the decommissioning of nuclear power plants in some member states and for long-term nuclear waste management activities. it is important that the 7th euratom framework programme for nuclear research can continue until 2013 as it will allow companies, research centres and universities to contribute to the efficiency of nuclear energy (fusion and fusion) research and radiation protection.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the regulation laying down the rules for the participation of undertakings, research centres and universities in indirect actions under the european atomic energy community framework programme and for the dissemination of research results (2012-2013). i voted for a stronger focus and higher budgetary expenditure on initiatives ancillary to the core nuclear research activity, in particular on investments in human capital and actions aimed at addressing the risk of a shortage of skilled labour in the coming years (grants for nuclear researchers). in my amendments i proposed that when independent expert groups are appointed, appropriate measures should be taken to ensure a reasonable balance between the number of women and men and between the member states carrying out nuclear research and training. i believe that when independent expert groups are appointed, a reasonable balance between business and academia must be ensured. the rules for the participation of undertakings, research centres and universities should provide a coherent, comprehensive and transparent framework so that, through simplified procedures, easy access is guaranteed to interested parties.
in writing. − the free movement of persons within the european union and the right to recognition of professional qualifications and skills will only become a reality when existing barriers are reduced to a minimum and certain national rules restricting access to skilled jobs disappear. developments in labour markets require greater transparency, simplification and flexibility of the rules on the recognition of professional qualifications. modernising the system for the recognition of professional qualifications is key to enhancing economic growth and building the confidence of professionals and citizens. i believe that the fast pace of innovation requires an open attitude on the part of european and national authorities to accept new skills, qualifications and academic studies and to facilitate the transfer of knowledge and innovation. i stress the need to develop a sustainable workforce by establishing recruitment and retention strategies, promoting gender equality, lifelong education and training, with a focus on improving working conditions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report and i would like to give you some of the reasons why. the right to obtain employment or provide services in another member state is a fundamental right, guaranteed by the treaties. the system of recognition of qualifications is the key element and its modernisation can even be a source of economic growth. citizens need a simplified system, clear and shorter deadlines for obtaining professional recognition, transparency, a system capable of integrating professionals and generating trust. i hope that all of these things will soon become realities, not for us who are debating today, but for the millions of people who are waiting for them.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the implementation of the directive on the recognition of professional qualifications. the free movement of an increasing number of highly skilled people and workers is one of the main benefits of european cooperation and a competitive internal market, an important factor in the development of economies across the eu, and a right of all european citizens. the mobility of workers among eu citizens should be increased and direct and indirect obstacles should be removed, provided that a balance is struck between mobility and the quality of vocational qualifications. the directive encourages initiatives aimed at facilitating crossborder mobility both as a means of ensuring the efficient functioning of labour markets and as a means of stimulating economic growth and competitiveness within the eu. among other things, it should be borne in mind that the recognition of professional qualifications is closely linked to the completion of the bologna process, which aims at creating a single european area of higher education.
in writing. − parliament voted today in favour of the recognition of professional qualifications, but we must not forget that although these rules have been introduced at a general level, not all eu citizens can benefit from them. i am referring in particular to romanian citizens, who are still subject to restrictions on the labour market in many european countries. now, under the pretext of the crisis, some states that had lifted these restrictions have reimposed them. what good is it to recognize a person's qualifications if you don't give them the right to work? i wish with all my heart that this situation would change as soon as possible.
in writing. − global competition and the move towards a knowledge-based economy are creating new challenges for skills development and education. the current directive includes rules for the mutual recognition of professional qualifications in eu member states for 800 categories of regulated professions and automatic recognition for seven sectoral professions: architect, dentist, doctor, midwife, nurse, pharmacist and veterinary surgeon. the european centre for the development of vocational training estimates that the demand for highly skilled workers will increase in the european union by over 16 million jobs by 2020. i therefore support continuing vocational training, lifelong learning and recommend that member states review and improve the minimum duration of vocational training. i believe that dialogue and exchange of information within each profession must be intensified and that cooperation between the competent authorities and the national contact points must be improved both at national level and between member states. it calls on states to exchange general information on national education procedures and requirements and to organise exchanges of good practice to ensure quality of services. public authorities and social partners need to engage in a dialogue to enhance the professional integration of young people.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of directive 2005/36/ec on the recognition of professional qualifications, as the freedom of movement of persons is one of the fundamental freedoms guaranteed by the treaties. to benefit from freedom of movement, professionals need to have their qualifications easily recognised in all member states. the directive on the recognition of professional qualifications provides that any host member state in which a profession is regulated has the obligation to take into account qualifications obtained in another member state and to check whether they correspond to those it requires. although the internal market creates conditions for obtaining a job or providing services in another member state, the mobility of professionals is still low in the eu. greater mobility is also a solution for jobs requiring high skills, especially in the face of a shrinking labour force. the use of modern communication technologies, including databases and online registration procedures, would bring significant improvements in access to information and knowledge of procedures, as well as in meeting deadlines set by the general recognition system. we consider that the elimination of the qualification levels, including annexes ii and iii to directive 2005/36/ec, would considerably simplify the recognition procedure.
in writing. − i welcome the european commission's initiative to launch a consumer protection agenda and stress that the internal market must develop without undermining consumer protection, guaranteeing the free movement of services and paying particular attention to the protection of workers. calls on the member states of the union to give careful consideration to the design of smarter policies that provide consumers with information that is truly useful to them, without creating additional burdens for societies, thus responding to the many challenges facing the eu today: increasing consumer empowerment and reducing inequalities, encouraging sustainable consumption, reducing consumer exposure to unsafe products, and protecting consumers, especially children, from misleading advertising. i believe that special attention should be paid to intelligent energy systems; the use of new technologies should allow all network users to participate in the internal energy market in order to save energy and reduce energy costs. coordinated efforts are also needed to better inform consumers about more efficient ways of buying and consuming food, in order to prevent and combat food waste.
in writing. − i am pleased that we will have a consumer protection agenda in may 2012 and hope that it will put food safety, human health and product safety first. we all know that we do not have the same consumer capacity and the same conditions in all member states. we know that we have poverty and food shortages, that we don't recycle enough, that the most vulnerable group of people are children. i believe, as do my colleagues, that these are just some of the things that need to be addressed and corrected in the future agenda and i supported them with my vote.
in writing. − consumer protection is one of the areas where eu action brings benefits to consumers. i believe that the report contains guidelines on the most important aspects of consumer protection policy which parliament wants to see in the new strategy to be presented by the european commission next year. the commission will need to take into account the interests of consumers when proposing legislation and, in particular, with the member states, to communicate better on consumer rights so that consumer confidence is strengthened. the lack of certainty about consumers' rights makes consumers reluctant to engage in electronic commerce and, in particular, in cross-border online transactions, which are currently a very important aspect for the development of the digital single market. we also need additional guarantees as regards the safety of products on the market. it is therefore necessary to review the product safety directive and implement the toy safety directive, as called for in this report. special attention will also need to be paid to the protection of vulnerable consumers, as well as consumers in general, and the revision of the unfair commercial practices directive or the directive on misleading advertising will be very useful to this end.
in writing. − we all know that the more than 400 million consumers are the heart and driving force of the european economy. according to the latest eurobarometer survey on consumer activeness, from april this year, most consumers consider themselves informed, but at the same time, a fairly large number have some gaps in knowledge of basic consumer protection legislation. ladies and gentlemen, european citizens play a key role in achieving the europe 2020 goals and consumer spending generates over half of the union's gdp. in this context, i believe that european consumer protection policy must make an important contribution to shifting the focus of this policy to issues that focus on citizens. european consumer protection policy must empower union consumers through fair information, market transparency and effective protection against the risks and threats to which they are exposed.
in writing. - i voted for amendment no 1 to the report on a new strategy for consumer protection policy because, under article 169 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the union must contribute to the protection of the health, safety and economic interests of consumers. the union must also promote their right to information, education and organisation to defend their interests. according to the fifth edition of the consumer scoreboard (march 2011), eu consumers continue to face very different conditions. 44% of consumers said that uncertainty about their rights discourages them from buying goods in other member states and that late delivery, non-delivery and fraud are the main factors preventing them from making cross-border purchases. they support the need to ensure universal access to broadband communications networks as well as broad access to online goods and services, including by removing distribution restrictions, addressing geographical segmentation and developing electronic payment services. to increase the number of consumers accessing goods and services online, we ask the commission to legislate on the mutual recognition of electronic signatures, on electronic identity and on the promotion of electronic invoicing. i support the elimination of unfair contract terms in the sale of goods and services.
in writing. − online gambling is on the rise, to some extent outside the control of national governments, and is not a market like others, given the risks it poses to consumer protection and the fight against organised crime. different regulation of this sector in the member states creates major difficulties in protecting consumers and combating illegal online gambling and the potential crime associated with it at european level. the central objective pursued must therefore be to significantly reduce this black market. in order to achieve this, one of the options i encourage member states to pursue is a total ban. it is also necessary to establish minimum standards at european level for the protection of minors, the fight against addiction, but also for the fight against money laundering and other criminal activities associated with gambling. i urge the commission to formulate standards applicable at european level and binding on all licensed online gambling operators. member states would be free to impose additional criteria at a later stage. determined action by the commission and the member states is important to ensure a high and uniform level of consumer protection at european level.
in writing. − i welcome the adoption of this report, as i believe that recent developments and, in particular, the development of internet services have created a need to regulate some previously unregulated aspects. if until now the services consisting in the offer of games of chance were not sold across borders, with the development of the internet this has become possible. given that member states have quite different regulations on gambling, with two regulatory models based either on a controlled monopoly or on the licensing of operators, it has become necessary to establish a minimum set of rules, in particular with regard to consumer protection and fraud prevention. i also support the rapporteur's view that it is appropriate to adopt a set of standards for the creation of transparent and non-discriminatory licensing systems for gambling operators for those member states that apply the licensing-based system. last but not least, i believe that action should be taken against black-money gambling. i can therefore only support the rapporteur's suggestion to create a so-called 'white list' of legal operators so that those who use gambling are better protected.
in writing. - i voted in favour of regulations on online gambling. the central objective pursued must therefore be the significant reduction of this black market as well as the grey market. one of the options available to member states to achieve this objective is a total ban, which would require tough enforcement measures. member states are free to opt for this solution on the basis of the principle of subsidiarity. an open and organised online gambling market requires an independent and strong national regulatory authority, able to set the framework conditions under which gambling is to be conducted and, above all, able to enforce them. national regulatory authorities should have the necessary powers to be able to sanction any infringement and to act against illegal operators. it is worrying that the online gambling sector is growing steadily, reaching 10% of all gambling in europe, with a total market volume exceeding eur 10 billion.
in writing. − i voted for the report on online gambling in the internal market because it does not support the deregulation/liberalisation of online gambling. in order to effectively protect consumers, especially young people and vulnerable players, from the negative aspects of online gambling, the eu needs to adopt common consumer protection standards. in this regard, given the cross-border nature of the internet, there is a need for extensive cooperation between national regulatory authorities. until now, cooperation in this field between member states has taken the form of bilateral procedures only. i consider that a pan-european code of conduct in the field of online gambling is needed, which should address the rights and obligations of both the service provider and the consumer. this code of conduct should ensure responsible gambling, a high level of protection of players, in particular minors and other vulnerable persons. the code of conduct should also include support mechanisms at eu and national level to combat cybercrime, fraud and misleading advertising, as well as a set of principles and rules to ensure the uniform protection of consumers of online gambling across the eu.
in writing. − the beekeeping sector, as an economic and social activity, plays a crucial role in the sustainable development of rural areas through the creation of new jobs. beekeeping also provides an important ecosystem service through pollination, which contributes to the enhancement of biodiversity by maintaining plant genetic diversity and maintaining balance. i invite the commission to focus research on technological developments, disease prevention and control, the definition of sustainable agricultural practices, the promotion of non-chemical alternatives and the encouragement of integrated pest management techniques and the development of veterinary products against bee disease agents. member states also need to take action to mitigate the risks to bee health. research needs to be harmonised and it is very important that national authorities support the dissemination of appropriate scientific and technical knowledge on bee health among beekeepers. i voted in favour of this report. beekeeping is part of europe's agricultural heritage and national traditions and we must fight together against the decline of bee colonies across europe.
in writing. − this is not the first time we have discussed this subject in parliament, but i am glad that this time it is an own-initiative report. we know from previous debates that the number of bee colonies in the member states is declining and that we have health problems in these colonies. we have consequences in agriculture, but also in ensuring the need for honey for consumption on the european market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the measures to protect and improve the beekeeping sector, given that the existing permissive provisions on the quality of honey and the presence of organic or synthetic external components (including antibiotics) have led to an uncertain situation, as member states establish different methods of analysis of the tolerance level, which could distort competition on the internal market. uniform legislation on the permitted levels of antibiotic residues in honey and other apiculture products should be introduced in order to ensure the smooth functioning of the internal market in honey and to avoid distortion of competition between beekeepers in the various member states. normally, the minimum concentration level of these substances does not represent a danger to human health, so zero action levels (nals) or reference values (rpas) for honey should be introduced.
in writing. − as there is no representative and comparable information at european level on beehive losses, i believe it is necessary to quantify beehive losses and to implement an appropriate monitoring system common to all member states. the european commission and the member states need to complement their efforts to help bees and beekeepers survive, as the health of bee colonies is affected by numerous lethal factors and veterinary research and practice have little role in the effective prevention or control of bee diseases. i also consider it important to create national surveillance systems and harmonised standards at eu level for the collection of data on bee health to allow for informed and independent scientific monitoring and also consider independent and timely research on bee mortality to be necessary.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because beekeeping is a hugely important economic and social activity, which plays a crucial role in the sustainable development of rural areas in europe, creating jobs and providing an important service to the environment through pollination. it also contributes to the improvement of biodiversity by preserving the genetic diversity of plants, and bee colonies provide important ecological assets and food security. i believe it is important to take urgent action to protect bee health, taking into account the specific characteristics of beekeeping, the diversity of factors involved and the principle of proportionality and subsidiarity. i have supported the commission's pilot surveillance programme on bee health and i also support the establishment of the european reference hives network to monitor bee health in relation to environmental conditions and farming and beekeeping practices. last but not least, i agree that, under the new common agricultural policy in 2013, the eu should provide specific support to young beekeepers to counterbalance the unfavourable age structure in the beekeeping sector.
in writing. − beekeeping plays a crucial role in the sustainable development of rural areas and provides income, directly or indirectly, for over 600 000 citizens. the report emphasizes the need to reverse the worrying trend of increasing bee mortality and the decline in the number of beekeepers in europe, which could have a serious impact on food production. an estimated 84% of plant species and 76% of food production in europe depend on pollination by bees. therefore it needs: to increase the level of support for honeybee-health-related research on disease prevention and control, particularly the impact of environmental factors on the bee colony immune system; continuous research and development of veterinary medical products for current eu honeybee-disease-causing agents; more coordinated action at eu level with a network of national surveillance systems and harmonised standards for data collection; more flexible rules for the authorisation and availability of veterinary products for honeybees; to encourage a greater degree of information-sharing among member states, beekeepers, farmers, industry and scientists on ecotoxicological factors affecting honeybee health; adequate training for beekeepers on disease prevention, as well as for farmers on safe use of plant protection products; to boost financial aid for apiculture under the new cap after 2013
in writing. − beekeeping is often a marginal issue when we talk about agriculture in the european union. however, it provides the main or additional income for more than 600 000 citizens in the european union. this sector provides vital services to agriculture through pollination and contributes to the maintenance of biodiversity. it is estimated that 84% of plant species and 76% of food production in europe depend on bee pollination, and their economic value is much higher than the value of honey produced, estimated at eur 15 billion per year in the eu. unfortunately, in the last decade, hives have faced increased mortality from both pesticides and specific diseases. i voted for the report on bee health and apiculture drawn up by mr tabajdi because i believe that it takes account of all the problems facing european apiculture.
in writing. − services of general economic interest contribute to the economic performance and competitiveness of member states by helping to prevent and overcome economic crises. the provision of those services of general economic interest can contribute to the achievement of growth objectives, in particular in the areas of employment, education and social inclusion, and to the achievement of high productivity, employment and social cohesion. i believe that in order for social services of general economic interest to fulfil their function, they must be accessible to all citizens, regardless of income or resources. they must also be of high quality and clearly defined within a sectoral scheme. i voted in favour of this report because social services of general interest play an important role in guaranteeing the fundamental rights of citizens and contribute essentially to promoting equal opportunities.
in writing. − i voted against this report because i consider the rapporteur's approach to state aid for services of general economic interest to be inappropriate and contrary to the objective of a competitive internal market. at present, there is no single and clear definition of an sgei and, given the diversity of these in the member states, it is probably very difficult, if not impossible, to have such a definition. i think that in this area it is counterproductive to harmonise just for the sake of harmonisation, each state applying a definition according to its national specificity. in these circumstances, a horizontal directive on the subject of the sgei seems to me to be inappropriate, since it is impossible to legislate without first having a definition of the subject-matter of the legislation. the treaty (tfeu) is very clear on the applicability of the competition rules to these services, provided, of course, that the public service mission is not jeopardised. the rapporteur's proposals aim to exempt certain sgeis from the competition rules, in particular the one concerning the exemption from notification without setting a ceiling for state aid for hospitals, social housing, etc., or the one concerning the raising of the ceiling for the de minimis rule. these proposals have no objective justification and are dangerous for competition.
in writing. − i voted for the reform of the state aid rules applicable to services of general economic interest because they play a key role for the citizen and are very important for the well-being of the whole of society. in the eu, it is the national, regional and local authorities who define the services to be provided in the general public interest, which are of particular importance to all citizens, but which, without state intervention, would not be provided or would be insufficiently provided. the state intervention aims at guaranteeing access to these services for all citizens, i.e. the provision of high quality services at affordable prices for all citizens. in the context of the crisis, support for maintaining the existing, threshold-free exemptions for hospitals and social housing enterprises is encouraging, as is the commission's announcement that it intends to exempt other categories from the notification obligation for state aid received.
in writing. − i voted for the reform of eu state aid rules applicable to services of general economic interest (sgeis). these are services which, without state intervention, could not always be provided or would be provided insufficiently, and social services of general interest (ssigs) play an important role in guaranteeing fundamental rights and contributing to equal opportunities. protocol 26 on services of general interest, which is annexed to the treaty on european union and to the treaty on the functioning of the european union, underlines the importance of services of general interest. the sgei must ensure a high level of quality, safety and accessibility, equal treatment and the promotion of universal access and user rights. i voted for the reform of the eu state aid rules applicable to sgeis to ensure that the implementation and compliance with protocol 26 is facilitated. to enable the future provision of smart energy or broadband communications services, substantial investment is needed to modernise infrastructure, particularly in regions where it is lacking, in the energy, telecommunications and public transport sectors. the union shall contribute to the establishment and development of trans-european networks in the transport, telecommunications and energy sectors. it is therefore necessary that the specific services are available and accessible to all european citizens.
in writing. − poverty and social exclusion are the most important social determinants of health and living conditions. disparities between the poor and the rich in terms of adequate access to social and health services, income and welfare gaps remain key and continue to widen in certain areas. i believe that poverty is a multifaceted phenomenon and requires an integrated response, taking into account the different stages of life and different types of needs of citizens and also based on guaranteeing access to rights, resources and services to meet the basic needs of every individual. exclusion and poverty cannot be reduced without combating inequalities and discrimination or without guaranteeing the development of national economies and solidarity with the most vulnerable social classes, i.e. without a fair and adequate distribution of national wealth. i therefore urge member states to take serious steps to promote access to fundamental rights for disadvantaged groups, as extreme poverty is a violation of human rights and a serious affront to human dignity, fostering stigma and injustice.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report with all my heart. the figures are frightening: 116 million people in the union are living in poverty, a quarter of the 500 million people! the risk directly affects the rural environment, women and young people. i agree with the idea that poverty can be considered a violation of human rights. homelessness is one of the worst forms of poverty. poverty affects their health and shortens their life expectancy. i think we need the member states' actions to be coordinated by the commission in this area. member states need technical assistance. i support the report and i ask the commission to adequately fund initiatives to combat poverty and social exclusion, in particular those on early school leaving and combating child poverty.
in writing. − in the european union there are a significant number of people who are experiencing poverty, reaching 8% of the working population. according to statistics, 20 million of them are children, which significantly reduces their chances of success in life. in addition, the financial and economic crisis has further affected the situation of the most vulnerable segments of the population, whether young people, women, the elderly, migrants, people with disabilities or the roma population. as a complex phenomenon, poverty needs to be addressed in an integrated way, involving european, but also local, regional and national actors, both in the public and private spheres. it is essential that authorities take into account the different stages of life and take measures to guarantee access to resources and services for vulnerable populations. as a flagship initiative of the europe 2020 strategy, the european platform to combat poverty and social exclusion has an ambitious mission: to reduce the number of poor peruvians by 20 million in the next few years. to this end, i believe it would be useful to implement the open method of coordination so that all european citizens enjoy equal opportunities in life.
in writing. − in the european union there are over 80 million people at risk of poverty, including 20 million children and 8% of the working population. the european platform against poverty and social exclusion developed by the commission takes no account of the gender dimension of poverty and social exclusion. the commission and the member states should adopt a gender perspective to eradicate poverty and combat social exclusion and should take into account the gender dimension in national recovery plans. i call on the commission and the member states to take action to prevent the feminisation of poverty by promoting employment and entrepreneurship among women, by tackling the gender pay gap, by facilitating reconciliation between work and family responsibilities, by developing childcare facilities, by a service system for dependent persons and by promoting flexible working arrangements. combating child poverty should focus on prevention, ensuring equal access to high-quality early childhood education and care services and other child-oriented facilities through an appropriate allocation of these services and centres at regional level.
in writing. − i supported the creation of a european platform against poverty and social exclusion precisely because 22.4% of the romanian population has an income that is below the national poverty line. gdp per capita was in 2010 about 55% lower than the average gdp per capita in the european union. not only does romania, in these circumstances, allocate only 14% of gdp to social protection, while the eu average is 27% of gdp, but the purchasing power of romanians has also decreased dramatically in the last year due to the austerity measures adopted by the current government. because, for now, the measures taken by the romanian government are only destroying the foundations of the european social model, not taking into account that in the european union, social protection has reduced poverty by 38%, i believe that this platform is necessary to help countries like romania to fight poverty and social exclusion.
in writing. − i voted for the parliament's resolution on the european platform against poverty and social exclusion because, as a result of the economic and financial crisis, the quality of life of many european citizens has decreased. i voted for amendments 6 and 7, which called on member states to agree on an eu-wide target for minimum income systems and to establish minimum wages (by legislation or in collective agreements) to ensure that wages are equal to at least 60% of the average wage (national, sectoral, etc.). i voted for amendment no 8, which calls for the eu to support the introduction of minimum social and environmental standards to prevent poverty and social exclusion, in particular energy poverty and rising rents, which lead to evictions and homelessness. i voted for paragraphs 71 and 95, which reiterate parliament's call for sectoral legislative initiatives on the quality and accessibility of social services of general interest, particularly in the fields of health, education, public transport, energy, water and communications, and encourage member states respectively to ensure a minimum income based on at least 60% of the average income of each member state.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i will try to react to the most frequent questions and comments, but first i would like to thank all honourable members for a very interesting and lively debate. i believe that most of us in this room feel the same way: we are really going through the defining moment in european history. i think, judging from most of your interventions, that we have come to the same conclusions: we need more europe, not less; we need to move forward together, or risk fragmentation. how much more proof do we need of how interdependent we are in europe? therefore i think that the answer should be a stronger, more responsible union, and one which safeguards what makes us unique: the community method. our work programme for 2012 brings us closer to deeper integration of economic policies and governance in the euro area. clearly, the deepening of euro area integration must be done through the community method. i agree absolutely with mr swoboda. the commission will do everything possible to prevent a possible split in the european union. i also agree with the many speakers who said that we need to offer even more assistance and help to the countries in need. therefore, we are exploring all the possibilities we have at our disposal. we have just established a task force for greece and we are looking at other ways to help the countries with problems to absorb european funds better. i am sure that the discussions we will be having next year about how to simplify our programmes will also be very important in that respect. to return to the subject of what action we intend to take, i would like to assure you that we really do feel a sense of urgency in the commission. we know that we are in an extremely demanding and difficult situation and that urgent steps are needed. you have seen how many steps we have taken so far. i think the governance package will truly change the character of how we govern – from both the macroeconomic and the microeconomic point of view – the european union as such and member states’ economies in particular. we will be having a deep debate on this issue tomorrow with president barroso and vice-president rehn, so i will not go into further detail now. i would just like to assure all of you that we will soon be presenting you with a list of proposals and a request to fast-track them. some of them have been mentioned here in this chamber this afternoon. these are the proposals through which we believe we can guarantee growth and speedily create jobs. they relate to the single market and are oriented towards removing barriers in the market. they are focused on using new technologies, including digital technologies, to create jobs and growth. turning to the economic situation, the commission will come on 23 november with a new package, alongside the annual growth survey. it will comprise not only an analysis of the state of the economy in the european union, but also very clear and concrete country-specific recommendations concerning what the commission believes should be improved in this or that member state. here again, we will need your help to reinforce the message from the european union and support the measures which, sometimes, can only be taken at national level. in addition, we will put forward two other very important proposals in this area which are based on article 136. one will be a communication on the external representation of the euro area and the other – as promised – will be the green paper on stability bonds. we know that we need to have a very thorough look at this proposal, and you know how important that discussion will be. some of you referred to the discussion on treaty change. as you know, the president of the european council has been asked, in close collaboration with the president of the commission and the president of the eurogroup, to explore the possibility of limited treaty changes in the context of the strengthening of economic governance. an interim report, including a roadmap, will be presented in december 2011 and should offer the first orientations. as you know, the report should be finalised by march 2012. we are absolutely convinced in the commission that treaty change is not a short-term remedy for the crisis and that it has to be seen as part of the wider thrust towards reinforced economic governance. i think what is very important for this parliament is that we are also absolutely convinced that parliament should be consulted on this measure. parliament should be involved in the process of thinking about how to approach this issue, and the commission will definitely proceed in this manner. with regard to programming, i think that this is the first programme on which the european parliament and the commission have cooperated so closely. i calculate that we have had more than 80 meetings between the commissioners and the respective committees. many of them were devoted to the so-called structured dialogue, so we really see it as a common project. in response to mr szájer, we are also reflecting on the proposals we heard from the european parliament. there will be a proposal on the status of the european political parties. we will continue making progress on comitology. as has been said, on the trade area our work is done. in agri we are continuing, and we promise that this process will be completed by 2012. i believe that this will be done. some of you asked about the proposals which we promised to deliver this year. as you know, we promised to deliver 40 strategic initiatives. 23 have already been delivered to the legislator and 11 will be done before the end of the year. here i would like to assure mrs trautmann, mr őry and mr cercas that both the posting of workers directive and also the social services of general interest directive will be presented to parliament in december of this year. in the end, we aim to deliver to you 34 out of 40 promised directives. clearly, the rest need more elaboration and analysis, but i can assure you that they will be coming very soon next year. to reply to various interventions from the floor, with regard to smes, i would like to assure you that every impact assessment now contains a chapter on smes and how our policies will influence them and their ability to perform in the single market. we are very much aware of how important it is to reduce the administrative burden and, as was correctly pointed out, a 25% reduction of the administrative burden has already been delivered. the commission has delivered even more. we have delivered 31% of the proposals, and 6% of them are now in the legislative process. but legislation at european level is one thing; how it is transposed at national level is another. therefore we need the good cooperation of the national member states to actively reduce administrative burdens at national level. in response to mr duff, who asked about where we stand on the accession of the european union to the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms, i would like to briefly assure him that the commission is committed to speedy accession and that the current draft accession agreement results from technical negotiations with the council of europe. we believe that this is a well-balanced compromise text. therefore the commission would be willing to reopen this package only if absolutely necessary, to address the concerns of the two member states. the commission and the presidency are working very hard to reach a common position and to find a possible compromise so that we can conclude this process as quickly as possible. i will respond very briefly to all the various interventions on the financial transaction tax. i think that we have to be very fair about this question. what we are looking for is a fair contribution back to society from the financial industry, bearing in mind how much society has helped the financial industry. european governments had to provide eur 4.6 trillion in credit guarantees alone. i think it is a fair approach to try to look for additional revenues in the european union. should we tax labour? should we tax consumption? should we again transfer the burden to the citizens? we in the commission do not think so. therefore the legislative process will continue and we believe that, in the end, we will be able to find a good solution. apart from the revenue side, we also have to look at how healthy the regulatory effect will be, especially when we see what kind of results high-frequency trading can cause. this process will have a positive effect on this as well. lastly, on mrs grässle’s question concerning the staff regulations, i am sure that she is well aware that we are going through what i believe will be the last phases of the social dialogue. i have a conciliation meeting with staff unions planned for tomorrow afternoon and we definitely would like to present the proposal for staff regulation reforms before the end of the year. concerning the enforcement of european law, this is a very important issue and we are taking our powers very seriously. to give just one concrete example, we are taking three member states to court for failure to transpose the service directive. in this case, we are asking for financial penalties as well.
