in a time of multiple crises, it is important to finally close the debate, this time under the fourth eu presidency, and make it possible to award the title of 'european heritage' in practice. the essence of the title would reinforce our values, our sense of belonging to the eu. by recognising differences, we are also strengthening intercultural dialogue. this is particularly important for all of us to stress. by fixing the criteria for selecting sites, by extending the geographical criteria, by providing clear and simplified provisions, we are taking steps towards citizens who expect a lot from us. it is important that the intergovernmental initiative finally becomes a formal eu action. objects that can be grouped around a specific theme and that can be jointly awarded the title represent an opening to young people in comparison with other initiatives in the field of cultural heritage. these are the signs of attention that our young people need.
the decision to establish a union action on the 'european heritage label' will enhance the sense of belonging to the union of european citizens, based on common elements of history and heritage. the brand focuses on the symbolic value of sites for european integration and the history of the union. i propose that the v.a. urechia library in galatia be awarded the european heritage label. founded in 1871 and opened in 1890, the library was defined in the reports of the time as the intellectual arsenal of society, necessary for good administration. the headquarters of the v.a. urechia library was the first headquarters of the european danube commission, which began its work in 1856 in galati, to ensure free movement on the danube. 155 years after the establishment of this committee, the european council adopted the european union strategy for the danube region, in recognition of the importance of the danube region for the history, present, future and cohesion of the union. v.a. urechia said that the strongest city is the one where the citizens defend themselves with learning, with science. the city of european culture, the urechia library in galatia, is worthy of the european heritage label.
the 'european heritage label' will support the assumption of belonging to the common cultural space of our continent. european principles and history, as well as mutual understanding, are among the elements that add value to the union. the brand initiative focuses on promoting the designated sites, disseminating information and increasing accessibility to the public. we thus acknowledge that the project did not receive the visibility it deserved in the intergovernmental phase. i welcome the agreement reached with the council, in particular the simplification and clarification of the transitional procedures. the issue of transnational sites also seems to me to be significant for the process of european construction. however, i think we should consider in the future opening up access to this project to european countries that are not yet part of the union and they cite as an argument a symbolic eu initiative: the designation of sibiu as european capital of culture when romania's accession to the union was uncertain. this designation was a real european success. the 'european heritage label' will undoubtedly raise awareness among our citizens of the diversity of our common history and boost cultural tourism. congratulations to your colleague paliadeli, congratulations to the commissioner.
i should like to begin by welcoming the debate on this detailed report by mrs paliadeli. i would stress that the 'european heritage label' is complementary to other similar programmes such as the unesco world heritage list. the mechanism supports the exchange of good practices between sites in order to improve the information and communication component. the 'european heritage label' also ensures the harmonisation of environmental protection measures in the areas where cultural sites are located. it is important to include in the programme the historical monuments of the union around which europe has been created today. the promotion of sites with a cross-border dimension is welcome. at the regional level, they have been the foundation of the european construction. romania was among the 15 countries that initiated this project in 2007, and the romanian athenaeum in bucharest was on the first list of recipients of the distinction.
in writing. the european cultural heritage label is an initiative that i particularly appreciate, especially in the current context, when the european union has divergent rather than convergent tendencies. that is why i believe that we are discussing this proposal, which is already at second reading, at the appropriate time when it can really add value to the idea of a united europe. based on a successful intergovernmental initiative, the heritage label is well placed to continue in the same vein when it becomes a community programme. in addition, it benefits from the experience gained through other similar programmes, most notably the european capital of culture, which has an undeniable scale. although i disagreed with the rapporteur at first reading on the scope of this initiative and insisted that the eu's neighbouring states should be included in order to promote transnational eu-non-eu sites, i am now convinced that it is better to take things step by step. and if we have remarkable results at union level, we can think in the coming years about extending this programme to non-member countries.
in writing. the european union is founded on a number of important principles that most european citizens know. for these principles to work in practice, it is also important to know each other from different european nations. i would like to remind you of the success of other programmes with similar objectives, such as the european capitals of culture programme (the city i represent, cluj-napoca, is a candidate to become the european capital of culture in 2020). based on the experiences of these programmes, we can be confident that the 'european heritage label' will also be a successful initiative.

in writing. − on 5 october 2011, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) in favour of ireland, to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis. the application concerns 4 866 redundancies in 1 482 undertakings located in two neighbouring regions which together constitute the whole of the irish state. almost 80% of the enterprises are located in the southern and eastern region, while the remaining 20% are located in the border, midlands and western region. the redundancies occurred during the nine-month reference period from 1 july 2009 to 31 march 2010. following the economic and financial crisis and the closure of many smes in the construction sector, which had enjoyed steady growth for a decade, the unemployment rate in this sector increased sharply by 19% in 2009-2010. ireland's economy is also export-oriented, which has resulted in a credit crunch which has in turn severely affected the mortgage lending market and thus the construction sector. that is why we support the mobilisation of the egf to support irish workers who have been made redundant, to help them reintegrate into the labour market.

in writing. − the european heritage label seeks to enhance the value and profile of sites that have played a key role in the history and construction of the european union, so that european citizens have a better understanding of european construction and the common cultural heritage. the distance separating the european union from its citizens is largely due to a lack of knowledge about europe's history, its role and the values on which it is based. the european heritage label thus aims to contribute to bringing european citizens closer together and to reinforcing the sense of european identity by improving knowledge of the common history and common european heritage, especially among young people. the involvement of the european union in the european heritage label will strengthen coordination between member states and contribute to the development and proper application of common, clear and transparent selection criteria and new selection and monitoring procedures for the label, thus ensuring the relevance of sites to the objectives.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a decision establishing a european union action on the european heritage label. the objective of the proposal is to enhance the sense of belonging to the european union among european citizens, based on the common elements of history and heritage, as well as to value diversity and to deepen intercultural dialogue. the brand does not focus on the beauty or architectural quality of the sites, but rather on their symbolic value for european integration and the history of the union, and on the activities they can offer and their educational dimension, especially for young people. the proposal introduces common, clear and transparent criteria for the european heritage label, which will be applied by all participating member states. the selection and monitoring procedures will ensure that only the most relevant sites are awarded the label and that those that no longer meet the necessary criteria are stripped of it. each member state may pre-select up to two sites every two years, both national and transnational. a jury of independent experts will select at most one site per country that is acceptable for the brand. the first selection will take place in 2012 and we want the new member states to participate as much as possible.
in writing. − one of the main causes of railway stagnation is the many discrepancies between the existing rules at national level. the type of regulation is far too varied to be positive for the rail sector. this problem is exacerbated by the poor implementation of the first railway package by member states. following the parliament's resolution on this issue of 11 june 2010, the commission referred 13 member states to the court of justice of the european union 'for failure to correctly implement the first railway package'. the numerous infringement procedures under union law clearly demonstrate the need to clarify and improve the legislation. another concern is the lack of investment by member states in infrastructure, the quality of which is largely at the heart of the sector's competitiveness. many member states have neglected rail financing, giving all their support to road infrastructure. the reform should contribute to the achievement of a european railway area. the current reform should go beyond the boundaries of nationally defined interests in the railway sector. the time has come to build a true european railway area where passengers and goods can easily cross borders.
in writing. − reform of the single european railway area is necessary because the sector has been in steady decline for years, while road transport of passengers and goods has increased, leading to congestion and environmental degradation. unfortunately, the objectives of the 2001 railway package have been missed, so measures are needed to make the sector more attractive compared to other modes of transport. rail freight - now at 10% while road freight has increased to 45.9% - has potential for growth and can play a key role in the eu's achievement of its goals of a more sustainable and greener transport system for europe. to this end, measures are needed to mitigate the many discrepancies between existing national rules and to remedy the underfunding of the railway sector in the absence of member states' investments in infrastructure. i also believe that, in order to enhance safety, compliance with safety standards should be a key precondition for applying for a licence.
in writing. − rail transport has not been able to develop as well as other modes of transport for various reasons. international rail transport, in particular freight, has declined in recent years, due to the fact that transnational rail services face numerous technical, legal and political obstacles. i believe that rail transport can play a key role in meeting the community's co2 reduction targets and can be very cost-effective. as a sustainable and environmentally friendly transport system for europe, the commission must give railway transport a greater role and must make every effort to eliminate the many discrepancies between existing rules at national level.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive on the establishment of the single european railway area. the main aspects of the proposal adopted are: transparent market conditions for the relevant rail services; ensuring strict separation of the accounts of the infrastructure manager and the railway undertakings; compliance by operators and undertakings with social and health protection legislation in order to avoid social dumping and unfair competition. the commission is to present by 31 december 2012 a proposal for a directive containing provisions on the separation of infrastructure management operations and transport operations. i voted for amendment 125 which calls for the abolition of compulsory service in case of strike and for amendments 51 and 52. they require the infrastructure manager to manage its own it services to ensure that commercially sensitive information is adequately protected. member states shall ensure that both railway undertakings and infrastructure managers, which are not fully independent of each other, are responsible for their own staff policies. we call on the commission to monitor the use of networks and the development of framework conditions in the railway sector, in particular infrastructure charging, railway infrastructure investment, price developments, the quality of rail transport services, employment conditions and social conditions.

in writing. − i voted for the resolution on european cinema in the digital age because i believe that the digital age creates new opportunities for the audiovisual sector, especially in the film industry. this ensures increased efficiency in the distribution, screening and availability of films, as well as better audio and video quality offered to european audiences. i voted for paragraph 92 which calls on the member states to include film education in their national education programmes. although european cinema provided more than 30 000 jobs in 2010 and almost one billion cinema tickets were sold in the eu, there is a geographical imbalance in europe in terms of the accessibility of cinemas and films to citizens, with the imbalance being more pronounced in eastern europe and in rural areas. the digitisation of the european film industry and its cinemas must be supported at european and national level in order to avoid limiting access to cultural diversity and availability. i support the need to standardise systems based on iso standards in the areas of film production, distribution and projection and to ensure the interoperability of digital projection systems and materials, as well as other devices. the development of digital cinema requires respect for intellectual property and related rights in the information society.
madam president, the european union’s relations with the united states of america are one of the most important stabilising factors at global level. although there have been some negative aspects to go with the positive ones, these relations are stable and based on a fundamental set of values which are becoming universal. it would be unrealistic to say that these relations have not been affected by the economic crisis. our position differs from theirs on certain aspects of the crisis, because its effects have been different on the two sides of the atlantic, but i hope that these natural differences will not endanger our good relations. it would be unproductive to reduce these transatlantic relations to just the economic dimension; both the eu and us are engaged in management processes such as globalisation and sustainable development, combating the effects of climate change, maintaining global stability and promoting democratisation all over the world. we need to support the development of free and open democracies and promote peace and stability, especially in the middle eastern and north african countries. we also need to make substantial efforts to finally find a sustainable solution to the palestinian issue. we also need to cooperate more closely to solve the iranian nuclear file and to radically change the human rights situation in iran and syria. as vice-chair of the development committee, i consider that urgent coordinating measures are needed in order to provide the necessary funds for continuation of the existing programmes in the poorest countries of africa and central america in particular. we are the world’s biggest donors, and this dialogue is very important from this point of view.
madam president, the current financial crisis is by far the gravest challenge we face in common. we are being challenged both separately – europe in its very integration, the us in its world-leading role – but most importantly together as the west. however, given the complexity of our relations, we need a more strategic dialogue, educating the new elites on both sides of the atlantic on our common stakes regarding primarily the current financial crisis, the middle east, the revolutions in the arab world, afghanistan and pakistan, iran as well as the bric countries. in security terms, due to the absence of major threats to europe and the shift of us attention towards the pacific, we run the risk of a diminished us participation in ensuring the security of our continent. to avoid it, one needs to increase, not decrease our own defence efforts in both the un and nato and address the potential negative impact of decision-making fragmentation.

acting president of the council. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the european parliament is not a party to the treaty. first of all, i would like to thank both committees and the two chairmen, mr reul and mr harbour, for their questions. it is very important that we can discuss today the 2009 telecommunications package, and in particular the very important issue of the open internet and the principle of net neutrality. these issues are extremely important, especially in our time, when the internet and all the information and communication tools are the engine of our economy and may be one of the tools that will help europe and even the whole world out of the crisis. the success of the internet, in my view, is the success of the openness and the ability to use it in a simple, accessible and clear way for every citizen. that is why this discussion is, in my view, as president-in-office of the council, extremely important. as regards the first part of the question relating to the assessment of the implementation of this package in the member states, i would first like to point out that we are all aware that since the adoption of the new eu telecoms rules in november 2009, national regulatory authorities have been required to promote access to information and the use of applications and services of their choice among end-users. these opportunities shall be promoted by supporting the requirements for transparency of information to the subscriber. in addition, national regulatory authorities are also granted a very important right to set minimum quality of service requirements. member states shall recognise the importance of effectively implementing those requirements while preserving the open nature of the internet and ensuring a generally accessible stable internet. member states are also aware of some concerns about discriminatory forms of data management and handling, price transparency and quality of service, both online and in terms of personal data protection. states therefore emphasise the importance of providing consumers with transparent information so that everyone can make an informed choice about the offer they choose, whether limited or otherwise, in full the consumer must, however, be aware of the offer that is made to him, and stress the need to address issues of discrimination and degradation of service quality that may result from certain traffic management practices. in this context, the council underlines the important role of berec and the european commission, together with the national regulatory authorities, in analysing the market and assessing the compliance of operators with the provisions of the regulatory framework. what's happened so far? we are aware, of course, that not all member states have implemented the package yet. we must remember that these are several comprehensive directives that require in-depth analysis, and these implementation processes are nearing completion in each member state. the introduction of net neutrality and all the requirements related to transparency have already generated a great deal of debate in the member states. such debates have taken place in poland, for example, or in france. the debate with market participants and with the participants in the internet chain, i.e. telecommunications operators, content providers and individual market participants, means that we will also be able to discuss partial self-regulation, which is very important. so these regulations are already in effect. as regards the second part of the question, i would point out that the council, recognising the need for a uniform approach to this issue, prepared its conclusions for the commission's communication on the open internet and net neutrality. therefore, at the next council of ministers on 13 december, we will adopt such council conclusions and i think this will provide a common and linked to the provisions of the amended regulatory framework approach to this subject. the council welcomes the commission's commitment to monitor the processes of implementation of the union regulatory framework and its readiness to further analyse these aspects of net neutrality, which present significant and persistent problems, and encourages the commission and berec to monitor current practices in order to eliminate instances of traffic mismanagement. where traffic management is already in place, it should be done in a manner that respects proportionality, transparency, ensures uninterrupted flow and guarantees price transparency and quality of service requirements in a form that does not affect network neutrality. in its conclusions, the council endorses the commission's intention to assess, on the basis of the data from the berec study, the need to publish additional guidance or to adopt further regulations. if the need arises, such documents will be prepared and the council will deal with them in accordance with its legislative powers. sorry i was late. thank you very much. thank you.
member of the commission. − madam president, i am pleased to be here to respond on behalf of the commission in the absence of neelie kroes, who has had to go to warsaw. open internet is an issue that affects every one of us and is increasingly an economic essential. the commission has stressed on several occasions the importance of having an open internet, accessible to everyone, from the innovators who provide content, to those who use it. the commission thinks that the best way to deliver an open internet is through competitive markets. but for competition to work properly, consumers need to make informed choices, and to know exactly what service they are getting. they also need to be able to switch operators easily and quickly. the new telecoms rules approved in 2009 specifically require operators to be transparent about the service they offer and the traffic management techniques they apply. they also help their consumers to switch operator, in particular by improving number portability procedures and conditions for contract subscription and termination. if needed, they empower national regulators to set minimum quality of service requirements. these rules, which had to be implemented by may this year, have not yet been fully transposed in all member states. the commission is vigilantly monitoring their implementation. this will allow us to ensure that open and neutral internet principles are respected in practice. in addition, the commission has asked the body of european regulators for electronic communications (berec), in which all the member states’ telecoms regulators are represented, to undertake a rigorous fact-finding exercise on these issues, including barriers to changing operators, blocking or throttling of internet traffic, voice over internet services, transparency and quality of service. we need to know what the situation is: whether customers really do know what service they are signing up to, whether throttling and blocking are really common practices and what the impact is on the service quality delivered to the end-user. we also want to make sure that consumers can switch providers easily, if they do not like the service they are getting. in parallel, berec is working on guidance and transparency. it is working on a framework for net neutrality and quality of service, which looks specifically into how to use minimum quality of service requirements as specified in article 22 (3) of the universal service directive. it is also working on the competition issues relating to net neutrality. building on berec’s and any industry’s inputs and based on its own analysis, the commission will decide whether additional guidance or more stringent measures regarding open internet and net neutrality are necessary – and by the way, as the council has rightly stated, we will make public berec’s findings. it is very important that we have the facts and figures before acting. if we do need to act, we must do so in a coordinated way across europe. i would therefore urge national regulators to collaborate with their peers and the commission when considering regulatory action in this area, and to act on the basis of facts. at this stage, i cannot yet tell members yet whether the commission will develop additional guidance or general legislative measures to enhance competition and consumer choice, such as by further facilitating consumer switching. however, we are very confident we will receive all the necessary input to make an informed decision. the house can be sure that any proposal in this area will be subject to an in-depth assessment of their impact, including on fundamental rights. much is at stake in the area of open internet and net neutrality. the commission wants to make sure that sound policy initiatives are developed that help deliver the objectives of the digital agenda for europe.
on behalf of the alde group. – madam president, without a shadow of doubt, the internet has radically changed our societies and our lives and has been a driver for competitiveness, innovation and economic growth in europe over the past years. it has boosted cross-border trade through e-commerce, contributing to the development of the internal market, and it has allowed for the development of online services to the benefit of european consumers. what we have achieved so far has been possible to a large extent thanks to the openness of the internet. we should continue on this path and take all necessary measures to preserve the open internet, which will help us further develop the digital single market. of course, traffic management is necessary in order to be able to provide an adequate quality for different services. but this should not be a pretext for anti-competitive practices such as blocking, throttling and so on. we have all witnessed cases where mobile voice-through-ip services have been blocked. i therefore call on the commission, berec and the national regulatory authorities (nras) to closely monitor traffic management measures, especially for mobile internet, and take the necessary measures where anti-competitive behaviour is proved. in my view, the revised telecoms framework agreed in 2009 provides the necessary safeguards against such anti-competitive practices, but we probably need more active nras, which use their prerogatives to set minimum quality-of-service requirements. potential abuse in traffic management can be harmful to competition and can also affect freedom of expression and the freedom to conduct business, which are of the utmost importance. consumers should also be more effectively protected against misleading advertising, namely on the speed of the internet. i believe that some additional guidelines from the commission on these questions could help member states to better apply eu legislation and would enable consumers and businesses to profit from the open internet.
the open internet and net neutrality in europe are priorities for the achievement of the digital single market. the internet should provide high quality services in a framework that promotes and respects fundamental rights. we call on the commission to ensure that internet service providers do not block, discriminate against, impede or reduce a person's ability to use a service, to access, use, send, publish, receive or offer any lawful content, application or service that they want, regardless of the source or target. we ask the commission to provide parliament with data on current traffic management practices, the interconnection market and network congestion. we call on the commission to closely monitor the adoption of any national regulations on net neutrality, their effects on the internal market and on national markets. we consider that effective competition of electronic communications services, transparency of traffic management and quality of service, as well as the possibility of switching easily between providers, are minimum conditions necessary for net neutrality.
mr president, the european parliament can today show its leadership in promoting human rights and entrepreneurship both in europe and worldwide. net neutrality is about freedom of speech, freedom to access and share information and freedom of choice for consumers. the internet governs our lives, whether we are talking about individuals, about companies or about institutions. we need a rich content of information and to facilitate access to information which could improve our lives and lead to concrete economic growth. however, we also need to protect our citizens and institutions from misuses of the internet, like cyber attacks, which could lead to dangerous effects on society. we have to keep the balance between protection and censorship, and at the same time to ensure that as much information as possible is accessible via the internet, in order to develop our society.
the principle of net neutrality is fundamental to the preservation of the internet's innovative character, free competition and respect for human rights. we need to have a neutral, european, not national, internet that allows users to have no conditions limiting access to applications or services. transparency, quality of service, elimination of misleading advertising and the possibility for consumers to change their internet provider must be supported and enhanced in order to protect neutrality and citizens' rights. in some member states, such as romania, there is a strong regional discrepancy in internet access. many areas are not covered by providers, and those that are often do not provide quality services. we need to consider regional cohesion at european level on internet access, because there is a high risk of creating ... author. − mr president, first of all please allow me to welcome the presence of commissioner vassiliou in this plenary, although the topic we are talking about today is not within her mandate. you will see that there are good reasons for me to mention this. for quite some time we have been waiting for the european commission to prove that roma integration is not just a trendy word but a policy we are genuinely committed to. providing money is one aspect; important but not enough. we have been waiting in vain for the commission to demonstrate full respect for fundamental rights, as enshrined in the eu treaties and the charter of fundamental rights, in relation to roma evictions and expulsions from france. the beauty of being in europe is that the council of europe also exists and its european committee for social rights, in the decision taken in june this year, considered the french measures ‘incompatible with human dignity’ and ‘an aggravated violation of human rights’. it also stated that such violations represent a threat to the ‘shared fundamental standards of all the council of europe’s member states, namely those of human rights, democracy and the rule of law’. how was it possible for the european commission not to see this, since respect for human dignity represents the foundation of the european union? the french constitutional council saw it in its decision of march. the french conseil d’etat noted it in its judgment of april this year and stated that the french authorities did not have the right, in contravention of the principle of equality before the law, to implement the policy of evacuating unlawful settlements by designating their occupants on the basis of ethnic origin. our european commission did not see the discriminatory behaviour of the french authorities, thus allowing the french government to defend its actions invoking not the french constitutional council, nor the conseil d’etat, but the european commission’s conclusions that the evictions and expulsions were compatible with european law. what an embarrassment!
roma communities in europe today face specific challenges that require enormous efforts from the union, the member states and roma communities themselves. unemployment, lack of education and skills in the labour market, and the associated discrimination and social exclusion, are also affecting the future of roma in europe. we can fight discrimination against them by eliminating all the unfortunate situations in the union, such as the denial by some member states of the existence of minorities in their territory, and even the existence of collective criminal laws against minorities in some member states. but that's not enough. programmes that contribute to the social inclusion of roma communities should also be funded. this can be achieved by promoting education and access to the labour market. although the primary responsibility lies with the member states with a large roma population, the problem is common. the future of europe as a whole depends on the path we take now towards roma integration. i sincerely hope that in a decade, we will be able to talk about significant successes in this area, and the changes will be measurable not just in statistical indicators, but in the daily lives of local communities.
with this debate, we are sending a strong message to the member states, just one month before they present their own strategy to the european commission. i would like to point out that the romanian government has made significant progress in developing a national strategy for roma inclusion. in the six sectoral areas, the responsible ministries of labour, education, regional development, economy, agriculture, health, culture and home affairs together with local authorities will take some 63 well-defined measures. i would like to stress that the funding will be provided from the budget of each ministry, there will be no budget of the strategy itself. the implementation and monitoring of the programme will be coordinated by the deputy prime minister, the general secretariat of the government and the national agency for roma. we are all aware of the problems facing the roma. but romania's responsibility is even greater, with the largest roma minority in europe. but how they're represented matters. that is why i would perhaps recommend that, in the next european parliament elections, political parties offer an eligible seat to a roma citizen. commissioner, i would like to believe that this strategy will be successful throughout the union, but given the populist and profoundly un-european reaction of some governments to the question of romania and bulgaria joining the schengen area, i have reservations.
the recent violence against the roma minority proves what i have been saying since before the eu roma strategy was adopted, that it will remain a declaration of good intentions unless it is implemented correctly and effectively. simply adopting a non-binding strategy at european level is not effective. this is evidenced by the fact that most member states have not yet established a national roma inclusion strategy. some member states are not even considering adopting a strategy. the european commission must urgently oblige them to do so and not wait until the end of the year. it is time to put the issue of roma integration back on the european agenda, at the highest level. i therefore believe that all these european 'task forces' mentioned by the commissioner here must also deal with the roma problem in particular, and not in addition. the presidents of the commission, the european parliament and the european council should also be involved in these 'task forces'. these roma 'task forces' should ensure real coordination between actors at european and national level and the participation of local authorities and roma communities as the main drivers in the effective implementation of the strategy. we can no longer afford to treat half-heartedly this profound and shameful issue of the situation of the roma ethnic group in the european union. it is time to move from words to deeds, otherwise we risk the european union losing its credibility for good.
there are still large economic and social disparities between the different regions of the european union and a significant proportion of the roma community lives in regions that are among the least economically and socially advanced in the european union. the structural funds are the main source of reducing economic and social disparities and i consider their use for roma integration to be extremely significant. these funds can help improve infrastructure in poor communities, most often inhabited by roma. i therefore believe that the commission should subsequently ask the member states to ensure, through the operational programmes which will be made available to them for the next programming period, synergy with national roma integration strategies, thus ensuring the improvement of roma's lives.
in writing. the european union has to face the reality of the roma community, a reality dictated by the economic situation of roma in general, but especially by aspects related to the nomadic lifestyle and low level of education. the main problem facing the roma population is the low level of education and, by extension, the lack of vocational qualifications. education is an opportunity to obtain a qualification, a profession and a job, which are mandatory conditions for roma social integration. i think this is the main issue that national strategies have to address. the national approach is not sufficient. education programmes must also have a cross-border approach in order to influence the part of the roma population that has remained faithful to its nomadic traditions. the member states of origin have the greatest role to play in the process of roma integration, but the eu also has a very important role to play. framework programmes should be developed and applied in a similar way in all member states. coordination between national roma contact points is essential. the exchange of information is also extremely important. projects and measures that have achieved positive results in one member state must be adopted and multiplied in the other member states.
in writing. – the eu framework missed an opportunity to call for the elimination, not just of school segregation but of inappropriate placement of roma children in special schools, to help reduce the gap in educational achievement between roma and other eu citizens at secondary and tertiary levels. promotion graduation of roma at university level is crucial to empower roma. roma youth will be in a much more effective position to achieve social inclusion if they have good education. the significant participation of roma professionals in formulating an implementing roma policy is essential to their success. the epsco conclusions included this essential element, but inclusion is not possible without participation. while robust monitoring is outlined in the framework, the mechanisms to ensure it need to be further developed. effective monitoring would be easier if the role of the national contact points on roma were clearer. in the eu framework, these contact points are given a coordination and development role but the epsco conclusions only refer to a monitoring role. the solution would be for another independent commission to undertake the evaluation. experience in some eastern european countries has shown that if the same body implements, monitors and develops policy; poor policy implementation is likely to result.
in writing. we've been talking about a roma strategy for years. this year it was finally adopted, but in some member states their situation remains critical. the situation of the largest ethnic minority in the european union is still characterised by discrimination and social exclusion, poverty, unemployment and prejudice. more seriously, roma european citizens are being denied the freedoms and rights guaranteed to union citizens by the treaties. they continue to be exploited without appeal and treated as second-class citizens. sadly, at times even the media contributes to the stigmatization of these people and to the prejudice that is already deeply rooted in many people's consciences. more involvement is needed from both the european commission and the member states' authorities and roma community leaders to really improve their situation. in conclusion, i would like to ask the commission to ensure that the fundamental rights of european citizens are respected, regardless of ethnicity.
in writing. a viable digital single market could improve competitiveness and boost economic growth in the eu. this is essential for the development of european small and medium-sized enterprises. trust in electronic transactions needs to be strengthened. currently, only 54% of european internet users buy or sell goods on the virtual marketplace. at the same time, e-commerce has a supporting role for cross-border trade. the removal of all barriers to the use of electronic commerce is important. in particular, fiscal obstacles must be removed. it is necessary to avoid discrimination between the provision of electronic services and the provision of goods. for example, the same vat rate should be applied to both printed and electronic books. my country ranks 10th in the world in terms of quality of internet connection-access ratio. a number of projects to cover the broadband white areas are to be launched, for which eur 84 million of european funding will be allocated.
on behalf of the alde group. – madam president, despite diverging views political groups might have about nuclear technology, it is good to see there is a wide convergence and agreement in this parliament on the need to continue investing in nuclear research and development. it is worrying to see the decreasing interest of science students in nuclear engineering. do we really think we can afford to disregard our nuclear needs in energy consumption, in medical applications and in nuclear safety with the managed decommissioning and dismantling of nuclear power stations for the decades to come? unfortunately, contrary to what some populists would have us believe, in the case of nuclear energy you cannot decide to just switch off the power and hope that all related problems magically disappear. we will need more scientists and engineers to deal with the challenges posed by nuclear power, but also to make the most of the opportunities it offers for growth, innovation, health and many other applications. that is why we must dedicate more investment to training and we must change public perception to attract students and encourage scientific careers and excellence in this field. in research, one always invests without knowing if and when the scientific breakthrough will be made. as regards the iter project, we either say we have already spent too much money – and if we decided to stop it here it would be lost – or we continue investing and keep the faith. i believe the last option is the one we should take. however, i do not agree that this project should continue to get massive financial injections without ensuring any kind of democratic control. now, parliament is required to agree on additional funding of eur 1.3 billion over two years without knowing how these funds will be spent. i believe the minimum we should demand is to be regularly informed and updated on the construction progress and have access to internal audit documents. in addition, we must make sure that such a cost explosion does not occur in the future and have it ring-fenced in the next multiannual financial framework. lastly, the commission will soon make its proposal on the modernisation of public procurement, and i believe that proper and transparent public procurement should also be a part of a european nuclear safety policy because corruption and mismanagement in building nuclear power plants could have unimaginable – or imaginable – consequences. i hope the commission will take this aspect into consideration when drafting that proposal.
i welcome the proposal for a council decision on the framework programme of the european atomic energy community for nuclear research and training activities and i congratulate the rapporteur, mr březina. in view of the possible cross-border impact of nuclear incidents, enhancing nuclear safety and, where appropriate, safety aspects should be a priority. the general objectives of the 2012-13 framework programme place particular emphasis on nuclear safety, improving nuclear waste management, safety and radiation protection and contribute to the creation of the innovation union and the construction of the european research area. the work programmes of the projects will also include standardisation activities. i believe it is essential that a high level of qualification and appropriate working conditions in the nuclear field be maintained within the community. particular attention shall be paid to initiatives accompanying core nuclear research activities, in particular with regard to investments in human capital and appropriate working conditions and actions aimed at addressing the risk of skills shortages in the coming years. member states should review professional qualifications, training and competences in the nuclear field within the union in order to provide an overview of the current situation and to enable the identification and application of appropriate solutions. continued support for the retention and training of staff is also necessary to maintain the union's nuclear independence and a constant level of nuclear safety provision and improvement. it is essential to maintain expertise in the union in radiation protection and dismantling of nuclear installations, as nuclear energy will play a key role in the union's energy mix, including in decommissioning and long-term waste management. in decommissioning obsolete systems, particular attention should be paid to long-lived nuclear waste.
i would first like to congratulate mr březina on this very technical and important report for europe at a time when the future of nuclear energy is closely linked to the guarantees we can give to citizens that this energy is safe for all citizens, whether their country has such plants or not. i say this because, after the accident in japan, nuclear safety and security has become an even greater priority, given the possible transboundary impact of possible nuclear incidents. i also believe that it is essential that the union pays particular attention to human capital initiatives, because young people who will take over the reins need time to train for the appropriate specialisation. a reassessment of nuclear specific vocational qualification programmes, training and competences within the union is important. we must avoid a skills gap, whether in the nuclear industry or in medicine, which is no less important for european citizens and, above all, for their health. the professional experience of those at the end of their careers is important in this area, as they can pass on the knowledge acquired during their years of work. last but not least, it is important to find the most appropriate solutions for the safest possible management of long-lived radioactive waste, and here research has a key role to play, which is why the union must provide the necessary funding.
nuclear energy will play a strategic role in europe's energy mix for at least another half century. in this context, the creation of a new high-technology sector in the field of fusion energy is essential. europe needs secure, sustainable, green and viable energy. at the same time, the safety and efficiency of the use of nuclear resources need to be strengthened. ensuring long-term waste management solutions is of utmost importance. the union should allocate sufficient financial resources to achieve these objectives. the largest low-temperature laboratory in europe for specific technological applications will be created in romania. funded by european funds, the râmnicu vâlcea laboratory will contribute to the construction of the first nuclear fusion reactor at cadarache.

i would like to highlight an issue that has not yet been clarified in relation to the future of the european integrated maritime policy. it is necessary that the black sea finds its own place in this policy to be treated in the same way as other basins. there should be a black sea fisheries management body, different from the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean. i believe that the european union must make every possible diplomatic effort to bring the non-eu black sea states as close as possible to the principles of our common fisheries policy, which is not only in the interest of the black sea member states of the european union but also in the interest of the union.
in view of technological developments and the investment required in the european union's space policy, i would like to stress the important role that the use of satellite navigation systems plays in monitoring, controlling and supervising fishing activities. romania and bulgaria became members of the european union in 2007, which extended the common fisheries policy to the black sea. unfortunately, apart from bilateral agreements, there is no global agreement on the regional management of fish stocks in the black sea. the commission's support is needed to develop the regional dialogue with a view to developing a common marine strategy in the black sea area, involving the other black sea littoral states. it considers it appropriate to set up a black sea advisory council as a form of communication and technical cooperation between fisheries stakeholders. if a basic sharing agreement continues to remain in abeyance, there is a risk of resource collapse and the economic damage that has already occurred in the case of fishing for certain resources will spread widely.

first of all, i think that cluster munitions should be banned, not because they have any value during the conflict, but because they are a source of illegal arms trafficking post-conflict. in my opinion, apart from the position of my country, romania, which - as ms băsescu said - has not signed this convention, i believe that the ottawa convention should be ratified by all european states. it is a ratification of principle, because this process of giving up the dispersion ammunition and replacing it with weapons that can be milder if it can be admitted that a weapon used in a war can be milder it is necessary to be carried out. but we too believe that this recommendation has only the power to stimulate the negotiations taking place within the un and, in this context, i have agreed to abstain from voting on this resolution.

in writing. − the international criminal court is currently going through a difficult time, due to political and financial circumstances beyond its control. she is increasingly unjustly attacked for political reasons, her arrest warrants are often ignored, and her current budget is not up to the task. as the eu has been and continues to be a strong supporter of the icc, there is a need for the union to assist the court more in facing challenges and difficulties of both political and financial nature. no one can deny the importance of such an international court that investigates serious cases of human rights violations, genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes. it is therefore important that more and more states recognize the authority of the international criminal court. it took 83 years to reach an international agreement and establish the icc. now, the states that have ratified the rome statute of the icc must also regulate the court's right to investigate crimes of aggression. the signatory states must bring their national legislation into line with the provisions of the rome statute, as they have undertaken to do.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on eu support to the icc for the continued provision of financial and logistical assistance to the court and for the extension of support to the court through political and diplomatic actions. it is worrying that most of the icc's 17 arrest warrants have not yet been executed, ensuring impunity and perpetuating brutal human rights violations. it is also essential for the strengthening of the role of the icc that eu member states which have not yet done so should enshrine cooperation with the icc in their national legislation and conclude framework agreements with it for the enforcement of the court's judgments.
in writing. − i consider it important and necessary to develop an integrated maritime policy at european level so that europe's maritime, coastal and outermost areas benefit from sound economic development, ecological protection and environmental protection. i strongly support the promotion of an integrated maritime policy at community level and attach great importance to the harmonious development of a european maritime area. i also believe that both regional cooperation and the exchange of good practice are very good tools for achieving the objectives of this policy. the european union and the member states concerned need to promote their policy of leading in international maritime affairs, as this allows for better international management of maritime affairs, as well as the achievement of the union's priorities. this is extremely important, given the global nature of the problems facing the maritime sector, in order to prepare joint projects.
in writing. − integrated maritime policy promotes a sectoral approach to maritime governance, promoting the identification and exploitation of synergies between all eu policies relating to the seas, oceans and coastal regions. we need to continue to develop maritime coordination and i believe that we need to implement rapidly strategies for europe's sea basins, adapted to the needs of each coastal region. i also believe that to achieve tangible results at eu level, we need to promote better the international dimension of the integrated maritime policy. this can be achieved by improving and stimulating dialogue, cooperation and coordination with third countries and, in particular, those bordering a european sea basin.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation establishing a programme to support the further development of an integrated maritime policy. i voted that, under the growth, jobs and innovation objective, the programme should promote initiatives for growth and employment in the maritime sector, support training, education and career opportunities in maritime professions such as the training of those responsible for ships and maritime transport, support actions to make maritime professions more attractive and encourage the mobility of young people in maritime sectors. we support encouraging research, development and promotion of green technologies, marine renewable energy sources, and green shipping, as well as supporting measures to develop and promote a strategy for coastal, maritime and island tourism. i voted for the amendment which calls for funding for various objectives to include: integrated maritime governance and activities related to sea basins, the tools for developing an integrated maritime policy, promoting the international dimension of the integrated maritime policy and the visibility of europe's maritime profile, defining the limits of sustainability with regard to maritime activities through the adoption of the marine strategy framework directive, as well as sustainable economic growth, job creation and innovation.

in writing. − maintaining the open and neutral character of the internet as the main driver of innovation and consumer demand is essential. the commission must ensure that internet service providers do not block, discriminate against, impede or reduce the ability of any person to use a service and to access, use, send, publish, receive or offer any content, application or service that they want, regardless of the source or target, the text says. the equal treatment of data traffic on the internet (video, audio or text) is known as net neutrality. eu guidelines are needed to ensure the proper and consistent implementation of the provisions of the telecommunications package on network neutrality. the potential for anti-competitive and discriminatory behaviour in traffic management, especially on the part of vertically integrated undertakings, is worth highlighting. the european executive needs to assess the need for further regulatory measures to ensure freedom of expression, freedom of access to information and freedom of choice for consumers and media pluralism. the commission, together with the body of european regulators for electronic communications and in cooperation with the member states, should monitor the development of traffic management practices and interconnection contracts.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the principle of net neutrality is fundamental to the preservation of the innovative nature of the internet, free competition and respect for human rights. in europe we need to have an internet neutral, which allows users to have no conditions limiting access to applications or services. it should also allow anyone developing an application on the internet not to be subject to decisions by internet service providers (isps). i consider that providers of electronic communications networks and providers of internet access services should not impede or delay traffic on their networks, except in certain cases where this is necessary, such as to implement a legal obligation to do so. i argued that member states should initiate effective communication programmes to raise awareness among citizens about net neutrality, as citizens need to be informed about their rights to report abuse. at the same time, i believe that, in addition to the proposals in the commission's communication, monitoring programmes for internet service providers should be developed and penalties implemented in the event of irregularities being identified.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution. i believe that excessive regulation of the internet must be avoided, so as not to hinder the development of this field. at the same time, transparency in the management of traffic by internet service providers should be ensured so that consumers have real information that is useful in their decision-making.
in writing. - dispersion munitions pose serious risks to the civilian population because of the lethal effects they can have. in post-conflict contexts, the use of these munitions has, on many occasions, resulted in serious injury and even death of civilians due to unexploded ordnance, which ends up being found by children or other innocent people. there are many states that still use cluster munitions against civilians. cambodia, thailand and libya are just a few examples. urgent measures are therefore required to ensure the removal of unexploded cluster munitions in order to prevent the killing or injury of others. we now have a convention on cluster munitions, which came into force a little over a year ago, ratified by 111 states. however, all member states that have not yet acceded to the cluster munitions convention need to adopt strict and transparent national measures prior to accession. this includes a moratorium on the use, production and transfer of cluster munitions and the initiation of procedures for the destruction of existing stockpiles of munitions under emergency conditions. the ep's call to the council and the commission to include the banning of ammunition as a standard clause in agreements with third countries is welcome.
in writing. − a viable digital single market could improve competitiveness and boost economic growth in the eu. • it is essential for the development of european smes. trust in electronic transactions needs to be strengthened. at present, only 54% of european internet users buy or sell goods on the virtual marketplace. at the same time, e-commerce has a supporting role for cross-border trade. the removal of all barriers to the use of electronic commerce is important. in particular, fiscal obstacles must be removed. it is necessary to avoid discrimination between the provision of electronic services and the provision of goods. for example, the same vat rate should be applied to both printed and electronic books. my country ranks 10th in the world in terms of quality of internet connection-access ratio. a series of projects to cover the broadband white areas are to be launched, for which eur 84 million in eu funding will be allocated.
in writing. − i have initiated this resolution together with colleagues from other political groups to raise the issue of the inconsistency between the rules applicable to vat on cultural goods sold in physical and electronic form. the eu has adopted the digital agenda, and we have the ambition to develop a digital internal market. this is welcome and is in line with the evolution of european consumer behaviour, which is increasingly buying cultural content (music, newspapers and magazines, books, etc.) on the internet. given that member states have the possibility of applying a reduced rate of vat to physical cultural goods, the objective being to promote access to those goods, i do not see why there should be a different treatment for the same goods sold online, since the objective is exactly the same. so we are talking about an aspect of the vat directive which is obsolete in view of the new consumer trends. i therefore support the revision of the directive to introduce equal tax treatment for these products, regardless of the way they are sold. such developments, together with copyright reform, facilitating the free circulation of audiovisual content online, will contribute to the creation of a genuine digital internal market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because at eu level we are currently facing certain difficulties in the process of creating the digital single market. these are due to technological, legislative, cultural and linguistic barriers as well as to the consumption taxes that apply to goods and services. all this leads to a marked fragmentation of the market at member state level, which may jeopardise the achievement of our common objectives. i believe it is essential that the european union should allow the application, at least temporarily, of a reduced rate of vat on cultural services supplied by electronic means. this would help european citizens to benefit from more affordable prices for certain online products and services, which would support the sector and increase the eu's competitiveness in this area. at the same time, greater accessibility of cultural goods available online would reduce the high levels of piracy observed in this sector and reduce the financial losses incurred by certain producers or suppliers.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on modernising vat legislation to boost the digital single market. in july 2010, the council adopted directive 2010/45/eu on the common system of vat as regards the rules on invoicing. this directive, which will be transposed by 1 january 2013, establishes new vat rules on electronic invoicing, creating equal treatment of paper invoices and electronic invoices. in addition to vat legislation, e-invoicing is part of a complex of legal requirements, including accounting, audit, personal data protection, archiving and customs rules. it is estimated that applying the same vat rules to both paper and electronic invoices will reduce the administrative burden on businesses by up to eur 18 billion in the medium term. in order to ensure the interoperability of electronic invoices and the interconnection of electronic invoicing models, business partners and service providers should aim at aligning aspects such as risk management, addressing and routing, roaming arrangements, standards, communication tools and security requirements. by the end of the year, cen should propose interoperable addressing and routing procedures in the e-invoicing sector.
in writing. − under the treaty on european union, the eu is founded on the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities. those values are common to the member states in a society characterised by pluralism, non-discrimination, tolerance, justice, solidarity and equality between women and men. we need a gender balance in decision-making to be achieved by increasing the representation of women in the leadership structures of parliament, in the offices of political groups, in the offices of committees and delegations, in the composition of delegations and other missions such as election observation, and by representing men in areas where they are under-represented. at the same time, the european parliament committees responsible for the multiannual financial framework and the structural funds should assess the gender impact of the proposed priorities for expenditure, revenue sources and governance instruments before the adoption of the multiannual financial framework, in order to ensure that the post-2013 mff takes gender into account and that all eu-funded programmes include gender equality-related objectives in the basic regulations and allocate specific funds to achieve these objectives.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the integration of the gender perspective in the work of the european parliament. as vice-president responsible for gender mainstreaming in the european parliament's committee on transport and tourism, i believe that an effective information policy is needed, which systematically takes account of gender equality and avoids gender stereotypes. we call on the parliament's committees responsible for the multiannual financial framework and the structural funds to assess the gender impact of the proposed priorities in terms of expenditure, revenue sources and governance instruments, before adopting the multiannual financial framework (mff). this will ensure that the 2014-2020 mff is gender-sensitive and that all eu-funded programmes include gender equality objectives in the core regulations and allocate specific funds to achieve these objectives. we call on the commission to address and prioritise gender inequalities in a more consistent and systematic manner in the design and implementation of all policies and we stress the need to improve gender mainstreaming in all policies in order to achieve the european union's gender equality objectives.

author. - we are discussing again the human rights situation in iran, which confirms our fears about the tehran government's practice of responding to legitimate citizen grievances with force, abuse and in defiance of international public opinion. the abuses by the iranian authorities are particularly targeting minority groups, whether they are religious groups, journalists, women or human rights defenders. any attempt to structure a responsible civil society, any form of rejection of the methods of governing power in iran are drastically repressed. iran has some answers to the legitimate objections and concerns expressed by the international community regarding the human rights situation. it has chosen to do so by strengthening internal repression, further restricting freedom of expression, other rights and civil liberties. this attitude fully justifies the sanctions imposed by the international community. the power in tehran must show some sense and end the abusive practices that have been going on.
the author. - one minute is far too short to recall the string of human rights violations in iran. it is, as we know, about arbitrary arrests and detentions, unfair trials, torture and degrading treatment, discrimination against various minorities, the death penalty. i'll concentrate on the latter. as you know, the worldwide trend is to abolish the death penalty. several un resolutions call for the introduction of an international moratorium. despite these facts, iran remains the country with the highest proportion of capital punishment, relative to the number of citizens. often, these executions are carried out in secret. various reports indicate more than 300 secret executions for the past year. sometimes minors are the victims of these executions. i would also like to join my colleague in calling for the immediate release of pastor youcef nadarkhani, who is accused of apostasy because he converted to christianity at the age of 19. in conclusion, i believe that the human rights dialogue between the european union and iran must be resumed in order to address the issue of the death penalty and other human rights violations.
on behalf of the epp group. iran is one of the few countries in the 21st century where citizens are brought before a court and forced to choose between their faith and life. this is the statement made by human rights watch regarding pastor nadarkhani, sentenced to death by hanging. the report of the united nations commission on human rights of november 4 says: "the high number of executions, including public and stoning, the use of torture, the cruelty of punishments such as amputation, arbitrary arrests, unfair trials, discrimination, and the drastic limitation of freedom of expression and association are all warnings that urgently need to be heeded. i regret the decision of the foreign affairs council on monday to postpone the tightening of sanctions on iran. it takes more courage, a clear and consistent message. we don't negotiate respect for human rights.
i want to draw attention today to camp ashraf, located in iraq, which is sheltering 3,400 iranian dissidents, living in extremely difficult conditions. the united nations recently declared that these persons must be protected internationally from persecution in their own country and called for their fundamental rights to be respected. however, the iraqi prime minister has said he wants the camp closed by the end of this year, creating a very serious humanitarian situation. in this context, the appointment of a european union representative responsible for camp ashraf is a positive signal. that is why i believe that he must be involved in order to obtain a delay in the terms of dismantling the camp until the refugees can be safely transferred to third countries. the united nations high commissioner for refugees also has the responsibility to administer the process of rapid reintegration and to guarantee protection for these persons. the only possible solution to the situation of iranian asylum seekers in the ashraf area is a peaceful one.
on behalf of the epp group. blogger alaa abdel fatah is one of the approximately 12,000 civilians tried by military courts since the beginning of the revolution in egypt. he was arrested following a peaceful protest by coptic christians on october 9, which sparked the most violent act by military authorities against civilians since the fall of the mubarak regime. twenty-five people were killed and 300 more were injured. the commission and the council must call on the egyptian authorities to stop the trial of civilians by military courts, to release immediately all political and prisoners of conscience, and to ensure a serious and independent investigation into the violence in maspero following the peaceful demonstration for the rights of coptic christians. we all have to make sure that the beginning of the revolution in egypt and the revolution in egypt leads to a real democracy.
together we applauded the changes in egypt this spring, we stood in solidarity with those who, in the heart of the egyptian capital, fought for democracy and freedom. unfortunately, we have to say that the changes in egypt are minimal, that the methods and abuses are still present, that the military rules by force and ignores the objections of the international community. we have seen in the last two months an increase in internal violence in egypt, violence that has also affected religious minority groups, such as the coptic christians. according to figures presented by egyptian human rights activists, more than 12,000 civilians have appeared before military courts since the fall of the mubarak regime, raising serious questions about egypt's democratization process. this is the situation of alaa abdel fatah, who refused to be investigated by the military justice, which he accuses of bias. i join those who have called for the release of alaa abdel fatah and all those like him. we also demand that the right to a fair trial be guaranteed in a civil court, with due respect for all procedural rights. i think we need to watch more closely what's happening in egypt to make sure that this kind of abuse stops.
we also discussed the human rights situation in egypt in the previous plenary session. we're doing it now. this was also emphasized by the office of the united nations high commissioner for human rights last week when it said, and i quote: 'the shrinking space for freedom of expression and association in egypt is extremely worrying.' i join those calling for the immediate release of alaa abdel fatah, a dissident blogger against the mubarak regime, who is in detention today. he was detained and will be tried by a military court for daring to criticize the actions of the security forces during the maspero protests. the lines written by alaa abdel fatah in cell 19 of bab el-khalek prison, i think, sums up the absurdity of the situation very well. i quote again: "after the egyptian revolution, i didn't expect to find myself in mubarak's prisons". as my colleagues have requested, i believe that the arrest and presentation of such detainees to military courts must cease. that's not democracy.
if we look at regimes that flagrantly violate human rights, one might say that alaa abdel fatah's situation is not that serious. but egypt wants to become a democracy. and that requires that the fundamental principles be respected in every situation. in a true democracy, civilians are not brought before military courts. it may seem like a small thing, but it's not. if accepted and treated lightly, such exceptions can open the way to any slip-up. the egyptian military played a major role in the overthrow of mubarak's regime. but now they have an even more important task: to fulfill their responsibilities, thus laying the foundations for a true democracy. clarifying the violent incidents against coptic christians is also an important aspect of this process.
we are, of course, looking forward to the new measures that the european council will take - there is a lot of talk about this. i fully agree with what commissioner rehn said, namely that the credibility of the european union, of all the actors in the european union, depends very much on how we implement the decisions that have been taken. but here, unfortunately, things are not going so well. for example, the european financial stability facility: the decision taken in october to increase the commitments of this facility is not happening. we also have not had very good news about the negotiations between the private creditors and the greek government, with the private creditors' commitment to reduce the public debt by 50%. the implementation of the decisions we have taken must therefore be carried out with the utmost rigour, because the credibility of the european union, the credibility of the euro, also depends on it. i would certainly be glad if, by the end of this year, we could have a communication from the european commission on how these decisions are being implemented.
in writing. the next european council will also discuss the extension of the schengen area to romania and bulgaria. the two countries have fully implemented the provisions of the schengen acquis and thus fulfil all the necessary criteria for entry into the european area of free movement. the merger must take place as soon as possible. unfortunately, the netherlands is the only country which, without any reason based on european legislation, has a negative position. i believe that this situation must be clarified at the next european council. the council must assess this situation in the light of european law and treaties and take a decision to forward to the european ministers of justice and home affairs. the jha council in december must do what is necessary to ensure that the two countries receive what they deserve by meeting all the requirements.
in writing. the european council of 9 december 2011 will focus on the economic situation in the eu, the member states' debt crisis and increased convergence within the euro area, as well as on elements related to the completion of the internal market and the implementation of the digital agenda. but european leaders should take urgent action to boost growth and create jobs. in this context, measures to increase energy efficiency, complete the internal energy market and develop energy infrastructure are becoming extremely important for energy security and the balance of the eu's trade balance. the european council should analyse the results of the stress tests carried out on nuclear power stations in different member states and adopt decisions to increase the safety of european nuclear reactors. the development of transport and communication infrastructure and information technology is also essential for the completion of the internal market and for the economic and social development of the eu. all these measures for growth and job creation should be linked and supported by the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020. i welcome the inclusion on the agenda of the december european council of an item on the accession of romania and bulgaria to the schengen area, as well as the signing of the treaty of accession of croatia to the eu.
