in writing. – the report ‘application of croatia to become a member of the european union’ welcomes the conclusion of the accession negotiations with croatia. however, crucial challenges remain to be properly addressed in order to ensure the sustainability of the reforms introduced by the croatian authorities during the accession process in the fields of the judiciary, anti-corruption and confiscation of illegally or unjustified gained assets. croatia must pursue the full implementation of the reforms adopted. moreover, the country still needs to establish a convincing track record of recruiting and appointing judges and state prosecutors based on transparent, objective and merit-based criteria. a track record of convictions in high-level political corruption and fraud cases is also needed. finally, transparency and integrity in public administration need to be further strengthened as well as depolitisation and professionalism in the police. adopting and implementing the crime of illicit enrichment is also needed in croatia. these issues must remain top priorities on the political agenda of croatia under the supervision of the commission.

economic growth and employment in europe. and so this european semester is very directly linked to strengthening economic growth and thereby employment in europe, and it is ultimately the most acting president of the council. - mr president! - what are you doing? i listened to this debate with great interest. i think that such discussions are necessary, first of all, to increase understanding of the whole process and the european semester. what's he for? the european semester is not an instrument to provide an immediate solution to the problems of the current crisis. it is an instrument designed to be part of long-term economic cooperation within the european union, to strengthen the way in which union priorities are translated and coordinated by all member states and to strengthen the transmission of those priorities, as defined at union level, to national parliaments, i.e. to those institutions which ultimately take most of the decisions affecting the actual implementation of union priorities. i think we have to remember that. i think the whole process is based on the community institutions at the moment. there were voices in the chamber saying that there were concerns that we were moving away from the community method, that elements were being introduced that were not provided for in the treaty, that the dictates of individual member states were emerging. but please note that the whole process is based from the outset on drafts prepared by the european commission, on discussions in the council and at european council level, on documents adopted within the eu institutions. so in my opinion the community method is preserved. and the most important part of the process, and one that many member states have pointed out is that the final decision is left to the sovereign national parliaments. we have to remember that and take care of it. the removal of this sovereignty from the european parliaments in budgetary decisions is not accepted by virtually any member state. there is no such option. in discussing the european semester, its evaluation after the first year of operation, and the further changes that are being made to the functioning of the european semester, we should focus on how to increase and strengthen this message to the european parliaments. how can national parliaments be more involved in the discussion of priorities that improve the efficiency of the european union as a whole? but all of this depends on improving the efficiency of the functioning of individual member states. we already know from experience that it is not possible to build the european union's increased competitiveness on the basis of just a few member states. we all have to go in the same direction. the appropriate pace for each member state should be found. not everyone can lift the same weight at the same time. but what the european commission does, by preparing its annual growth survey, is to give an indication of the direction in which the union should develop in the near future. this is then translated into individual recommendations for the member states and checked to see if they are reflected in the national reform programmes and then in the national budgets. this is the element that we have been missing: the signal was sent from brussels, from the european institutions, to the capitals and that was really the end of it. we haven't had a feedback in the decision-making process yet on how this is going to be taken into account. so this is a huge value addition to the whole process and that's what we should be focusing on. i find many interesting ideas in mrs berès' report, particularly on how the european parliament and the other eu institutions could be involved in the process of involving national parliaments in the decision-making process and showing them that they too have a direct responsibility for the implementation of the eu priorities that serve our common good: increasing and sustaining economic growth in the member states and improving competitiveness throughout the european union.
in writing. the economic crisis has shown that better tools are needed to correct macroeconomic imbalances. the 'economic governance semester' is designed to assess national economic and fiscal policies at european level before they are adopted. it would provide a structural framework for the coordination of budgetary and economic policies of the member states, in line with the stability and growth pact and the eu 2020 strategy. the economic crisis has led to an increase in macroeconomic imbalances and competitiveness gaps following the introduction of the euro. this has led to the need for the union to tackle them on the basis of a symmetrical approach that would target both deficits and excessive surpluses. the enhanced framework for economic governance should be based on different interlinked policies aimed at sustainable growth and jobs that are coherent with each other, in particular a union strategy for growth and jobs. experience in recent years has highlighted the need for improved economic governance in the union, which should be based on a stronger national ownership of commonly agreed rules and policies and a stronger framework for the supervision of national economic policies at union level.
in writing. there has been a lot of talk in european and national contexts about the economic and financial crisis and its effects, the sovereign debt and public deficit crisis, job losses and the precariousness of existing jobs. but too little was done: half-hearted decisions were made and the euro area member states in difficulty were looked at with an eye of blame, as responsible for the domino effect on the union's overall economic situation. however, it must be acknowledged that the crisis we are facing, the most serious in the last seven decades, has been created by certain weaknesses in the economic and monetary union and by the structural problems of the euro area countries, particularly in terms of their differences in competitiveness, as jacques delors rightly pointed out recently. member states should therefore consider economic and fiscal policies as a matter of common concern and should seek to strengthen macroeconomic coordination in the framework of the european semester. for the european project to advance the ideals of democracy, peace and economic prosperity, it must be credible and backed by the pillars of truly effective economic stabilisation policies.
in writing. the economic and financial crisis has led to an accentuation of inequalities and macroeconomic imbalances. the recently concluded first 'european semester' highlighted the need for the european union to tackle these issues on the basis of a symmetrical approach based on more democratic legitimacy and interconnected policies at european level, aimed at achieving the objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy. regional policy will continue to play a particularly important role in the development of national programmes in the european semester and at the same time will be a key instrument for achieving the medium and long-term objectives set. a strong and well-funded cohesion policy can prevent future economic and financial crises in europe and protect the less developed regions in particular. it is also very important to involve local and regional partners in achieving the objectives of the european union, taking into account the characteristics and different levels of development of the 271 european regions. this will lead to a greater ownership of the strategy objectives at all levels and ensure a better awareness of the objectives and results on the ground.
i welcome the discussion of this report in the context of the changing global economic balance. cooperation with developing countries, which currently have a major trade influence, should therefore be encouraged. i would stress the relevance of paragraph 5 of the report. today, the union's trading relations need to be geographically diversified. europe's partnerships need to take account of the challenges of the present. for example, making financial aid conditional on meeting environmental requirements. i would point out that developing countries with economic potential are lacking in this area. their contribution to the implementation of treaties such as the kyoto protocol is therefore essential. furthermore, these states must ensure compliance with the legislation developed by the international labour organisation. rapid economic development can lead to abuses and violations of fundamental rights.
in writing. i welcome the agreement reached following the conciliation procedure between parliament and the council on the regulation establishing a financing instrument for the promotion of democracy and human rights worldwide. the agreed changes bring greater flexibility to the use of european funds for the promotion of human rights in the world by making the expenditure on taxes and duties paid by beneficiaries of these funds eligible in special cases. such flexibility could lead to increased efficiency of those funds and unlocking funding for programmes and projects in third countries. however, it is important that this eligibility is granted on a case-by-case basis and not in an automatic manner, in order to eliminate any abuse. equally important, the revision of this regulation also contributes to greater coherence of the european union in terms of the instruments for financing its external policy, bearing in mind that the european instrument for democracy and human rights was, along with the development cooperation instrument, the only instrument that did not provide for any exception to the principle of ineligible expenditure on taxes and duties.

in writing. with the number of people living with hiv increasing both in europe (2.2 million in 2009), and globally (34 million people living with hiv, up 17% on a decade ago), it is time for the european executive to seriously examine its strategy for preventing the spread of the disease. the statistics now available show that this increase in the number of patients is the result of two different trends: the continued expansion of the number of people infected with hiv and the increase in the life expectancy of those affected by the disease as a result of the discovery of new treatments and medicines. in these circumstances, the european executive needs to examine both the strategic lines of action for preventing the spread of hiv infection, with a view to making the social and health policies implemented at this level more effective, and the policies for investing in research, prevention, treatment and support of the sick, with a view to spreading good practices and european models.
president of the european central bank. − madam president, i am delighted to be making my first appearance here as president of the ecb and i am honoured to present to you the ecb annual report for 2010. the first thing i wish to do is pay homage to my predecessor jean-claude trichet. during all his tenure he had a very fruitful and very constructive dialogue with the european parliament and i intend to continue on this route with the same force, the same strength that he displayed. today’s session is an opportunity for us to take a wider perspective on ecb policies. in that way, i will also touch on a number of the broader themes of the resolution of the european parliament. let me begin with a few words on the main monetary policy decisions we have taken and the challenges we have faced during 2010 and 2011. as you know, the ecb’s monetary policy is constantly guided by the goal of maintaining price stability in the euro area over the medium term. and when i say this, i mean price stability in either direction. this applies to both the setting of official interest rates and the implementation of non-standard measures. this autumn, tensions in financial markets have intensified again with very adverse effects on financing conditions and confidence. downside risks to the economic outlook have increased. the weaker degree of activity is itself moderating price, cost and wage pressures. it is in this context that the ecb decided to reduce its key interest rates by 25 basis points in early november 2011. dysfunctional government bond markets in several euro area countries hamper the single monetary policy because the way this policy is transmitted to the real economy depends also on the conditions of the bond markets in the various countries. an impaired transmission mechanism for monetary policy has a damaging effect on the availability and price of credit to firms and households. this is the very important monetary policy reason for the ecb’s non-standard measures. but of course, such interventions can only be limited. governments must – individually and collectively – restore their credibility vis-à-vis financial markets. tensions in sovereign bond markets have been accompanied by stress in the banking sector given the financial interlinkages between governments and banks. the ecb has taken several measures in 2010 and 2011 to ensure that banks continue to have access to funding sources. this has enabled them to continue lending to firms and households. most importantly, the ecb has extended its policy of fully allotting liquidity demanded by banks at fixed rates against collateral. the maximum maturity of these liquidity-providing operations was first extended to six months and then later to 12 and 13 months. a new covered bond purchase programme has recently been initiated, with a size of eur 40 billion. in addition, liquidity in us dollars has been offered to banks for three-month periods. yesterday, in a globally coordinated action with the federal reserve, the bank of japan, the bank of england, the bank of canada and the swiss national bank, we have agreed to lower the price on us dollar provision in other constituencies including the euro area. we have furthermore agreed, as a contingency measure, to establish temporary bilateral liquidity swap arrangements so that liquidity can be provided in each jurisdiction in any of the currencies, should market conditions so warrant. as the ecb’s governing council meets on thursday next week, we are now in the pre-decision period, and nothing that i say should in any way be interpreted in terms of future monetary policy decisions. but as far as the current situation is concerned, there is frankly not much more to say beyond what i have said in recent statements. we are aware of the continuing difficulties for banks due to the stress on sovereign bonds, the tightness of funding markets and the scarcity of eligible collateral in some financial segments. we are also aware of the problems of maturity mismatches on balance sheets, the challenges of raising levels of capital and the cyclical risks related to the downturn. let me now turn to the overall functioning of europe’s economic and monetary union. looking back at 2010 and 2011, notable progress has been achieved in reinforcing economic governance – though i recognise that this may not be evident in times of crisis. the european parliament has contributed decisively to that progress, and the ecb commends its work. the ‘six-pack’, the european semester, the euro plus pact: all these initiatives have set the stage for closer coordination and more intensive scrutiny of economic policies in the eu, particularly in the euro area. yet we are at a difficult stage at present. we have set up these new mechanisms, but their positive effects on the credibility of government fiscal policies are not yet visible. and the government changes that have taken place in some of the more exposed countries have not yet had much of an effect on the continuing fragility of financial markets. fundamental questions are being raised and they call for an answer. at the heart of these questions are not only the credibility of governments’ policies and the actual delivery of the promised reforms, but also the overall design of our common fiscal governance. i am confident that the new surveillance framework will restore confidence over time. i am also quite sure that countries overall are on the right track. but a credible signal is needed to give ultimate assurance over the short term. what i believe our economic and monetary union needs is a new fiscal compact – a fundamental restatement of the fiscal rules together with the mutual fiscal commitments that euro area governments have made. just as we effectively have a compact that describes the essence of monetary policy – an independent central bank with a single objective of maintaining price stability – so a fiscal compact would enshrine the essence of fiscal rules and the government commitments taken so far, and ensure that the latter become fully credible, individually and collectively. we might be asked whether a new fiscal compact would be enough to stabilise markets and how a credible longer-term vision can be helpful in the short term. our answer is that it is definitely the most important element to start restoring credibility. other elements might follow, but the sequencing matters. and it is first and foremost important to get a commonly shared fiscal compact right. confidence works backwards: if there is an anchor in the long term, it is easier to maintain trust in the short term. after all, investors are themselves often taking decisions with a long-term horizon, especially with regard to government bonds. a new fiscal compact would be the most important signal from euro area governments for embarking on a path of comprehensive deepening of economic integration. it would also present a clear trajectory for the future evolution of the euro area, thus framing expectations. on the precise legal process that brings about a move towards a genuine economic union, we should keep our options open. far-reaching treaty changes should not be discarded, but faster processes are also conceivable. whatever the approach, companies, markets and the citizens of europe expect policy-makers to act decisively to resolve the crisis. it is time to adapt the euro area design with a set of institutions, rules and processes that is commensurate with the requirements of monetary union.
on behalf of the s&d group, i would like to welcome you to the european parliament, mr draghi. i would first like to thank my colleague, mr tremosa, for his very good cooperation on this matter. in the current context of financial instability, the role of the central bank is virtually fundamental. the actions it has taken to respond to the turbulence in the financial markets are, however, still not enough in my view. but the bank's independence must be maintained, and it must become, as you said, a lender of last resort for the euro area countries, acting to fight against speculation, to combat the worsening crisis. in effect, by assuming its role as central bank, it would contribute significantly to increasing confidence in the soundness of the euro area architecture. at the same time, a strengthened role for the european central bank must be complemented by, i would say, radical measures such as the issuing of common euro area bonds, the harmonisation of member states' taxation and the strengthening of the european financial stability facility. in this respect, i welcome the commission's proposal of 23 november for the issuing of common euro-area bonds. i think the member states must understand that this issue is necessary for the stability of the financial markets and that everyone has a stake in a solution based on solidarity. this would effectively reduce the total cost of debt and guarantee liquidity in european financial markets. finally, i would like to say one thing, and i really believe it: the european currency cannot function without fiscal union, which is essentially a complement to monetary union.
we must thank the rapporteurs who, in extremely difficult circumstances, with virtually no possibility of negotiation, have succeeded in achieving the european parliament's objectives as far as possible. we must also be satisfied that there is a budget, that we have reached an agreement on the budget. in this time of crisis, i think it was not beneficial to have another budget crisis. this situation was only possible because of the wisdom of parliament, which could block the whole process. unfortunately, i didn't see the same level of wisdom at the council. we have now gone through the budgetary procedure under the lisbon treaty twice. it was the same thing every time: the council has imposed the figures on payments and has not accepted any negotiation, which is not normal at all. i do not think that this procedure of saying the figures and then distributing them to european politicians is the normal procedure. i think we should do the opposite: first we see the needs and then we calculate the budget. each time, the council issued a declaration committing itself to accepting the budget amendment if the amounts required for payments could not be reached. he didn't keep his word, you see what happened with the budget amendment number six and i don't know if he'll do it next year. we cannot continue in this way, because we do not trust the figures put on the table by the commission. two very important procedures are coming up next year: the 2013 budget and the mff. if we go through the exact same procedure, i don't think it's going to be good for the european union.

in writing. - i voted for the report on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) in the case of portugal, to provide support for workers in the machine-building industry affected by major changes in the structure of world trade. the application concerns the mobilisation of eur 1 518 456 from the egf in favour of portugal in the event of the redundancies of 726 workers in three undertakings active in the manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers. the redundancies took place between 1 july 2010 and 1 april 2011 in two neighbouring regions, norte and centro. the reason for these redundancies is the reduction in demand for new cars in the european union. eu car production fell by 17% in 2009 and by 23% in 2008 compared to the same period in 2007. the decrease in demand for electrical automotive equipment, combined with the inability to further reduce production costs and/or access credit, led to the closure of the lear plant and production unit in guarda and its relocation to morocco. i support the need to mobilise the egf to support workers made redundant. i also believe that the eu must strengthen its industrial policy to prevent european industry from being relocated to third countries.
in writing. − the commission proposal provides that the structural funds may finance expenditure on operations containing contributions to support repayable assistance. the document also clarifies that the assistance reimbursed to the body providing the assistance in the member state is booked separately and reused for the same purpose. i believe that this proposal clarifies the use of all forms of reimbursable assistance at project level and provides significant support for the use of the structural funds. in addition, it provides for a new obligation to incur expenditure in a timely manner (within two years of payment in full) and to report on the financial engineering instruments used. this is a useful tool for monitoring and evaluating the overall performance of these types of support.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the report by danuta hubner on the amendment of regulation 1083/2011 on financial management for certain member states experiencing financial difficulties. hungary, romania, latvia, portugal, greece and ireland were the most affected by the crisis and received financial assistance through the european financial stabilisation mechanism (efsm) for euro area countries, or the balance of payments mechanism for non-euro area countries. the measure adopted is temporary and allows the commission to increase by 10% the co-financing rates applicable during the intervention period of the support mechanisms, without modifying the global funds allocated to these countries under the cohesion policy for the period 2007-2013. the member state concerned shall submit a request to the commission within two months of the date on which the member state fulfils one of the conditions referred to in the regulation. the application shall detail the purpose of using the derogation and provide information on the complementary measures envisaged to concentrate funds for competitiveness, growth and employment, including in relation to the modification of operational programmes. the commission shall have 30 days from the date of submission of the request to object. the regulation will apply retroactively and the measure will cease to apply once the member state leaves the support mechanism.
in writing. − according to statistics presented by the european commission earlier this year, more than six million young europeans are leaving the education and training system. they face obstacles in finding stable employment, with their low level of education also being a cause of unemployment, poverty and social exclusion. i believe that equal access to high quality education from an early age needs to be improved, as early school leaving has serious consequences not only for economic growth, social stability but also for social cohesion in the eu, harming the career path, health and well-being of young people. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted for the honeyball report because i appreciate the emphasis on the inclusion of vulnerable groups in mainstream education. in romania, the school drop-out rate has increased by one third in the last ten years, from 1.8% to 2.4%. the phenomenon is aggravated by the current economic and social crisis. the roma community is still the most affected: according to studies, 4 out of 5 out-of-school children in romania are roma. the reasons for this situation are many. one is the difficulty of the family in supporting and encouraging children to pursue some form of education. in these circumstances, concrete and structured support from the school, the community and the authorities is needed. at the moment, one of the problems in this area is the lack of good practice at national level. this is why, for example, the roma education centre was set up in bihor county, which helps develop alternative educational programmes. one of the actions is the 'summer kindergarten', a non-formal education programme aimed at closing the gap in pre-school preparation between roma and non-roma children entering the first grade. i support these types of initiatives, which will make a significant contribution to the implementation of the national roma inclusion strategy.
in writing. − early school leaving is a complex phenomenon and a huge challenge facing europe. the eu's efforts to implement a number of measures and tools to better support member states in developing effective and efficient national policies to combat this phenomenon are therefore important. the europe 2020 strategy furthermore sets six main objectives for member states, one of which is to reduce early school leaving by 10% by 2020. the previous target, set in 2003, was not met by more than seven member states, as the early school leaving rate for all young people aged 18-24 at the end of 2009 was 14.4%. high rates of early school leaving have strong social and economic implications. early school leaving has a negative impact on economic growth, causing economic and social instability. interventions aimed at mobilising the energies and developing the skills of young people are therefore essential for the future economic and social development of the member states. it is estimated that reducing the rate of early school leaving in europe by just 1% would create an additional almost half a million young people with qualifications each year.

in writing. − in the last decade, the number of people infected with hiv has fallen by almost 20% and, for the first time in 2009, due to improved access to treatment, more than 50% of hiv-positive women gave birth to uninfected children. progress is largely due to the increased use of antiretroviral drugs. this is why the commission must continue to use all the opportunities available under the r & d framework programme to identify funding for promising projects in hiv/aids research and the development of new antiretroviral medicines, vaccines and innovative microbicides. these encouraging statistics also show that the commission and the member states must continue to promote communication campaigns to provide people with clear information on hiv infection, how to prevent it and what behaviours are at risk.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i would first like to thank the rapporteur for the very solid work done and for the efficient way the negotiations on this dossier were concluded, which has permitted a first reading agreement. i would also like to praise the role of mr albrecht, the rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on legal affairs, as well as the important role played by all the shadow rapporteurs. i would like to thank the european parliament in general because it has contributed to maintaining the level of ambition of the commission’s proposal. one thing in particular which i believe is very important for our citizens, the letter of rights, has been maintained in the final text as well as the actual list of rights and the moment when the rights apply. i also welcome the fact that additional rights were added to the list of rights, notably the right to remain silent, which shows again that it is very good that parliament has codecision possibilities because parliament preserves the rights of the individual. the measure on the right of information in criminal proceedings, as you know, is part of the procedural rights roadmap and the implementation of this roadmap is one of my top priorities. the letter of rights and right to information is now the second measure adopted; with the right to interpretation and translation having already been adopted. so we are progressing quickly on this issue and i think that is good for the europe of the citizens and of rights. in some member states i am asked the question: why do you do this – are those rights not the usual rights that everybody has? unfortunately it still happens in some member states that someone can be brought to trial and not know that he has a right to a lawyer or to an interpreter. we have even heard of cases where people have been tried in court and did not know or did not understand what the accusation against them was. with this measure, accused persons will receive a letter of rights, in a language they understand, and will be guaranteed to receive adequate information about the charges they face. this is important in today’s europe in which millions of people exercise their right to free movement and travel to other eu member states, be it to work, for study or for retirement. they need to know, if they find themselves caught up in criminal proceedings, that their rights are protected and that parliament has helped to do this. in addition, this measure will also play a vital part in promoting mutual trust between justice systems in the eu, which in turn is necessary to enhance judicial cooperation, because without trust this cooperation cannot function. here, together with those instruments of mutual recognition, we are creating a continent of justice, rights and security for european citizens, and i thank the parliamentarians who make this possible.

judicial practice differ considerably from one member state to another. if suspects are not properly informed, criminal proceedings may be unfair, which may result in unnecessary costs due to delays in proceedings, costs related to the exercise of appeals and the failure of criminal investigations. there are no rules at a sufficient level and the existing ones are not properly implemented. neither the minimum standards laid down in the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms, nor the convention and its implementing mechanism, provide sufficient protection in all cases with regard to the provision of adequate information on rights and, in particular, on charges. the way in which states reflect these rights in national practice is not uniform. this reinforces the need for action at community level. union instruments facilitating judicial cooperation between member states are based on the principle of mutual recognition of judgments, and such semi-automatic recognition requires mutual trust between judges and between courts. the available data show that the problem of insufficient information is acute, and not limited to certain member states. the adoption of this directive is therefore a very important step towards better protection of fundamental rights in the european union. in conclusion, i would like to thank the in writing. – this european council's major achievements are: 1. the split between eurozone and non-eurozone member states was avoided; 2. compulsory economic, fiscal and budgetary governance was agreed upon. this opens the way to a new european architecture. what starts with a treaty may finish with a constitution. the summit's negative results are: 1. the concept of solidarity is missing from the envisaged solutions. or, solidarity is key to economic growth and job creation, both being the foundation of a social europe. 2. the lack of short-term solutions, necessary to regain the confidence of the markets, but also that of the european citizens. the uk's self-isolation is an opportunity rather than a crisis. even if regrettable, it is not lethal. the future negotiations must include all willing eurozone and non-eurozone members. including the eu institutions is also necessary. legal coherence must be ensured between the inter-governmental treaty and european legislation; eventually, they should form one juridical instrument. the treaty should regulate the coherence between various internal and external european policies. all its signatories would be automatically included into the schengen area and the eurozone. this might represent the birth of a new europe, with uk joining it or being only its partner.
in writing. the european council conclusions (8-9 december 2011) underline the need for new economic governance to be complemented by a monitoring of social and employment policies, in particular those that can positively influence macroeconomic stability and growth. we welcome the fact that the european council has identified the need for specific measures at both national and european level for the most vulnerable groups, in particular the young unemployed. i believe that it is essential for growth and for reducing budget deficits that member states define urgently measures capable of creating jobs on their territory. we call for the adoption of a 'fiscal pact' leading to a 'fiscal stability union' in the euro area and measures to strengthen the stabilisation instruments and provide the necessary financial resources to be preceded by a broad and transparent public debate process. on the energy front, the european council called for a swift agreement on the energy efficiency proposal and for the comprehensive nuclear safety review to be given priority. we welcome the request to the eu council to adopt the decision on the accession of bulgaria and romania to the schengen area as soon as possible, the european council once again recognising that all the legal conditions for taking this decision have been met.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on amending the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 on budgetary discipline and sound financial management as regards the multiannual financial framework to meet the additional funding needs of the iter project. the initial draft budget for nuclear research in the multiannual financial framework 2007-2013 is insufficient due to the substantial increase in iter project costs. the council, in its conclusions of 12 july 2010, confirmed the increased financial needs of the project and agreed on a limit of eur 6,6 billion (2008 value) of the european contribution to the construction phase of iter until 2020, including eur 1,4 billion for the period 2012-2013. the council agreement of november 2010 on the reallocation within the multiannual financial framework and the seventh eu research framework programme of eur 1,3 billion to cover iter's additional needs does not contradict and does not cancel the council's commitment to an overall european contribution to iter's construction costs of eur 6,6 billion. given the importance of the iter project for the eu's energy future, we support securing the additional commitment appropriations needed for the 2012-13 period.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on draft amending budget no 7/2011 of the european union for the financial year 2011, section iii commission, as it seeks to mobilise from the eu solidarity fund (eusf) the sum of eur 38 million in commitment and payment appropriations to alleviate the effects of the earthquake that hit the region of murcia in spain and the floods in the region of veneto, italy. we support the rapid provision of financial assistance through the european union solidarity fund (eusf) to those affected by the earthquake in the region of murcia, spain and the floods in the region of veneto, italy. i consider it important that all stakeholders in member states affected by such natural disasters, both at local and regional level, as well as national authorities, assess as soon as possible the damage caused and the financing needs and improve coordination for possible future requests for the mobilisation of the eusf, in order to speed up the mobilisation of the eusf as much as possible. we regret that for the floods in the veneto region the eusf will only be mobilised 13 months after the end of october 2010, the period during which the aforementioned torrential rains occurred.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the earthquake in may this year in the murcia region of spain and the floods in the veneto region of italy in 2010 had a disastrous impact on both the population and infrastructure of the areas concerned. the direct damage in murcia was estimated by the commission, on the basis of calculations provided by the spanish authorities, at a total of eur 842,8 million, and in the case of the veneto region, the direct damage was estimated at eur 3717 million. i therefore consider it extremely important that financial assistance is provided quickly through the eu solidarity fund (eusf) to those affected by natural disasters and i also share the rapporteur's concern that, as regards the floods in the veneto region, the mobilisation of the fund will only take place 13 months after the torrential rains that occurred at the end of october 2010. i believe that all stakeholders in the member states, both at local and regional level, and also national authorities, should better assess needs and improve coordination for possible future requests for the eusf in order to accelerate its mobilisation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the eu solidarity fund (eusf), in accordance with point 26 of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 between the european parliament, the council and the commission on budgetary discipline and sound financial management. unfortunately, europe is increasingly confronted with extreme events such as droughts, floods, forest fires and earthquakes. the eu and the member states must show solidarity with the people in regions affected by natural disasters. the eu's main tool for dealing with these disasters is the eusf, which complements member states' budgets for emergency measures such as the immediate restoration of infrastructure and equipment in the fields of energy, drinking water, wastewater, transport, telecommunications, health and education. spain submitted a request for funding following an earthquake in the region of murcia, with damages amounting to eur 842,838 million, and italy submitted a request for funding following floods in veneto, with damages amounting to eur 676,357 million. i support the mobilisation of the eusf for a total amount of eur 37 979 875: eur 21 070 950 for spain and eur 16 908 925 for italy, in commitment and payment appropriations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the european union has put in place legislative and budgetary instruments to provide additional individual support to workers affected by major changes in the structure of world trade and to assist them in their long-term reintegration into the labour market. as a direct result of the global financial and economic crisis, the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was extended for applications submitted from 1 may 2009 to include support for workers made redundant as a result of the financial crisis. italy stated that the construction sector had been severely affected by the crisis and that demand for new housing had decreased drastically due to lack of funds. data available at eu level confirm the significant decline of this sector for seven consecutive quarters. i therefore support the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund to allocate eur 3 918 850 to the redundant workers in the trentino-alto adige/südtirol region. they also argue that the competent institutions should make the necessary efforts in the future to improve the procedural and budgetary mechanisms with a view to accelerating the mobilisation of the egf.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 3 918 850 from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) for italy, in respect of 643 redundancies (528 of which were assisted) in 323 construction enterprises in the trentino-alto adige/sudtirol region during the nine-month reference period from 1 march 2010 to 1 december 2010. in recent years, the construction sector has been severely affected by the economic and financial crisis. between 2008 and 2011, the italian market for new housing contracted by 35,5% and the public works market by 28,7%. since the start of the crisis, the construction sector in italy has lost 230 000 jobs. the economic and financial crisis has led to a sharp reduction in lending to the construction sector and a decline in demand for new homes, due to reduced consumer confidence and lack of funds. available data confirm that the construction sector in the eu-27 has been in decline for seven consecutive quarters (q1 2009 - q3 2010) compared to the same period in previous years, mainly due to the decline in private investment in the residential sector. i support the mobilisation of the egf, but i ask for data on the reintegration of beneficiaries into the labour market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the right to information in criminal proceedings. the establishment of minimum common standards in criminal proceedings would help to respect the fundamental rights of eu citizens and overcome the difficulties encountered in applying the principle of mutual recognition in criminal cases, as a consequence of the lack of trust between judicial authorities. the main purpose of the proposal is to assert the right of the suspect or accused person to be informed of his or her rights.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that mutual recognition should be the basis of judicial cooperation in both civil and criminal matters in the european union, so as to ensure the best possible protection of individual rights. mutual recognition is based on trust in the criminal and civil justice systems of other member states, which needs to be strengthened by creating detailed rules for the protection of the rights of european citizens.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, as i believe that the right to information in criminal proceedings must be guaranteed in all member states. today, european citizens have the right to move and reside throughout the european union, but they must also abide by the rules of 27 often very different judicial systems. in this context, harmonisation of legislation on the provision of information to the accused in criminal proceedings is fundamental and ensures that the rights of european citizens are protected in any of the member states of the european union.
in writing. − it is normal for any person suspected or accused of having committed an offence in the european union to be promptly informed of his procedural rights in an easily understandable language. it is gratifying that we have succeeded in introducing into this proposal that suspects should be promptly informed of at least the following procedural rights: the right to be assisted by a lawyer, any right to free legal advice and the conditions for obtaining it, the right to be informed of the charge, the right to interpretation and translation. citizens can only fully exercise their rights if they know them, and the adoption of this report by our institution demonstrates once again that the european union is committed to strengthening the fundamental rights of its citizens.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the directive so that those accused of committing a crime are informed of their rights in a language they understand. the directive applies regardless of the legal status of the accused within the eu. anyone who is remanded in custody (including on the basis of a european arrest warrant) will be informed of the reasons for his or her arrest and will receive a letter with his or her rights, which include: the right not to make statements, to have a lawyer, including on his or her own initiative, to inform the consular authorities and another person, for example a family member, to know for how long he or she is being held until brought before a judge, the right to emergency medical care and the right to access evidence in the case file (at the latest at the end of the criminal investigation, with certain exceptions on grounds of national security, the rights of another or an important public interest). the letter must also show how the lawfulness of the arrest can be challenged, what the appeal procedure is against the detention decision or how to apply for provisional release. the directive is part of a package of measures designed to ensure, at eu level, certain procedural rights for those accused of committing a crime in the area of freedom, security and justice.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the adoption of the european parliament and council directive on the european protection order. this directive will specify the measures which will continue to protect a person from a criminal offence, from another person who may endanger his life, physical or psychological integrity, dignity, personal liberty or sexual integrity. the ultimate objective is to prevent new criminal offences, reduce the consequences of previous criminal offences and strengthen the protection of victims.
in writing. − the european protection order aims to protect victims of gender-based violence against harassment, abduction or attempted murder. victims of crime who enjoy protection in one member state should now enjoy the same protection if they move to another member state. member states will have three years to transpose this directive into national law. these rules should also cover all victims of crime and criminality, not just victims of gender-based violence. most protection measures are granted to women who become victims of gender-based violence, but the european protection order can cover victims of any gender as well as other types of crime. the european protection order may also be applied for in respect of relatives of the beneficiary of the european protection order. these adopted rules will apply to victims or potential victims who need protection against a criminal act by another person which could in any way endanger the life, physical, mental or sexual integrity of the victim, as well as his or her freedom or dignity. such acts could include harassment, abduction, stalking and 'other forms of coercion'.
in writing. −in the coming years, europe will increasingly need to welcome new economic migrants, which will enable it to cope with demographic change. it is therefore desirable that the union should design its immigration policy as a means of regulating the need for labour on the community market, with a focus on the establishment of active policies to allow access to highly qualified workers on the one hand and to the least qualified on the other. however, i do not think it is in the interests of the european union to maintain restrictions on non-eu nationals who wish to pursue self-employed economic activities or those of micro and small enterprises, including cross-border professional activities, since these often cover activities in the service sector. europe is considering a series of actions to enable it to emerge from the crisis, which is why i believe we must give a chance to third country nationals who are willing and able to make their own contribution to the implementation of these objectives.
in writing. − i supported this new directive because i believe that it is better to have legal migration and the new legislation will allow foreign workers to obtain work and residence permits in the eu, granting similar rights to eu nationals in terms of working conditions, social security and access to public services. i am glad that the european parliament's amendments have been passed and that non-eu citizens and those registered as unemployed will be able to benefit from vocational training and education.
in writing. −the new single work permit legislation will allow foreign workers to obtain work and residence permits through a single procedure. i voted for migrants from non-eu countries who work legally in the eu to enjoy similar rights to eu nationals in terms of working conditions, social security and access to public services. member states will have two years to adapt their national legislation to the new rules. as a general rule, non-eu workers will enjoy the same access to social protection as eu citizens, but member states could apply restrictions to holders of employment contracts of less than six months. member states will also have the possibility to restrict access to public services, such as public housing, to foreign workers in employment. eu countries could apply their own specific restrictions to these rights. i voted for non-eu workers to receive pensions in their home countries under the same conditions and at the same rates as nationals of member states. at the same time, non-eu citizens and those registered as unemployed must benefit from vocational training and education.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that bureaucracy in the day-to-day management of businesses must be reduced. in this respect, i welcome the initiative to create the subcategory of micro-enterprises with a view to developing a legal framework adapted to their needs. in many cases, they provide the premises for economic growth at local level, in particular through development clusters. bringing together micro-enterprises with a similar activity object plays a crucial role in revitalizing disadvantaged areas. i believe that the establishment of a clear and simplified set of rules for drawing up annual accounts will foster the development of this category of enterprises. the definition of the exemption from the publication requirement is a necessary benchmark for the correct transposition of the directive. the adaptation of the european regime in this area to national and local economic specificities is also welcome.
in writing. − i consider this second reading agreement between parliament and the council to be a balanced one and a step forward in simplifying the obligations of micro-entities in respect of annual accounts. although very important, accounting requirements can sometimes be a source of unnecessary complications for micro-entities that do not have an extremely high turnover. as a result, overly stringent requirements represent an administrative burden that is disproportionate to their objective and prove to be counterproductive. i am glad that parliament has succeeded in persuading the council of ministers to raise the threshold for the applicability of the exceptions in respect of the net turnover to eur 700 000 instead of eur 500 000 as was previously intended, and from eur 250 000 to eur 350 000 in respect of the total balance sheet. thus, more micro-entities will be able to benefit from these exemptions which lighten their burdens and allow them to focus on their core activities, which is positive for their competitiveness.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament legislative resolution on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending, as regards micro-entities, council directive 78/660/eec on the annual accounts of certain types of companies, as i consider it important to reduce the administrative burden for micro-entities by simplifying the financial reporting rules applicable to them. according to the commission's estimates, the cost of complying with the current reporting requirements of the accounting directives is on average eur 1 558 per undertaking. it is estimated that companies would still spend around 25% of that amount, even in the absence of any legal reporting obligation, on the information needs of administrators and third parties. the commission therefore estimates that the remaining 75%, i.e. eur 1169 represents the approximate amount of the accounting burden of a company. i argue that it is important that member states should be able to exempt from the obligations laid down in the directive on the annual accounts of certain types of companies companies companies which, at the date of drawing up the balance sheet, do not exceed the limits of two of the following three criteria: balance sheet total: eur 500 000; net turnover: eur 1 000 000; average number of employees during the financial year: 10.
in writing. − it is a technical document on the mechanisms and conditions for providing financial support to member states in difficulty in the context of the economic crisis and sovereign debt. it includes some of the first corrections, brought about by the implementation of support measures in favour of countries such as greece, ireland, portugal and romania. the most important provision, which justifies my vote in favour of adopting this document, concerns the possibility of facilitating the management of union funding. in order to support the acceleration of investment in the member states and regions concerned and to increase the impact of funding on the economy, it is necessary to allow the eafrd contribution rate to be increased to 95% of eligible public expenditure in regions eligible under the convergence objective and to 85% of eligible public expenditure in other regions experiencing serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability.
in writing. − i believe that, in the context of the financial crisis, some member states are facing budgetary constraints that could prevent them from meeting their commitments under the co-financed community programmes. in this context, i believe that supporting the commission's proposal and speeding up the legislative procedure in a way that allows it to enter into force before the end of this year is in the interest of the rural economies of the member states concerned and in the wider economic interest of the european union as a whole.
in writing. − the risk of losing european payments in the budget years 2011 and 2012 due to missing national funds is serious, and should be taken into consideration. the eu commission proposed to top up the co-financing of rural development projects in countries like greece, ireland, portugal, latvia and romania. this will help to accelerate investments and consequently boost their economies. these co-financing rates will not increase the total amount, but will be applied only until the end of 2013. the year 2012 is very important from this point of view. we should see immediate results. i endorse the present report because it points out one of the problems that structural funds have and i believe it is of major importance. there is of course a risk of an overall reduction of the total amount that was programmed.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1698/2005 as regards certain provisions relating to financial management for certain member states experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability. thus, in order to facilitate the management of union funding, to support the acceleration of investments in member states and regions severely affected by the crisis and to enhance the impact of funding on the economy, it is allowed to increase the eafrd contribution rate to 95% of eligible public expenditure in regions eligible under the convergence objective and to 85% of eligible public expenditure in other regions experiencing serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability. this temporary increase in co-financing rates should be seen in the context of the budgetary constraints faced by all member states and those budgetary constraints should be reflected appropriately in the general budget of the eu. in addition, as the main purpose of this mechanism is to address specific current problems, it should apply for a limited period of time to the expenditure incurred by the paying agencies until 31 december 2013.
in writing. − the elimination of barriers to trade is one of the most important ways in which the european authorities can boost the competitiveness of the european union's economic players. free access to markets for european economic operators is a factor designed to boost their competitiveness and capacity for innovation and constitutes one of the priorities of the economic policy of the european union. it is the task of the european union, together with its trading partners and the european external action service, to define and renegotiate technical and quality standards so that they do not become anti-tariff barriers to access for union producers to external markets. negotiating transitional periods and consensual trade arrangements with the union's partners will stimulate european producers while protecting european production standards or geographical indications. the union must also insist on the principle of reciprocity just as non-union companies can participate in eu public procurement procedures, so european companies must have free access to tenders from authorities in foreign states. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because i believe that the world trade organisation is the most appropriate regulatory framework for free and fair trade globally. on the other hand, we need a reform of the way the wto operates and takes decisions so that the democratic deficit is eliminated. it is regrettable that several developing countries with a high degree of trade openness have suffered as a result of the economic crisis, in particular through job losses. i believe that the european union must be a strong player in the negotiations for the conclusion of the doha development agenda, by promoting the interests of the least developed or developing countries. we need to think about the needs of fragile states and create, through the wto, fairer rules for them.
in writing. − trade relations with countries around the world have always been and continue to be the basis for the development of economic relations at all levels with those countries. as these relations are often hampered by various obstacles, i think it would be useful if the european commission proposed to examine the possibility of establishing an early warning mechanism to detect such obstacles. as the european external action service is developing, i believe that the union should consider involving eu missions more closely, precisely in order to be able to identify such obstacles in good time and find solutions to avoid blockages in trade relations with third countries and, above all, blockages in the way of investors.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because, in addition to removing trade barriers that impede trade between the eu and its trading partners, we also need to achieve reciprocity in market access. in this way, we increase the chances of european firms gaining more market share abroad, which is important given that by 2015, 90% of global economic growth will be generated outside the eu and we need to help european investors seize all the opportunities that exist.
in writing. − i voted for the parliament's resolution on trade and investment barriers because i believe that the removal or reduction of unjustified non-tariff and other regulatory barriers applied by the eu's main strategic partner countries, through regulatory dialogue, should be one of the priorities of the eu's new trade policy. we invite the commission to address these issues in all multilateral and bilateral trade agreements, in particular free trade agreements, and to ensure that non-tariff barriers receive at least the same attention as is currently given to tariff elimination in all appropriate regulatory bodies, in particular in its negotiations with industrialised and emerging economies. i believe that due priority should be given to barriers to trade and investment affecting european service sectors, including information technology and telecommunications, financial services, construction services, retail and distribution. we call on the commission to pursue a cross-sectoral, comprehensive and sustainable strategy on raw materials, so that restrictions and duties on raw materials exports applied by some countries do not affect global economic development and the achievement of the europe 2020 strategy objectives.
on behalf of the alde group. i believe that this debate on the lisek report today is a significant debate for the future of the common security and defence policy. i would like to welcome a report on substance, a report which analyses the subject but also tries to offer solutions and which, beyond all this, is a report which offers the chance of cohesion in the field of security and defence policy. we now have the opportunity, to paraphrase al gore, to turn this crisis into an opportunity for the defense industry and for the future of our common security policy; but i cannot help stressing that this dramatic reduction in defence budgets in the member states may pose a risk to our common security, may maintain the already significant gaps between the united states and the nato member countries of the european union and may make the union vulnerable in terms of its ability to respond. i believe that the instruments we already have - and i am referring to the european defence agency - must be used in a meaningful way: we must increase its capacity to react and its capacity to integrate for this policy of 'pooling and sharing', which is the only solution for europe to have common capabilities, not to lose what it has, to ensure interoperability in the common defence system and to be effective in the missions it has and which, unfortunately, it is likely to have. i believe that europe has an obligation to build a common technological and industrial base, to use the research capacity that some of the member states have and to continue to give priority to honest procurement solutions, because one of the causes that has made these budgets vulnerable is the corruption issues in the defence procurement system. we already have a code of conduct, but we will have to use that code of conduct much more effectively and when we do succeed in making purchases, we will do so on grounds of expediency in the interests of european citizens.
mr president, the current effort to save the euro carries important security and defence implications which need our attention. first, the envisaged rigorous fiscal and budgetary discipline calls for continuing down-sizing of our defence budgets while security challenges continue to accumulate, including in our immediate neighbourhood. even if neither of those challenges is yet a threat, their accumulation, if unattended, might confront us with a dangerous and threatening mix in the future. second, europe is increasingly forced to sell its assets, and not always to a friendly buyer. again, if this is not attended to, we might end up with strategic european assets in the wrong hands. third, the effort to save the euro has already undermined the eu’s internal solidarity. with decision-making concentrated in the hands of the euro countries, suspicion and even recrimination have crept to the surface, potentially undermining our pooling and sharing effort. fourth, at a time when the us is diminishing its contribution to nato and talk about a smaller alliance has already been initiated across the atlantic, europe’s credibility – as both global actor and security provider – suffers.
the financial crisis has shown us more clearly than ever that we have two options: either division on the verge of european disintegration or enhanced cooperation. the second way is, at the level of this parliament, i think generally far preferable, firstly because in a globalised world it is the only way in which we can play a meaningful role. china's defense budget, which ms. gomes was talking about earlier, has increased in the last 10 years by almost 200%. in the meantime, the member states of the union are on the verge of reducing all their expenditure in this sector. the only logical solution is therefore better coordination of defence planning and a pooling and sharing of our capabilities. the intervention in libya has clearly shown us why we need to do this. in addition to our involvement in nato, i believe the time has come to build a true european defence capability. the report we are voting on proposes concrete steps to achieve this objective, and i would point out three elements among those steps: 1. the creation of a european semester of security and defence reviews; 2. strengthening the 'security' section of the framework programme for research and technological development; 3. the development of a military erasmus to facilitate the development of a common culture and approach to security. i would like to end by congratulating my colleague lisek on his excellent work.
i fully agree with our colleague lisek that the sharing and use of capabilities is no longer an option but a necessity. defense budgets are too small at the moment, so the best way to ensure military capabilities is cooperation. simulators, for example, can be used in rotation. plus, we can buy a lot more f-16s together. we already have two examples of how nato member states are using capabilities together: military transport planes, for which each country pays a certain number of flights, by charter, and maritime cooperation between france and britain, in which one provides the ports and the other the ships. the european air transport command initiative is a very useful example where the use of existing capabilities is optimised by transferring competences to a common structure. we need to adapt this model to other sectors of operational support, such as transport helicopters, maritime patrol aircraft and maritime transport capabilities.

member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr perello, and all the members of the committee on the environment for their work and commitment in reaching this agreement at first reading. i welcome the agreement reached between the three institutions on the amendment of the fruit juice directive. this fruit juice directive contains a number of provisions which ensure the free movement of products within the european union, their quality and - as mr perello said - consumer protection. the compromise reached clarifies the key points, particularly as regards consumer information, and thus meets parliament's wishes on these points. i would also like to point out that this is one of the first proposals by the commission in the agricultural field which follows the ordinary legislative procedure established by the treaty on the functioning of the european union. i am particularly pleased that, thanks to a joint effort between our institutions, the discussions could be finalised at first reading. i think that was a very good experience for all that will follow in this ordinary procedure in the agricultural field. this proposal for a directive introduces a number of new provisions. it provides for a ban on the addition of sugars to fruit juices, and also specifies a period of time during which the consumer may be informed of this ban, as mr perello has said. some existing provisions have also been clarified. the provision on 'multifruit' juices has been revised so that the consumer is clearly informed by the name of the product in the list of fruits which make up the juice. the three institutions also agreed, at the request of parliament, that fruit nectars containing sweeteners could not bear the words 'without added sugar' on the labelling. at the request of parliament too, we introduced a new article to confirm that imported products must comply with the requirements of the directive, just as those developed in the european union. finally, other provisions, such as the distinction between straight fruit juice and juice based on concentrate, have not been aligned with the codex standard, which in this particular case is less demanding. we therefore remain more demanding on this point than the codex standards. this decision, approved by a large majority of member states and supported by parliament, is in line with our objective of encouraging better consumer information. with this agreement on the amendment of the fruit juices and similar products directive, we now have a legislative text which clarifies certain requirements of the current directive, enriches it with new provisions and thus fulfils the objectives which were set. in conclusion, i would like to give my agreement on behalf of the commission to the compromise which was reached and approved by coreper on 18 november. i therefore also hope that there will be a positive vote on this agreement which has been reached.
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on agriculture and rural development. − this proposal for a directive aims to improve certain provisions concerning the composition, use of reserved names, production specifications and labelling of fruit juices in order to ensure better distribution within the european union. the report is the second amendment to directive 2001/112/ec and aims to make a better distinction between fresh fruit juices, concentrated fruit juices and nectars. i wanted to simplify the rules on flavour restoration and to remove the mention of sugar from the list of authorised ingredients. at the same time, there is a proposal to allow the words 'without added sugar' to appear on the labels of fruit juices for a limited period. as far as the producers are concerned, we must give them the time they need to adapt to this situation - the production of sugar-free juices - and to inform consumers of all products in all countries that they will find new products in stores without this mention, at the same time as those produced so far. we must not forget that they, the consumers, must be aware of all the changes brought about by the new directive, and last but not least i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on this very important report.

in writing. the aim of this proposal for a regulation is to reduce the amount of phosphorus used in household washing machine detergents and to better harmonise the different national rules. phosphates end up in our water systems, rivers, streams, lakes and especially in the danube basin and the baltic sea. phosphorus in household laundry detergents and automatic dishwasher detergents (mav detergents) contributes significantly to the direct presence of phosphorus in water channels, causing eutrophication. i welcome the widespread consensus that in household laundry detergents the maximum amount of phosphorus should be set at 0.5 grams per dose for a standard load of laundry. expressing this limit in grams per load and not in percentage by weight, as originally proposed by the commission, will allow laundry detergent manufacturers to produce more compact, concentrated formulations that will not contain more than 0,5% phosphorus by weight of a current 'standard dose', but in which phosphorus (from phosphonates) could constitute more than 0,5% of the total weight; likewise for the inclusion in the proposal of household mav detergents, the limit should be set at 0,5% by weight.
in writing. i would like to welcome the outcome of the negotiations with the council on the use of phosphates and other phosphorus compounds in household detergents. i believe that these measures to limit the phosphorus content of detergent must necessarily be linked to improved waste water treatment, but also to improved agricultural techniques - agriculture is also a source of phosphorus for surface waters. the rapporteur's proposal to also focus on the feasibility of banning phosphates and the possible consequences of such a ban for industrial detergents is more than welcome if we really want to clean up european waters, but we must be realistic and recognize that at present this is not technically or economically possible. however, i believe that more investment is needed in identifying alternatives to phosphates and other phosphorus compounds in detergents to better achieve our environmental and public health objectives. in addition, i would like to draw attention to the fact that our efforts must not stop here and that we must promote this approach to limiting the phosphate content of detergents in other non-eu countries as well.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive on fruit juices and certain similar products intended for human consumption. it is necessary to support the european sector by adapting the directive to international law and the codex and by establishing the same rules for all products marketed in the eu. the aim is to promote the free movement of these products, but also to clarify legislation on their labelling and classification, authorised ingredients and the admissibility of certain practices. the revision of the proposal will therefore also benefit imported products currently marketed in the european union. the new directive will give third country producers the opportunity to improve product quality through more sustainable production processes. uniform rules for all actors will also prevent fraud and unfair competition and help clarify the information provided to consumers.
in writing. − we supported the new changes, as the labels for juices will be much clearer in the future. juice mixtures, for example, will reflect the exact proportions of the composition. thus, a mixture of 90% apples and 10% oranges will have to be clearly labelled 'apple and orange juice', whereas such mixtures are currently marketed with the label 'orange juice'. labels such as 'juice mix' will only be used if three or more types of fruit are present. i believe that all of this clarification will be extremely helpful to people who suffer from diabetes or who are on a diet.
in writing. − the aim of this legislative proposal is to amend council directive 2001/112/ec by incorporating more of the provisions of the codex alimentarius standard. the parliament’s draft report suggests that the rules arising from adaptation of the directive to the codex should be equally applicable to all products marketed within the eu, regardless of whether they are produced in the eu or imported. the commission and the member states shall carry out information campaigns to inform consumers of the different categories of juices and similar products. concerning the issue of flavour reconstitution, i support the commission’s proposal that it should remain optional. the report suggests limiting the commission’s powers to adopt the delegated acts from ‘an indeterminate period of time’ to five years with the possibility of proceeding to a tacit renewal. moreover, an 18-month transition period added to the transposition period would serve to use up stock manufactured according to old standards and to adapt to new rules. adapting the directive to the codex alimentarius standard will allow the same criteria to be applied to products manufactured in the eu and to imported products. consequently, consumers will no longer be confused on the safety and quality of juices.
in writing. − we have had many discussions in the environment committee over the last few years about the labelling of food and drink. broadly speaking i think that eu legislation is ensuring clearer and more accurate labelling for the consumer and is helping people to make informed choices about what they eat and drink. this directive adds to that, specifically by requiring the labelling of natural sugars in fruit nectar and by clarifying the rules around ‘no added sugar’ claims. clear and honest labelling is one of the main tools we have to tackle diet-related problems in the eu, and whilst the food information to consumers regulation and the health and nutrition claims regulation provide most of the legal framework for this, additions are sometimes necessary. i would like to thank the rapporteur for his efforts to negotiate with the council and congratulate him on this report.
