reporting for the tran opinion - in the field of transport, there are some key points that need to be clarified. in the rail transport sector, the completion of the single european railway area, the opening up of the market, the continuation of the cancellation of historic debts of railway undertakings and the strengthening of regulatory bodies are essential factors in ensuring fair competition. the infringement procedures launched by the commission against member states for the inadequate application of the first railway package should be continued. in the aviation sector, the most important aspect is the completion of the single european sky because it will propose a performance scheme that will bring price transparency. there are passenger rights now in all areas of transportation. i think i proposed and i think it's good that there should be a tourist menu in the same sense. thank you to mr. schwab and mr. fox for your cooperation.
it is clear that the european union's competition policy has over the years led to the removal of many obstacles to the free movement of goods, services and people and has enabled the interests of european consumers to be protected. however, i believe that it is possible to improve the regulation in this area. i shall refer here to one of the subjects dealt with in this report, namely the regulation of credit rating agencies. this oligopolistic sector is characterised by barriers to market entry, lack of transparency and conflicts of interest. the ratings published by these agencies are, unfortunately, not just opinions. they affect the well-being of all european citizens through higher interest rates and increased price volatility. however, we lack strict rules on transparency and on holding agencies accountable for errors. the european executive must step up its efforts to increase competition in this sector. i therefore welcome its recent proposal in this area, while also stressing that the option of establishing a european public credit rating agency should also be considered. the independence of such an institution from the private sector would aim to increase competition and eliminate conflicts of interest.
i too would like to congratulate my colleague schwab on this very good report. i have three things i want to discuss. as regards the temporary state aid scheme, it must be admitted that it was a useful one and that its extension was a good idea in principle. of course, the extension cannot go on indefinitely, and if we have to make these extensions, we must add strict conditionality, especially with regard to the banking system - i am referring to the distribution of dividends, to the size of the balance sheet - because there must be a balance between the stability of the banking system and a satisfactory degree of competition. as regards the energy package, i encourage the commission to be very careful as most member states are behind in implementing the third energy package. as regards the amount of the anti-trust fines, i am in favour of staggering payments - we must not bankrupt european businesses, but neither should it be an excuse for those who knowingly engage in anti-competitive practices.
i would like to congratulate mr. schwab on his report. i would like to welcome the adoption of the third railway package, which will improve competition in rail transport. i think it is a step forward towards the realisation of a single european transport area. as a member of the itre commission and parliament's rapporteur for the e-government report, i would like to stress the importance of implementing e-procurement systems to increase transparency and access to the public procurement market, which amounts to 16% of the european gross domestic product. i also ask the commission to urgently amend the directive on electronic signatures so that we can ensure that they are mutually recognised throughout the european union. finally, madam president, i would ask the commission to review the legislation so that we give more bargaining power to the final consumer. unfortunately, citizens often do not read a service contract and do not have the power to negotiate changes to its terms.
i'd like to congratulate the reporter. mr. schwab has put in a lot of effort and produced an extraordinary report. i would like to draw attention to the restructuring of banks, which has been one of the main challenges facing the european union in the field of competition. in order to avoid distortions of competition, i believe that banks should turn to the use of private capital resources, including through restructuring and conversion of debt into equity instruments. only if strictly necessary and there is no other possibility should national governments be allowed to intervene, in which case national inspectors must ensure that recapitalisation plans do not lead to any excessive reverse leverage. we must be very careful and do everything possible to minimise distortions of competition in the internal market and we must strike a balance between aid to financial institutions and respect for competition.
i voted in favour of this report because the support for afghanistan must be maintained if we want the progress in that country to be irreversible. with the international military presence diminishing, the importance of civilian aid will increase even more. the assistance provided by the union must be subject to appropriate budgetary control. it's not just accounting concerns, but ways of making sure that the funds are used in the best way. to the same end, better coordination between donors is needed, including in terms of reporting and auditing. i would draw your attention to article 22, which makes very useful proposals on this subject. i also underline romania's commitment to security and stabilisation efforts in afghanistan, as demonstrated by its participation in operations with almost 2 000 soldiers.
i voted in favour of this report because i appreciate the amendment to regulation no 1406/2012 as presented by my colleague. a new financial framework and a clearer allocation of competences are needed for the european maritime safety agency to function optimally. i believe that it should promote cooperation between the specialised border police departments of the member states, but also of third countries. i am referring to the series of naval exercises carried out by the romanian border police in conjunction with the turkish coast guard in september 2011. this will strengthen cooperation between the black sea basin states and reduce the time needed to respond to maritime incidents. support cooperation between specialised educational institutions for the exchange of experience and good practice. for example, the naval academy mircea cel bătrân is involved in the erasmus programme.
i voted for this resolution because in syria the brutal repression against the citizens continues. in recent months, the regime has already claimed over 5,000 victims, according to un estimates. we cannot stand by and watch this situation unfold. the international community must take a stand and the european union has a duty to step up its efforts to get the syrian leaders to stop the violence. i welcome the eu's decisions on new restrictive measures against syria and hope that they will have the desired effect. to this end, it is important to define as soon as possible concrete details for putting the new sanctions into practice. i stress the importance of constantly evaluating which measures are more effective. i appreciate the positive role turkey has played in responding to the syrian crisis, including through its efforts to respond to humanitarian emergencies.
i voted in favour of the resolution because the european union needs a solid framework for preventing and correcting macroeconomic imbalances. the economic, financial and structural indicators in the scoreboard will help to identify member states that may be affected by such situations. alert thresholds shall be established for each indicator. it is important, however, that they are complemented by a country-specific economic analysis. i call attention to the in-depth balance sheet. it should include a rigorous assessment of the sources of imbalances. however, the speed and transparency of the analysis are essential. in the event of serious macroeconomic imbalances being identified, monitoring needs to be intensified. i support the integration of the procedure for monitoring economic imbalances into the forthcoming european semesters.
i voted in favour of this report because the union needs a competitive, efficient and integrated transport system. i welcome the commission's proposal to create a unified transport network. it will contribute to the completion of the internal market in this field. i would point out that at european level the transport sector provides some 10 million jobs and accounts for around 5% of gdp. the differences between the eastern and western regions of the union in terms of the level of infrastructure development need to be reduced. stability of project financing must be ensured. i would like to draw attention to the importance of developing transport networks in the new member states. in my country, the €2.2 billion transylvania motorway project will link european and central asian markets.
on behalf of the alde group. i have chosen to explain my vote because, as rapporteur on this report, i abstained from voting on it. i understand that there are people in this parliament who avoid debating a report when it says nothing or says very little, as is the case with this strategy on central asia. although the european union adopted a strategy in 2007, and this parliament has two resolutions, the report does not really assess how the strategy has been implemented; it is an inventory of problems, in a language that is difficult to understand, which clearly shows that the situation in the area is not even known. they talk about a security situation, ignoring the fact that there are neutral countries in the area. the involvement of these countries in the afghan conflict is unknown. but beyond that, this report imposes a certain kind of thinking which, in my view, is detrimental to this parliament. it gives directions and tries to export economic and cultural models to an area that is totally different, throwing this area further into the beach of influence and interest of a russia that wants to rebuild a former soviet union. i think that this kind of superficial approach, marked by a lack of information, marked by a biased approach, at least in our relations with central asia, has no place. i believe that central asia can become a priority and is a priority for many of the member states, and the fact that we condition a number of agreements in the area of human rights is necessary, but this conditioning must not remain declarative. it must be followed by involvement in this area, by an attempt to export our models, our good european practice, and supported by educational cooperation with these countries.
i voted in favour of this report because it seeks to underline the importance of strategic relations with central asia. their potential has not been fully exploited at union level, including in economic and commercial terms. for the countries of the region, cooperation with the european union means access to a huge retail market, an alternative export destination, and new opportunities for technological and industrial development. from the union's perspective, economic relations offer opportunities for diversifying sources of supply of energy and raw materials. efforts to achieve nabucco need to be stepped up. i also stress the importance of launching other projects to link up energy and transport networks. for example, romania proposed to kazakhstan to participate in the agri gas transportation project as well as the connection to the constanța-trieste oil pipeline project.
i voted for this report because we need to adapt the community acquis on health and safety at work to the new risks in this field. for example, sustainable solutions are needed to reduce psychosocial risks. the austerity measures during the economic crisis must not affect the level of safety at work. i would like to mention that employees of smes are most often exposed to occupational risks. 82% of all accidents at work and 90% of all fatal accidents occur in smes. it is necessary to develop a european programme for the monitoring of occupational risks. i support the idea of creating unique methods for assessing the impact of health and safety at work. at the same time, national strategies must be implemented effectively, with the involvement of workers and social actors.
in writing. − i appreciate the work of the rapporteurs who have presented the advantages and disadvantages of the various forms of aid to afghanistan. i appreciate your firm request to the european commission for more transparency on the agreements with the afghan side to verify the efficiency of the use of funds. there are grievances about the way the funds are being used, related to the high level of corruption in the afghan administration. the recommendations in the report are therefore important and will have to be taken into account by the european commission. it's a well-written, professional report that i voted for.
in writing. − the european union must respect its status as a partner with countries outside the european community, but also as a guarantor of respect for human rights, the rule of law and all instruments of democracy throughout the world. the european union has taken on the responsibility of supporting afghanistan in strengthening the rule of law. but this commitment does not mean a lack of control over european funds for the afghan people. in this context, the stabilisation and reconstruction process in afghanistan should be further supported. this support is necessary, but must be accompanied by additional measures to control and coordinate expenditure following referrals from the court of auditors, which identified certain irregularities in the management of european funds. we must be willing to provide assistance to afghanistan to ensure that regional and national institutions function in an efficient and transparent manner. in this regard, it is necessary to support the strengthening of the role of the afghan parliament, judiciary and audit authorities. the national and subnational elected bodies must be helped and encouraged to exercise close supervision of the use of european funds.
in writing. − in the context of the re-examination of european competition policy, it is imperative that decision-makers do not forget that the key to the success of the european economic and social model has been and remains the balance between incentive and competition policies. it is equally important that the re-examination of the legislative framework should always have the ultimate interest of consumers as its reference and objective. it is important that the procedures for sanctioning anti-competitive practices are as transparent as possible and as easy to understand for european consumers. it is equally important that european competition measures increase the transparency of the price-setting process so that consumers make a legitimate and informed decision. last but not least, compensation or penalties for infringements of european competition rules must be reoriented in principle and institutionally towards consumers. in many cases, fines imposed on producers or traders are collected by the state, thus depriving consumers affected by the lack of competition of the remedies they deserve. the creation of a european fund to cover the cost of crossborder actions in the field of competition can make up for regulatory shortcomings or inefficiencies in national legislation, while contributing to the development of the european economic framework.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the annual report on the competition policy of the european union, as i considered that stricter rules in this area were needed, especially in times of crisis. competition should be encouraged, in particular in the energy, credit rating agencies and banking sectors. the problem of 'too big to fail' banks, which received state aid during the crisis, needs to be addressed. it is surprising that these institutions can benefit from unlimited access to liquidity, but the european central bank has consistently expressed its reluctance to become the lender of last resort for the member states.
in writing. − the competition rules that the european union has been implementing for several decades are proving effective, with the fall in the cost of making calls abroad being one of the most representative examples. the union and the member states must continue to work together to remove any obstacle to the free movement of goods, services, persons and capital, and to update the rules in force periodically, so as to enable the union to meet the challenges it faces and to respond to rapid global developments. i also believe that the existence of flexible procedures allows the union's competition policy to remain a constructive and stabilising factor and provides an opportunity for adaptation to real situations, especially as regards the possibility for all consumers to make an appropriate choice.
in writing. - i voted for this report because i believe that workers who are made redundant should be supported in their search for a new job. union assistance in this regard needs to be more dynamic. the co-financing of active labour policies by the egf is all the more important in times of financial and economic crisis. the workers made redundant by renault in france should be granted financial assistance. i stress the need to speed up the procedure for granting subsidies. the efficiency and transparency of their award are of paramount importance. i believe that the 65% co-financing rate through the european globalisation adjustment fund should not be reduced. i recall that in september, nokia decided to relocate its business from romania to asia. as a result, over 2200 employees are to be made redundant as of january 2012. in order to provide financial support to them, romania is preparing to apply for financial assistance from the egf.
in writing. −this application fulfils the conditions for establishing the financial contributions as provided for in article 10 of regulation (ec) no 1927/2006. the application does not cover workers at renault who opted for early retirement and could not benefit from egf assistance under regulation (ec) no 1927/2006, but whose pension rights have been affected by the interim application of the pension reform. i support the mobilisation of eur 24 493 525 from the egf to support the workers concerned by the application. measures financed by the egf should lead to long-term employment. we ask the commission to ensure firm and careful monitoring and guidance to ensure that the proposed training offer corresponds to local economic trends. however, egf assistance should not replace actions which are the responsibility of undertakings under national law or collective agreements, nor measures to restructure undertakings or sectors.
in writing. − as we know, public access to official eu documents is a very important issue for the transparency of the european institutions and other eu bodies. i appreciate the rapporteur's ideas and especially his perseverance in supporting them, this being the second report on this subject, because of the deadlock that has arisen since the adoption of the first report. first, it should be noted that public access to eu documents increases the transparency of the eu institutions, which in turn leads to a higher level of trust and citizens' closeness to the eu. i am pleased to see that the report has made a number of ambitious changes to the commission's proposal, proposals which give citizens wider access to the commission's text, while ignoring the case law of the court of justice of the european union on some issues (e.g. turco v council). second, the definition of 'documents' retained is much more appropriate than that of the commission. third party documents held by institutions must be accessible under the current system, which has worked quite well. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of personal data.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on public access to european parliament, council and commission documents. the effects on officials' tasks of drafting, recording, negotiating, classifying and archiving eu documents should be harmonised, while protecting the efficiency and transparency of the eu institutions. with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the message should be to increase the transparency of the way the eu institutions, offices, bodies and agencies operate, including bringing european forces closer to citizens.
in writing. − i voted against the report on public access to european parliament, commission and council documents because it does not help to achieve the european objective of greater transparency. moreover, this report ignores existing legislation and interinstitutional agreements. the proposed text also fails to take account of the protection of parties in competition cases and of personal data. the need for transparency should be a basic principle for european legislation and the public should have a right of access to all relevant documents concerning eu legislation, but this transparency should not be confused with and identified with access to information leading to certain institutional decisions. such identification would be to the detriment of the institutions, as the publication of informal information on ongoing procedures could lead to interinstitutional decisions being influenced by lobby groups, for example. i believe that access to documents should be legally supported, contribute to transparency and eliminate bureaucracy, not create confusion.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal to amend the regulation on public access to european parliament, council and commission documents. after the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the legal basis for public access to documents is article 15 (3) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, as consolidated. this provision extends the right of public access to documents of all union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. this regulation shall apply to all documents held by an institution, body, office or agency of the union, that is to say, documents drawn up or received by that entity and held by it, in all fields of activity of the union. this provision shall apply to the court of justice, the european central bank and the european investment bank only where they perform administrative functions. transparency should also reinforce the principles of good administration in the union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies, in accordance with article 41 of the charter and article 298 tfeu. internal administrative procedures should be defined accordingly and sufficient financial and human resources should be made available to put the principle of openness into practice. the institutions shall take the necessary measures to create a common interface for the registers of the institutions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the regulation establishing a european maritime safety agency. the commission proposal is based on a 2008 consultation of emsa stakeholders, an external evaluation and an impact assessment carried out by the commission. the proposal also reflects emsa's five-year strategy adopted by its management board. the commission also published a report (com ((2011) 0286)) showing that the use of an eu oil spill detection and monitoring system reduces costs by around 20% compared to the use of national systems. as a result of the implementation of the third maritime safety package, emsa has already been given new tasks. emsa has concluded a number of standby oil spill response vessel contracts with private operators who will switch from their normal activity to pollution response in the event of an emergency. the commission proposal states that these vessels could also be used to combat pollution from other sources, including oil platforms.
in writing. − the european union and the member states are making a major effort to prevent the effects of accidental pollution, especially in the case of marine pollution from oil platforms or tankers, and the proposal to establish a joint european coast guard service is all the more appropriate in such situations, which require rapid intervention and effective coordination of response actions.
in writing. − emsa, the agency set up in 2003 in the wake of the pollution caused by the tanker 'erika', is responsible for ensuring a high, uniform and effective level of maritime safety and prevention of pollution from ships in the eu. the regulation proposed by the commission refers to the fact that the agency's expertise in this area should be used to the full and its role in providing support and assistance to the bodies or entities concerned (the commission and the member states) in preventing pollution from oil installations should be strengthened. we need to extend emsa's activities so that its expertise and current technical services can be used for a wider range of policies. the previous amendments to the agency's statute are not sufficient to address the new challenges that emsa will face, many of which represent external challenges either to emsa alone or to emsa and the eu as a whole.
in writing. − the proposed regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1406/2002 establishing a european maritime safety agency (emsa) is an opportunity to strengthen the existing functions of emsa to boost environmental protection objectives and accident response capacity in eu waters. the agency's tasks relate to both accidental and illegal discharges. initially, they focused on hydrocarbon pollution. since 2007, however, the agency has also been active in the field of marine pollution caused by dangerous and harmful substances (e.g. chemicals). the agency should carry out inspections in third countries in the mediterranean and black sea and baltic sea regions in whose waters oil and gas exploration and production activities are carried out, and provide assistance to those third countries to strengthen their capacity to improve the safety of their offshore operations. cooperation with third states in the implementation of tasks should be strengthened to allow for a more rapid approach. the organisation of the monitoring and detection system for oil spills at eu level is also less costly for the european taxpayer (by around 20%) and more efficient than doing so at national level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1406/2002 establishing a european maritime safety agency (emsa), as the purpose of extending the powers of the emsa is to ensure a high, uniform and effective level of maritime safety and the prevention of pollution from ships. while the emsa should focus on the priority tasks in the field of maritime safety, the agency should also be entrusted with additional tasks reflecting the development of maritime safety policy at eu and international level. the agency has already demonstrated that certain tasks, such as satellite monitoring systems, can be carried out more effectively at european level. where these schemes can be used to support other policy objectives, member states save money in their national budgets, which is a real european added value. the emsa should act in the interest of the union and follow the guidance of the commission, promoting the union's policy on maritime safety through scientific and technical cooperation with third countries. one year after the entry into force of the new regulation, the commission shall present a study on a system of coordination of national coast guard services, clearly highlighting its costs and benefits.
in writing. - the syrian regime must be firmly condemned by a democratic space like the eu, where human rights are a fundamental value. there is clear evidence of the brutal repressive measures taken by the syrian regime against its own people, including children and women, the latter having, moreover, made a great contribution to the struggle for democracy in syria. the syrian authorities must immediately end the violent repression against peaceful protesters and harassment of their families and release all detained protesters, political prisoners and journalists. the regime in damascus must immediately allow access to international humanitarian organisations, human rights organisations and the international media. it's the only way to demonstrate goodwill on the part of the syrian leadership and commitment to democratic values. this should be done in parallel with independent and transparent investigations into the systematic, serious and widespread violations of human rights and fundamental freedoms committed by the syrian authorities and military security forces. all those responsible must be held accountable without delay at the international level. the syrian people have legitimate demands and it is imperative to promote a national political dialogue involving all democratic forces and civil society in syria.
in writing. - unfortunately, the arab fall did not give us the same reason for hope as the arab spring. the syrian government's tough stance has generated an equally tough stance from the government's opponents, who see no military solution to the crisis. i do not think it is in the eu's interest to support a solution in syria similar to that in libya. i don't think that diplomacy has exhausted its solutions in the case of syria. violence never solves things, it only complicates them, not to mention the suffering of the innocent. an important aspect is the determination of all members of the international community to respect the sanctions. perhaps a dialogue with the russian federation, china and other traditional allies of syria, who do not welcome the sanctions, could bring about a change of attitude. what is certain is that we have an obligation to do everything within our power to stop the repression in the streets of syrian cities and to make the democratization process a reality.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the scoreboard for monitoring macroeconomic imbalances, as it underlines the importance of closer coordination of member states' economic policies. i also believe that both current account deficits and surpluses need to be monitored, as both contribute to the creation of macroeconomic imbalances.
in writing. − regarding parliament's resolution on the scoreboard for monitoring macroeconomic imbalances, i voted for amendments 5 and 6, which call on the commission to submit proposals for indicators on income inequality and poverty reduction and stress the need for the unemployment indicator to be considered as an independent indicator, on a par with other indicators. i also voted in favour of amendment no 1, which states that the thresholds for current account imbalances envisaged so far (+6%, -4%) are not consistent with the principle of symmetry and flagrantly favour, a priori, member states with current account surpluses. i voted in favour of amendment 2, which stresses that the approach taken in the case of unit labour costs seems to be somewhat inconsistent with the provisions of article 6 of the regulation on the prevention and correction of macroeconomic imbalances, which explicitly states full compliance with article 152 tfeu, because this article sets from the outset a level of nominal wage increase that triggers the alert mechanism even in situations where gdp and productivity growth rates would allow growth above the set threshold.
in writing. − a health report on a health measure, which will bring more coherence to infrastructure development projects across the union, generate a more rational allocation of resources and put an end to waste, encourage the use of new technologies in the field, including for pollution reduction. i note the emphasis on further developing rail transport in the member states. i note in this context that the imf and the ec have made the granting of loans to romania conditional on the closure of over 1500 kilometres of railways. it is an unfortunate approach to say the least, which runs counter to the strategies proposed in this roadmap. i voted in favour of adopting the report because i am convinced that the measures proposed will lead to better integration of the transport networks in the member states and their development in the newly admitted countries.
in writing. − the creation of a single european transport area as a goal of the future european transport policy is directly linked to regional, environmental, economic, social, and employment policy. it serves the completion of the internal market, and accounts for some 5% of eu gdp and over 10 million jobs. it stimulates research and innovation, and helps the eu keep its lead and ‘excellence’ in the world. i strongly support increased wise (using the criterion of european-value-added) investment in transport as a precondition for sustainable growth and jobs for the whole of the eu, while helping to fight our way out of the crisis. we need clear and ambitious imperative targets, to be realised by the member states / the commission in both the medium and long run, for example: the commission has to draw up legal rules to reduce co2 and other greenhouse gas emissions by 20% compared to the 1990 reference figures and to set targets for the different modes of transport and to specify deadlines for commission proposals on issues including: the european railway agency (to be expected by 2012), social and working conditions and the ‘blue belt’ (both 2013), the internalisation of external costs for all transport modes (2014) and urban mobility (2015).
in writing. − i voted for the parliament's resolution on the roadmap for a single european transport area towards a competitive and resource-efficient transport system, as a single european transport area that removes all barriers between transport modes and national systems, without unfair competition and social dumping, is in the interests of european citizens. the transport sector is essential for the development of the eu, its regions and cities, accounting for around 5% of gdp and providing some ten million jobs. i stress the importance of developing transport infrastructure in the new member states, including road infrastructure, and of connecting their transport networks with those of neighbouring states. we ask the commission to take into account the development needs of the transport infrastructure in the new member states in the future multiannual financial framework, so that by 2025 the transport infrastructure in the new member states reaches the level of the infrastructure in the other member states. we call on the member states to remove the main bottlenecks in the european transport area by creating intermodal infrastructure and to give priority to cross-border projects between member states, without neglecting connections with neighbouring countries, and to propose an approved financing plan by 2015.
in writing. − the situation in european prisons has steadily deteriorated as they have become overcrowded, as a consequence of the deterioration in the social status of many european citizens. moreover, there is a systematic violation of the rights of the prisoners, the abuses committed against them. breaking the law doesn't justify mistreatment in prison. on the other hand, the situation of prison employees has deteriorated for exactly the same reasons. the report correctly puts the issues in context and makes pertinent recommendations. i particularly welcome the recommendation to the member states and the ec to establish and apply minimum standards for conditions of detention and imprisonment, and uniform standards for compensation to persons who have been wrongfully detained or sentenced. i voted in favour of the report, which has the quality of being realistic and proposing rational and feasible solutions.
in writing. − it is an important document addressing an issue which has generated and is generating discriminatory treatment in the labour market for european citizens from the newly admitted countries, especially those from romania and bulgaria. i have drawn attention to this unacceptable phenomenon and its consequences. despite the efforts of meps, some governments are still prolonging measures restricting access to the labour market for workers from certain countries. although the proposals and demands contained in the resolution are not as firm as they would be to bring about a change of substance, they are a step in the right direction. if we can follow what happens to the recommendations in the resolution, i hope we will not talk about these discriminations anymore. with that hope, i voted to pass the resolution.
in writing. - i think that states that impose restrictions on the labour market make a massive mistake by ignoring the economic interest of their own society and forcing it to confine itself to political judgments. following this logic, states that impose restrictions will try to extend them, turning them into electoral tools. the european union should act more boldly, especially in the current economic climate. we are in an economic impasse because the european perception of many member states is in a deadlock and many european governments have abandoned their claims of good europeanism under the pressure of elections. i am glad that we have had such a lively debate in the european parliament on this subject and i hope that the two resolutions adopted this year will have the effect of lifting the restrictions on the labour market for romanians and bulgarians. i would like to conclude by saying that the decline in economic activity does not exclude the need for growth. romanian workers are excluded from austerity, but required by any serious plan for growth. for example, a romanian bricklayer puts about 5,000 bricks a day in london. british construction companies have noticed the difference and prefer romanians, as an englishman is harder to find and does not have the same productivity.
in writing. the european parliament adopted today a resolution on the full free movement of workers within the european union. this resolution, which was added to the agenda of the plenary in extremis, was not examined in advance by the responsible parliamentary committee. this resolution aimed to open the labour markets of the eu member states fully to romanian and bulgarian workers. i have decided to vote against this resolution, on the basis of the clause in the treaties which allows a two-year delay in the total opening up of the labour markets. i support the free movement of workers in accordance with the european treaties every day as a member of the parliamentary committee on employment and social affairs. but the unprecedented crisis we are experiencing, the importance of unemployment, especially among young people, forces us to concentrate all our efforts at national level so that citizens can find their way back to employment. as the permanent rapporteur of the european social fund (esf) in the 27 member states, i am strongly committed to the professional integration of european citizens to promote their social integration. but we must keep in mind that in these difficult economic times, we cannot accept everything.
in writing. − at a time when social conflict is increasing, it is of the utmost importance to guarantee social cohesion in europe through effective integration policies promoting equal treatment, decent working conditions and social protection, and not to use derogations from fundamental freedom as a political weapon. mobile workers from romania and bulgaria have had a positive impact on the economies of member states which host mobile workers, being a milestone for eu integration, economic development, social cohesion, individual upgrading at professional level. the transitional measures imposed are counterproductive for combating false self-employment, undeclared work and irregular employment since workers without the right to enter the regular labour market freely sometimes have to work as a false self-employed or irregular worker, resulting in abuses of their labour rights. i have voted today for all transitional measures to be eliminated, given that there are no real economic justifications to restrict the right to work and reside on the territory of another member state for romanians and bulgarians. bulgarian and romanian citizens have the right to enjoy equal treatment with the rest of european citizens and this is also a way of ensuring fair competition between businesses and preventing any social and economic dumping.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on the free movement of workers in the eu, because it is a fundamental right of union citizens. we consider that the existing barriers to the free movement of romanian and bulgarian workers are counterproductive for eu citizens and call on the member states to abolish all the transitional measures in force, given that there are no real economic justifications to restrict the right of romanian and bulgarian citizens to work and reside in the territory of another member state. we call on the commission to clearly define 'serious labour market disturbances or the risk of such disturbances' and to prepare clear indicators and an improved methodology, based on economic and social indicators, to assess whether there are clear justifications for prolonging the partial or total restrictions imposed by certain member states to deal with the negative disruptions in their national labour markets that could be caused by romanian and bulgarian workers. we call on the commission and the member states to remove the transitional restrictive periods so that bulgarian and romanian citizens can enjoy equal treatment as provided for in the treaties, thus guaranteeing fair competition between businesses and preventing social and economic dumping.
in writing. − i voted in favour of adopting the report, based on the finding that the eu strategy for the countries of central asia has proved to be correct and that, despite the problems that still persist, we can see many changes for the better in terms of the objectives pursued. the report rightly stresses the importance of supporting efforts to democratize and to ensure that citizens' rights and freedoms are fully respected. the eu can contribute more effectively to structuring and strengthening civil society in the five countries covered by the report. i note with satisfaction the interest shown in supporting actions aimed at the sustainable development of the economies of these countries, which have suffered dramatically since the collapse of the former ussr. i note the attention given to actively combating poverty in the area, a scourge that is fueling social violence, religious fanaticism and even acts of terrorism. the eu's determination to meet its obligations, even in these conditions of crisis, is remarkable.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the state of play of the eu strategy for central asia as this region is of major importance to the union in terms of its trade potential and energy security and as the region has been affected by the recent global financial and economic crisis. i stress the importance of energy in relations with the countries of central asia, as it is a major source of revenue for these countries, as well as a potential source of energy security for the eu. the eu and the countries of central asia share a common interest in diversifying export routes and cooperating on energy and environmental sustainability. i would stress that the lack of energy (e.g. for heating and electricity) is making the situation worse for the poor in the central asian countries and the eu, in line with its climate change commitments, should step up its assistance in the region to develop a sustainable energy policy, including on the basis of energy efficiency and renewable energy sources. i believe that the review of the eu strategy for central asia must take into account the need to support its objectives with sufficient financial resources and to establish appropriate distribution models that reflect the realities of each country in the region.
in writing. − as several studies by international and european organisations indicate, one of the most important aspects of making health policies more effective, both in terms of reducing costs and improving overall health, is to encourage disease prevention. the organisation of work or production must not contravene this imperative of european policies. it is important that the action of the european institutions should be directed towards monitoring occupational risks and diseases, and that efforts should be made to integrate the definitions and instruments of health policy used by the member states. policies should have the objective, in line with the europe 2020 strategy, of preventing discriminatory treatment or differentiation between categories of european employees on the basis of access to health services. policies must also take into account the position of the more vulnerable occupational categories exposed to additional health risks. policies must therefore serve the interests of young or old employees, foreign workers or those employed on temporary contracts. another priority is the importance of creating a single european legislative framework governing the obligations of subcontractors towards their employees in the field of insurance and health services.
in writing. − the eu has strong legislation on health and safety at work, enabling the implementation of the european treaties and the charter of fundamental rights in the field of occupational health. but this is far from enough to guarantee safety and health at work, as the realities are pushing us to take more and more account of psychosocial risks. these risks are not sufficiently covered by community or national legislation. at european level, companies address these risks by offering training programmes, but workers are most often the ones who suffer from poor work organisation and management style. it is therefore necessary to study the relationship between workplace inconvenience and work organisation. the positive role of persons who legitimately alert to unrecognised risks within a company should be mentioned. the alerting process should be protected, as is the case in certain countries in europe and other parts of the world. in the uk, whistleblowers have been protected from dismissal and pressure since 1998. in the united states, their protection depends largely on the subject of the report and the status of the whistleblower.
in writing. − a very valuable report on an important area: health and safety at work. it's an area where i've seen a steady deterioration in the situation of employees, regardless of their nature. an example would be the increase in workplace suicides, or the deaths of some employees from exhaustion. also, under pressure from employers, a series of changes in legislation have been introduced, which worsen the situation of employees, their physical and mental health. the findings of the report are worrying and underscore the need for immediate action to change the situation. i consider the european commission's recommendation to facilitate the development of european standards for health and safety in enterprises to be essential, stressing the need for cooperation between member states to investigate the causes of accidents at work and to share best practices. i also think it is important to ask the european commission and the member states to propose measures to improve the working conditions of people with cancer or other occupational and chronic diseases. i voted in favour of adopting this report, convinced of its necessity and of the measures proposed by the authors.
in writing. − demographic changes at european level require appropriate measures by member states to ensure the necessary services for older people, namely the availability of trained staff in areas such as cleaning, care services and nursing homes. this requires, however, that member states also make efforts to ensure that accident prevention policies are respected, especially in the case of parttime work schemes, for which women are preferred. i believe that particular attention should be paid to outsourcing of certain jobs, such as cascading subcontracting, those for workers posted abroad or temporary contracts for young people and students.
in writing. − the theme of this report is topical, as we all know that jobs tend to be more productive the healthier they are. in the context of the current financial crisis, there is a risk that companies may consider reducing investment in occupational safety and health. young people are a vulnerable group, as they are more concerned with immediate job security, not considering the long-term consequences of a disease or injury in their youth. it is precisely to protect them that i believe that we must develop: 1. a european programme for monitoring occupational risks among young people based on health indicators; 2. - vocational training programmes with sector-specific information for the first months of work of young workers.
in writing. − the eu is currently facing an ageing population, the trend towards longer working lives and the need to ensure an increase in healthy life expectancy. inequalities were found within socio-occupational categories in life expectancy and difficult working conditions. 168 000 european citizens die each year as a result of accidents at work or occupational diseases, and 7 million are injured in accidents at work. labour inspection has an indispensable role, through education, persuasion and encouragement, in verifying the application of existing legislation and prevention by verifying the respect of decent working conditions for vulnerable groups of workers or for occupations that can be carried out 'off-the-shelf'. member states must ensure high quality standards of education and further training for labour inspectors, monitor regular medical checks, assess the results with a view to ensuring that workers are in a state of health compatible with the requirements of the workplace and strengthen sanctions against undertakings that do not comply with their obligations in respect of fundamental workers' rights. i ask the ec to develop guides to good practice in this area, stressing the need for member states to organise exchanges of good practice to increase the efficiency of workers at work.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the mid-term review of the european strategy 2007-2012 on health and safety at work, as the right to health is a fundamental right and as every worker benefits from the legal guarantee of healthy, safe and dignified working conditions. studies show that young workers aged 15-24 are at particularly high risk of injury, and the long-term consequences of an illness or injury in their youth can be considerable. i therefore continue to support the need to integrate the theme of health and safety at work into existing eu programmes such as 'youth on the move'. i voted against the part of paragraph f that considers extending working life for older workers is a solution to the labour shortage. i also voted against paragraph 71 because i believe that in order to reduce stress at work it is not enough to introduce special instructions on the ability to work under stress, as well as workshops on teamwork skills and to improve the integration of a particular group of employees, but that working conditions must be improved in a concrete way.
author. − rafiq tagi was a journalist and writer in azerbaijan and criticised the iranian government and religious oppression in azerbaijan. the journalist has received death threats since 2007, when an iranian fatwa was issued calling for his death. this year, on november 23rd, rafiq tagi was killed. there is suspicion that iranians or local islamic extremists are responsible for this murder. the azerbaijani authorities are investigating this murder. investigations must be swift, effective and impartial, and the murderers and those who ordered tagi's death must be identified and brought to justice. the iranian authorities have an obligation to cooperate with factual information and evidence during the investigation. in addition, the iranian authorities must urgently ban iranian clerics from publicly calling for the killing of people. the outcome - and therefore the responsibility for this investigation - is largely iran-related. i ask the azerbaijani authorities to do everything possible to protect the lives and safety of those living in azerbaijan for whom the fatwa, that is, the demand to be killed, has been issued.
i too express my regret at the death of the journalist rafig tagi and i condemn in the strongest possible terms this heinous murder, which demonstrates the consequences of religious extremism on human rights, first and foremost the essential right to life. the killing of this prominent journalist raises serious questions about the human rights situation in azerbaijan. this is all the more worrying as the country is a member of the eastern partnership, the council of europe and actively participates in the european neighbourhood policy. and yet, despite its international partnerships, azerbaijan has yet to demonstrate a serious commitment to ensuring press freedom and protecting fundamental freedoms activists. i too call on the azerbaijani authorities to carry out an urgent and objective investigation into the circumstances of the stabbing of rafig tagi and to act with all responsibility to end the impunity enjoyed by the perpetrators of crimes committed in the name of religious beliefs. i also call on the commission and the other european institutions to make any progress in cooperation with azerbaijan conditional on ensuring respect for human rights.
i would like to add my voice to that of mr vigenin, who said that we must choose our subjects very carefully. beyond what unfortunately happened in azerbaijan, we must emphasize one thing that is necessary: this type of crime knows no borders. i think we have to cooperate, all the member states, to try to prevent such actions, which are acts of cruelty, certainly, significant, but i don't think we can blame azerbaijan for this assassination. all we can ask azerbaijan is to mobilize and try to make the investigation much faster and more effective, because the discovery of the perpetrator, his conviction, is a main means of persuasion in order to prevent such heinous crimes.
the author. - we are also discussing afghanistan and pakistan today; in both countries we can identify some elements that can be described as positive - for example, in afghanistan, certain women have been appointed to positions of responsibility; gulnaz, who was a rape victim, was recently pardoned, initially sentenced to prison; on the other hand, in pakistan, the adoption of the law on the prevention of practices against women, as well as the law against acid attacks at the beginning of the week - all these are encouraging signs. but there are still things in both countries that are extremely, extremely serious: in afghanistan, domestic violence, as in pakistan; on the other hand, in afghanistan, stoning, disfigurement for violating social norms; in pakistan, women are victims of honor killings; forced conversion to islam; there are practices that are more than worrisome and we have to denounce them here.
the author. − this resolution, although addressed to these two countries with different situations in terms of the situation of women, has some issues in common, namely a dramatic situation in terms of equal opportunities, women's rights and, in particular, violence against women, with a preference for what is happening in pakistan. but we must admit that the situation in afghanistan has improved, at least from a legislative point of view. the recent constitution of afghanistan has an explicit provision on equal opportunities. the 2009 law on combating violence against women was put into effect. i also think that the representation of women has improved, but we have to admit that it will be a difficult situation after the troops have left afghanistan because, in these conditions, i think that what has been gained in this period is at risk of being lost very quickly. the european union must therefore step up its cooperation programmes to maintain an improved situation.
indeed, as my colleagues have said, there have been some improvements in afghanistan, but i find it appalling that the situation of women in afghanistan is still almost unchanged 10 years after the signing of the bonn agreement on the creation of the transitional government under the presidency of hamid karzai. high rates of maternal and infant mortality, the marginalization of women in society, the existence of fundamentalist courts in some regions and frequent armed attacks against girls and women attending schools or attempting to participate in public life are deeply worrying. despite progress in their representation in parliament and administration, afghan women remain victims of domestic violence, trafficking and forced marriage, lack of healthcare, and police and judicial discrimination. the saturday night explosion at the girls' school in pakistan speaks volumes about the plight of women in this country with which the european union is trying to develop a partnership but which risks being undermined by the brutal violation of human rights. i join the call to the afghan and pakistani authorities.
in writing. – we say that women are among the most vulnerable people in afghanistan and pakistan. however, their vulnerability rests solely on the way society perceives and treats women. vulnerability is a social construct, and what is made by people can by remade by people. violence is a main factor that makes women vulnerable. in afghanistan, on 12 november, a woman and her daughter were executed by stoning in ghazni, kandahar, an area where sharia law is imposed. in pakistan, asia bibi, a christian woman, mother of five children is the first woman to be sentenced to death under the blasphemy laws. she is being held on death row, while an islamic cleric offered a cash prize of about eur 5000 for her killing. the government in the two countries must put an end to such abuses and ensure the protection of the life and integrity of all, including women. the eu must urge the authorities of afghanistan and pakistan to protect women’s rights. we must assist, including with funding, the political actors and civil society who struggle to bring democracy, human dignity, and basic human rights in their countries.
the author. - i understand that some of our colleagues are wondering why we are talking about tunisia. i think we're talking about tunisia because we have a very interesting issue that concerns the tunisians. i could, in fact, see it when i was in the elections in this country, and that is a problem is how quickly the structures of authority can change and, in particular, the law enforcement and police forces. opinions were divided at the time of the elections, and i was talking to tunisian citizens: some said that the police and the security forces were intimidated and too weak; now this case of zakaria bouguira shows us the other side, the other opinion, namely aggressiveness. the key word in this regard i think should be the careful examination of the file, the punishment of those who are guilty for this particular case. in this way, tunisian citizens will have real confidence in their institutions.
zakaria witnessed the violence of the security forces against 13 young moroccans at the airport in tunis on november 13. because he tried to film, the police violently stopped him and took him and the 13 young people to the police station. there they were all subjected to other acts of violence and intimidation. zakaria was released within hours, but nine of the 13 youths remained in detention for another eight days. we demand an independent and impartial investigation into this case for those who were arrested and beaten. the tunisian revolution was actually about ending the abuses of the state. the recent free elections are one of the hallmarks of democracy, but they must be complemented by irreversible measures to respect human rights and freedom. the judiciary and law enforcement must uphold the law and build the rule of law, and we must support this, including financially.
i think this resolution should be seen by us as an early warning resolution about human rights violations in tunisia, because otherwise i don't understand why we have this double standard - a long silence on an authoritarian regime of ben ali and very quick action on a matter that is still under judicial investigation. but it is very clear that the tunisian authorities must understand from this incident that the rule of law is built with responsibility, to investigate, to punish those guilty of legal violations, otherwise it will become a habit. i hope that this resolution will be a wake-up call, unfortunately, also to the member states where similar things are happening and where things are being ignored; i hope that this resolution will also be a wake-up call to all those who understand how to control their populations by means of surveillance, because it is not only tunisia that is at risk of this path; the temptation of the totalitarian type is also found in the european union.
